What the AI assistant helps with Working with PILOT: setting up devices and objects, reports and templates, geofences, routes, events, notifications, users, and access rights API and integrations: API methods, authorization, request parameters, response handling, and code examples Pilot Extension: extension structure, required files and components, examples, and local testing The assistant can suggest links to the official documentation. If the information is not enough, it will help you prepare a request to technical support. How to ask a question 1. Go to the AI assistant 2. In the field at the bottom of the window, describe your question or task 3. Click the button to send the message 4. Read the answer. Follow the links to the documentation if you want to see detailed instructions For example, you can ask: How do I set up daily report sending? Why is the object online but no new points appear? Show an example API request for getting the list of objects Which files are needed to create an extension? To help the assistant understand the task better, say which section you are working in, what you want to do, and at which step the difficulty arose. If you need to refine an answer, ask a follow-up question in the same chat. For a different task, click “New chat” on the left side of the window. Chat history The “Recent chats” list on the left shows your conversations. Click a chat name to return to the messages and continue the discussion. How to rename a chat To change the name of a chat you have already worked with: 1. Click next to the chat 2. Select “Rename” 3. Enter the new name 4. Click “Save” How to delete a chat Click next to the conversation name and select “Delete”. Rating an answer Below the assistant s answer there are positive and negative rating buttons . Use them to mark whether the answer was helpful. If you want to explain what should be clarified or improved: 1. Click “Comment” below the answer 2. Enter your remark in the “Comment on the answer” window 3. Click “Save” Display settings The arrow at the top of the left panel collapses or expands the chat list. The theme button in the upper right corner of the chat switches between light and dark themes. The cross in the upper right corner of the window closes the AI assistant.

The additional settings menu is in the right part of the top panel. Click its icon to choose the interface language and theme, view news, contact support, or log out of the account. Interface theme Choose the display mode that is comfortable for your eyes: the light theme suits daytime work, and the dark theme reduces eye strain in the evening or at night. Interface language Choose the language that suits you. News Click “News” to open a window with the latest publications about the platform and the company. Here you can learn about PILOT updates and new features. Technical support If you have a question or need help, select “Tech support”. Describe what you want to do and at which step the difficulty arose. If an error appears, attach a screenshot, which will help specialists understand the situation faster. Extensions Select “Extensions” to open the list of PILOT s additional tools and enable the ones you need. For example, here you can enable AI Support if it is connected for your account. Logging out Click “Log out” to end your session under the current account. This is especially useful if you work on a shared computer.

In the work area you can work with the information of the current section and tab. To change the width of the work area, hover the mouse over the divider and drag it in the direction you need. Divider If you want to hide or show the work area, click the divider.

The map is a tool that clearly shows what is happening with objects. The map displays: Monitored objects Their current location Movement routes Significant geographic points and places Geofences Additional information about objects, for example status, speed, and direction The map is available when you work with tabs and sections. Most often it takes up most of the screen. If you want the maximum view of the map, you can hide the work area. To do this, click the screen divider . If you want to see only the map and remove all panels, titles, and browser buttons, press F11, and the screen expands to the full size of the monitor. Searching for objects on the map When you select objects in the list, they are displayed on the map automatically. 1 — Selecting an object in the list. To select an object, select the checkbox next to it 2 — The object on the map Moving around the map To move around the map, press the left mouse button and, without releasing it, drag in the direction you need. The map moves with the cursor. If you want to see another area, just drag the mouse.

All map tools are gathered in one place: a special panel in the lower right corner of the screen. Zooming There are several ways to change the map scale: 1. Buttons on the map toolbar and In the upper left part of the map there are buttons for quick zooming in and out. When you click the buttons, the map zooms in or out, but the point that was in the center stays in place. 2. Mouse scroll wheel Turn the mouse wheel: away from you to enlarge the map, toward you to reduce it. The cursor points to the area you want to examine in more detail. 3. Mouse double click Double-click the left mouse button at any point on the map, and it zooms in immediately. The current coordinates are always visible in the lower right corner and are updated as you move the mouse cursor over the map. Printing the map This function prints the current view of the map. When you click the print button, three print orientation options are offered: 1. Landscape: the map is printed in horizontal orientation. This orientation is convenient for displaying extended areas or objects arranged horizontally. 2. Portrait: the map is printed in vertical orientation. This format suits areas that extend vertically. 3. Auto: the system automatically chooses the best print orientation depending on the current map view and its proportions. Measuring area This tool helps you calculate the area of a section you select on the map. How to use it: 1. On the map, mark the corners of the shape you want to measure one after another 2. When you finish drawing the shape, the program calculates and shows its area automatically Measuring the distance between points This tool helps you easily calculate distances between any points on the map. How to use it: Click on the map to mark the first point 2. Click again to mark the second point 3. A line showing the distance appears between the points If you need to measure several segments, keep clicking on the map to add new points. The length of each segment is shown next to it. Choosing a map To change the map, click the map type selection button . Measuring distance along roads With this tool you can determine the distance along roads between selected points on the map. How to use it: 1. Click the first point on the map 2. Mark the intermediate points of the route one after another 3. Finish building the route with a second, final click 4. The system automatically calculates the path along existing roads. The total length and duration of the route are shown on the screen. Distance to the nearest vehicle This tool helps you quickly find the nearest vehicle and find out the distance to it from a selected point on the map. How to use it: 1. Click any point on the map for which you want to find the nearest vehicle 2. The system automatically determines the nearest vehicle and displays: — the vehicle number or object name — the distance from the selected point to the vehicle — the time it will take the vehicle to reach the point Geocoder The geocoder lets you find a point on the map by a specified address. How to use it: 1. Enter an address or coordinates in the geocoder field 2. A hint with a refined address appears below the input field 3. Click the hint with the exact address in the drop-down list 4. View the point you need on the map Coordinates : the current coordinates, updated as you move the mouse cursor over the map.

In professional cartography, a special term, “base map”, is used when choosing maps. For simplicity, we will use the more familiar term “map type”. The map type is the base layer of the cartographic image used in the monitoring system to display spatial data. PILOT offers several map types for displaying space in the user interface. The choice of a specific map type depends on your needs and preferences. Some maps are better suited for navigation, others for studying terrain or finding infrastructure objects. To change the map, click the map selection button . In the menu that opens, select the map type you need. It becomes the main one and will be loaded by default when you open the system. Map type Appearance Description OSM An open online map that is regularly updated by users around the world 2GIS A detailed city map with street and building names. It offers a high level of detail and a convenient interface for finding places Yandex A map from the Russian company “Yandex” showing cities and regions with roads, objects, transit maps, and traffic Yandex Sat High-resolution satellite images from “Yandex” with detailed visualization of the terrain Google Map The standard Google map with global coverage and regular updates Google Terrain A Google Maps display mode that emphasizes terrain relief and elevations Google Sat High-resolution satellite images from Google with regularly updated data Wiki Mapia A detailed map with object descriptions, created from OpenStreetMap and “Wikipedia” data TomTom A navigation map from TomTom that shows detailed road routes and is used in car navigation TomTom Dark The dark version of the TomTom navigation map TomTom Sat High-resolution satellite images from TomTom ArcGIS A professional geographic information system with many data layers Cosmo Sat High-quality satellite images of the entire surface of the Earth Dark The dark version of the map. Convenient for evening and night work, it reduces eye strain Gray A map in gray tones with a neutral design and improved readability

In the upper right part of the map there are additional functions that help display more contextual information on the map: connect custom layers, view streets, assess road conditions, and see GPS jamming zones. In this article: • Object layers : display of additional geographic data from KML/KMZ files • Street view : go to panoramic images of the area • Traffic view : display of road congestion on the map • GPS jamming : display of zones with different levels of GPS interference Object layers The “Object layers” function turns the display of additional geographic data from uploaded KML/KMZ files on the main map on and off. How to use the function: 1. Find the “Object layers” panel in the upper right corner of the map 2. Expand the list of available layers and select the checkboxes next to the layers you want to see You can enable several layers at the same time or turn off the additional data completely, leaving only the main map. To learn how to upload and work with KML/KMZ files, see the “KML settings” section. Street view The street view function lets you see panoramic photos of the area. Three viewing options are available: GSV: panoramic images from Google with high image quality and wide territory coverage YR: street panoramas from “Yandex”. They have good coverage in Russia and some neighboring countries OSC: panoramas created by a community of users. They may contain more recent images in some areas To enable street view: 1. Select the checkbox for this option in the upper right part of the map 2. Drag the yellow figure on the map to the place you need 3. Choose the viewing option you want: GSV, YR, or OSC 4. After you choose one of the options, the corresponding panorama service opens, where you can view interactive panoramas of the selected area. Traffic view The traffic view function shows current road congestion using color indication: Green: free-flowing traffic Yellow: moderate congestion Red: heavy traffic jams To turn on traffic display, select the checkbox for this option in the upper right part of the map. GPS jamming The “GPS jamming” function shows zones where GPS signal interference was recorded on the selected date. This data helps you assess areas where object coordinates may be determined less accurately because of an unstable GPS signal. The function is available on the map as a separate checkbox in the upper right part of the map. After you enable it, colored cells with the interference level are displayed on the map. A legend is displayed in the lower left corner: green: low interference level, 0–2% yellow: medium interference level, 2–10% red: high interference level, more than 10% You can also select the date for which to display data. To do this, use the “Date” field in the layer panel.

The system has built-in weather visualization from Windy.com, an online platform with interactive weather maps and forecasts. Weather data is displayed on top of the map and is automatically synchronized with its panning and zooming. How to connect the weather layer Getting an API key Register on the Windy API portal Create an API key 3.) You will receive a key in this format: 4epwZKT8erOIe6Boq2gfdhffs50ky By default, a trial (test) key is issued Trial limitations: — the GFS model is available — available layers: wind, temperature, pressure 2. Setting up the key in PILOT To make the weather layer available: 1.) The Windy configuration must be connected in the contract 2.) In the admin panel, add the following parameter in the contract settings: windy_api_key = your_key After you save the settings, the weather functionality becomes available to the contract s users. How to enable weather 1. Open the map 2. A “Weather” checkbox appears in the list of layers 3. Select the checkbox 4. After you enable it, the weather layer appears on top of the map, and the forecast time panel is displayed at the bottom To turn weather off, just clear the checkbox. How to choose a forecast model Click the globe icon in the weather panel and select a model. The availability of models depends on the plan. Free GFS: a global model with basic detail. Suitable for a general understanding of the weather situation around the world Pro ICON: high detail for Europe NAM: an accurate model for North America AROME: very high detail (especially for France and nearby regions) GEOS5: a NASA model for global analysis CAMS: an air quality monitoring model HRRR: frequent hourly updates for the USA ECMWF (with a separate subscription) ECMWF: one of the most accurate global forecast models, used for professional analysis The system automatically detects the plan and shows only the available models. How to choose the weather layer type Click the drop-down arrow and select the data type. Free: Wind Temperature Pressure Pro (additionally): Humidity Precipitation Thunderstorms Cloud cover Visibility Satellite images Weather radar and other professional parameters. After you make a selection, the map updates automatically. How to work with the time panel When the weather layer is on, a time panel appears at the bottom of the map. It helps you view the forecast by hours and days. Play: starts the forecast animation. The map shows how the weather changes over time Pause: stops the animation at the selected moment Time slider: drag it manually to go to the date and time you need The panel is shown only when the weather layer is on. If you turn weather off, the panel is hidden automatically.

In the contract settings, you can change some of the system s operating parameters yourself. To open the contract settings, click the icon on the top panel. Here you will find the sections for configuring your account: Privacy Personalization Map and geocoding Report list KML settings Object tags Staff and groups Report scheduler Tokens The set of tabs available to you on the left may vary and depends on which modules are connected to your account.

In “Privacy” you can configure account security and notifications: — set up e-mail — change the password — restrict login by IP — enable additional protection with a code — choose the type and method of receiving notifications — reset the cache Setting up e-mail In PILOT, e-mail is used to receive reports and notifications. How to add an e-mail address: 1. In the “Personal settings” tab, find the “Users e-mail addresses” section 2. Click the “Add Email” button 3. Enter a valid e-mail address 4. Click the “Save” button To receive reports and notifications, you must confirm your e-mail address. The system will send you information only after confirmation. E-mail statuses: — e-mail confirmed — e-mail not confirmed How to confirm your e-mail address: 1. Click the “Send confirmation e-mail” button 2. Open your mailbox 3. Find the e-mail from the PILOT system 4. Follow the link in the e-mail 5. The e-mail address will be confirmed automatically The “Update email list” button updates the statuses of the added e-mail addresses. Changing the password How to change the password in your account: 1. In the “Privacy” tab, find the “Change password” section 2. Come up with a new strong password 3. Enter the new password 4. Repeat the new password in the next field 5. Click the “Save password” button If you select the “Send by e-mail” checkbox, an e-mail with the new password will be sent to the e-mail address specified in your account. IP filtering protection IP filtering is a technology that gives access to the account only to allowed IP addresses. How to enable IP address filtering: 1. In the “Privacy” tab, find the “IP address filtering” section 2. Select the “IP address filtering” checkbox 3. Enter the IP addresses from which you allow logging in to your account. For example, the addresses of your work and home computers. 4. Click “Save” When you enable the function, your current IP address is added automatically so that you don't lose access. You will be able to log in to the account only from the specified IP addresses. If you want to turn this function off, just clear the checkbox and save the changes. Two-factor authentication Two-factor authentication (2FA) is an additional level of account protection. In addition to the username and password, a one-time code is used to log in. This reduces the risk of unauthorized access, even if third parties learn the password. PILOT offers two 2FA methods: TOTP authentication: through an authenticator app E-mail authorization: with confirmation by e-mail The contract administrator must enable the use of two-factor authentication. TOTP two-factor authentication This is an additional level of protection for your account. In addition to your regular password, you will use a temporary code to log in. How to enable TOTP two-factor authentication: 1. Before your first login install a two-factor authentication app for iOS or Android Google Authenticator for Android Google Authenticator for iOS Microsoft Authenticator for Android Microsoft Authenticator for iOS Twilio Authy for Android Twilio Authy for iOS 2. In the “Privacy” tab, find the “Two-factor authentication” section Click the “Connect” button next to “TOTP authorization” 4. Scan the QR code with the installed app 5. Enter the code from the app How to log in with TOTP: 1. Open a browser and go to https://pilot-gps.com/ 2. Enter your credentials: username and password 3. Click the “Log in” button 4. In the window that appears, enter the six-digit code from the app. To do this, open the authenticator app on your smartphone, find the six-digit code displayed, and enter it in the required field on your computer screen. The code refreshes every 30 seconds. If you didn't manage to enter the code before it refreshed, just wait for a new code to appear and enter it. 5. Click the “Log in” button E-mail two-factor authentication (Email 2FA) This is an additional level of protection for your account. After you enter your username and password, the system additionally asks for a code that is sent to your personal e-mail. You can log in only after entering this code. How to enable Email 2FA: 1. In the “Privacy” tab, find the “Two-factor authentication” section 2. Click “Connect” next to “E-mail authorization” 3. Select a confirmed e-mail from the list 4. Click “Send code”. An e-mail with a confirmation code will be sent to the selected address 5. Enter the code from the e-mail and confirm the connection How to log in with Email 2FA 1. Open a browser and go to https://pilot-gps.com/ 2. Enter your credentials: username and password 3. Click the “Log in” button 4. Enter the one-time code sent to your e-mail 5. Click “Log in” How to turn off 2FA Go to the “Two-factor authentication” section and click “Disable” next to the active method. Setting up notifications You choose which notifications to receive. Choose only the ones that are really important. To receive notifications, you need to confirm your e-mail address. How to set up notifications: In the “Privacy” tab, find the “Notification settings” section View the list of available notifications 3. Select the checkboxes next to the notification types you want to receive 4. For each selected notification type, mark the formats in which to receive notifications 5. Click the “Save” button Reset cache Sometimes the system may not show all current information. This happens because the browser stores old data. To make everything work correctly again: 1. In the upper right corner of the “Privacy” tab, find the “Reset cache” button 2. Click it, and the system clears the old data and loads current data After that, everything will be displayed correctly again.

In the “Personalization” tab you can configure how information is displayed in the system: — general display settings — tooltips — the measurement system General display settings Display settings help you personalize the interface. You can choose how information is displayed on the map and in other interface elements. Available display settings: Show geofence names: display text labels with geofence names on the map Show global tags: display labels shared by all users for sorting object information Show tag labels: display additional labels on objects Show global service templates: display ready-made maintenance schemes available to all users Show object tree tooltips: enable pop-up tooltips when you hover over objects in the list • Show LRS radius: display the coordinate accuracy radius when the device determines its location by LBS (cell towers) Group markers on the map: combine closely located objects into groups, making the map more readable Marker animation: add movement to icons on the map Full-screen map: display the map at full screen How to set up: In the “Personalization” tab, find the “Settings” section 2. In this section you will see a list of options 3. To enable an option, select its checkbox 4. After selecting the options you need, click the “Save settings” button in the “Personalization” tab Tooltips In the “Tooltip elements” section you can choose what additional information is displayed when you hover the cursor over an object icon on the map. How to set up: In the “Personalization” tab, find the “Tooltip elements” and “Additional tooltip elements” sections Select the elements you need by selecting the checkbox in the required field 3. Click “Save settings” in the “Personalization” tab Measurement system Here you can configure: 1. The measurement system: Metric: kilograms, liters, kilometers Imperial: pounds, gallons, miles 2. The number format 3. The first day of the week for the calendar and reports How to set up: In the “Personalization” tab, find the “Measurement system” section Select the options you need from the drop-down lists Click “Save settings” in the “Personalization” tab Now all data will be displayed in a format convenient for you, and the calendar and reports will match your work schedule.

Here you can configure: — address display — display of events on the map — color indication of speed Address display You can configure which address components are visible in the system, for example in reports or in pop-up windows on the map. Hide the address if there is a geofence: the system shows only the geofence name if the address is inside it Reverse address order: display the address in reverse order, from the country to the house number How to set up: In the “Map and geocoding” tab, find the “Address display settings” section 2. In this section you will see a list of address components 3. To enable a component, select its checkbox 4. After selecting the settings you need, click the “Save settings” button in the “Map and geocoding” tab Displaying events on the map In the “Display of events on the map” section you can configure which event types are displayed in the object s history. When you go to the “Events” tab in the “History” section, you will see the list of events you selected for display. The places where these events occurred are also marked on the map with markers. For example, you see “Parking” events in the list and select a record you are interested in. When you click the event record, the exact place where it was recorded appears on the map. How to set up: In the “Map and geocoding” tab, find the “Display of events on the map” section Select the event type to display in the object s history by selecting the checkbox in the required field Click “Save settings” in the “Map and geocoding” tab This way, in the “Display of events on the map” section you can select event types and then view them in the list and on the map in the “History” section. Color indication of speed Color indication of speed shows speed changes in different colors. On the track in the movement history, you will see how fast the object was moving at each moment. How to set up: In the “Map and geocoding” tab, go to the “Speed in color” section 2. Select the checkbox next to the “Speed in color” function to display the track in the history in color. Color indication of speed is already set up in the system by default: Gray: the vehicle is stationary Green: slow driving, up to 60 km/h Yellow: medium speed, up to 90 km/h Red: fast driving, over 90 km/h If you want to change the color of the standard indication: Double-click the color field you want to change 2. Select the color you need from the list 3. Click the “Update” button 4. Click the “Save” button in the “Speed in color” section If you want to add a new color field: Click the button for adding a new color 2. In the new field, select a color and set the speed 3. Click the “Save” button To delete a color field, click the icon next to it.

In the “Report list” tab you choose which report types you want to use. The types selected here will be available when you create a new report. How to set up: Go to the “Report list” tab Select the report types by selecting the checkbox next to the report name you need 3. Click the “Save settings” button The selected report types are displayed the same way in both the web version and the mobile app. To learn how to work with reports and configure them, see the “Reports” section.

KML/KMZ is a special file that lets you put additional geographic data on the map: — points — lines — areas — images This file works like an additional transparent layer that can be overlaid on the main map. Such a layer helps display the information you need: mark important objects, show boundaries, or plot a route. The main map stays visible, and the additional information is overlaid on top. You can upload a KML/KMZ file to PILOT and see the additional geographic data on the map. Where to get a KML/KMZ file: 1. Create one yourself: In Google Earth Edit a text document manually 2. Download ready-made files: From specialized sites with geographic data From open map databases From specialized communities and forums How to upload a file to PILOT: Go to the “KML settings” tab 2. In the “KML/KMZ upload” section, select the data source for uploading “URL”: if the file is on the internet “File”: if the file is on your computer 3. Add a link to the file or select the file on your computer 4. Enter the file name that will be displayed in PILOT 5. Click the “Save KML/KMZ” button If you want all users of the contract to see the file, select the “For all” checkbox. To delete an uploaded KML, click next to it. After a KML file is uploaded, the “Object layers” tool appears on the map. How to display layers on the map: 1. Find the “Object layers” panel: a list with checkboxes for selection. It is located in the upper right part of the map 2. Expand the list and select the checkboxes next to the layers you need. You can select one or several layers at the same time 3. The selected layers are displayed on the map, and the main map stays visible.

An object tag is a short label with information that helps you quickly understand what an object is. Think of a tag as a name sticker for each object. The sticker displays information: A short name A color code A description In the tag information you can specify, for example, the type of object, its role, or its state. Tags are needed to: — quickly find the object you need — tell one object from another — track and group objects — organize objects in the list How to add object tags: Go to the “Object tags” tab in the contract settings 2. Click the “Add label” button In the window that opens, fill in the tag information: Come up with a name Choose a color Write a short description Select with checkboxes the objects that will have the label 4. Click the “Save” button If you want a tag to appear automatically when a new object is created, set it as a “Default” tag. In this case, when you create a new object, this tag will be present in the tags field automatically. You won't have to add this tag to the object card manually. After you fill in the tag information, a record for it appears in the “Object tags” tab. This is how objects with tags look in the list. When you view the object list, in the “Labels” column you will see color markers that correspond to the objects tags. You can add several tags to one object to describe it by different criteria.

In the “Staff and groups” tab you can create employee accounts and configure their access to PILOT. For each user you can define the available objects, reports, modules, and actions in the system. This section describes: — creating and editing users — configuring the user card — assigning access rights — creating and applying rights templates — searching for users — viewing login history — assigning available reports — setting up IP filtering — blocking and unblocking accounts The available settings depend on the connected modules and the rights of the current user. An administrator can create users and manage their access.

Users can be created and configured by an administrator. When creating an account, enter the login details, and then define which objects, tags, modules, and actions will be available to the employee. How to create a user 1. Open “Contract settings” and go to the “Staff and groups” tab 2. Click the “Add user” button in the upper right corner 3. In the card that opens, fill in the user data on the “Settings” tab Required fields are outlined in red: Login: the name the user will enter to log in to PILOT Password: the password for logging in. Click the edit icon in the field to set the password Name: the employee s name or another clear name for the account Type: the user s access level. PILOT has two user types: Administrator: can add users and objects, work with drivers, and manage the rights of the contract s users User: works only with the objects, data, and functions assigned to them. The available capabilities are determined by their rights Email: the e-mail address. Click the send icon in the field to send the user an e-mail with a link to log in to PILOT Mobile phone: the employee s contact number Information: additional details about the user. Fill in this field if necessary 4. Click “Save” The created account appears in the list in the “Staff and groups” tab. After creating the user, open their card and configure access on the corresponding tabs. Depending on the connected modules, you can assign here: — vehicles — drivers — object tags — rights to view and change data — access to modules — interface parameters — other available functions The set of tabs depends on the contract configuration and the administrator s rights. How to edit a user 1. Open the “Staff and groups” tab 2. Find the user in the list 3. Double-click the user s row 4. Make changes in their card 5. Click “Save” How to delete a user Find the user in the “Staff and groups” tab and click the trash icon in their row. After deletion, the user loses access to PILOT. Before deleting, make sure the account is no longer needed. The account owner and the user you are currently logged in as cannot be deleted in the PILOT interface. This restriction protects the account from losing access. The account owner is highlighted in green in the list. If you need to delete the owner, first assign another contract owner in the admin panel. After the owner is changed, deletion becomes available. If you don t have access to the admin panel, contact the administrator or technical support.

The user card configures the employee s credentials and rights in PILOT. Here you can define which objects, drivers, tags, reports, and modules will be available to them, and which actions they can perform. The card may contain the following tabs: Settings : login, password, contact details, user type, and additional account parameters Climate chambers : access to the modes, objects, and data of the “Climate” module Vehicles : selecting the objects the user can view and use Drivers : selecting the drivers available to the user Object tags : assigning the tags the user can use to find and filter objects Rights : permissions to view, create, change, and delete data, as well as access to individual functions and modules Interface : configuring the available sections and interface elements “Situation center” event groups : access to event groups and “Situation center” functions The set of tabs depends on the connected modules, the contract configuration, and the rights of the user who performs the configuration. Therefore user cards in different accounts may differ.

The “Settings” tab specifies the account data, login parameters, and the history period available to the user. Main settings Fill in the user data. Required fields are outlined in red: Login: the name the user enters to log in to PILOT Password: the password for logging in. To create or change it, click the edit icon in the field Name: the employee s name or another clear name for the account Type: determines the access level: Administrator: can add users and objects, work with drivers, and manage the rights of the contract s users User: works with the objects and functions assigned to them. The available capabilities are determined by their rights Information: additional details about the employee. Fill in this field if necessary Email: the e-mail address. Click the send icon in the field to send the user an e-mail with a link to log in to PILOT Mobile phone: the employee s contact number Additional settings Number of login attempts (The number of possible login attempts): specify the allowed number of authorization attempts. The parameter limits repeated login attempts with incorrect credentials. A value of 0 turns off attempt counting. Number of days to store history: specify the period for which historical data is available to the user, including when building reports: 0: use the standard period of 365 days a positive number: keep history for the specified number of days −1: do not keep history The maximum period is determined by the contract configuration Users default parameters . It is added by a user with access to the admin panel. If you need to increase the available period, contact the administrator or technical support. For example, a value of 730 in the max_days_available_history parameter lets you give the contract s users access to two years of history. After the configuration is applied, the “Number of days to store history” field is filled in with the set number of days. After filling in the fields, click “Save”. Then go to the other tabs of the card to assign objects, tags, and the necessary access rights to the user.

The “Climate chambers” tab configures the user s access to the data of the “Climate” module. You can grant access to the whole mode or only to individual objects and sites. The module has two modes: NORMAL (Standard): the standard mode for working with climate sensors. It shows connected objects and sensors, their current readings, update time, and charts VELAVU: a mode for equipment, sites, and premises loaded from the Velavu platform. In this mode you can view the structure of sites, buildings, and floors, as well as the location of devices and RFID tags on the map or plan. To grant access: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Climate chambers” tab 3. Select the checkbox next to the mode you need NORMAL: access to the module s standard data VELAVU: access to the Velavu integration data 4. To grant access only to individual data, expand the mode you need and select the checkboxes next to the corresponding elements: in NORMAL mode: groups or objects with climate sensors in VELAVU mode: sites, buildings, or individual floors 5. Click “Save”

The “Vehicles” tab configures the user s access to monitored objects. The user will see in PILOT only the objects selected here. To grant access: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Vehicles” tab 3. Expand the folder you need 4. Select the checkboxes next to the objects that should be available to the user. To select all objects in a folder, select the checkbox next to its name 5. Click “Save”. New objects are not assigned to users automatically. After creating or importing an object, open the cards of the users you need and grant them access manually. This also applies to objects received from a mapping contract. To close a user s access to an object, clear the corresponding checkbox and save the changes.

The “Drivers” tab is available if the corresponding module is connected to the account. Here you configure the user s access to driver data. The user will be able to see and use only the selected records. To grant access: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Drivers” tab 3. Expand the group you need 4. Select the checkboxes next to the drivers available to the user. To select the whole group, select the checkbox next to its name 5. Click “Save” New drivers are not assigned to the user automatically. After adding a driver, grant access to them in the “Drivers” tab if necessary.

The “Object tags” tab configures the user s access to tags used to classify and quickly search for objects. The user will be able to see and use only the selected tags. To grant access: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Object tags” tab 3. Select the checkboxes next to the tags you need 4. Click “Save” To close access to a tag, clear the corresponding checkbox and save the changes.

The “Rights” tab configures the actions the user can perform in PILOT. For example, you can allow them to view reports and edit objects but forbid creating or deleting data. Rights are combined into thematic groups. The set depends on the connected modules and the account configuration. Here there may be permissions for: — working with vehicles — creating and editing objects — managing sensors and tags — viewing and building reports — working with geofences — access to financial data — changing contract settings — using additional modules Configuring rights To grant rights to a user: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Rights” tab 3. Expand the group you need 4. Select the checkboxes next to the allowed actions 5. Click “Save” The checkbox next to a group enables all the rights nested in it. If the user needs only certain capabilities, expand the group and select them manually. To find the right you need faster, enter its name in the search field. Grant only the rights the employee needs for work. Access to objects, drivers, and tags is configured separately in the corresponding tabs of the card. Rights templates A template saves a configured set of rights and helps you quickly assign the same permissions to several users. For example, you can create the templates “Dispatcher”, “Manager”, or “Reports specialist”. How to create a template 1. Open the card of a user with a suitable set of rights 2. Go to the “Rights” tab 3. Click the save template icon 4. In the “Saving a template” window, enter a clear name 5. Click “Save” The template appears in the list of saved templates. To open this list, click the icon in the “Rights” tab. In the list you can view and delete templates you no longer need. How to apply a template To assign saved rights to another user: 1. Create a user or open their card 2. On the “Settings” tab, expand the “Type” field 3. Select the option marked “(template)” 4. Fill in the rest of the user s data 5. Click “Save” The selected set of rights will be applied to the user.

The “Situation center event groups” tab (Control Room event groups) configures which event groups are available to the user when working with the “Situation center” module. The event groups themselves are created and configured for the whole contract in “Contract settings”, in the “Control Room” (“Situation center”) tab. In the user s card you can only grant or close access to groups that already exist. To configure access: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Situation center event groups” tab 3. Select the checkboxes next to the event groups the user should see 4. Click “Save” If you clear a checkbox, the corresponding event group stops being displayed for the user.

The “RFID tags” tab configures the user s access to the contract s RFID tags. The user will be able to see and use only the tags marked in their card. The tab is displayed in the user s card if the RFID module is connected for the contract. The list shows: ID: the RFID tag identifier Name: the tag name Description: additional information about the tag Contract: the contract the tag belongs to How to assign RFID tags to a user 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “RFID tags” tab 3. Find the tags you need using search or a filter 4. Select the checkboxes next to the tags that should be available to the user 5. Click “Save” To assign all available RFID tags to the user at once, click the checkmark icon in the upper right corner. The checkboxes are selected next to all tags in the list. To close access to an individual tag, clear the checkbox next to it and save the changes. If the list of tags has changed, click the refresh icon to load current data.

The “Commands” tab is displayed in the user s card if the “Commands” module is connected for the contract. Here you configure which commands the user can use to control hardware. Commands are grouped by device type. The list shows the command name and the hardware compatible with it. To grant access: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Commands” tab 3. Select the checkboxes next to the commands available to the user 4. Click “Save” To select all commands, select the checkbox in the list header. The edit icon next to a command opens its settings. In the editor you can change the command parameters, select objects, set restrictions by geofences and time, and configure other available execution conditions.

The “Interface” tab configures which sections and modules are displayed to the user. If the checkbox is selected, the corresponding element is available in the interface. If you clear the checkbox, the element is hidden. Example: hiding the object tree The Online Tree parameter controls the display of the object tree in the “Online” tab. To hide the object tree: 1. Open the user s card 2. Go to the “Interface” tab 3. Expand the “Main” group 4. Clear the Online Tree checkbox 5. Click “Save” 6. Refresh the page in the user s account Object tree enabled If the Online Tree checkbox is selected, a tree with folders and vehicles is displayed on the left side of the work area. Object tree hidden If the checkbox is cleared, the object tree is not displayed. Instead, another available tab opens on the left side of the work area, for example “Counterparties”. The map and the other permitted modules remain available.

In the “Staff and groups” tab you can find a user by login, account name, or e-mail address. 1. Enter part of the value in the search field in the upper right corner 2. The list updates automatically and shows only matching records You can type your query in uppercase or lowercase letters; case does not affect the search results. To show all users again, clear the field with the icon . Account owner The account owner is highlighted in green in the user list, so they can be told apart from the other users of the contract. The owner cannot be deleted through the PILOT interface. If you need to assign another owner, contact the administrator or technical support.

The authentication history helps you check when and from which device a user logged in to PILOT. To open the log: 1. Go to the “Staff and groups” tab 2. Find the user you need 3. Click the login history icon in their row 4. In the window that opens, specify the start and end of the period 5. Click the search icon For each login the following is displayed: — user ID — login — role — login time — last activity time — IP address — browser — operating system To save the log on your computer, click the download icon . The data is exported in CSV format. To reload current information, click the refresh icon .

For each user you can choose the reports that will be available to them in PILOT. 1. Open the “Staff and groups” tab 2. Find the user you need 3. Click the report list icon in their row 4. In the “User rights to reports” window, select the checkboxes next to the reports you need 5. Click “Save” To find a report quickly, enter part of its name in the search field . The “Select all” button assigns all available reports, and “Clear all” removes all assignments. If you clear the checkbox for a report and save the changes, it stops being displayed for the user.

IP filtering restricts account login by IP address. After you enable it, the user can log in to PILOT only from allowed addresses. To set up IP filtering: 1. In the “Staff and groups” tab, find the user you need 2. Click the filter icon next to their name 3. In the window that opens, select the “Enable filtering” checkbox 4. Specify the allowed IP addresses, one address per line 5. Click “Save IP list” When filtering is enabled, the current IP address is added to the list automatically. If necessary, add other addresses from which the user will log in to PILOT. Incorrect IP filtering settings can block the user's access. Before saving, make sure all the required addresses are in the list. If the network's IP address changes, the new address will also need to be added.

Blocking temporarily prevents a user from logging in to PILOT but keeps their account and access settings. In the “Status” column, the user s state is indicated by color: green icon: the user is active red icon: the user is blocked How to block a user 1. In the “Staff and groups” tab, find the user you need 2. Click the green icon in the “Status” column 3. In the confirmation window, click “Yes” The status changes to red . After blocking, the user cannot log in to PILOT How to unblock a user 1. Find the blocked user in the list 2. Click the red icon in the “Status” column 3. In the confirmation window, click “Yes” The status changes to green , and the user can log in to the system again with their previous credentials.

The report scheduler is a tool for generating and sending reports automatically on a schedule. With the scheduler you can: — select the report type — set the period whose data is included in the report — specify the time and frequency of report generation — select objects or tags — specify the e-mail addresses the report is sent to To use the report scheduler, confirm your e-mail address on the “Privacy” tab. How to create a schedule 1. Open the “Report scheduler” tab 2. Click “Add new schedule” 3. In the window that opens, configure the report parameters, the data period, and the generation schedule 4. Select the objects or tags to generate the report for 5. Click “Save” The schedule is then created, and reports are generated and sent at the specified frequency. Report parameters In the “Report parameters” block, fill in the following fields: Name — enter a descriptive name for the schedule Language — select the language of the generated report Report type — select a report from the list. The list shows only the report types you have access to. You can view the available reports on the “Report list” tab Sensor groups (Select tags) — select the sensor tags whose data should be included in the report. Tags let you generate a report only for the sensors you need. You can assign tags in the sensor settings . The availability of the field and the list of tags depend on the selected report type. Grouping — specify how to group data in the report, for example by dates or by objects Breakdown — select the intervals the data in the report is split into, for example by day, by week, or with no additional breakdown If you select a report type that supports maps, additional settings appear in the scheduler. Which settings appear depends on the selected report: Show maps (Show maps) — adds a static map with the object s route for the report period to the report. Map type (Map Type) — lets you select the base map used in the report, for example OSM or Google Sat. The selected base map is used when the “Map type” (Show maps) option is enabled Show parking — marks parking locations on the map with P icons. This option is available only after “Show maps” (Show maps) is enabled Show odometer (Show odometer) — adds odometer readings at the start and end of the trip to the table, if the selected report supports this option These settings are saved in the schedule and applied every time the report is generated automatically. Report time zone — select the time zone used to determine the data period and the time of events in the report Format — select the file format: PDF or Excel Page size — select the page size, for example A4 Orientation — select the page layout: “Portrait” (vertical) or “Landscape” (horizontal). For reports with many columns, select “Landscape” to fit the table to the page width. Emails — specify one or more e-mail addresses to send the report to. To remove an address from the list, click the cross next to it. Make sure your e-mail address is confirmed on the “Privacy” tab. You cannot use the report scheduler without a confirmed address. Recipients can unsubscribe from a specific report using the link in the e-mail. If no recipients remain in the list, PILOT suspends report generation. The schedule is kept. After you add a new recipient, sending resumes from the current period. Report data period In the “Report data period” block, set the time interval whose data should be included in the report. From — specify the time from which data is included in the report Previous day — enable this option if the start time of the period belongs to the previous day To — specify the time up to which data is included in the report Period — select the duration of the period The “Previous day” option lets you generate reports for intervals that start on one day and end on another. For example, if you specify: period start — 20:00 enable “Previous day” period end — 08:00 the report will include data from 20:00 of the previous day to 08:00 of the current day. Generation schedule In the “Generation schedule” block, specify when and how often the report should be created. Next generation — select the date and time of the nearest report generation and sending Frequency (Generate) — specify how often the report should be generated: daily — the report is generated every day weekly — the report is generated once a week monthly — the report is generated once a month selected days — the report is generated only on the specified days of the week Below the schedule settings, the “Data period” is displayed — the automatically calculated interval whose data will be included in the next report. Selecting objects or tags On the right side of the window, select the objects to generate the report for: “Objects” — the report is generated for the selected objects “Tags” — the report is generated for the objects grouped by the selected tags You can select individual objects or an entire group of objects. Use the search bar and filters for quick search. Saving the schedule Before saving, check the schedule settings and click “Save”. The schedule appears in the scheduler, after which reports are generated automatically and sent to the specified recipients. Unsubscribing from a scheduled report You can stop receiving a scheduled report using the link in the e-mail. You do not need to sign in to PILOT to unsubscribe. Unsubscribing applies only to the report and e-mail address shown on the confirmation page. Other scheduled reports will continue to arrive. The other recipients of this report keep their subscription. How to unsubscribe 1. Open the e-mail with the scheduled report 2. Click the “Unsubscribe from this scheduled report” link 3. On the page that opens, check the report name and e-mail address 4. Click the “Unsubscribe” button PILOT removes the specified address from the recipient list and shows a message confirming a successful unsubscription, with the report name. If you are already signed in to PILOT, following the link and unsubscribing keep your current session. Unsubscribing from a scheduled report You can stop receiving a scheduled report using the link in the e-mail. You do not need to sign in to PILOT to unsubscribe. Unsubscribing applies only to the report and e-mail address shown on the confirmation page. Other scheduled reports will continue to arrive. The other recipients of this report keep their subscription. How to unsubscribe 1. Open the e-mail with the scheduled report 2. Click the “Unsubscribe from this scheduled report” link 3. On the page that opens, check the report name and e-mail address 4. Click the “Unsubscribe” button PILOT removes the specified address from the recipient list and shows a message confirming a successful unsubscription, with the report name. If the last recipient unsubscribes, PILOT suspends report generation. The schedule is kept and continues to be updated. After you add a new recipient, sending resumes from the current period.

A token is a unique access code that lets other users see the location of objects without having access to your account. Put simply, a token is like a temporary pass. It gives limited access to specific information without revealing your personal data or password. On the “Tokens” tab you can create two types of tokens: Monitor token — for viewing the location of selected objects via a public link Access token — for signing in to PILOT without entering a password View token (Monitor token) A Monitor token gives another person access to a map with the selected objects and their movements. The recipient of the link does not get a login, a password, or full access to the account. Rights to manage view tokens Separate rights are used to manage Monitor tokens: Edit Tokens — allows you to create and edit monitoring tokens and location sharing links. Delete Tokens — allows you to delete monitoring tokens. For a regular user to be able to create, edit, or delete a link in the PILOT web version, an administrator or master must grant them the right to edit and delete tokens. How to grant rights to a user In “Contract settings”, open the “Staff and groups” tab 2. Double-click the user in the list to open their card 3. Go to the “Rights” tab 4. Expand the “Tokens” group 5. Select the required rights: Edit Tokens — to create and edit tokens Delete Tokens — to delete tokens 6. Click “Save” How to create a view token In the “Monitor tokens” section, click the “Add token” button 2. In the window that opens, fill in the token information: Specify the validity period — select the date and time when the token starts and stops working Select which map to use to display the objects Specify whether to display object markers or sensors on the map From the list, select the objects to track with this token 3. Click “Save” 4. The system creates a unique link or an iframe — an embed code 5. Copy the link or code and send it to whoever needs access to the information Access token This type of token is used to sign in to the system without a password. When you follow the special link, PILOT signs you in as the user, the same way as with a login and password. A token can have a limited validity period or be unlimited. How to create an access token In the “Access tokens” section, click the “Add token” button In the new window, specify the date and time when the token starts and stops being valid. If you do not specify an end, the token works indefinitely. Click “Save” To edit a token, click the pencil icon , and to delete it, click the trash can icon .

A template lets you transfer display settings from one account to another. This is convenient when you create accounts with similar parameters or configure several partner accounts: you can export the required parameters to a file and then apply them again. Creating and uploading templates is available only to users with master rights. The buttons for exporting and uploading display settings templates are available on any tab of “Contract settings”. A template can include settings from the “Personalization” and “Map and geocoding” tabs, including: — the list of available reports — the system of units — general display parameters — the address format — display of events on the map in history — the contents of pop-up hints Exporting a template 1. Open “Contract settings” and go to any tab, for example “Staff and groups” 2. Click the “Download settings” icon 3. Select the checkboxes for the parameters to include in the template 4. Click “Export” The template file is saved to your computer. You can use it to transfer the selected settings to another account. Uploading a template Before uploading, make sure the account you want to apply the settings to is open. 1. Open “Contract settings” and go to any tab, for example “Staff and groups” 2. Click the “Upload template” icon 3. Click “Browse” and select the previously saved file 4. Click “Upload” 5. When the upload is complete, refresh the page The parameters included in the template are applied to the selected account.

An object is a vehicle, machinery, person, animal, or any other moving or stationary object that is being monitored. To track an object, a special device that sends data to our system is installed on it. To set up object tracking, go to the “Online” tab. Here you can add objects for monitoring and, if you wish, combine them into groups. After you add objects, you see the object list on the same tab In this section you will learn: — how to add an object — how to work with the object card — how to work with the object menu — how to work with the object list — how to view additional information about an object

To create objects, you must have rights to create and edit objects. In PILOT, you can add an object manually or import it from a WLP file. Adding an object manually On the “Online” tab, click the “Add object” button 2. In the card that opens, fill in the required fields. They are highlighted with a red frame: Vehicle number — enter the registration number or a descriptive name for the object Device type — select the model of the GPS tracker or other terminal installed on the object The GPS device installed on the object must be in the list of supported hardware . Device ID/IMEI — enter the unique identifier of the hardware. It is usually printed on the device body, the packaging, or in the manufacturer s documentation 3. Click the “Save” button — the object appears in the object list You can fill in the remaining details right away or add them later when editing. A detailed description of all tabs and parameters is given in the article “Object card” . Transferring objects from a WLP file In PILOT, the function for transferring data from a WLP file is designed to help customers who previously used the Wialon system. Before you start transferring objects, let s look at the file types you will use: WLP files store the basic information about an object: its name, type, and characteristics. WLN files contain the entire history of an object s movements and sensor readings for a certain period. How to transfer objects from the Wialon system: Download the list of objects with parameters from Wialon 2. Upload the objects to PILOT: Upload the WLP file with the object using the button Select the checkbox if you want to transfer sensor readings Click “Upload” The objects are added to the system automatically How to upload a group of Wialon objects: Export the group of objects from Wialon to WLP files Pack the WLP files into a single ZIP archive Upload the archive using the button To transfer an object s history: In Wialon, select the object and parameters, then download the file in WLN format 2. In PILOT, find the object you want to transfer the history to in the object list 3. Right-click the object — the object menu opens 4. In the object menu, select “Import WLN” 5. In the import window, upload the required WLN file using the “Choose file” button 6. Specify how to process the uploaded data: • Select the “Recalculate routes” checkbox if you need to restore the object s routes • Select the “Recalculate sensors” checkbox if you need to restore sensor readings 7. Click “Upload”

The object card stores information about the vehicle and the settings of the hardware associated with it. Here you can change the main characteristics of the object, configure the device and its connection, add SIM cards, add fuel parameters, and other data. To open the object card, double-click the object in the list, or open the object s context menu and select “Edit”. The card has several tabs: “Main” — vehicle information, its image, the device, and connection parameters “SIM cards” — slot numbers, MSISDN, ICCID, and carriers of the SIM cards of the main and additional devices “Info” — additional information about the object “Settings” — operating and display parameters of the object “Additional parameters” — additional characteristics and settings “Fuel” — parameters related to fuel accounting “Files” — documents and other files of the object The set of tabs depends on the connected modules and the user's rights, so the card may look different for different accounts. After making changes, click “Save”. To discard unsaved changes, click “Reset”.

The “Main” tab contains information about the vehicle and the parameters of the connected hardware. To add an object, fill in the required fields. You can add the remaining data right away or later when editing the card. After the object is saved, the top of the tab shows: the object ID the account ID mileage — if its value is configured on the “Info” tab engine hours — if their value is configured on the “Info” tab the object image — the standard image of the selected make, model, and modification, or a photo you uploaded Object information Vehicle number Enter the number or a descriptive name for the object. It is displayed in the object list, on the map, and in reports. Vehicle type and color Select the vehicle type, for example a passenger car, a truck, or special equipment. The system uses the corresponding icon in the object list and on the map. Next to it you can select the color used to display it. Group Select the folder where the object is placed in the object tree. Creating and configuring groups is described in the article “Object list” . Make Select the vehicle manufacturer. Model Select a model from the list. The list of available models depends on the selected make. Modification If necessary, select a specific version of the model, for example a variant with a particular body type, engine, or year of manufacture. After you select the make and model, the system automatically adds the standard image of the vehicle. Template Select a ready-made set of settings for the object, for example a sensor template or an eco-driving template. Use the template that matches the installed hardware and the purpose of the vehicle. Description Add information that may be needed when working with the object: department, purpose, operating specifics, or other additional information. Device tags Assign tags for additional classification and quick search of objects. Creating tags is described in the article “Object tags” . Object photo On the “Main” tab you can add a photo of the vehicle: 1. Click the camera icon next to the image 2. Select a file on your computer and upload the photo 3. Turn on the toggle next to the photo if you want to show it instead of the standard vehicle icon The photo is displayed in the object list and on the map. If the toggle is off, the system keeps using the standard icon of the selected vehicle type. To delete the uploaded photo, click the trash can icon next to the image. Device and connection This block configures the main telematics hardware of the object. Device type Select the model of the GPS tracker or other terminal installed on the vehicle. The selected type determines how incoming data is processed and the connection parameters. If the model you need is not in the list, contact technical support. Device ID/IMEI Enter the unique identifier of the main terminal. It can be an ID, a serial number, or an IMEI — it is usually printed on the device body, the packaging, or in the manufacturer s documentation. PILOT uses this value to determine which object the incoming data belongs to. A lock icon is displayed next to the “Device ID/IMEI” field. It protects the identifier from accidental changes. To edit the value, click the lock — the field becomes available for input. Additional devices You can link other installed hardware to the object, for example an additional tracker or a video device: 1. Click the edit icon in the “Additional devices” (Additional Devices) field 2. In the window that opens, click “Add” 3. Enter the IMEI — the unique identifier of the additional device 4. Select the device type 5. Click “Save” The additional device settings include service parameters: Ignore Coord — do not use the additional device s coordinates to determine the object s position Ignore Retrans — do not forward the additional device s data through the configured retransmission channels Enable these parameters only if the connection scheme requires it. If you are not sure about the setting, contact your administrator or technical support. Server and port After you select the device type, PILOT automatically shows the server address and port the terminal must send data to. Click the copy icon next to the field to copy the value and use it when configuring the hardware. The field is filled in by the system and cannot be edited manually. Time zone Select the time zone the object operates in. It is used to display time correctly in history, events, and reports. Packet time offset Specify the difference in hours if the device transmits time in a format other than GMT. The default value is 0. Change the offset only if the time of the device s messages differs from the actual time. Availability of settings The set and availability of fields depend on the user s rights. For the “User” role: — the “Device type” field is not available for viewing — mileage, engine hours, and packet time offset may be available for viewing only To change parameters that are not available, contact a user with master or administrator rights.

The “SIM cards” tab (SIM cards) stores information about the SIM cards installed in the main and additional devices of the object. The availability of the tab depends on the user s role and rights. Only a user with master rights can add and change this information. The data is grouped by hardware: Main device — the main terminal of the object Additional device — other hardware added to the object card For each SIM card, fill in the following fields: Slot — the number of the connector or position of the SIM card in the device. If the hardware supports one SIM card, enter 1. For devices with several SIM cards, select the number of the corresponding slot. MSISDN — the phone number assigned to the SIM card by the carrier. The number length may differ depending on the country and carrier, so enter it in the format provided by the carrier ICCID — the unique serial number of the SIM card. It usually has 19 or 20 digits and is printed on the SIM card itself, its packaging, or in the carrier s account SIM provider — the carrier that serves the SIM card How to add a SIM card 1. Open the “SIM cards” tab 2. Find the main or additional device in which the SIM card is installed 3. Fill in the information about the first SIM card 4. If the device supports several SIM cards, click the plus icon next to its name 5. For each added row, select the slot number and enter the data of the corresponding SIM card 6. Click “Save” If an additional device is connected to the object, the information about its SIM cards is filled in separately in the “Additional device” block. To delete an added row, click the trash can icon . The “Reset” button cancels changes that have not been saved yet.

On the “Info” tab, fill in the vehicle details: On the “Info” tab, fill in the vehicle details: Year of manufacture of the vehicle VIN Engine number Engine displacement in liters. You can select the value with the arrows in the field or enter it manually Engine power in horsepower Total number of seats and number of passenger seats in the vehicle Select how to specify the validity period of your vehicle registration certificate: “Valid until” — enter the exact expiration date of the document “Issue date” — enter the date the document was issued Series and number of the registration certificate and its validity period Insurance policy number and its validity period To specify the validity period of the registration certificate or the insurance policy, click the calendar icon and select a date. After you fill in the parameters on this tab, do not forget to click “Save” to apply your changes. How to set up a reminder for document deadlines: Click the icon to set up a reminder about the expiration of the insurance or the registration certificate. 2. In the window that opens, enter a name for the reminder 3. In the “Date” field, enter the end of the document s validity period 4. Select the repeat interval — how often to send reminders 5. Specify how many days before the document expires the reminder should be sent 6. Specify how you want to receive the reminder To receive reminders by e-mail, confirm your e-mail in “Privacy” . 7. Write the reminder text: Enter the reminder subject — what exactly the notification should be about Write a title for your reminder — what appears at the top of the message Create the reminder text with automatic data substitution To do this, use variables: %current_time% — current time %reminder_name% — reminder name %current_moto% — current mileage %current_mil% — current mileage in miles %agent_id% — account number %vehicle_name% — vehicle name %driver_name% — driver name These variables are automatically replaced with real data when the message is sent. For example: The insurance of %vehicle_name% expires on %current_time% To keep receiving notifications after the specified period ends, select the “Repeat the procedure when maintenance is completed” option 8. Click “Save” — the reminder is created.

The “Settings” tab contains parameters that the system administrator configures through special configurations. Configurations are ready-made sets or templates of settings that the administrator can apply to objects. To learn how to add an object settings configuration through the admin panel, see here . To configure the parameters, contact the administrator, who will add the required configurations to your contract; they will then appear on the “Settings” tab of the object card. Settings defined by a configuration are automatically applied to all objects in the contract. The “Settings” tab defines parameters that affect how the device works in the system. For example, here you can configure the trip and parking detector, the splitting of trips into time segments, and data filtering. 1. Speed source Select the speed source to get correct data about the vehicle's movement. GPS speed is used by default, but if necessary you can select another parameter, for example speed from the CAN bus. If CAN speed is selected as the source, then: the chart in “History” shows the speed from CAN in basic reports (trips, time in motion, parking, etc.) movement is calculated from the CAN speed time in motion and stops are also calculated from the CAN speed If the selected parameter contains no speed data, the system automatically falls back to the standard GPS speed. Make sure you select a speed parameter. If you accidentally select, for example, mileage or another indicator, the calculations may be incorrect. In the “Speed source” block, the “Formula” field lets you set a conversion of the parameter value into a correct speed. CAN bus speed is not always transmitted in the required units. For example, the value may arrive in knots or meters per second. In this case, the formula lets you convert the device's technical data into a form suitable for display and calculations in the system. For example, if the speed arrives in m/s, you can use the formula: * 3.6 (conversion from m/s to km/h) 2. Trip and parking detector With the “Trip and parking detector” function you configure: The minimum speed at which the system starts registering a trip The minimum time between trips that must pass between the end of one trip and the start of the next for the system to separate them The minimum parking time during which the vehicle must remain stationary for the system to record it as parking The maximum distance between tracking points at which the system treats them as part of the same trip 3. Ignition accounting, speed recovery, and CAN mileage If you enable the “Ignition accounting” function, a trip is recorded only when the vehicle's ignition is on. The “Speed recovery” function restores the driving speed if the speed data was lost or distorted. When “CAN mileage accounting” is enabled, the trip history and reports show the mileage received from the CAN bus — the vehicle's on-board computer — rather than the mileage calculated from the GPS tracker data. The GPS signal is sometimes lost, so mileage from the CAN bus data is more accurate. 4. Split trips into segments by time The “Splitting trips into time segments” function divides each trip into several parts by time. You can configure the intervals at which trips are split, for example every 2 or 4 hours. Instead of one record for the whole day, you get data for short intervals. This level of detail is useful, for example, when preparing waybills for specific periods rather than for the whole day. 5. Event filtering With the “Event filtering” function, configure the parameters the system uses to determine the reliability of the received data. Minimum number of satellites for accurate coordinates. For the device to determine accurate location coordinates, it must receive signals from at least 3 satellites. Some devices determine the location with 2 satellites, but in that case the accuracy of the coordinates is lower. Maximum HDOP value. HDOP is a horizontal error indicator that characterizes the accuracy of the device's coordinates. The lower the HDOP value, the more accurate the coordinates. You can set the maximum HDOP value at which the system accepts data as reliable. If the HDOP in a message is higher than the specified value, the message is filtered out — deleted — so that inaccurate data is not used. The system also automatically filters out messages without coordinates or with zero latitude or longitude values, even if the device did not mark them as invalid. Maximum speed value. Points with a speed above this value are filtered out when building history tracks and in speed, violation, and mileage reports. 6. Formula The “Formula” field in the track settings is intended for filtering data packets when building tracks. It is a tool that helps exclude certain data from track building based on specified conditions. How it works: The formula returns TRUE or FALSE for each data packet. If the result is TRUE, the packet is not used to build the track; if the result is FALSE, the packet is used to build the track. For example, =%S% 5 In this formula, %S% is the speed parameter. The formula returns TRUE if the speed is below 5 km/h. All packets with a speed below 5 km/h are filtered out. You can also use more complex formulas with logical operators, parentheses, and multiple conditions. To learn how to work with formulas, see this article . For example, =%S% 5 || %S% 200 This formula excludes from tracks the data where the speed is below 5 km/h or above 200 km/h. The Valid flag in raw data Valid is a field in the raw data of a packet that shows whether the packet is considered reliable for further coordinate processing. Valid = 0 means the packet is considered unreliable. Such packets are stored in the system but are excluded from processing when tracks, geofences, and other operations that require reliable coordinates are recalculated. The Valid = 0 mark is assigned in only two cases: • the packet has no coordinates, or zero latitude or longitude values are transmitted • the packet falls under the specified filtering formula After such a packet is saved, its participation in recalculation can no longer be changed: it will not be used when the data is reprocessed. The filters by the number of satellites, speed, and other parameters from the “Event filtering” block work differently. They are applied dynamically, only during data recalculation. If you change the parameters of these filters and run the recalculation again, the result may change. For example, if the minimum number of satellites in the object settings is 4, packets with fewer satellites may be excluded when tracks and reports are recalculated. But the packets themselves do not get the Valid = 0 mark. If you want such packets to be marked as unreliable right away, use a filtering formula. For example: %satsinview% 4 This formula marks packets where the number of satellites is less than 4 as Valid = 0. These packets are stored in the system but do not participate in the recalculation of tracks, geofences, and other data. 7. Additional Speed control. If the speed exceeds the specified limit, the system reports speeding. Loss of connection. If the connection with the device is lost and not restored within the specified time, the system sends a connection loss message. Idle. If the object does not move for the specified time, the system records this as idle. Next to these fields there are additional control icons: Bell icon — controls notifications for the limit: — notifications are sent, — notifications are disabled The limit itself keeps working: the data is recorded in the system and shown in reports. To change the mode, click the icon.
