In the trip report, you can select a specific record, and the map shows the corresponding route with marks for the start and end of the movement. When viewing an idle report, select the required record, and a stop marker appears on the map. Click it to get all the details about this idle period. 1 — Marker on the map 2 — Report settings When you finish working with the map, click the “Clear” button in the upper right corner of the map to remove all displayed data. Additional parameters Some reports support additional parameters. They help display more data or filter the results when building. The set of parameters depends on the selected report type. Where to set the parameters: Open the “Reports” tab and select the report type 2. A block with additional settings appears below. Set the required parameters and click “Build report”. Which parameters exist: 1. Switches (checkboxes) Show or hide additional columns and report elements. To show the information, select the checkbox. To hide it, clear the checkbox. For example, the “Trips and parking” report has the following additional parameters: columns with drivers and vehicle type, and a chart. If you do not select any parameters, the report is built with the default settings. 2. Numeric parameters Used for filtering by values and setting a range. Enter numbers; the units of measurement are shown next to the field (sec, min, temperature, etc.). If you do not need an upper threshold, in some reports you can leave it empty or set it to 0. For example, in the parking report, specify “Minimum time (sec)” and, if necessary, “Maximum time (sec)” — the parking duration in seconds. Report settings Most reports can be customized: After the report is built, click the button 2. Select the required parameters with checkboxes — for example, object, geofences, sensors, etc. 3. Click “Build report” to update the report with the selected parameters Example In the “Idle events on the route” report, all parameters are displayed by default. But you can select the settings you need and get the report only for the selected parameters. This way you get only the information you need. Downloading and printing a report A built report can be downloaded in CSV, Excel, or PDF format, and also sent to print. To do this, click the button for the required format or the printer icon at the bottom of the report. Downloading as PDF When you select PDF, the PDF export window opens, where you can configure the page size and orientation: 1. In the Page size field, select the page size: A5, A4, A3, or A2 2. In the Orientation field, select the orientation: Portrait — vertical page layout Landscape — horizontal page layout 3. Click “Export” to download the file For reports with many columns, select landscape orientation and, if necessary, a larger page size — this makes the table easier to read. Report scheduler Use the report scheduler to set up automatic sending of reports to your e-mail. The report scheduler is a tool that sends reports automatically on a schedule. How to work with the report scheduler: Configure which reports you need 2. Select the time when it is convenient for you to receive them 3. Reports are sent to your e-mail automatically For more information about setting up the scheduler, read this article .

In PILOT, all reports are divided into types depending on what they are for and what data they use. Each report is generated as a table. Tables are the main way of displaying data in reports. Each report type has its own set of columns, calculation logic and separate display settings. The system provides basic reports used to analyze standard monitoring data: trips, mileage, time in motion, events and other universal indicators. These reports are available regardless of the connected modules. The system also has reports for modules . They are designed to work with specific system modules (for example, “Drivers”, “Fuel”, “Geofences”, etc.) and use additional data and settings available only when the module is active.

This section contains reports related to user management and monitoring of users actions in the system. They help you track account changes, logins, password resets, blocks, and other user actions. With the reports you can: — view the history of administrative actions — monitor the creation, modification, disabling, and blocking of accounts — track successful and failed login attempts — analyze the number and duration of user sessions — find out which user, under which login or with which role, performed an action

The “Administrative actions” report shows the history of user actions in the system for the selected period. It lets you find out who made which changes to the data, and when. Each row of the report corresponds to one registered user action. What the report displays User name — the name of the user who performed the action Role — the user s role in the system, for example “Administrator” User activity — the action performed and information about the changes Date — the date and exact time the action was performed The data in the report may be split by days. The names of some actions are displayed using system designations. For example, UPDATE means a data change.

The “Blocked users” report contains information about users whose access to the system was blocked during the selected period. It lets you find out the date and method of blocking, and also check the number of allowed and incorrect login attempts. What the report displays Role — the role of the blocked user in the system Login — the user s login for signing in to the system Block date — the date and time the account was blocked Block method — the way the user was blocked, for example blocking by an administrator Allowed login attempts — the permitted number of login attempts Incorrect attempts — the number of failed attempts to sign in to the system

The “Created users” report contains information about the accounts created in the system. It lets you check the user s creation date, role, account status, and validity period. What the report displays Login — the user s login for signing in to the system Creation time — the date and time the account was created User role — the user s role in the system, for example “Administrator” or “User” Display name — the user name displayed in the system Last password set — the date and time the password was last set Account expires — the account expiration date. If no period is set, the value “unlimited” is displayed Status — the current state of the account, for example active or blocked Created by — the user who created the account

The “Disabled user account” report contains information about accounts whose access was disabled during the selected period. After blocking, the user cannot sign in to the system with their account. Access remains closed until the administrator unblocks the account. What the report displays Login — the login of the user whose access to the system was disabled Changed date — the date and exact time the account state was changed Current status — the current state of the account. The value “block” means the user is blocked and cannot sign in to the system Changed by — the name of the user or administrator who changed the account state

The “Inactive users” report contains information about accounts that were disabled during the selected period. It lets you find out when the account was created and disabled, who disabled it, and what state it is in now. What the report displays User name — the user s login for signing in to the system Display name — the user name specified in the account settings User creation date — the date and time the account was created User disable date — the date and time the account was disabled Disabled by — information about the initiator or method of disabling, for example by the system administrator Account state — the current status of the user s account

The “Failed login attempts” report contains information about unsuccessful authorization attempts during the selected period. What the report displays User name — the name or login of the user on whose behalf the login attempt was made Number of attempts — the number of registered login attempts Failed attempt time — the date and time of the unsuccessful authorization Possible login attempts — the number of login attempts If the system could not identify the user or obtain certain details of the login attempt, the corresponding fields may remain empty.

The “Login history” report contains information about users logins to the system for the selected period. It lets you find out who signed in to the system and when, from which IP address, and how long the session lasted. What the report displays Name — the user s display name Login — the user s login for signing in to the system Email — the user s e-mail address Date — the date and time of login to the system Role — the user s role in the system IP — the IP address from which the user signed in Duration — the length of the registered user session

The “Login summary” report contains summarized information about users logins for the selected period. It lets you find out the number of logins of each user, the time of the last login, and the total and average session duration. What the report displays Name — the user s display name Email — the user s e-mail address Last login — the date and time of the user s last login in the specified period No logins — the number of registered logins of the user In the current version, the name of the “No logins” column is displayed incorrectly and will be clarified in one of the following versions of the system. Total duration — the total duration of all of the user s sessions Avg Duration — the average duration of one session

The “Modified users” report contains information about account changes for the selected period. It lets you find out which account was changed, when it happened, what data changed, and who made the changes. What the report displays User name — the login of the user whose account was changed Modified time — the date and time the changes were made Modified attributes — the name of the changed account parameter, for example lang — interface language Modified by — the login of the user who made the changes User role — the user s role after the changes Old role — the user s role before the changes

The “Password reset” report contains information about user password changes for the selected period. It lets you find out for which account the password was changed, when it happened, and who performed the action. What the report displays User name — the login of the user whose password was changed Password change date — the date and time the password was reset or a new one was set Changed by — the login of the user or administrator who changed the password

The user activity report contains the history of actions performed by users in the system for the selected period. It lets you find out which user, with which role, performed a certain action, when it was performed, and from which IP address. What the report displays User name — the display name of the user who performed the action Role — the user s role in the system User activity — the action performed and information about the object it relates to Date — the date and exact time the action was performed IP — the IP address from which the action was performed Location — the user s location

The user actions report contains information about actions performed by users in the system for the selected period. It lets you find out which user, under which login, performed an action and when it was performed, and also determine the user s IP address and location. What the report displays Name — the display name of the user who performed the action Login — the user s login for signing in to the system Description — the action performed and information about the object it relates to Date — the date and exact time the action was performed IP — the IP address from which the action was performed Location — the user s location, determined by the IP address

This section contains reports related to the “Agro” Module. With these Reports you can: — monitor the progress of field work — analyze the duration and distance of completed work — calculate the area treated based on the working width of the equipment — track fuel and working fluid consumption — compare results across different fields and Geofences — assess the efficiency of agricultural machinery use

The Agricultural Report contains information about the field work of the selected monitored Objects and their attached implements over the specified period. Use it to determine the duration and distance of completed work, calculate the area treated, and analyze fuel or working fluid consumption. Data is grouped by Object, trailer, and zone. For each zone, separate work periods are displayed, and the “Zone total” row shows the summary figures. What the report shows • Start — date and time the work in the zone began • Stop — date and time the work ended • Duration — length of the corresponding work period • Distance — distance traveled by the Object during the work • Width — working width of the trailer or implement per pass • Area treated — area calculated from the distance traveled and the working width of the implement • Fuel consumption — volume of fuel used during the corresponding period • Fuel consumption/ha — fuel consumption per hectare of area treated • Start location — address where the work began • End location — address where the work ended The “Zone total” row shows the summary figures for all work periods in the corresponding zone: • total work duration • total distance traveled • total area treated • total consumption of fuel or working fluid Selecting a trailer Before generating the report, you can select the trailer the Object worked with. After you click “Generate report”, the “Report parameters” window opens, showing: • Trailer — the selected attached implement • Width — the working width of the implement used to calculate the area treated If needed, you can change the width before generating the report. After you confirm, the system recalculates the area treated using the specified value. Report settings By default, the report shows fuel consumption figures. Use the “Report settings” button to choose the consumption type: • Fuel consumption (Fuel Consumption) — shows the volume of fuel used and consumption per hectare • Fluid consumption (Fluid Consumption) — shows the volume of working fluid used and consumption per hectare Preparing the report The Agricultural Report is available when two Modules are connected and configured: • Geofences — used to create and define the boundaries of the fields to be treated • Trailers — used to register agricultural equipment, link it to monitored Objects, and set the working width The report is generated when the vehicle is inside a field Geofence and a trailer with the “Agro” option enabled is attached to it. If the Modules are not connected or are configured incorrectly, the area treated is not shown in the report.

This section contains the main Reports for analyzing the operation of vehicles and other monitored Objects. They help you monitor Mileage, Trips and Parking, working time, engine hours, fuel consumption, equipment utilization, fleet status, and the performance of specialized tasks. With these Reports you can: — analyze Mileage based on GPS, CAN bus, and odometer data — view Trips and Parking, their duration, addresses, and coordinates — monitor movement time, engine operating time, and ignition-on time — compare equipment operation during working and non-working time — track fuel consumption, refuels, and fuel drains — analyze travel speed, equipment utilization, and axle load — monitor Driver performance and the completion of assigned routes — view routes, Parking, and Events on charts and Maps — generate waybills and monitor document validity periods — assess the composition and changes of the fleet over the selected period The specific set of indicators, filters, and additional parameters depends on the selected Report, the Object’s hardware, and the system settings.

The Points Report contains information about the location and status of vehicles at each recorded route point. Use it to trace vehicle movement and find out its speed, heading, coordinates, and status at a specific moment. Before generating the report, you need to select: — a period of no more than one day — no more than three vehicles A separate data block is generated for each selected vehicle. Each row of the report corresponds to one point received from the GPS tracker. What the report shows № — sequence number of the point since the start of the selected period GPS date/time — date and time the point was recorded by the GPS tracker Driver — name of the Driver assigned to the vehicle Speed — vehicle speed at the moment the point was recorded Heading — direction of vehicle movement in degrees Distance — distance traveled during the interval between points Travel time — duration of movement during the corresponding interval Latitude — geographic latitude of the point Longitude — geographic longitude of the point Place — address or description of the vehicle location Status — vehicle state at the moment the point was recorded, for example “Stop” Geofence — name of the Geofence the vehicle was in Received date/time — date and time the point was received by the system from the GPS tracker

The BRAG Report is designed to assess driving safety and assign Drivers to BRAG categories. The Report was developed to meet QatarEnergy requirements for IVMS vehicle monitoring systems. The system analyzes recorded violations: speeding, harsh acceleration, braking, and cornering, as well as seat belt violations. Based on the results, each active Driver is given an overall score and a color category. Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicles or a vehicle group. Drivers for whom data was received during the selected period are included in the calculation. General information The top of the report shows: Contractor — contractor name Project — project name Department — the unit the report was generated for Report period — start and end of the analyzed period Generated — date and time the report was generated Report type — report type, for example Weekly/Monthly Fleet Overview The Fleet Overview block contains general information about the fleet: Total Vehicles — total number of selected vehicles Active Drivers — number of Drivers with recorded activity during the selected period Total Distance (km) — total vehicle mileage in kilometers Total duration — total vehicle operating time The number of active Drivers may be lower than the number of vehicles: only Drivers for whom the system received the necessary data are included in the BRAG distribution. BRAG Performance Distribution The BRAG Performance Distribution block shows the distribution of active Drivers across four categories. For each category, the number of Drivers and their share of the total number of active Drivers are displayed: BLUE — Outstanding — outstanding driving performance GREEN — Acceptable — acceptable performance AMBER — Attention Required — performance requires attention RED — Action Required — action must be taken The category color is also used to highlight the Driver’s name in the detailed table: blue — BLUE category green — GREEN category yellow — AMBER category red — RED category The higher the overall score and the number of violations, the more attention the driving style requires. Fleet Performance Summary The Fleet Performance Summary block contains summary indicators for the selected fleet: Fleet Average Score — average overall score of the Drivers Total events — total number of recorded events and violations Events per 100 km — average number of events per 100 km of mileage. This indicator lets you compare the results of Drivers and units with different mileage. Individual Driver Performance The Individual Driver Performance block gives detailed results for each Driver. The table shows: Driver ID — Driver identifier Driver Name — Driver name Duration HH:MM:SS — total Driver working time Distance (km) — distance traveled Overspeed 120 kph — number of speeding events in the 120 km/h category Overspeed 100 kph — number of speeding events in the 100–119 km/h category Overspeed 80 kph — number of speeding events in the 80–99 km/h category Overspeed 60 kph — number of speeding events in the 60–79 km/h category Overspeed 40 kph — number of speeding events in the 40–59 km/h category Overspeed 30 kph — number of speeding events in the 30–39 km/h category Harsh Accel — number of harsh accelerations Harsh Braking — number of harsh braking events Harsh Cornering — number of harsh cornering events Seatbelt Violation — number of seat belt violations Driver Score — the Driver’s overall score, which determines the Driver’s BRAG category Preparing data for the report Violation data comes into the report from the Notifications configured for the vehicles. Therefore, before using the report, you need to create the required Notifications and assign them to the corresponding vehicles. The algorithm identifies the Event type by the Notification name. The names must strictly match the established template: BRAG Harsh Braking BRAG Harsh Acceleration BRAG Harsh Cornering BRAG Overspeed BRAG Overspeed 30-39 BRAG Overspeed 40-59 BRAG Overspeed 60-79 BRAG Overspeed 80-99 BRAG Overspeed 100-119 BRAG Overspeed 120 BRAG Seatbelt Violation Assign the Notifications to the vehicles whose data should be included in the report. If the Notification name has been changed, the Notification is missing, or it is assigned to the wrong vehicle, the algorithm may not recognize the Event. In this case, the violation will not appear in the report and the overall figures may be calculated incorrectly.

The “Connection Loss” report contains information about the periods when the system did not receive data from monitored Objects. Use it to find out which vehicle lost its connection, when it happened, how long it lasted, and where the Object was according to the last data received. Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicles and enter a value in the “Min. time (sec)” field. The “Min. time (sec)” field sets the minimum duration of a connection loss for the Event to be included in the report. The value is specified in seconds. For example: 120— the report shows intervals of two minutes or longer 300— the report shows intervals of five minutes or longer Short intervals shorter than the specified value are not included in the report. This setting helps filter out brief connection interruptions and keep only significant Events. What the report shows Object — name of the vehicle or other monitored Object Folder — the folder containing the Object in the Object list Start — date and time the interval began during which the system did not receive data from the Object Stop — date and time the interval ended or data transmission was restored Duration — total duration of the connection loss Address — address or location of the Object according to the last available data

The Report contains information about plan activation for the monitored Objects in the account. Use it to check the activation cost of each Object, the billing start date, the hardware identifier, and information about the installed SIM cards. What the report shows № — row sequence number License plate (fleet number) — the state registration or fleet number of the Object specified in the system IMEI — unique identifier of the installed hardware SIM card 1 — number of the first SIM card SIM card 2 — number of the second SIM card, if installed Plan installation date — date the plan was activated and billing for the Object began Price — activation cost with the currency

The Summary Report contains key information about the operation of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to check mileage and travel time, refuels and fuel drains, speeding, and parking. Before generating the report, select the period and the vehicles, and check the boxes for the data you want to include: Refuels Drains Speed Parking Distance You can select all parameters or only the ones you need. A separate data block is generated for each selected vehicle. What the report shows The beginning of the block shows the Object — the name of the vehicle the figures are calculated for. Distance If the “Distance” box is checked, the following is shown: Mileage — distance traveled by the vehicle over the selected period Travel time — total duration of movement Max. speed — maximum recorded speed Average speed — average travel speed Refuels If the “Refuels” box is checked, recorded increases in fuel level are shown: date and time of the refuel volume of fuel added, in liters Drains If the “Drains” box is checked, recorded decreases in fuel level are shown: date and time of the drain volume of fuel drained, in liters Refuel and drain data is shown when a fuel level sensor is present and correctly configured. Speed If the “Speed” box is checked, the “Speeding” section shows cases of exceeding the set speed: date and time the speeding began recorded speed duration of the speeding in seconds Parking If the “Parking” box is checked, the following is shown: date and time the parking began parking duration

The “Vehicle Operation” report contains summary indicators of vehicle operation for the selected period. Use it to assess mileage and travel time and to identify trips outside working hours, speed limit violations, travel outside Geofences, and idling. Data can be split by day. Each row corresponds to one vehicle for the specified time interval. The “Total” row shows the summary figures for all vehicles. What the report shows № — row sequence number Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object Total distance (km) — total mileage for the reporting period Travel time (hh:mm) — total duration of movement Distance traveled outside working hours (km) — distance traveled outside the set working hours Number of speed limit violations — number of recorded speeding cases Distance outside Geofences (km) — distance traveled outside monitored Geofences Time outside Geofences — time the vehicle spent outside Geofences Fuel consumption (norm) (l) — calculated fuel consumption according to the set norm Idling during working hours — total duration of idling within the set working hours

The “Data Quality” report is designed to check the quality of the telematics data received from monitored Objects over the selected period. Use it to identify missing or delayed data, gaps between packets, GPS problems, sudden coordinate jumps, and other anomalies. The Report helps you assess how suitable the received data is for building Tracks, calculating Mileage, processing Sensor readings, and performing subsequent recalculations. It takes into account not only the loss of connection with the Object but also the quality of the data already received. The indicators are calculated separately for each Object for each day of the selected period. What is analyzed When assessing data quality, the system checks: — delay in packets arriving at the server — intervals between adjacent packets — sudden coordinate jumps — GPS signal quality, including the number of satellites and the HDOP value — invalid packets and packets without coordinates — packets with identical timestamps — exceeding the maximum speed set for the Object What the report shows Object — name or number of the monitored Object Start — start of the analyzed period Stop — end of the analyzed period Score — overall data quality score on a scale from 0 to 100. The higher the value, the better the data quality Status — overall state of data quality: ok— the data meets the set requirements warning— deviations requiring attention were detected bad— significant data quality problems were detected no_data— there is no data for the analyzed period Points — number of telematics packets received during the period Problems — total number of detected deviations Delay max — maximum delay of a packet arriving at the server Gaps — number of significant gaps between adjacent packets Longest gap — duration of the longest gap GPS problems — number of problems caused by an insufficient number of satellites or an HDOP value above the allowed limit Coord jumps — number of detected sudden coordinate jumps Threshold values The analysis uses allowed data transmission intervals, delays, gaps, the rate of coordinate change, and other threshold values. They can be configured individually for each Object. If some parameters are not set, the system uses default values and the Object’s existing settings, including the minimum number of satellites, maximum HDOP, maximum speed, and allowed time without connection.

The Detailed Report shows how a vehicle moved over the selected period. It lets you view the time and route of Trips, the vehicle location, Driver data, and travel speed. The report can be generated for only one vehicle at a time. The selected period must not exceed three days. What the report shows Object — the vehicle the report was generated for Date and time — date and time of the Event Location — the address where the vehicle was at the given moment Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip Travel speed — vehicle speed at the given route point Max. speed — maximum speed on the corresponding segment Status — Trip type, for example, Trip start or Parking end For each Trip, summary information is also provided: Trip number duration average speed maximum speed distance traveled

The “Offline Devices” report contains a list of selected Objects with which there is no connection at the time the report is generated. Use it to find out which device is not transmitting data, how long the connection has been missing, and when the last Event was received from it. The Report shows the current state of the Objects and is built for the current day only. If you select several vehicles, only those that are offline at the time of generation are included in the report. What the report shows Group — the group the monitored Object belongs to Object — name or number of the vehicle Message — connection status information, for example, how long the connection has been missing or a message that the device has never connected Device type — type of the monitored Object, for example, car or bus Last event — date and time of the last Event received from the device The “Total” row shows the total number of Objects that are offline.

The “Equipment Operation by Day” report is designed to monitor the daily operation of monitored Objects. Use it to assess the duration of movement and Parking, working time on the line, ignition-on time, daily Mileage, and average speed. What the report shows Object — name or number of the monitored Object; Time moving — total duration of the Object’s movement during the day. The minimum speed at which an Object is considered to be moving is set in its settings Parking time — total time during which the Object was not moving; set in the Object card on the “Settings” tab Working time on the line — the sum of moving time and stop time during working hours Stop time during working hours— total duration of stops included in working time. The minimum duration of such a stop is determined by the “Min. parking time” parameter in the Object settings Ignition on — total time the ignition was on Time off duty — the part of the day not included in working time on the line. Calculated as the difference between 24 hours and working time; Distance — the Object’s Mileage for the day Avg. speed — the Object’s average speed for the day

The Events Report contains information about the Events recorded by the system for the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. Use it to find out which Event occurred, when and where it was recorded, how fast the Object was moving, and which Driver was assigned to it. What the report shows Object — name or number of the monitored Object Date and time — date and time the Event was recorded Event — Event type and additional details Speed — the Object’s speed at the time of the Event. If speed is not determined for the Event, the field may be empty Drivers — the Driver assigned to the Object at the time of the Event Geofences — the Geofence where the Event was recorded Place — address or description of the Object’s location at the time of the Event The content of the report depends on the Events, Sensors, and Notifications configured for the selected Objects.

The “Route Idling Events” report contains information about cases when a monitored Object remained stationary for longer than the allowed time. Use it to find out where and when the idling occurred, which Driver was assigned to the Object, and which Geofence it was in. How idling is determined The allowed idling duration is set in the Object card in “Settings” in the “Idling, sec.” field. The Event is generated as follows: 1. The vehicle stops 2. The countdown of the set idling time begins 3. If the vehicle does not start moving before this time expires, the system records the Event 4. Idling continues until movement resumes or the ignition is turned off, if the ignition state is taken into account For example, if the idling time for an Object is set to 00:10:00, the Event appears after the vehicle has been stationary for more than 10 minutes. If needed, you can enable ignition tracking in the Object settings. In this case, an idling Event is recorded only when the vehicle is not moving with the ignition on. 1 — Set the idling time 2 — Enable ignition tracking What the report shows Object — name or number of the monitored Object Date and time — date and time the idling Event was recorded Event — information about exceeding the allowed idling time, for example “Idling for more than 00:10:00” Drivers — the Driver assigned to the Object at the time of the Event Geofences — the Geofence where the idling was recorded Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the place where the Object was during the idling

The Idling Report is designed to monitor the duration of vehicle idling. It lets you determine when and where idling occurred, how long it lasted, which Driver was assigned to the Object, and how much fuel was used during this period. How idling is determined Idling is a period during which the vehicle did not move for longer than the allowed time set in the Object settings . The allowed duration is set in the Object card in the “Idling” field. If needed, you can enable ignition tracking. In this case, idling is recorded only if the vehicle is not moving with the ignition on. 1 — Set the idling time 2 — Enable ignition tracking What the report shows Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle or identified by the system, for example, by iButton Department — the group the vehicle belongs to Vehicle type — type of vehicle, for example, passenger car or truck Start — date and time the idling began Stop — date and time the idling ended Duration (hh:mm:ss) — idling duration, calculated as the difference between the start and end times Address — the address where the vehicle was during the idling Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the idling location Excessive fuel consumption Before generating the report, you can check the “Excessive fuel” box. If a fuel level or fuel consumption sensor is configured for the Object, an additional column appears in the report: Excessive fuel — the amount of fuel used by the vehicle during idling. Filter by Drivers If you enable the “On Driver” option, an additional “Drivers” panel opens to the right of the Object list. 1 — Enable the Driver filter 2 — Select a Driver from the list In this panel you can select one Driver, several Drivers, or a group of Drivers. The report will show only Events related to the selected Drivers.

The Fleet Size Report contains information about the number of vehicles in the User’s groups and about changes in the fleet during the reporting period. Use it to assess the initial fleet size, track new arrivals and vehicles taken out of service, and determine the current number of Objects. What the report shows • Object or User group — name of the User group the figures are calculated for • Existing fleet — number of vehicles in the group at the start of the reporting period • Removed from fleet — number of vehicles removed from the group or taken out of service during the reporting period • New deliveries — number of vehicles added to the group during the reporting period • Current fleet — number of vehicles in the group at the end of the reporting period The bottom total row shows the total number of vehicles in the existing fleet, the total number of removed Objects and new deliveries, and the current size of the entire fleet.

The Garbage Collection Tracking Report contains information about garbage truck visits to waste collection points over the specified period. Use it to monitor the completion of assigned routes, check vehicle arrival and departure times, and identify the collection points actually visited. Data is grouped by vehicle and date. For each vehicle, the list of collection points visited during the corresponding day is shown. What the report shows • Vehicle ID — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Vehicle Type — type of vehicle • Driver Name — the Driver assigned to the vehicle • Assigned Route — the route assigned to the vehicle • Notes — additional notes • Collection Point — name or full address of the waste collection point • Location — the actual location of the visited point; shown as a link together with geographic coordinates • Arrival — date and time the vehicle arrived at the collection point • Departure — date and time the vehicle left the collection point • Comment — additional information about the visit to the collection point The links in the “Location” column take you to the corresponding point on the Map. Comparing the Collection Point with the actual location helps you check whether the required point was actually visited. The Report helps you: — monitor compliance with waste collection routes — check the sequence in which points were visited — determine how long the vehicle spent at each point — identify missed points or deviations from the assigned route — analyze vehicle and Driver performance by day

The GLONASS Report contains summary information about organizations’ vehicles for the selected period. Use it to compare the number of registered vehicles with their actual deployment, and to identify Objects with zero Mileage, missing navigation data, or repair status. What the report shows Organization name — the organization the vehicles belong to Registered in GLONASS — number of vehicles registered in the GLONASS system Actual deployment — number of vehicles that actually operated on the given day Zero mileage — number of vehicles with no Mileage recorded for the day No navigation — number of vehicles from which no navigation data was received Vehicles under repair — number of vehicles marked as under repair At the bottom of each block, the totals are shown: Total table count — total number of records in the table Total vehicles — total number of vehicles If there is no data for the selected day, 0 is shown in the corresponding columns.

The Report contains information about changes in fuel level for the selected vehicles over the specified period. In addition to refuels, the report also shows fuel drains. Use it to find out when and where the fuel level changed, determine the volume of a refuel or drain, and compare the Sensor readings at the beginning and end of the Event. What the report shows Object — name or number of the vehicle Date — date and time the fuel Event was recorded Fuel start — fuel level at the beginning of the Event Refuel — volume of the fuel level change. For a refuel, this is the amount of fuel added; for a drain, the amount drained Fuel end — fuel level after the Event ended Type — kind of fuel Event: Refuel — the fuel level increased Drain — the fuel level decreased Geofence — the Geofence where the Event occurred Address — address or description of the refuel or drain location The data is generated from fuel level sensor readings. For Events to be displayed correctly, the Sensor must be installed and configured for the corresponding vehicle.

The “Trip Details” report contains detailed information about the movement and state of the selected Object over the specified period. Use it to trace the route by individual GPS points, find out the Object’s speed, heading, coordinates, and location, and check the readings of connected Sensors. Before generating the report, you need to select a period of no more than three days and no more than three monitored Objects. A separate data block is generated for each selected Object. Each row corresponds to one point recorded by the GPS tracker. What the report shows № — sequence number of the point GPS date/time — date and time the point was recorded by the GPS tracker Speed — the Object’s speed at the moment the point was recorded Heading — direction of the Object’s movement in degrees Distance — distance traveled during the interval between points Travel time — duration of movement during the corresponding interval Latitude — geographic latitude of the point Longitude — geographic longitude of the point Place — address or description of the Object’s location at the moment the point was recorded Status — state of the Object, for example “Stop” or “Moving” Geofence — name of the Geofence the Object was in Received date/time — date and time the data was received by the system from the GPS tracker Temperature — temperature Sensor reading Humidity sensor — humidity Sensor reading Battery — battery charge level Door — door state, for example, open or closed The columns with temperature, humidity, charge level, and door state are filled in when the corresponding Sensors are present and correctly configured.

The Monthly Mileage Report contains information about the distance traveled by the selected vehicles in each month of the reporting period. Use it to compare Mileage by month and find out the total Mileage of each vehicle over the entire selected period. Before generating the report, select the vehicles and a period that may cover one or more months. The system automatically splits the data by calendar month and creates a separate column for each month. What the report shows Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object Month — the vehicle’s Mileage for the corresponding month Total — the vehicle’s total Mileage for the entire selected period.

The Mileage Report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out the time and place each Trip started and ended, its duration, the distance traveled, and the average and maximum speed. The “Total” row shows the total duration, total distance, and maximum speed for the corresponding Object. What the report shows Object — name or number of the monitored Object Begin — date and time the Trip started End — date and time the Trip ended Start — address or description of the Trip start location Stop — address or description of the Trip end location The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location. Duration — Trip duration, calculated as the difference between the start and end times Distance — the vehicle’s Mileage for the Trip Avg. speed — average travel speed during the Trip Max. speed — maximum speed recorded during the Trip Fuel data Before generating the report, you can check the “Fuel” box. In this case, fuel level and consumption information for each Trip is added to the table: Fuel level at start — fuel Sensor reading at the start of the Trip Fuel level at end — fuel Sensor reading at the end of the Trip Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the Trip, in liters Fuel consumption — average fuel consumption during the Trip, calculated in liters per 100 km The figures are generated when a fuel level or fuel consumption sensor is present and correctly configured. If there is no Sensor or no data was received from it, the corresponding columns may show zero values.

Mileage Report No. 2 contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to find out the time and place each Trip started and ended, the assigned Driver, odometer readings, duration, distance, and travel speed. What the report shows Begin — date, time, and place the Trip started End — date, time, and place the Trip ended Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip Odometer at start, km — odometer reading at the start of the Trip Odometer at end, km — odometer reading after the Trip ended Next maintenance, km — remaining Mileage until the next maintenance Duration — Trip duration Distance, km — distance traveled during the Trip Avg. speed, km/h — average travel speed during the Trip Max. speed, km/h — maximum speed recorded during the Trip

An engine hour is a unit for measuring the operating time of an engine or other equipment. In the simplest case, one engine hour corresponds to one hour of engine operation. In some systems, the calculation may also take engine speed and load into account. Engine hours help determine the actual operating time of machinery, monitor its use, and plan maintenance by operating time rather than by Mileage alone. The Engine Hours Report contains information about the operating time of the selected Objects over the specified period. Operating periods are determined from the readings of the Sensor configured for calculating engine hours. The “Total” row shows the total operating time and total fuel consumption for the corresponding Object. What the report shows Sensor — the Sensor whose state is used to calculate operating time, for example, an ignition Sensor; Start — date and time the Sensor switched to the active state and engine hour counting began; Stop — date and time the Sensor switched to the inactive state and counting ended; Duration — operating time during the corresponding interval; Fuel — amount of fuel used during operation. For engine hours to be calculated correctly, you need to configure the corresponding Sensor for the Object. Fuel data is shown when a fuel level or fuel consumption sensor is present and correctly configured.

The Netstar Report is an electronic trip sheet (e-Trip Sheet) with detailed information about the vehicle’s operation over the selected period. The report shows, in sequence, the movement and Parking intervals, speed indicators, Mileage, violations, and fuel consumption. Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicle. In the “Report parameters” window you can specify: Crew Member 1–4 — crew members Controller — the responsible controller The information you enter is used to generate the electronic trip sheet. General information The top of the report shows: Trip Sheet Number — the electronic trip sheet number generated by the system Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle Crew Members — the crew members specified before generating the report Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object Period — the dates the trip sheet was generated for What the report shows Each row corresponds to a separate movement or Parking interval. Status — state of the vehicle: moving or a numbered Parking Start — date and time the interval began End — date and time the interval ended Duration — duration of the movement or Parking Distance — distance traveled during the movement interval Max. — maximum speed during the interval Average — average speed during the interval Driver ID — Driver identifier Speeding — information about recorded speeding Harsh Braking — information about harsh braking Harsh Acceleration — information about harsh acceleration Over Idle — duration of exceeding the allowed idling time Started at — start time of the recorded action or Event Ended at — end time of the recorded action or Event Work — type of activity during Parking, for example Rest/Sleep/Eat/Other Work — working time category, indicated by the codes NT/OT/DT If a particular Event was not recorded, a dash is shown in the corresponding column. Summary indicators The bottom of the report shows summary information: Total distance — total Mileage Driving time — total duration of movement Parking time — total duration of Parking Number of Stops — number of Parking stops Average speed — average travel speed Max. speed — maximum recorded speed Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated fuel consumption according to the set norm Fuel consumption (by sensor) — fuel consumption according to Sensor readings Average by norma — average normative consumption per 100 km Average by sensor — average consumption per 100 km according to Sensor readings

The “No Movement” report is designed to find vehicles that did not move for a set amount of time or traveled less than a set distance over the selected period. Use it to determine which vehicles have been stationary for a long time, when data was last received from them, and where they are. Before generating the report, you can set the following parameters: 1 — Vehicle not moving time (hours) — the minimum number of hours the vehicle has not moved. The report includes Objects whose time without movement is equal to or greater than the specified value 2 — Vehicle has traveled less than (km) — the maximum distance traveled by the vehicle over the selected period. The report includes Objects whose Mileage is less than the specified value For example, if you enter 2 in the first field and 5 in the second, the report shows the vehicles that meet these conditions: those that have not moved for at least two hours and have traveled less than five kilometers. What the report shows Group — the group or folder the vehicle belongs to Registration — registration or fleet number of the vehicle Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle Last movement date — date and time when the vehicle was last moving Last update time — date and time the last data was received from the Object Status — current state of the Object and Parking duration Location — the vehicle’s last known location Difference — interval between the date of the last movement and the time of the last data update

The Parking Report contains information about the Parking of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out when and where a vehicle was parked, how long the Parking lasted, and which Geofence the Object was in. Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicles. You can also set the duration of the Parking to be included in the report: 1— Min. time (sec.) — minimum Parking duration. Shorter Parking is not included in the report. For example, with a value of 120, Parking of two minutes or longer is shown. 2— Max. time (sec.) — maximum Parking duration. Parking longer than the specified value is not included in the report. A value of 0 means the maximum duration is not limited. These parameters help you exclude Parking that is too short or too long and keep only the intervals needed for analysis. What the report shows Vehicle number — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle Start — date and time the Parking began Stop — date and time the Parking ended Duration — total Parking duration Place — address or description of the place where the vehicle was Lat — geographic latitude of the Parking location Lon — geographic longitude of the Parking location Geofence — the Geofence where the Parking was recorded The “Total” row shows the total duration of all Parking of the corresponding vehicle over the specified interval.

The Raw Speed Report contains raw speed and coordinate data for the selected Object over the specified period. Use it to view the sequence of recorded measurements, find out the vehicle’s speed, and determine its location at each moment. What the report shows Date — date the measurement was recorded Time — exact time the measurement was recorded Speed — vehicle speed at the moment the data was received lat — geographic latitude of the Object’s location Lon — geographic longitude of the Object’s location

This report shows information about the operation of the Sensors installed on the refrigerator unit, as well as its location and speed over the selected period. When generating the report, you can set the minimum recording interval (in seconds). The minimum recording interval (in seconds) is a parameter that determines how often the system records the state of the refrigerator unit and adds new rows to the report. For example, if you set the interval to 900 seconds (15 minutes), the temperature, door state, ignition, and other parameters are shown in the report at 15-minute steps over the selected period. To track the parameters of specific Sensors and get their readings in the report, you need to configure them on the Object. For example, if temperature and humidity Sensors are installed on the refrigerator unit, their readings are shown in the report. What the report shows Gps Date Time — date and time within the reporting period Geographic latitude and longitude coordinates to determine the Object’s location Place — place where the movement began Speed — speed of the Object Ignition sensor — state of the ignition Sensor AC unit status — Sensor showing whether the refrigerator unit is on or off Back door, Left door, Right door — door states (rear, left, right)

The report is designed to monitor refrigerator unit operation while the vehicle is moving and parked. It helps you track temperature, equipment state, speed, and Object location over the selected period. When generating the report, you can set the minimum recording interval (in seconds). This parameter determines how often the system records data and adds rows to the report. For example, if you set the interval to 900 seconds (15 minutes), information about temperature, ignition, and other parameters is shown in the report at 15-minute steps over the selected period. What the report shows GPS date/time — date and time the data was recorded Latitude / Longitude — coordinates of the Object at the time of recording Place — address or detected location of the Object Speed — travel speed at the time the data was recorded Ignition sensor — ignition state (on / off) AC unit status — Sensor showing whether the refrigerator unit is on or off Back door — rear door state (open / closed) Ground — state of the connection to the “ground” of the vehicle’s on-board network (power circuit monitoring) RFID — radio-frequency identification data (if tag-based authorization is used)

The Report contains information about loading and unloading operations of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out when and where the cargo weight changed, determine the operation type, and compare the weight Sensor readings before and after the operation. An increase in the recorded weight is treated as loading, and a decrease as unloading. Each row of the report corresponds to one detected operation. What the report shows Vehicle number — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle Date — date and exact time the operation was recorded Weight at start (kg) — weight Sensor reading before the operation began Weight difference (kg) — amount of weight change during loading or unloading Weight at end (kg) — weight Sensor reading after the operation ended Operation type — kind of recorded change: Load — the vehicle weight increased Unload — the vehicle weight decreased Address — address or description of the place where the operation took place The address is shown as a link that takes you to the corresponding location. Summary indicators The bottom of the report shows: Total weight load — total weight of cargo loaded Total weight unload — total weight of cargo unloaded Max weight load — maximum weight of a single loading Min weight load — minimum weight of a single loading

The Rotation Sensors Report contains graphical information about the vehicle’s speed and the operation of rotating mechanisms over the selected period. Use it to compare the Object’s movement with the intensity of connected equipment, for example, loading and unloading mechanisms. A separate chart is generated for each selected Object. The horizontal axis shows the date and time, and the vertical axes show travel speed and the rotation speed of the mechanisms. What the report shows Speed, km/h — travel speed of the Object Loading, rpm — rotation speed of the loading-related mechanism Unloading, rpm — rotation speed of the unloading-related mechanism Each indicator is shown in a separate color on the chart. This lets you determine periods of movement, when the mechanisms start and stop working, and compare their activity over time. Rotation data is shown when the corresponding Sensors are present and correctly configured on the Object.

The “Trips” report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out when and where each Trip started and ended, its duration, the distance traveled, the speed, and the coordinates of the start and end points. To view individual Trips, click the icon to the left of the Object name. After it expands, detailed data for each Trip appears under the summary row. To collapse the list, click the icon. What the report shows Object — name or number of the vehicle Begin — date and time the Trip started Start — address or description of the Trip start location End — date and time the Trip ended Stop — address or description of the Trip end location Duration — Trip duration Distance (km) — distance traveled during the Trip Avg. speed (km/h) — average travel speed Max. speed (km/h) — maximum speed recorded during the Trip Start coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip start location End coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip end location Fuel data Before generating the report, you can check the “Fuel” box. In this case, the following columns are added to the table: Fuel level at start — fuel Sensor reading at the start of the Trip Fuel level at end — fuel Sensor reading after the Trip ended Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the Trip Average fuel consumption per 100 km — fuel consumption based on Sensor readings, converted to 100 km Fuel consumption by norm — calculated fuel consumption according to the norm set for the Object Fuel consumption by norm/100 km — the set fuel consumption norm per 100 km The actual fuel level and consumption figures are generated when a fuel Sensor is present and correctly configured. Viewing a Trip on the Map You can expand the “Map” block above the report. To see the route of a specific Trip, first expand the Trip list using the icon, and then click the row you need. The Map shows: — the vehicle’s route — the start and end points of the Trip — the direction of movement along the route — the vehicle’s position — the sections of the route corresponding to the selected Trip

The “Mileage Plus” report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out the time and place movement started and ended, the Trip duration, the distance traveled, the speed, and the coordinates of the start and end points. What the report shows • Object/Event — name of the vehicle or the Event associated with it • Begin — date and time the Trip started • Begin/Message — address or description of the place where movement started • End — date and time the Trip ended • Stop — address or description of the place where movement ended • Duration — Trip duration • Distance (km) — distance traveled during the Trip • Avg. speed (km/h) — average travel speed • Max. speed (km/h) — maximum speed recorded during the Trip • Start coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip start location • End coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip end location • Agent ID — identifier of the monitored Object The total row shows the duration, distance, and average and maximum speed for the corresponding interval. Fuel data Before generating the report, you can check the “Fuel” box. In this case, the following columns are added to the table: • Fuel level at start — fuel Sensor reading at the start of the Trip • Fuel level at end — fuel Sensor reading after the Trip ended • Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the Trip • Average fuel consumption per 100 km — actual fuel consumption converted to 100 km • Fuel consumption by norm — calculated consumption according to the norm set for the Object • Fuel consumption by norm/100 km — the set fuel consumption norm per 100 km The actual fuel level and consumption figures are shown when a fuel Sensor is present and correctly configured.

The “Points” report contains information about the telematics points received by the system from the GPS tracker of the selected Object. Use it to check the recording and receipt time of each point, the coordinates, speed, heading, ignition state, and other transmitted parameters. Before generating the report, you need to select: — one vehicle — a period of no more than one day What the report shows № — sequence number of the point Gps Date — date the point was recorded by the GPS tracker Gps Time — time the point was recorded by the GPS tracker Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle at the time the point was recorded Speed — the Object’s speed determined from GPS data Latitude — geographic latitude of the Object’s location Longitude — geographic longitude of the Object’s location GPRS Received Date — date the point was received by the system GPRS Received Time — time the point was received by the system Ignition — ignition state at the time the point was recorded Heading — direction of the Object’s movement indicated by a compass point, for example N, SE, or W Acceleration/Deceleration — recorded value of the Object’s acceleration or deceleration Downloading the report Next to the “Generate report” button there is a download button. Use it to download the report in XLSX format for viewing and further processing in a spreadsheet program.

The Shifts Report is designed to monitor vehicle operation against a shift schedule in the “Time Control” Module. Use it to compare the actual departure and return times of vehicles with the set shift boundaries, identify late arrivals, and view movement and Parking intervals. One shift per day is counted for each vehicle. The day boundary is determined by the time zone specified in the Object settings. How a shift is determined The start of a shift is when the vehicle leaves the specified Geofence The end of a shift is when the vehicle returns to that Geofence Allowed start and end times are set for the shift If the vehicle left later than the set time, the system may record a “Late departure” Event If the vehicle returned later than the set time, the system may record a “Late return” Event The report shows, in sequence, the vehicle’s movement and Parking intervals during the shift What the report shows Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle Departure/Return — shift start or end Event: leaving the specified Geofence or returning to it Working time violation — detected deviation from the set schedule, for example, late departure or late return Status — state of the vehicle in the corresponding interval, for example Movement or Parking Date — the date the shift belongs to Start time — actual start time of the displayed movement or Parking interval End time — actual end time of the interval Shift start — set shift start time Shift end — set shift end time Duration — duration of the corresponding interval. Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle during the interval. For Parking, a zero value is usually shown. Start place — address or description of the Object’s location at the start of the interval. End place — address or description of the Object’s location at the end of the interval. For the start and end of a shift to be determined correctly, first configure the working Geofence and the vehicle’s schedule: 1. In the Geofence settings, assign the required Object and check the “Working” box for it. Leaving this Geofence is treated as the start of a shift, and returning to it as the end of the shift. 2. In the Object card, open the “Working time” tab, select the working days, and set the schedule for weekdays and days off. 3. Check the Object’s time zone: it determines the day boundaries and is used to match actual Events against the set schedule 4. Check the minimum parking time in the Object settings. This parameter determines how long a stationary Object must remain still before it is counted in the report as Parking.

The “Shifts Summary” report contains summary information about vehicle operation relative to a base working Geofence, for example “Office”. Use it to find out when the vehicle started work and first arrived in the base Geofence, how long it stayed there, the number of departures, daily Mileage, and odometer readings. For each vehicle, data is generated by day for the selected period. For the report to be generated correctly, you need to assign one base Geofence to the vehicle and set the “Working” option for it. The system uses this Geofence to record entries and exits. What the report shows • Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Start date — the date the figures are calculated for • Start time — time the vehicle began work • Arrival time in the “Office” base Geofence — time of the vehicle’s first arrival in the working Geofence • Idle duration in the base Geofence during the day — total time the vehicle was stationary in the working Geofence • Number of departures from the base Geofence during the day — number of recorded exits from the working Geofence • Time of last entry into the base Geofence during the day — time of the last recorded entry • Time of last exit from the base Geofence during the day — time of the last recorded exit • Odometer reading at start of day — odometer value at the start of the counted period • Odometer reading at end of day — odometer value at the end of the counted period • Mileage — distance traveled by the vehicle during the day Idle duration is determined according to the Parking settings of the corresponding vehicle. An image with an example of the report will be added to the guide in one of the upcoming versions.

This is a summary report for analyzing vehicle operation by shift. It shows how Mileage and working time are distributed between the first shift, the second shift, and time outside shifts. The report is built based on the working time settings in the Object card. For example, two shifts are set in the Object’s working time: Shift 1 — from 06:00 to 17:00 Shift 2 — from 18:00 to 05:00 Friday — day off The system uses this schedule to split data into time intervals: movement from 06:00 to 17:00 falls into Shift 1 movement from 18:00 to 05:00 falls into the second shift movement between shifts and on days off falls outside shifts What the report shows 1st Shift (km) — Mileage in the first shift 2nd Shift (km) — Mileage in the second shift After Duty (km) — Mileage outside shifts Total (km) — total Mileage 1st Shift Hours — driving time in the first shift 2nd Shift Hours — driving time in the second shift After Duty Hours — driving time outside shifts Ignition On (hh:mm) — total ignition-on time Running (hh:mm) — driving time Idling (hh:mm) — idling time Sensor (hh:mm) — operating time of the selected Sensor Trips — number of Trips Average speed — average speed of Trips Avg Km / Trip — average Mileage per Trip Avg Time (hh:mm) / Trip — average Trip duration Fuel Consumption — fuel consumption

The Report for Sky Favorit contains information about vehicle movement and Parking over the selected period. Use it to find out when and where a vehicle was moving or parked, assess the duration and distance of Trips, and check the operation of the door, air conditioner, and heater. What the report shows • Status — state of the vehicle: moving or a numbered Parking • Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began • End — date and time the movement or Parking ended • Dur. — duration of the corresponding interval • Distance (km) — distance traveled during the movement interval • Start — address where the movement or Parking began • Stop — address where the movement or Parking ended • Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the start and end points of the interval • Door open (count) — number of recorded door openings • Air conditioner (Duration) — air conditioner operating time • Heater (Dur) — heater operating time The door, air conditioner, and heater indicators are shown when the corresponding Sensors are present and correctly configured. Summary indicators The bottom of each Object’s block shows: • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle • Driving time — total duration of movement • Parking time — total duration of Parking • Average speed — average travel speed • Max. speed — maximum recorded speed • Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated consumption according to the set norm • Fuel consumption (by sensor) — consumption according to the fuel Sensor readings • Average l/100 km (by norm) — normative fuel consumption per 100 km • Average l/100 km (by sensor) — actual consumption per 100 km based on Sensor data Actual fuel consumption data is generated when a fuel Sensor is present and correctly configured.

The Smart Waste Management Report is designed to analyze waste container servicing over the selected period. Use it to assess the intensity of waste collection, identify areas where containers fill up regularly, and adjust collection schedules and routes. The Report consists of two blocks. Collections Chart The chart shows the number of recorded servicing operations for each selected Object. Object names or numbers are shown on the left, and the values on the bars show the number of servicing operations during the reporting period. The chart lets you: — assess the intensity of work for each Object — compare the number of servicing operations — identify Objects with high or low workload — check compliance with the waste collection schedule Bins Statistics Map The Map shows the places where the system recorded waste containers being full. The number on a marker shows the number of such Events at the corresponding point. When you select a marker, the Bins Statistics window opens with the following information: Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the point Address — address or description of the location Total full alerts — total number of fullness Notifications Bin full alerts list — list of Objects for which Notifications were recorded, and the number of Events for each The Map lets you identify zones where containers regularly fill up or overflow, determine areas that may need more frequent collection, and plan vehicle routes based on the actual load. The Report data is generated from recorded servicing Events and container fullness Notifications. For the information to be displayed correctly, the corresponding Sensors and Notifications must be configured for the selected Objects.

The Special Sensors Report contains charts of Sensor readings for the selected Objects over the specified period. Use it to trace how parameters change over time, identify sharp deviations and periods with no data, and compare the readings of several Sensors. A separate block of charts is generated for each selected Object. The content of the report depends on the hardware and Sensors installed on the Object. What the chart shows — the horizontal axis shows the date and time the data was received — the vertical axis shows the Sensor values in the corresponding units — individual Sensors or indicators are shown in different colors — when you hover over a line, you can see the exact time and the recorded value The example report shows: Fuel level sensor signal level, dB — signal level of the fuel level sensor GSM/GPRS network level, units — indicator of the device’s mobile network connection quality Satellite signal level, units — indicator of satellite signal reception quality CAN speed, km/h — vehicle speed received from the CAN bus On-board network, Volts — voltage of the vehicle’s on-board network Sharp rises and drops in the lines show a change in the corresponding parameter. Horizontal sections mean the value stayed relatively constant. To display readings, the special Sensors must first be added and correctly configured on the Object . If a Sensor is missing, configured incorrectly, or did not transmit data during the selected period, the corresponding chart may not be displayed.

The Speed Report contains charts of speed changes for the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to trace speed dynamics, determine periods of movement and stops, and identify sudden changes or high speed values. A separate chart is generated for each selected Object and time interval. What the chart shows Horizontal axis — date and time the data was recorded Vertical axis — vehicle speed in km/h Blue line — change in the Object’s speed over time Zero value — no movement at the corresponding moment Gaps in the chart may mean there is no data for that period When you hover over the line, a pop-up window appears with the date, time, and the Object’s speed at the selected point on the chart.

The Equipment Summary Report contains daily indicators of the operation of machinery and the equipment installed on it over the selected period. Use it to assess the duration of operation, idling, operation under load, and downtime, and to check the number of recorded actions, fuel consumption, and distance traveled. What the report shows • Object — name of the monitored Object • Vehicle number — registration, fleet, or other vehicle number specified in the system • Date — the date the figures are calculated for • Operating time (ignition sensor) — operating duration determined from the state of the ignition Sensor • Idling — duration of equipment operation without load • Under load — duration of equipment operation under load • Downtime — duration of the period during which the machinery or equipment was not operating • Number of actions — number of recorded work operations or equipment activations • Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the corresponding day • Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle during the day The duration of the modes is shown in the “hours:minutes:seconds” format. The content and accuracy of the data depend on the presence and correct configuration of the ignition, load, equipment operation, and fuel consumption Sensors. If the required data was not received, some fields may be empty or contain zero or incorrect values.

The Total Mileage Report contains information about the distance traveled by the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to compare the daily Mileage of Objects based on GPS and CAN data, and to find the total Mileage for the entire reporting period. Data is grouped by date: each row corresponds to one day, and a separate column is generated for each selected vehicle. The top of the report shows the list of selected Objects and the analyzed period. What the report shows • № — row sequence number • Date — the date the Mileage is calculated for • Total — total Mileage of all selected vehicles for the corresponding date • Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object • GPS — Mileage calculated from GPS coordinates • CAN — Mileage calculated from CAN bus data The bottom total row shows the total Mileage based on GPS and CAN data for the entire selected period — both for all Objects together and for each vehicle separately. CAN data availability depends on the hardware and Object settings. If no data is received from the CAN bus, the corresponding value may be missing or equal to zero.

Summary Mileage Report No. 2 contains information about the distance traveled by the selected vehicles on the specified date. Use it to compare the Mileage of monitored Objects based on GPS and CAN data, and to find the total Mileage of all selected vehicles. What the report shows Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle Date — the date the Mileage is calculated for GPS — Mileage calculated from GPS coordinates CAN — Mileage calculated from CAN bus data. The bottom “Total” row shows the total Mileage of all selected vehicles for the specified date — separately for GPS and CAN data CAN data availability depends on the installed hardware and Object settings. If no data is received from the CAN bus, the corresponding value may be missing or equal to zero.

The Total Engine Hours Report contains information about engine operating time and the distance traveled by the selected vehicles over the specified period. An engine hour is a unit for measuring engine operating time. The Report helps you monitor vehicle use and plan maintenance based on engine operating time, not just the distance traveled. What the report shows • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Period — date and time the period began and ended for which the data is calculated • Engine hours — engine operating time over the specified period • Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle over the specified period The bottom “Total” row shows the total engine operating time and the total distance traveled by all selected vehicles over the specified period.

The “Trips and Parking (with Maps)” report contains information about the Trips and Parking of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to analyze the time and place movement started and ended, the duration of operation and Parking, the distance traveled, and speed indicators. The Report includes summary indicators for the selected period and detailed information for each Trip. When Maps are enabled, the vehicle’s route is displayed graphically. What the report shows • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Work start time — date and time the vehicle began work • Work start place — address where the work started • Work end time — date and time the vehicle ended work • Work end place — address where the work ended • Duration — duration of the counted Event • Operating duration — total vehicle operating time • Parking duration — total Parking time for the corresponding period • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip • Mileage — distance traveled by the vehicle • Maximum speed — maximum speed recorded during the Trip • Average speed — the vehicle’s average speed during the Trip Report parameters Before generating the report, you can select the Map type and configure additional display options: • Show odometer — adds the odometer readings at the start and end of the Trip to the table • Show maps — adds a Map with the vehicle’s route to the report • Show parking — shows Parking locations on the Map; this option becomes available after Maps are enabled Show odometer If you enable the “Show odometer” option, additional columns appear in the summary and detailed parts of the report: 1 — Odometer at start — odometer reading at the moment work or the Trip began 2 — Odometer at end — odometer reading at the moment work or the Trip ended Show maps If you enable the “Show maps” option, a Map with the vehicle’s route for the selected period appears below the table part of the report. Before generating the report, you can select in the “Map type” field the base map to be used to display the route.
