Show parking If you enable both “Show maps” and “Show parking”, Parking location markers are shown on the Map along with the route. When you select a Parking marker, a tooltip opens with the following data: • Start — date and time the Parking began • End — date and time the Parking ended • Duration — total Parking duration

The Trip Report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to determine the time and place each Trip started and ended, check odometer readings, and find the distance traveled. What the report shows • Type — the data source used to calculate Trip indicators, for example CAN • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip • Start time — date and time the Trip started • Start Odo — odometer reading at the start of the Trip • Start address — address recorded at the Trip start location • End time — date and time the Trip ended • End Odo — odometer reading at the end of the Trip • End address — address recorded at the Trip end location • Total Odo — distance traveled during the Trip, calculated as the difference between the final and initial odometer readings The bottom “Total” row shows the total distance traveled by the vehicle over the selected period.

The “Trips and Parking” report contains information about the movement and Parking periods of the selected monitored Objects. Use it to determine when and where a vehicle started and finished moving, how long it was on the road or parked, how far it traveled, and how fast it moved. Events are shown in chronological order. Each row corresponds to a separate Trip or Parking. The top of the report shows the monitored Object and the analyzed period. What the report shows • Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking”; Parking is also assigned a sequence number • Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began • End — date and time the movement or Parking ended • Duration — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking • Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking • Start — address where the movement began or the Parking location • Stop — address where the movement ended; for Parking the value may not be shown • Coordinates — geographic coordinates of the start and end of the Trip, or the coordinates of the Parking location The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location. Summary indicators The bottom of the report shows summary indicators, first for the current data block, for example for one Object for a day, and then for the entire selected reporting period. • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the Object within the current report block • Track Time — total Track duration, which includes moving time and short Parking recorded within the Track • Moving time — total time the Object was moving • Track Parking Time — total duration of Parking included in the Track; together with moving time it makes up the Track Time value • Parking time — total duration of all Parking of the Object, including Parking before the first Trip, between Trips, and after the last Trip within the reporting period • Average speed — the Object’s average speed while moving • Maximum speed — the highest speed recorded while moving Totals for the entire reporting period Below the divider line, similar indicators calculated across all report blocks are shown: • Total mileage for the period — total distance traveled by the Object over the entire selected period • Tracks Time for the period — total duration of all Tracks in the period, including movement and Parking within Tracks • Moving time for the period — total time the Object was moving over the entire selected period • Track Parking Time for the period — total duration of Parking included in Tracks over the selected period • Parking time for the period — total time the Object was parked within the selected period • Average speed for the period — the Object’s average speed over the entire selected period • Maximum speed for the period — the highest speed recorded over the entire selected period How Parking time is counted The Report covers the entire selected time interval, including the periods before the first and after the last Trip: • If the vehicle was not moving at the start of the reporting period, the system adds Parking from the start of the period to the first recorded movement • If the Object remained stationary after the last movement, Parking is shown until the end of the reporting period • If the end of the selected period is in the future, the last Parking is shown up to the current moment In this way, the report accounts not only for Trips but also for the gaps between them, so that the sequence of Events within the analyzed period remains continuous. Trips and Parking display filter At the top of the generated report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options. They let you change which rows are shown without selecting the reporting period again: • “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — all Events are shown • only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown • only “Parking” enabled — only periods when the Object was parked are shown To show or hide an Event type, check or uncheck the corresponding box. Report parameters Before generating the report, you can configure additional parameters: • Drivers — adds a “Driver” column to the table with information about the Driver assigned to the Object during the Event • Vehicle type — adds a “Vehicle type” column to the table with the vehicle category • Chart — adds a graphical representation of movement and Parking periods to the report The chart appears above the table part and shows the sequence of Events on a timeline: “Parking” — periods when the Object was not moving “Movement” — periods of the Object’s Trips The chart lets you visually compare the duration of Trips and Parking and determine when the state changes. For a detailed view, you can zoom in on a selected part of the timeline. The Reset zoom button restores the original chart scale.

The “Trips and Parking with Charts and Maps” report (Trips and Parkings (charts maps)) contains summary and detailed information about an Object’s movement and Parking over the selected period. It helps you find out the number and duration of Trips and Parking, the places where movement started and ended, Mileage, and maximum and average speed. The chart shows changes in speed and Mileage, and the Map shows the route and Parking locations. Report summary The Report Summary section shows the overall indicators of the Object’s operation for the selected period: • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Start time — date and time the first recorded movement began • Start location — address where the first movement began • Departure time — date and time the last recorded movement ended • End location — address where the last movement ended • Trips — total number of Trips • Movement duration — total time the Object was moving • Parking — number of recorded Parking stops • Parking duration — total duration of Parking counted between Trips • Mileage — total distance traveled by the Object • Duration — additional total indicator of the duration of recorded Events • Maximum speed — the highest speed recorded over the selected period • Average speed — the Object’s average speed The “Total” row shows the total values for the number of Trips and Parking stops, movement duration, Parking duration, and Mileage. Trip details The Trips details section contains a separate row for each Trip: • Start time — date and time the Trip started • Start location — address where the movement began • Departure time — date and time the Trip ended • End location — address where the movement ended • Duration — Trip duration • Parking duration — duration of the Parking associated with the Trip • Engine hours — engine operating time during the Trip • Mileage — distance traveled during the Trip • Maximum speed — maximum speed recorded during the Trip • Average speed — average travel speed during the Trip The Trip start and end addresses are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location. Parking details The Parkings details section contains information about recorded Parking: • Start time — date and time the Parking began • Departure time — date and time the Parking ended • Duration — total Parking duration • Location — address where the Object was located Chart Below the tables there is a chart of speed and Mileage changes over time. • Horizontal axis — time within the selected reporting period • Left vertical axis — vehicle speed in km/h • Right vertical axis — accumulated Mileage value in kilometers • Speed / “Speed” — change in the Object’s speed over time • Mileage / “Mileage” — change in accumulated Mileage Sections where the speed is zero correspond to periods with no movement. A rising Mileage line shows an increase in the distance traveled. When you hover over a point on the chart, a tooltip appears with the date, time, and recorded speed value. Map and Parking To add a Map to the report: 1. In the “Map Type” field, select the base map on which the route will be shown. For example, OSM or Google Sat 2. Check the “Show maps” box A static Map with the route for the corresponding period is added to the report. It may show the start and end points of the route. 3. To mark Parking locations, also check the “Show parking” box. The “Show parking” option becomes available after Show maps is enabled. If Parking display is enabled, Parking locations are marked with the icons. Odometer readings To include odometer readings, check the “Show odometer” box before generating the report. Additional columns with the odometer readings at the start and end of the Trip appear in the table part.

The “Trips and Parking for Aramco” report contains information about the movement and Parking periods of vehicles over the selected period. The Report lets you reconstruct the sequence of Trips and Parking, and determine their time and duration, start and end addresses, distance traveled, and summary operating indicators. What the report shows • Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking”, as well as the Event sequence number • Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began • End — date and time the movement or Parking ended • Duration — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking • Distance (km) — distance traveled during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking • Start — address where the Trip began or the Parking location • Stop — address where the Trip ended; for Parking the value may not be shown • Coordinates — coordinates of the start and end of the Trip, or the coordinates of the Parking location For a Trip, the “Coordinates” column shows two pairs of coordinates: the first corresponds to the start of movement, the second to its end. For Parking, the coordinates of the Object’s location are shown. The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location. Trips and Parking filter At the top of the generated report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options. Use them to change which data is shown: • “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — the full sequence of Events is shown • only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown • only “Parking” enabled — only Parking periods are shown To show or hide an Event type, check or uncheck the corresponding box. Summary indicators Below the table, summary indicators are shown, first for the current Object or report block, and then for the entire selected period: • Trips — total number of Trips • Movements — number of recorded movement periods • Parking — number of recorded Parking stops • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle • Moving time — total duration of all movement periods • Parking duration — total time the Object was parked • Average speed — the vehicle’s average speed over the selected period • Maximum speed — the highest speed recorded over the selected period • Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated fuel consumption based on the set norm • Fuel consumption (by sensor) — fuel consumption calculated from Sensor readings • Average consumption, l/100 km (by norm) — calculated average fuel consumption per 100 km • Average consumption, l/100 km (by sensor) — average fuel consumption per 100 km calculated from Sensor data In a separate summary block, the values are repeated with the “for the period” label and are calculated from all the data included in the report. The “Chart” option Before generating the report, you can enable the “Chart” option. In this case, a timeline appears above the table part that graphically shows the sequence of movement and Parking. The chart shows: • horizontal axis — date and time within the reporting period • “Parking” — periods when the vehicle was not moving • “Movement” — periods when the vehicle was moving The chart helps you determine when the Object was moving or parked, compare the duration of Events, and see long periods without movement.

The “Trips and Parking MC” report (Trips and Parkings MC) contains information about the movement and Parking periods of the selected monitored Object. It lets you reconstruct the sequence of Events, determine the time and duration of Trips and Parking and their start and end addresses, and calculate Mileage and other operating indicators. What the report shows • Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking” • Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began • End — date and time the movement or Parking ended • Dur. — duration of the corresponding Event • Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object while moving; no value is shown for Parking • Start — address where the Trip began or the Parking location • Stop — address where the Trip ended; for Parking the value may not be shown Summary indicators Below the table, summary indicators are shown, first for the current report block, then for the entire selected period: • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the Object • Track Time — total duration of the generated Tracks • Moving time — total time the Object was moving • Track Parking Time — duration of Parking counted within Tracks • Parking time — total duration of all Parking within the reporting period • Average speed — the Object’s average speed • Max. speed — the highest recorded speed The “for the period” block shows similar indicators calculated from all the data included in the report. Trips and Parking filter At the top of the generated report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options: • “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — all Events are shown • only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown • only “Parking” enabled — only Parking periods are shown The checkboxes let you change which rows are shown without regenerating the report. Parameters before generating the report Before generating the report, the following additional parameters are available: • Show debug • Auto reset [Beta] • Show max/avg speed • Reset milage • Update milage • Drivers • Vehicle type • Fuel • Chart Show debug The “Show debug” option is intended for diagnosing the calculation of Trips and Mileage. After you enable it, a “Debug menu” panel appears at the top of the generated report. The panel contains additional parameters: • Type • Mileage • Show TS • Show Lat/Lon These parameters let you view the internal data from which the Trips and Parking were generated. 1 — Type If you enable the “Type” option in the Debug menu, a “Type” column is added to the table. It shows the internal type or identifier of the Event used by the system to generate the row. For example: • renderStart — Event generated at the start of the reporting period • render_LP_tracks — Parking generated between movement segments • one_[…], m_start_[…], m_last_[…] — internal identifiers or methods of generating movement segments These values are intended primarily for diagnostics. They help determine from which Event or algorithm stage a Trip or Parking was generated. 2 — Mileage If you enable the “Mileage” option in the Debug menu, columns with detailed odometer data are added to the table: • Odo type — source or type of odometer data, for example CAN • Start — odometer reading at the start of the Trip • Stop — odometer reading at the end of the Trip These columns let you check which readings the value in the “Distance, km” column is calculated from. Odometer readings may be missing for Parking. 3 — Show TS If you enable the “Show TS” option, the values in the “Begin” and “End” columns are shown as timestamps — numeric timestamp values. The system uses a timestamp to store the exact time of an Event. This mode is intended for technical data checks. When the option is disabled, the time is shown in the usual date and time format. 4 — Show Lat/Lon If you enable the “Show Lat/Lon” option, geographic coordinates are shown in the “Start” and “Stop” columns instead of addresses: • lat — latitude • lon — longitude For a Trip, the coordinates of the start and end of movement are shown. For Parking, the coordinates of the Object’s location are shown. Auto reset [Beta] The “Auto reset [Beta]” option is used when calculating Mileage from odometer readings. The system automatically tries to detect resets or breaks in the sequence of readings, for example when a new odometer value is lower than the previous one, and takes them into account when calculating the distance. Reset milage The “Reset milage” option enables processing of Events related to resetting the Mileage readings. It is used to exclude an incorrect difference between the readings before and after a detected reset. Update milage The “Update milage” option enables the use of updated Mileage readings when generating the report. It affects the odometer values used and the calculated distance. The changes can be seen in the following data: • initial and final odometer readings • distance for individual Trips • total mileage Show max/avg speed If you enable the “Show max/avg speed” option, additional columns appear on the right of the table: • Max. speed — the highest speed recorded during the Trip • Avg. speed — the Object’s average speed during the Trip Drivers If you enable the “Drivers” option, a “Driver” column is added to the table. It shows the Driver assigned to the Object during the corresponding Trip or Parking. If no Driver was assigned or no data was received, the cell may stay empty. Vehicle type If you enable the “Vehicle type” option, a column of the same name is added to the table. It shows the category or type of the vehicle specified in the Object settings. Fuel If you enable the “Fuel” option, additional indicators are shown in the summary part of the report: • Total consumption, l/100 km — calculated fuel consumption • Balance at start, l — amount of fuel at the start of the reporting period • Balance at end, l — amount of fuel at the end of the reporting period • Total consumption for the period — total calculated fuel consumption over the entire selected period The availability and accuracy of these values depend on the presence of a fuel level sensor and its settings. Chart If you enable the “Chart” option, a timeline showing the sequence of Events appears above the table: • “Parking” — periods when the Object was not moving • “Movement” — periods of the Object’s movement • horizontal axis — date and time within the reporting period The chart helps you visually compare the duration of Trips and Parking, determine when each movement started, and detect long periods without movement.

The “Trips and Parking (Working Time)” report contains information about the movement and Parking of the selected vehicles according to the work schedule. Use it to determine how an Object was used during working or non-working time: when it was moving, where it was parked, how far it traveled, and how much time it spent in each state. What the report shows • Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking” • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the corresponding Event • Day of the week — the day of the week on which the movement or Parking took place • Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began • End — date and time the movement or Parking ended • Dur. — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking • Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking • Start — address where the movement began or the Parking location • Stop — address where the movement ended; for Parking the value may not be shown Summary indicators Below the table, summary indicators for the current Object or report block are shown: • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the Object during the counted time • Moving time — total duration of all movement periods • Parking time — total duration of all Parking • Average speed — the Object’s average speed while moving • Max. speed — the highest speed recorded while moving Below that, a separate summary block with indicators for the entire selected period is shown: • Total mileage for the period • Moving time for the period • Parking time for the period • Average speed for the period • Max. speed for the period Working time parameters Before generating the report, you can select which data to include: • Working time only — the report counts Events that fall within working time according to the configured schedule • Non-working time only — the report counts Events that fall within non-working time Working and non-working time is determined by the Object’s work schedule settings . Working time only When you enable the “Working time only” option, the report lets you analyze vehicle use during the hours set by the work schedule. The report shows: • Trips made during working time • Parking between Trips • Parking from the start of the working interval to the first movement • Parking from the last movement to the end of the working interval Non-working time only When you enable the “Non-working time only” option, the report shows movement and Parking outside the set work schedule. It helps you identify: • Trips after working hours end • vehicle use on weekends or non-working days • movement before the start of the work shift • long Parking outside working hours

The “Trips and Parking (Working Time) No. 2” report contains summary information about the movement of the selected vehicles according to the work schedule. Use it to determine when a vehicle was used, who drove it, where it traveled from and to, and to find out the movement duration, Mileage, and speed indicators. What the report shows • Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the movement • Day — the day of the week on which the Trips were made • Start — date and time the first movement began in the counted interval • End — date and time the last movement ended in the counted interval • Duration — total movement duration in the report row • Distance — total distance traveled by the vehicle • From — address where the movement began • To — address where the movement ended The addresses in the “From” and “To” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding locations. Totals by date Below each daily block, the indicators calculated from all rows for the corresponding date are shown: • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle during the day • Moving time — total movement duration for the day • Average speed — the vehicle’s average speed for the day • Max. speed — the highest speed recorded during the day Totals for the entire period The bottom of the report shows indicators for all data included in the selected reporting period: • Total mileage for the period — total distance traveled by the vehicle • Moving time for the period — total movement duration • Average speed for the period — average travel speed over the entire period • Max. speed for the period — the highest speed recorded over the entire period Working time parameters Before generating the report, you can select which data to include: • Working time only — Trips made within the Object’s work schedule are counted • Non-working time only — Trips made outside the Object’s work schedule are counted Working and non-working time is determined by the vehicle’s work schedule settings . Working time only When you enable the “Working time only” option, the report shows vehicle use during the hours set by the work schedule. This mode lets you assess: • the number and duration of working departures • Mileage during working time • the start and end points of movement • average and maximum speed • the assigned Driver’s work Non-working time only When you enable the “Non-working time only” option, the report shows Trips made outside the set work schedule. This mode lets you identify: • movement before the start or after the end of a shift • Trips on weekends and non-working days • vehicle use outside permitted hours • Mileage and speed indicators during non-working hours If a Trip crosses the boundary of the working interval, the report counts the part of the movement that corresponds to the selected mode.

The “Mileage (with Drivers)” report contains information about vehicle movement and Parking, with the assigned Drivers indicated. It lets you determine who drove the vehicle, when and where Trips and Parking took place, how far the vehicle traveled, and which operating indicators were calculated. What the report shows • Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking”; Parking may be assigned a sequence number • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Event • Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began • End — date and time the movement or Parking ended • Duration — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking • Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking • Start — address where the Trip began or the Parking location • Stop — address where the Trip ended; for Parking the value may not be shown • Coordinates — geographic coordinates of the start and end points of the Trip or of the Parking location • Max. speed — the highest speed recorded during the Trip • Trip type — Trip category determined by the system or the Object settings The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding locations. Summary indicators Below the table, the following indicators are shown for each Object and date: • Trips — total number of Trips • Movements — number of recorded movement periods • Parking — number of recorded Parking stops • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle • Moving time — total movement duration • Parking dur. — total Parking duration • Average speed — average travel speed for the corresponding period • Max. speed — the highest recorded speed • Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated fuel consumption based on the set norm • Fuel consumption (by sensor) — fuel consumption calculated from Sensor readings • Average l/100 km (by norm) — calculated average fuel consumption per 100 km • Average l/100 km (by sensor) — average fuel consumption per 100 km based on Sensor data Filter by Drivers If you enable the “On Driver” option, an additional “Drivers” panel opens to the right of the Object list. In this panel you can select one Driver, several Drivers, or a group of Drivers. The report will show only Events related to the selected Drivers.

The “Trips and Parking with Fuel” report contains information about the Trips and Parking of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to determine the time and place each Event started and ended, its duration, Mileage, and travel speed, and to analyze refuels, fuel drains, and fuel consumption. What the report shows • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Folder — the folder where the Object is located in the system • Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking” • Start — date and time the Trip or Parking began • Start address — address where the movement began or the Parking location • Stop — date and time the Trip or Parking ended • End address — address where the movement ended; for Parking the value may be missing • Duration — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking • Mileage (km) — distance traveled by the Object during the Trip; a zero value is shown for Parking • Refueled (l) — volume of fuel added during the corresponding Event • Drained (l) — volume of fuel recognized by the system as a drain • Fuel consumption by sensor (l) — volume of fuel used, calculated from fuel level sensor data • Fuel consumption/100 km (l) — actual fuel consumption per 100 km, calculated from Sensor data • Norm, l/100 km — the normative fuel consumption per 100 km set for the vehicle • Max. speed (km/h) — the highest speed recorded during the Trip • Average speed (km/h) — the vehicle’s average speed during the Trip Trips and Parking filter At the top of the generated report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options. They let you change which rows are shown: • “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — the full sequence of Events is shown • only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown • only “Parking” enabled — only periods when the Object was parked are shown To show or hide a particular Event type, check or uncheck the corresponding box.

The “Trips and Parking with Axle Load” report contains information about vehicle movement and Parking, supplemented with axle load indicators. It is intended primarily for trucks and lets you compare the route, Mileage, and Trip duration with the minimum, maximum, and average load values. Load data helps you monitor vehicle operation and identify possible excesses of permissible values. The permissible load depends on the type and design of the vehicle, the number of axles, and the applicable regulatory requirements. What the report shows • Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking” • Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began • End — date and time the movement or Parking ended • Dur. — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking • Distance (km) — distance traveled by the Object during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking • Start — address where the movement began or the Parking location • Stop — address where the movement ended; for Parking the value may be missing • Coordinates — coordinates of the start and end points of the Trip or the coordinates of the Parking location • Average weight — average load value recorded during the corresponding Event • Weight (min.) — minimum recorded load value during the Trip or Parking • Weight (max.) — maximum recorded load value during the Trip or Parking • Trip type — Trip category determined by the system or the Object settings The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding locations. Summary indicators Below the table, summary indicators for the selected Object and period are shown: • Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle • Moving time — total duration of all movement periods • Parking time — total duration of all Parking • Average speed — the Object’s average travel speed • Max. speed — the highest speed recorded over the selected period • Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated fuel consumption based on the set norm • Fuel consumption (by sensor) — fuel consumption calculated from Sensor readings • Average l/100 km (by norm) — normative average fuel consumption per 100 km • Average l/100 km (by sensor) — actual average fuel consumption per 100 km based on Sensor data Trips and Parking filter At the top of the report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options: • “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — the full sequence of Events is shown • only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown • only “Parking” enabled — only periods when the Object was parked are shown To show or hide a particular Event type, check or uncheck the corresponding box. Load data To show average, minimum, and maximum weight, compatible hardware that transmits axle load information must be installed and configured on the Object. If no data is received or the corresponding parameters are not configured, a dash or a missing value is shown in the weight columns.

The “Trips and Parking with Levels” report contains information about the movement and Parking of the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. Data is grouped by Object and date and shown as summary rows that you can expand to view the detailed sequence of Events. The summary row shows the time and place the counted period started and ended, its total duration, and the total distance. To view the Trips and Parking it includes, click the button to the left of the Object name. What the report shows • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object • Type — Event type: “Movement” or “Parking” • Begin — date and time the Trip or Parking began • Start — address where the movement began or the Parking location • End — date and time the Trip or Parking ended • Stop — address where the movement ended; for Parking it usually matches the place where it began • Duration (h) — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking • Distance (km) — distance traveled by the Object during the Trip; a zero value is shown for Parking

The Equipment Utilization Report contains information about the use of the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. It lets you compare the time machinery spent idling and under load, and determine the total engine hours and the distance traveled. Use the Report to assess the efficiency of equipment operation, identify long operation without useful load, reduce downtime, and allocate resources more efficiently. Report structure The information is presented in several sections: “Totals for the period” — summary indicators for all selected Objects “Equipment use for the period” — a pie chart showing the ratio of Parking, idling, and operation under load Breakdown by Object — indicators for each Object, split by date Totals Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object Description — additional information about the Object. If no description is set, the field stays empty Days — number of calendar days included in the analyzed period Idling — engine operating time without recorded useful load. The indicator is shown in two columns: % — the share of idling calculated by the system hh:mm — idling duration in hours and minutes Operation under load — time during which the equipment performed useful work. The indicator is shown in two columns: % — the share of operation under load calculated by the system hh:mm — duration of operation under load in hours and minutes Total engine hours — total engine operating time for the corresponding period in “hh:mm” format Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object over the specified period Equipment use chart Below the totals table, in the “Equipment use for the period” section, a pie chart is shown. It shows the ratio of the main equipment states: Parking — time when the equipment was neither working nor moving Idling — time the engine ran without useful load Operation under load — time the equipment performed useful work The chart lets you visually compare the states and determine what part of the selected period was actual work, idling, and Parking. Breakdown by Object Below the chart, separate blocks split by date are shown for each Object. Each daily block contains: Description — additional description of the Object Idling — percentage and duration of idling Operation under load — percentage and duration of operation under load Total engine hours — total engine operating time for the day Distance, km — the Object’s Mileage for the corresponding date This breakdown lets you compare the indicators of one Object by day and find periods of high load, long idling, or no work. This breakdown lets you compare the indicators of one Object by day and find periods of high load, long idling, or no work.

The “Vehicle License Expired” report is designed to monitor the validity periods of vehicle registration documents. It lets you identify in advance the Objects whose vehicle registration certificate (STS) has already expired or expires within the selected period. Check period Before generating the report, you need to specify the check range in months. The system calculates the checked interval starting from the current date and selects the vehicles whose STS validity falls within this range. For example, if a period of 3 months is selected, the report includes vehicles: whose STS has already expired whose STS expires within the next three months The larger the selected range, the more future expiration dates the check covers. For the report to be generated correctly, open the “Info” tab in each vehicle’s card and fill in the following data: STS number — series and number of the vehicle registration certificate Validity period — STS expiration date The system compares the specified date with the check period and adds the vehicle to the report if the document has already expired or expires within the selected range. What the report shows Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object Group — the group the vehicle is in Description — additional description of the vehicle Year — the vehicle’s year of manufacture specified in the Object card STS number — the document number specified in the Object card Validity period — STS expiration date

The Total Work Report contains time indicators of the operation of the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. Use it to compare the duration of movement and Parking, ignition-on time, and Maintenance periods, and to determine the time actually worked. What the report shows • Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object • Date — date and time the interval began and ended for which the indicators are calculated • Information — additional information about the monitored Object; if no information is specified, the field stays empty • Total time — total duration of the corresponding reporting interval • Movement duration — total time the Object was moving • Parking time — total duration of the Object’s Parking • Ignition on — total time during which the ignition was recorded as on • Ignition off — total time during which the ignition was off • Non-working time — the part of the reporting interval that falls within non-working time according to the configured Object schedule • Maintenance time — duration of the periods during which the Object was under Maintenance • Time worked — time within the work schedule minus Maintenance periods. Calculated as the total time minus non-working time and Maintenance time The “Working time only” option Before generating the report, you can enable the “Working time only” option. In this case, the indicators are calculated only within the working intervals set in the Object’s schedule. The option lets you exclude nighttime, weekends, and other non-working intervals from the analysis.

The “Waybills” report is designed to generate vehicle waybills according to the established standard forms. Some fields are filled in automatically based on the selected Object, the assigned Driver, the reporting period, and the data specified in the system. The Report lets you prepare a document for recording the operation of the vehicle and Driver, check the generated information, save the waybill to a file, or print it. Selecting the vehicle type Before generating the report, you need to select the vehicle type. The waybill form depends on the selected type: • Passenger car — a passenger car waybill is generated using standard interindustry form No. 3, approved by Resolution of the State Statistics Committee of Russia of 28.11.1997 No. 78 • Truck — a truck waybill is generated using standard interindustry form No. 4-P, approved by Resolution of the State Statistics Committee of Russia of 28.11.1997 No. 78 What the waybill shows The content of the document depends on the selected form. The waybill may include: • organization details • date, series, and number of the waybill • make and state registration number of the vehicle • fleet and personnel numbers • Driver details • driver’s license number and Driver class • license details • actual departure and return times • data on the Driver’s and the vehicle’s work • information on movement and fuel consumption • the Driver’s assignment • fields for marks, signatures, and technical inspection results The presence and completion of individual fields depends on the selected form and on what information has been entered in the organization, vehicle, and Driver cards. Saving and printing You can preview the generated waybill in the report. The following actions are available at the bottom of the window: • Download in Excel format — saves the waybill as a spreadsheet • Download in PDF format — saves the document in PDF format • Print — opens the waybill for printing

The “Working Time No. 2” report contains information about the Mileage and working time of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to compare odometer readings with the calculated Mileage, determine the number of Trips, and split working time into categories: regular, overtime, holiday, and Sunday. What the report shows • Date — the day the indicators are calculated for • Start odometer — odometer reading at the start of the first Trip on the corresponding date • End odometer — odometer reading at the end of the last Trip on the corresponding date • Total mileage, km — total distance traveled by the vehicle during the day • Number of Trips — number of Trips recorded for the corresponding date • Regular/working time — duration of work within the set work schedule • Overtime hours — duration of work beyond the set norm • Holiday working hours — duration of work on public holidays • Sunday working hours — duration of work on Sundays • Total mileage and hours — graphical comparison of Mileage with the working time categories. The colored sections of the bar show the distribution of the indicator, and the calculated Mileage value is shown below it Summary indicators The bottom “Total” row shows the summary indicators for the entire reporting period: • total vehicle Mileage • total number of Trips • total regular working time • total number of overtime hours • total working time on public holidays • total working time on Sundays • the total value in the “Total mileage and hours” column

This section contains reports related to the “Trips” Module. They help you monitor vehicle movement along bus lines, stop visits, the completion of loop trips, and schedule adherence. With these Reports you can: — check which stops a vehicle visited — monitor the sequence and timing of stop visits — analyze the number of full and incomplete loop trips — check compliance with the set schedule — get summary information on vehicle operation on routes

The Stop Visits Report is designed to monitor visits to bus stops by vehicles assigned to routes. Use it to determine which stops a vehicle visited, and to find out its actual arrival and departure times. Before generating the report, you need to select the vehicles and the bus line for which you want to check stop visits. What the report shows Each row of the report corresponds to one recorded visit to a stop by a vehicle. The report shows: Order — the position of the stop in the sequence of the route Route number — name or number of the route on which the stop was visited Stop — name of the visited stop Address — address of the stop Date — date of the stop visit Arrival time — time the vehicle arrived at the stop Departure time — time the vehicle left the stop Vehicle — number of the monitored Object that visited the stop If an RFID tag is linked to the stop, PILOT can determine a visit from the data of the RFID reader installed on the vehicle. The recorded visit is shown in the report in the same way as a visit determined by the Object’s coordinates.

The “Stop Visit Control” report helps you monitor how vehicles actually follow the set routes. Use it to check which stops a vehicle visited, when it arrived and departed, and how long it stayed at the stop. When generating the report, select the stops whose visits you want to check. If several stops are selected, the report shows all recorded visits to these stops by the selected vehicles during the specified period. What the report shows Each row is one recorded visit to a stop by a vehicle. The report shows: Stop sequence number — the position of the stop in the sequence of the route Route — name or number of the route the vehicle was following Stop name — name of the visited stop Address — location of the stop Date — day of the stop visit Arrival time — time the vehicle arrived at the stop Departure time — time the vehicle left the stop Parking — length of time the vehicle was at the stop Vehicle number — vehicle number

The Loop Trips Report is designed to analyze vehicle operation on routes. It shows how long the vehicle operated, as well as the number of completed full and incomplete loop trips. The system determines whether a loop trip is complete based on the visits to the stops assigned to the Trip and the set direction of movement. If the vehicle completed the route according to the specified conditions, the loop trip is counted as full. If the route conditions were not fully met, the loop trip is counted as incomplete. Each row of the report contains information about the operation of one vehicle on the route on the specified date. What the report shows Trip number — number of the Trip assigned to the monitored Object Vehicle number — vehicle number Date — date the Trips were performed Route arrival time — time the vehicle entered the route Departure time — time the vehicle left the route Time on route — total duration of the vehicle’s operation on the route, calculated as the difference between the arrival time and the departure time Number of Trips — number of full loop trips completed on the route Number of incomplete Trips — number of loop trips during which not all anchor stops were visited

The Report is designed to monitor actual schedule performance on the selected bus line. It compares the planned stop times (from the schedule matrix) with the actual stop visit times and clearly shows how closely the actual movement matched the plan. What the report shows The Report is built for one selected bus line and is generated as a table where: The first column is the schedule name Each following column is a stop on the route Each cell contains data for a specific stop for a specific Trip Each cell shows: Plan — planned arrival time at the stop Actual — actual arrival time at the stop Difference — deviation of the actual time from the planned time Object — the vehicle (license plate) that actually made the stop If no actual visit was recorded, the cell is marked “Missed” (not performed) How the report is generated 1. The selected bus line and its list of stops are taken 2. The history of schedule versions in effect during the specified period is loaded 3. For each day in the reporting interval, the schedule table to apply is determined: by specific date by day of the week or daily 4. For each planned Trip and each stop, the nearest actual visit to that stop is searched for 5. If an Event is found within the allowed deviation window, Plan / Actual / Difference / Object are shown in the cell 6. If no Event is found, the cell is marked “Missed” Comparison logic The Report checks schedule adherence not for a specific bus but by whether the stop was made on the line. If several buses operate on the line at the same time, the report counts any bus that actually made the stop at the right time. No more than one actual Event is used for each planned time. One actual Event is not reused to confirm several planned stops. If the schedule changes within the reporting period, the schedule version that was in effect at the time of the specific planned Trip is applied. Report color coding Green — minimal deviation, the stop was made close to the plan Yellow — acceptable deviation from the schedule Orange — noticeable time deviation. Red — large deviation or missed stop (no actual visit)

The Report is designed to show information about Object rental, with the Contract, amount, and rental type indicated. If needed, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon; a menu opens where you can turn individual fields off or on.

A configured Rent Car Module is required. This section contains reports related to the “Drivers” Module. They help you monitor Driver performance, driver’s license data, identifiers, and Trips, and analyze vehicle use. With these Reports you can: — see who drove a vehicle and when — track the assignment of Drivers to vehicles; — monitor the validity of driver’s licenses — analyze Trips, Mileage, and violations in Geofences — get summary information on all Drivers in the fleet

This report shows how each vehicle and Driver worked during the day. It lets you see: — when the first Trip started and the last one ended — how long the vehicle was moving, parked, and idling — the Mileage and speed for the day — how many Trips were made What the report shows The report is built by day: one table row = one working day of one vehicle Date — date the first Trip of the day started Object — vehicle Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle on that day (if no Driver is assigned, no driver is shown) First Trip start time — date and time the vehicle first started moving during the day Hours between the start of the first Trip and the end of the last (hh:mm:ss) — the vehicle’s total “working time” for the day: from the first Trip to the last, including movement and stops Driving time % — the share of working time spent moving Travel time (hh:mm:ss) — total movement time for the day Parking time (hh:mm:ss) — total time of stops and Parking between Trips Duration (hh:mm:ss) — total duration of the vehicle’s operation for the day (movement + Parking) Idling time (hh:mm:ss) — time when the vehicle was on but not doing work (for example, the engine was idling) Distance (km) — the vehicle’s Mileage for the day. Average speed (km/h) — average speed for the day (distance divided by moving time). Max. speed (km/h) — maximum recorded speed for the day Number of Trips — how many separate Trips were made during the day At the bottom of the table there is a “Total” row, which automatically calculates: — total working time — total Mileage — average indicators across all rows for the selected date

This report shows which Drivers have a driver’s license that is about to expire. For a Driver to appear in the report, the following fields must be filled in on the Driver’s card: 1. Driver’s license / ID number — license number 2. License validity / Expiry date — expiration date How to generate the report 1. Go to the Driver reports section 2. Select the “Driver’s License Expiring” report 3. Specify the check period — the range of months during which a driver’s license may expire 1 — License check period 2 — Select Drivers 4. Select the Drivers 5. Start generating the report What the report shows Each row is a separate Driver whose license expiration falls within the selected period. Driver — the Driver’s full name Group the Driver belongs to ID number — driver’s license number Contact number — contact phone number Registration — the Object the Driver is assigned to Expiry date — driver’s license expiration date

This report shows the violations Drivers committed inside the selected Geofence during the specified period. Before generating the report, specify: 1. The Geofence in which to check for violations 2. The Driver the report is generated for 1 — Select a Geofence 2 — Select a Driver What the report shows Object — the vehicle (monitored Object) in which the violation occurred Group — the group or unit the Object belongs to Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle at the time of the violation Zone — the Geofence in which the violation was recorded Date — exact date and time of the violation Violation — name of the violation

This report shows which identifiers are linked to each Driver — RFID cards, iButtons, passes, and other access keys. What the report shows Group — the group the Driver belongs to Driver — the Driver’s name or full name Identification number — ID specified on the Driver’s card ID — ID received by the system from the device when a tag is used Date — date the ID was last used Difference — field showing discrepancies between the data

This report shows cases when iButtons that are not in the system were used during the specified period. An iButton is an electronic Driver identification key. It is used to control access to monitored Objects. For the system to recognize the Driver correctly, the iButton must be registered in the system and compatible with the reader. What the report shows Object — the vehicle or monitored Object in which the key was used. Date — date and time the Trip started. iButton — identifier of the key that is not registered in the system

This report shows summary information about all Drivers registered in the system. What the report shows Group — the group the Driver belongs to Driver — the Driver’s name or full name ID Number — the Driver’s identification number in the system Tag ID — tag identifier Contact number — the Driver’s phone number Registration — the Object/vehicle the Driver is assigned to Date — date the Driver was registered in the system License Expiry Date — when the driver’s license expires.

The Report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicles over the specified period, with data broken down by Driver. Use it to determine who was driving the vehicle during each Trip, check its duration and distance, and analyze speed indicators. What the report shows • Period — date and time the period began and ended for which the report was generated • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip • Begin — date and time the Trip started • End — date and time the Trip ended • Duration — Trip duration • Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle during the Trip • Avg. speed — the vehicle’s average speed during the Trip • Max. speed — the highest speed recorded during the Trip At the bottom of each Object’s block, the vehicle’s total Mileage for the selected period is shown. Filter by Drivers Before generating the report, you can enable the “On Driver” option. After you enable it, an additional “Drivers” panel opens to the right of the Object list. In this panel you can select one Driver, several Drivers, or a group of Drivers. After the report is generated, it will include only the Trips related to the selected Drivers. 1 — Enable the Driver filter 2 — Select a Driver from the list

This report shows which Drivers were assigned to vehicles during the selected period. What the report shows Object – the vehicle or monitored Object Date – the time period the report is generated for Driver – name of the Driver assigned to the Object Begin – date and time the Driver was assigned to the Object End – date and time the Driver was unassigned Duration – the time the Driver spent behind the wheel during the selected period

This report shows information about Drivers’ Trips, splitting them into business and personal. It helps you analyze how much time and how many kilometers Drivers spent on work and on personal purposes. Before generating the report, select the Driver the report is generated for. What the report shows Group – Driver group in the system Object – the vehicle or monitored Object Driver – who drove the vehicle during the Trip Total Trips – number of all Trips during the selected period Business Trips – number of Trips marked as business Private Trips – number of Trips marked as personal Total distance – total Mileage for all Trips Business Trip distance – Mileage of business Trips only Private Trip distance – Mileage of personal Trips only Total duration – total time of all Trips Business Trip duration – time spent on business Trips Personal Trip duration – time spent on personal Trips
Driving Quality Driving quality is a measure of how well a driver operates a vehicle safely, economically and comfortably. Reports for the Eco-driving module.

The Driving Quality Report helps you understand how carefully and safely Drivers drive. The system records Events (harsh acceleration, braking, speeding, and others), converts them into penalty points, and generates a summary table. What the report shows Each row is the data for one vehicle on the selected date and the assigned Driver. The report shows: Object — the vehicle for which violations were recorded Group — name of the group the vehicle belongs to Date — the day the indicators are calculated for Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle at the time of the violation Distance — the section of the route (in km) on which Eco Driving Events were recorded Duration — total time of violations Types of violations For each Event type (acceleration, braking, cornering, speed, seat belt), the following is shown: number of violations / penalty points Total penalty — total number of points for all violations Penalty / 100 km — average number of penalty points per 100 km of Mileage The lower the value, the calmer and safer the driving style. At the bottom of the report there is a “Total” row — these are the summary indicators for all rows of the table. When generating the report, you can choose which data to use for the analysis: By Objects — to see which vehicles have more violations By groups — to compare indicators between vehicle groups By Drivers — to identify the most careful Drivers and those who break the rules most often If you do not select Objects, the report is built for all vehicles driven by the selected Drivers If you do not select Drivers, the report includes all Drivers, as well as periods when no Driver was assigned to the vehicle When generating the report, you can also take into account the eco weights settings . These settings let you define which violations are considered more serious and which are less significant. The penalty points and the overall score of Drivers and vehicles depend directly on the selected weights. The weights settings icon in the report is shown: — only to Users with administrator rights — only if the Eco Driving Module is enabled in the Contract

Driving Quality Report No. 2 is a log of all violations. This report breaks the data down to each individual Event: when, where, and which violation occurred. What the report shows Each row in the table is one recorded violation. The report contains the following columns: Object — the vehicle in which the violation was recorded Driver — the Driver assigned to this Object at the time of the Event Time — exact time the violation was committed Type — violation category (for example, speeding, harsh braking, etc.) Message — text description of the violation, set when the rule was created in the driving quality control Module Value — the actual measured value at which the rule was triggered (for example, speed, idling duration, acceleration value) Penalty — number of penalty points assigned for the Event Place — address where the violation occurred — a link that lets you open the point on the Map When you select a specific violation, its type and the place on the Map where it occurred are shown.

The Report is designed to show data on the current and previous Eco Driving rating. The Report contains: Vehicle - the monitored Object in the system; Excessive idling - the Object’s inactive time exceeds the set values; Speeding - violation of the set speed limits on roads**;** Harsh Braking - values of a driving style that involves smooth acceleration and braking to reduce fuel consumption and reduce emissions of harmful substances into the atmosphere. Harsh Acceleration - values of a driving style that involves smooth acceleration and braking to reduce fuel consumption and reduce emissions of harmful substances into the atmosphere. Distance - Mileage of the monitored Object during the specified Trip in km; Duration - violation time for the selected period. Current rating - an indicator that reflects achievements over a certain period based on recent driving activity. Previous rating - an indicator that reflects achievements over a certain period based on recent driving activity.

The Speeding Report is a report that shows when and where the driver of a vehicle exceeded the set speed limit. The Speeding Report can be obtained using special devices that connect to the vehicle’s on-board computer and record data on speed, acceleration, braking, cornering, and other parameters. If needed, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon, a menu opens where you can turn individual fields off or on.

The Report contains: Object - the monitored Object on which driving quality was recorded; Total distance (km) - the distance over which the violation was committed; Trip duration - the duration over which the violation was committed; Max. speed- the maximum speed recorded during the Trip. Speeding zone - a section of road on which a maximum speed limit for vehicles is set ; Speeding norm - vehicle movement at a speed exceeding the limits set by law or road signs ; Speeding duration range - duration of the speeding; Normal speeding duration- the time during which the vehicle moves above the set speed limit ; Total speeding duration - the time during which the vehicle moves above the set speed limit ; Speed score - speed score value; Total acceleration - value of total acceleration for the specified period; Acceleration score - acceleration score value; Total number of decelerations - value of total deceleration for the specified period; Deceleration score - deceleration score value; Time without seat belt- Trip time without a seat belt during the reporting period; Seat belt violation score - value for violations of driving without a seat belt; Excessive idling -the vehicle engine idles longer than necessary; Idling duration - value for idling duration; Total score - overall Trip score.

The RAG Events Report is a report that gives an overview of the main driving quality Events. The Report contains: Driver - the Driver assigned to this Object; Total distance (km) - the distance over which the violation was committed; Total acceleration - total acceleration score value; Acceleration score - acceleration score value; Total number of decelerations- total deceleration score value; Deceleration score - deceleration score value; Maximum speed (km/h) - the maximum speed recorded during the Trip. Total speeding time - the total time during which the speed was exceeded; Speed score - speed score value; Time without seat belt - the time during which the Driver drove without a seat belt; Seat belt violation score - score value for driving without a seat belt; Score - calculated from the sum of harsh turns, braking, and acceleration events.

RAG Summary Report This report type provides more detailed information on driving quality. When you select a specific violation, the violation type and its location on the map are shown. Object - the monitored object for which driving quality was recorded; Driver - the driver assigned to the Object; Month - the month in which the violation occurred; Distance - the distance over which the violation occurred; Duration - the duration of the violation; Distance - the distance over which the violation occurred; Duration - the duration of the violation; Number of harsh accelerations - the number of harsh accelerations; Number of harsh accelerations per 100 km - the number of harsh accelerations per 100 km; Number of harsh braking events - the number of harsh braking events; Number of harsh braking events per 100 km - the number of harsh braking events per 100 km; Number of harsh turns - the number of harsh turns; Number of harsh turns per 100 km - the number of harsh turns per 100 km; Maximum speeding, km/h - the maximum speed limit excess; Speeding duration - the time during which the speed limit was exceeded; RAG score - calculated from the sum of harsh turns, braking events and accelerations. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report displays a numeric or ordinal driving rating indicator for a driver. The report contains: Driver - the driver s name in the system; Group - the name of the group in the system**;** Rank - the driver s place in the driving rating; Mileage - the mileage value in km on the specified date; Score - the score; Group - the group. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report displays the driving rating as a percentage. The report contains: Driver - the driver assigned to the Object; No. of trips - the number of trips; Distance - the mileage value in km on the specified date; Number of speeding violations - the number of speeding violations on the specified date; Speeding time - the time the driver exceeded the speed limit on the specified date; Speeding percentage - the speed limit excess by the driver, as a percentage; Max. speed - the maximum speed recorded during the trip; Avg. speed - the average speed recorded during the trip; Excess idling - the value of the idling duration excess; Harsh braking - the number of harsh braking events; Harsh acceleration - the number of harsh accelerations; Rating - a score based on the sum of harsh turns, braking events and accelerations, as a percentage; Group rating - a score based on the sum of harsh turns, braking events and accelerations, as a percentage;

Evaluation Card No. 3 displays data by month. The report contains: Driver - the driver assigned to the Object; Calendar month - a score based on the sum of harsh turns, braking events and accelerations, as a percentage.
Hardware This section covers reports related to Object hardware. Reports in this section can be presented as tables and charts.

Two-State Sensors Report A two-state sensor is a type of sensor that can be in one of two states: active or passive. Such sensors are commonly used to monitor liquid level, pressure, temperature and other parameters. They can be mechanical, optical, magnetic, capacitive or inductive. The report contains: Object - the monitored object; Date and time - the date and time of the event; Event - the sensor state; Driver - the driver assigned to the Object. Geofences - the location of the event. Location - the address where the sensor was triggered. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The hardware operation report displays data on the operation of hardware. For the report to work correctly, all the necessary sensors of the connected hardware must be configured. The report contains: Date - the time period for which the report table is built. Object - the monitored object for which the report table is built. Hardware - the name of the hardware. Start - the date and time the hardware started operating. End - the date and time the hardware stopped operating. Duration - the hardware operating time, the difference between the end and the start. Distance - the distance traveled by the Object during the period. Start location - where the hardware started operating. Stop location - where the hardware stopped operating.
The hardware operation report displays data as a chart showing the Object, sensor readings, and the start and end times of operation.

This report is used to track and record the daily operation of various equipment. It includes the operating time in motion, parking time, resource consumption, and distance data for the reporting period. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the report table is built; Time in motion - the time the equipment started operating; Parking time - the time the equipment stopped operating; Working time on route - the equipment operating time; Stop time during working hours - the equipment stop time; Ignition on - the sensor state; Off-duty time - equal to the difference between 24 hours and the working time on route; Distance - the distance traveled by the Object during the period. Avg. speed - the equipment speed during the reporting period. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Multi-State Sensors Report This report type presents information as a table showing changes in multi-state sensor readings and speed over a given period of time. The report contains: Time - the time of the event; Sensor - the sensor name; Message - the sensor state; Speed - the speed of the Object.
The report displays changes in sensor operation as a chart.

The report displays changes in sensor operation as a table, including the mileage for the selected period. The report contains: Object - the vehicle registered in the system; Start - the date and time operation started**;** End - the date and time operation ended**;** Sensor - the sensor name in the system; Value - the sensor operating state; Mileage - the distance traveled by the Object, in km, during the specified period. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report is used to process fuel dispensing data for fuel tankers and fuel depots. The report contains: Object - the vehicle registered in the system; Operation - the operation type; Start - the date and time operation started**;** End - the date and time operation ended**;** Start vol. (L)- the initial fuel volume; End vol. (L) - the final fuel volume; Refuel (L) - the amount of fuel refueled; Dispensed (L)- the amount of fuel dispensed; Fuel drain (L) - the amount of fuel drained; Address - the address.

This report displays data on mileage, fuel consumption and speed. The report contains: Group - the Object s group in the system; Object - the vehicle registered in the system; Date - the date and time operation started**;** Mileage (km) - the distance traveled by the Object, in km, during the specified period; Mileage while speeding (km) - the mileage driven while exceeding the speed limit; Engine-off time - the engine operating time; Initial volume (L) - the initial fuel volume; Final volume (L) - the final fuel volume; Actual consumption (L) - the amount of fuel the vehicle consumed over a given distance, measured in liters per 100 kilometers**.** Refuel volume (L) - the amount of fuel the vehicle s fuel tank holds or the amount that was added to the tank during refueling; Fuel drain volume (L) - the amount of fuel that was removed from the system, from the vehicle s fuel tank; Actual consumption per 100 (km) (L) - an indicator showing how many liters of fuel the vehicle uses to travel 100 kilometers**;** Engine hours - the unit of measurement for engine operating time; Actual consumption per engine hour (L) - the amount of fuel the engine consumes in one hour of operation. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
Fuel This section covers fuel-related reports.

The “Fuel Consumption by CAN” report shows fuel consumption based on CAN data for the selected period. Use it to compare the amount of fuel consumed with the Object s mileage and to calculate the average consumption per 100 km. Sensor configuration requirements For data to appear in the report, a CAN fuel consumption sensor must be configured on the Object. In the sensor settings, specify: • Purpose — Fuel consumption • Type — Discrete integral • Save history — the checkbox must be enabled The sensor must transmit the cumulative fuel consumption value. To calculate the report, the system takes the initial and final values for the day and calculates consumption as the difference between them. If the sensor is configured with a different purpose or type, or if history saving is disabled, the data may not appear in the report. What the report shows • Object — the name of the monitored object for which the report was generated • Date — the date for which the data is shown • Consumption — the amount of fuel consumed on the specified date • Distance — the Object s mileage on the specified date • Fuel consumption — the average fuel consumption per 100 km Fuel consumption is calculated using the formula: (Consumption × 100 km) / Distance

This report helps you control fuel consumption: you can view and compare fuel data received from the sensor and from the CAN bus, and easily spot possible fuel drains and discrepancies in readings. The report is presented as a table in which, for each Object, you can see: Mileage — how many kilometers the vehicle traveled during the selected period Fuel level — how much fuel was in the tank at the beginning and at the end of the day Refuels — how much fuel was added (by the sensor and by the CAN bus) Fuel consumption — how much fuel was consumed during the trip (by the sensor and by the CAN bus) Average consumption — how much fuel is used on average per 100 km (by the sensor and by the CAN bus) Drained fuel — if any, how much fuel was drained All information is broken down by day so you can track trends and notice any deviations.

Summary Report No. 2 Summary Report No. 2 displays information on distance traveled, refuels, fuel drains, fuel consumption and engine hours for a given period. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the data is displayed. Mileage - the distance traveled over the given period of time. Fuel level at start, L - the amount of fuel at the beginning of the period. Fuel level at end, L - the amount of fuel at the end of the period. Refuels - the amount of fuel refueled during the given period. Fuel drains - the amount of fuel drained during the given period. Fuel consumption - the amount of fuel consumed during the given period. Consumption, L/100 km - the average fuel consumption per 100 km during the given period. Fuel consumption per norm - fuel consumption based on the fuel consumption norm set for the Object. Norm - the calculated fuel consumption per 100 km based on the fuel consumption norm set for the Object. Engine hours - the number of engine hours accumulated during the given period of time. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Summary Report No. 3 Summary Report No. 3 displays information on refuels, fuel drains, speeding and idling for a given period. The report contains: Vehicle number - the name of the monitored object for which the information is displayed. Refuels - the amount of fuel refueled, in liters. Fuel drains - the amount of fuel drained, in liters. Speeding - the date and time when speeding was recorded and the maximum speed recorded at that moment. Idling over 1 hour - the duration, date and time of the recorded idling. Idling addresses - the idling location.

Summary Report No. 4 This report displays information on refuels and distance traveled. The report contains: Object - the monitored object; Distance (km) - the distance traveled by the Object during the reporting period; Refuel - the amount of fuel refueled, in liters, according to the sensor; Average fuel consumption - the average fuel consumption per 100 km for the day; Idling duration - the Object s idling duration during the selected period. Parking duration - the Object s parking duration during refueling. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The report displays generator operation, showing the operating period, engine hours, fuel consumption, refuels, fuel drains and hourly fuel consumption. The report contains: Date - the report start date; Period duration - the duration of the period**;** Vehicle number - the monitored object; Engine hours - the unit of measurement for engine operating time; Fuel consumption by sensor - an indicator reflecting the amount of fuel consumed by the vehicle, based on data received from the fuel level sensor**;** Refuels - the amount of fuel refueled, in liters, according to the sensor; Fuel drains - the amount of fuel drained, in liters, according to the sensor; Fuel consumption per hour - an indicator showing how much fuel the engine consumes in one hour of operation.

The report displays generator operation, showing the operating period, the start and end of machine hours, and the duration. The report contains: Date - the report start date; Period duration - the duration of the period**;** Site - the site; Engine hours - the unit of measurement for engine operating time; Machine hour start - the date and time the generator started operating; Machine hour end - the date and time the generator stopped operating; Duration - the operating duration; Fuel consumption by sensor - an indicator reflecting the amount of fuel consumed by the vehicle, based on data received from the fuel level sensor**;** Refuels - the amount of fuel refueled, in liters, according to the sensor; Refueling time - Fuel drains - the amount of fuel drained, in liters, according to the sensor; Off-time leakage - accounting of time in the off state; Fuel consumption per hour- an indicator showing how much fuel the engine consumes in one hour of operation. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Fuel Drains This report type displays information about fuel drains. The report contains: Object - the monitored object on which a fuel drain was recorded. Date - the date and time of the fuel drain. Fuel level at start (L) - the fuel level at the start of the drain. Drained (L) - the amount of fuel drained. Address - the address where the fuel drain took place.

Liquid Consumption Report The liquid consumption report presents information as a diagram showing the amount of liquid consumed at a given moment in time. When you hover over a bar, additional consumption information pops up. It is intended for pulse sensors only. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the diagram is built. Date - the time period for which the diagram is built. Mileage, km - the monitored object s mileage on the specified date. Total consumption, L - the amount of fuel consumed on the specified date. Consumption, L/100 km (sensor/norm) - the amount of fuel consumed per 100 km of mileage according to the sensor readings (calculated as (Consumption * 100 km)/Mileage) / the amount of fuel consumed per 100 km of mileage according to the set norm (the norm is set on the Fuel tab). Idle consumption - the amount of fuel consumed while the monitored object has no speed. Consumption per engine hour, L/h - the amount of fuel consumed per engine hour, calculated as Total consumption/Engine hours.

Liquid Consumption Report (Table) The liquid consumption report (table) displays information on the liquid consumed during a given period of time. This report type is intended for pulse sensors only.
