The report contains: Date - the time period for which the report is built Object - the monitored object for which the corresponding data is shown in the report. Sensor - the sensor name. Start - the date and time the liquid flow started. Stop - the date and time the liquid flow ended. Duration - the duration of the liquid flow. Fuel - the amount of fuel consumed.

Liquids Report This report type presents information as a chart showing changes in speed and liquid levels. Refuels and fuel drains are marked with distinctive icons; click them to see additional information. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the chart is built. Date - the time period for which the chart is built. Balance at start, L - the amount of fuel in the tank at the beginning of the specified date. Balance at end, L - the amount of fuel in the tank at the end of the specified date. Refueled, L - the amount of fuel refueled on the specified date.

The fuel cards report displays data as a table with the number of the fuel card linked to the Object, the refueling date, the gas station number, the type and amount of fuel, as well as the price (with discount), the amount (with discount) and the card balance. When this report type is selected, the breakdown and time refinement parameters are unavailable for configuration. The report contains: Passenger car/Card - the Object and the number of the card used for refueling. Date - the date and time of refueling. Gas station - the gas station where the refueling took place. Fuel - the name of the fuel that was refueled. Operation - the operation performed using the fuel card. Quantity - the amount of fuel refueled. Refuel by sensor - the amount of fuel refueled according to the fuel sensor readings (if a fuel sensor is installed Price/Price with discount - the price of fuel per liter/the price of fuel per liter with the discount applied (if any). Amount/Amount with discount - the total price of the refueling/with the discount applied (if any).

The fuel cards report displays data as a table with the number of the fuel card linked to the Object, the refueling date, the gas station number, the type and amount of fuel, as well as the price (with discount), the amount (with discount) and the card balance. When this report type is selected, the breakdown and time refinement parameters are unavailable for configuration. The report contains: Vehicle number/Card number - the Object and the number of the card used for refueling. Date - the date and time of refueling. Location - the place where the Object was refueled. Gas station - the gas station where the refueling took place. Match - the status shown when the refueled fuel is displayed correctly by the sensor and the fuel volume matches its transaction. Fuel - the name of the fuel that was refueled. Operation - the operation performed using the fuel card. Quantity - the amount of fuel refueled. Refuel by sensor - the amount of fuel refueled according to the fuel sensor readings (if a fuel sensor is installed). Report color code legend (by what percentage one number exceeds the other). less than or equal to 3% - green, less than or equal to 5% - blue. less than or equal to 7% - orange, more than 7% - red. Price - the price of fuel per liter/the price of fuel per liter. Percentage - the percentage of discrepancy between the amount of fuel refueled at the gas station and the amount of fuel according to the sensor. Amount/Amount with discount - the total price of the refueling/with the discount applied (if any). Total value of refuels from the sensor . Additional notes on the report. This report has an important column, “Match”. In it you can see whether the gas station coordinates and the Object s refueling time match or not. If the Object was indeed refueled at the gas station, the report shows matching coordinates and the corresponding status. If the coordinates do not match, you can correct them by clicking Transactions, selecting the required transaction, and then selecting the “Change” or “Add gas station” option under the map. Even if the report has already shown a mismatch, you can go back to the previous period, change the location and refresh the report. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

A fuel pump report for refueling accounting. The report contains: Pump - the number of pumps Nozzle - the number of nozzles**.** Fuel - the fuel type. Total volumes - the total volumes in liters at the start. Total volumes - the total volumes in liters at the end. Total volumes difference - the difference in total volumes in liters. Total dispensed volume - the total dispensed volume in liters. Total amounts at start - the start of the total amounts. Total amounts at end - the end of the total amounts. Total amount difference - the difference in total amounts**.** Total dispensed amount - the total amount. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report displays information on the state of fuel consumption over a period of time. The report contains: No. - the sequence number of the monitored object in the report. Vehicle - the monitored object for which the reconciliation information is provided. Model - the model of the monitored object. Vehicle number - the license plate number of the monitored object. Distance - the monitored object s mileage values at the start and end of the period for which the report is built. Period - the mileage for the period for which the report is built. Since the beginning of the year - the mileage since the beginning of the year. Engine hours - the number of engine hours of the monitored object. Period - the number of engine hours for the period for which the report is built. Since the beginning of the year - the number of engine hours since the beginning of the year. Consumption norm, L - the fuel consumption norm of the monitored object (the norm is set on the Fuel tab). Summer - the fuel consumption norm in summer. Winter - the fuel consumption norm in winter. Fuel card - the fuel cards of the monitored objects. Consumption (L) - the consumption of fuel of various grades. Fuel supplier - the fuel card suppliers. Distance - the monitored object s mileage values at the start and end of the period for which the report is built. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Fuel Movement Report This report is used to account for fuel at the start of the day and at the end of the day. The report contains: Vehicle - the monitored object; Start - the time and date the vehicle started moving. Fuel at start of refueling (L) - the fuel level at the start of the day; Refuel (L) - the refuel in liters; Fuel after refueling (L) - the fuel level at the end of the day. Stop - the time and date the vehicle stopped moving. Address - the address where the refueling took place. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Fuel Report (Norm) This report type contains information on fuel consumption calculated by the norm. Consumption is calculated as the norm multiplied by the mileage. The norm is set on the Fuel tab. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the corresponding information is displayed. Date - the time period for which the corresponding information is displayed. Fuel type - the fuel type of the monitored object. Norm calculation type - the monitored object s mileage on the specified date. Norm - the fuel consumption norm of the specified monitored object. Fuel consumption - the amount of fuel consumed by the monitored object on the specified date. Mileage - the mileage of the specified monitored objects on the specified date. Engine hours - the number of engine hours on the specified date. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Fuel Report (by Trips) The fuel report (by trips) displays fuel indicators for the duration of a trip. The report contains: Date - the date of the trip. Vehicle number - the number of the monitored object. Distance, km - the monitored object s mileage during the specified trip. Total time - the duration of the specified trip. Start - the place where the specified trip started. Stop - the place where the specified trip ended. Fuel consumption - the amount of fuel consumed by the monitored object during the specified trip. Refueled - the amount of fuel refueled during the trip. Drained - the amount of fuel removed during the trip. Average km/L - the distance the monitored object covered on one liter of fuel. Average L/100 km - the average fuel consumption per 100 km during the trip. Average L/h - the average fuel consumption per hour of the trip. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Fuel Summary Report This report type displays summary information on fuel consumption for the specified period. Fuel data is generated from the fuel sensor readings. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the corresponding data is displayed. Date - the date for which the corresponding data is displayed. Distance, km - the monitored object s mileage on the specified date. Balance at start, L - the amount of fuel in the tank at the beginning of the specified date. Balance at end, L - the amount of fuel in the tank at the end of the specified date. Refueled, L - the amount of fuel refueled on the specified date. Drained, L - the amount of fuel drained on the specified date. Consumption, L - the amount of fuel consumed on the specified date. Average consumption, L/100 km - the amount of fuel consumed per 100 km of mileage, calculated as (Consumption * 100 km)/Mileage. Engine hours - the number of engine hours on the specified date. Average consumption, L/h - the amount of fuel consumed per engine hour, calculated as Consumption/Engine hours. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report shows how speed and fuel level changed over the selected period. Use it to control fuel consumption and track refuels and fuel drains. The report shows: Object — the vehicle for which the chart is built Date — the selected time period Distance, km — how many kilometers the Object traveled during this period Balance at start, L — how much fuel was in the tank at the start of the period Refueled, L — how much fuel was refueled during this period Balance at end, L — how much fuel remained in the tank at the end of the period Drained, L — how much fuel was drained during this period Total consumption, L — how much fuel was consumed in total during the period Consumption, L/100 km (sensor/norm) — fuel consumption per 100 km according to the sensor data and the set norm (you can set the norm on the “Fuel” tab in the Object settings.) Idle consumption — how much fuel was used while the vehicle was stationary with the engine running Consumption per engine hour, L/h — how much fuel is consumed per hour of engine operation The chart shows changes in speed and fuel level over the selected period: The blue line shows the driving speed (km/h) The purple line shows the fuel level according to the sensor data (L) The blue vertical bars are the periods when the ignition was on Green jerrycan icons mark refueling moments. Hover over or click an icon to see the volume of fuel refueled Red icons with a cross mark fuel drain moments. Hover over or click an icon to see the volume of fuel drained Below the chart there are tables of refuels and fuel drains that help you see when and where they took place, and check the fuel volumes and event addresses. The refuels table shows all refuels for the period. For each refuel it lists: Object — the vehicle Date — the time of refueling Fuel level at start, L — how much fuel was in the tank before refueling Refuel, L — how much fuel was refueled Fuel level at end, L — how much fuel there was after refueling Address — the place where the refueling took place (a link to the map) At the bottom of the table is the total amount of fuel refueled for the period The fuel drains table shows all fuel drain cases. For each fuel drain it lists: Object — the vehicle Date — the time of the fuel drain Fuel level at start, L — how much fuel there was before the drain Drained, L — how much fuel was drained Fuel level at end, L — how much remained after the drain Address — the place where the fuel drain took place (a link to the map) At the bottom of the table is the total amount of fuel drained for the period.

The fuel cards report displays data as a table for analyzing fuel consumption against the specified factory recommendations and the actual fuel consumption during operation of the Object. The report contains: Vehicle number - the number of the monitored object. Average factory consumption - the fuel consumption declared by the vehicle manufacturer. Mileage - the distance over the specified period of time. Consumption - the fuel consumption. Actual fuel consumption - the actual fuel consumption per 100 km. Fuel consumption difference - the difference in fuel consumption, as a percentage.

Refuels This report type displays information about refuels of a monitored object. The report contains: Object - the monitored object that was refueled. Date - the date and time of refueling. Fuel level at start (L) - the fuel level at the start of refueling. Refuel (L) - the amount of fuel added. Fuel level at end (L) - the fuel level after refueling. Address - the address where the refueling took place.

Refuels No. 2 This report displays refuels together with geofences. The report contains: Object - the monitored object; Date - the time and date of refueling; Refuel - how much was refueled (in liters); Mileage - the vehicle s current mileage; Geofence - the geofence in which the refueling took place. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The fuel report sensor / norm displays fuel indicators for the duration of a trip, based on the norm set in the GPS monitoring system. This report contains data on the Object, date, fuel type, average consumption and the difference. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the corresponding data is displayed. Folder - the location of the Object in the system; Date - the date for which the corresponding data is displayed. Fuel type - the fuel type; Fuel consumption - the amount of fuel consumed on the specified date according to the sensor. Norm calculation type - the type value; Average consumption, L/100 km - the amount of fuel consumed per 100 km of mileage, calculated as (Consumption * 100 km)/Mileage. Difference - the difference indicators in liters; Difference, %

The main purpose of the report is to calculate discrepancies in fuel consumption compared with factory figures. PetroApp Monthly - the report is built by month only. The report contains: Mileage - the mileage at the time of the transaction. Transaction - the transaction ID. Fuel price - the cost. Quantity - the volume in liters. Effective mileage (KM) - the total mileage for the period, calculated by the formula Mileage of the last transaction minus Mileage of the first transaction . Effective consumption (Liters) - the sum of all liters from the transactions. Only transactions that are followed by other transactions are included in the report. For example, transactions: 1. 07.03.2021 - 20 liters 2. 08.03.2021 - 30 liters 3. 09.03.2021 - 25 liters 4. 10.03.2021 - 40 liters Only 1, 2, 3 are included in the report. Average factory consumption (L/100KM) - the factory figure. It is taken from the Object settings. Consumption result - the difference as a percentage. Effective consumption Rate (L/100KM) - the calculated consumption per 100 km. The abbreviated PetroApp Monthly report with summary data. For the report to work correctly, also make sure that the tank size matches the vehicle and its fuel consumption.

This section contains reports related to the “Composite Objects” module. They help you control fuel movement and see receipts, consumption and balances across the entire fuel scheme that combines several tanks and sensors. With these reports you can: — track the fuel balance by day — analyze consumption and identify discrepancies between level and flow meter readings — control balances and fuel deliveries across the entire scheme sensors. For the reports to be generated correctly, the related elements and sensors must be configured on the composite object: the main tank, input or output flow meters, additional tanks and the links between them. The set of required sensors depends on the scheme of the particular composite object. Diesel Logbook The “Diesel Logbook” report shows the fuel balance of the selected composite object for the period. The report displays the opening balance, receipts, consumption, dispensing via outputs, discrepancy and closing balance. The report is built for one composite object only. For the calculation to be correct, tanks, flow meters and the links between the elements of the composite object must be configured on the Object. Fuel Movement The “Fuel Movement” report shows fuel movement across a composite object for the selected period. It can be displayed as a table or a chart. In table view, the report shows the fuel balance: opening balance, receipts, consumption, output readings and discrepancy. In chart view, you can view the sensor reading series and fuel level change events. To build the report, select a composite object and the required sensors. If necessary, you can use a breakdown by days and grouping by dates or Objects.

The “Composite Objects” report shows the daily fuel balance across the entire fuel scheme configured in the “Composite Objects” module. It helps you see how much fuel there was at the start of the day, how much was received, how much was consumed and how much remained overall for the composite object. What the report shows Each row of the table corresponds to one day of the scheme s operation and contains: Date — the day for which fuel movement was calculated Fuel at start — the estimated balance at the start of the day Delivery — the volume of fuel received by the composite object during the day Fuel consumption — the actual consumption based on the fuel level in the tanks Consumption by flow meters — the total consumption recorded by the dispensing flow meters Consumption difference — the difference between the consumption by level and the consumption by flow meters Fuel at end — the estimated balance at the end of the day At the bottom of the report there is a total row for the selected period with the total values of delivery, consumption and balances.

The “Diesel Logbook” report shows the fuel balance of the selected composite object for the selected period. Use it to control the opening and closing fuel balance, receipts, consumption, dispensing via outputs and possible discrepancies. The report is built for one composite object only. For the calculation to be correct, tanks, flow meters and the links between the elements of the composite object must be configured on the Object. What the report shows • Start — the fuel balance at the start of the selected period • Receipts — the volume of fuel received by the composite object • Consumption — the volume of fuel consumed during the period • Dispensed via outputs — the volume of fuel dispensed through output elements or flow meters • Discrepancy — the difference between calculated and actual values • Closing balance — the fuel balance at the end of the selected period A screenshot of the report will be added in the next version of the documentation.

The “Fuel Movement” report shows fuel movement across a composite object for the selected period. Use it to analyze receipts, consumption, fuel balances, output readings and fuel level changes based on sensor data. The report can be displayed as a table or a chart. To build the report, select a composite object and the required sensors. If necessary, you can use a breakdown by days and grouping by dates or Objects. What the report shows • Start — the fuel balance at the start of the selected period • Receipts — the volume of fuel received by the composite object • Consumption — the volume of fuel consumed during the period • By outputs — the volume of fuel dispensed through output elements or flow meters • Discrepancy — the difference between calculated and actual values • End — the fuel balance at the end of the selected period • Sensor readings — the values of the selected fuel sensors in chart mode • Fuel level change events — events related to changes in the fuel level A screenshot of the report will be added in the next version of the documentation.

Reports of the “Situation Center ” module help you view the events that occurred in the system during the selected period. They let you understand what happened to Objects, when it happened and whether the event was processed. The reports show who processed an event, when it was done and what comments the operator added.

The “Events” report shows all events recorded by the system during the selected period. It helps you understand what happened, when, and how operators handled these events. The main part of the report is a table. It displays the following fields: Group — the group of Objects the Object belongs to. Object — the monitored object that generated the event Time — the date and time the event occurred Type — the event description (for example, speeding, Alarm → Lane deviation, etc.). Group (on the right) — the event category (for example, Alarms). Status — the event processing state: unprocessed or processed Operator — the system user who processed the event Processing time — the date and time when the operator finished processing the event Comments — additional notes the operator added during processing
This section covers reports related to the Geofences module.

This report displays data on hardware operation within a zone. The report contains: Hardware - the sensor name; Start - the time and date the sensor started operating; End - the time and date the sensor stopped operating; Duration - the operating time; Distance - the monitored object s mileage in km on the specified date; Start location - where operation in the zone started; Stop location - where operation in the zone ended; Driver - the driver s name in the system.

This report displays actions of an Object over a specific period of time. The report contains: Event - the sensor event type; Event start - the time and date the sensor started operating; Event end - the time and date the sensor stopped operating; Duration - the operating time; Distance - the monitored object s mileage in km on the specified date; Address of event start - the event address; Address of event end - the event address at the end;

Geofence Idling Report The geofence idling report is used to monitor idling of monitored objects in geographic zones. It is available when the additional Geofences module is enabled. The report contains: Date - the time period for which the idling table is generated for the specified Object. Object - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated. Geofence - the geographic zone in which idling was recorded. Start - the date and time idling recording started. End - the date and time idling recording ended. Time in geofence - the time the monitored object spent in the specified geofence. Idling setting - the permitted idling time in the geofence (set in the Object settings on the “Geofences” tab, in the idling control field). Idling - the idling time of the monitored object in the geographic zone. Equal to the difference between the start and end of idling minus the permitted idling time. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The trips report is used for monitoring in geographic zones. The report contains data on the trip start and end date, duration, mileage, the zone recorded at the start and at the end, as well as coordinates. The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated. Zone - the geographic zone in which idling was recorded. Start - the date and time the trip started. End - the date and time the trip ended. Duration - the trip duration during the reporting period; Mileage - the distance in km over the specified period of time. Start location - where the trip started in the zone; Stop location - where the trip ended in the zone; Coordinates - coordinates are used to determine a location by latitude and longitude. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Geofences Report The geographic zones report (1) displays data as a table showing the Object name, mileage, time, the message about arrival in or departure from a particular zone, and the duration of stay in the zone at a given moment in time. The report contains: Vehicle - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated. Mileage - the distance traveled at the given moment in time. Start - the start time of the event in the geofence. Stop - the end time of the event in the geofence. Geofence - the geofence name. Duration - the length of time spent in the geofence. Driver - the name of the driver linked to the Object in the system. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Geofences Report No. 2 The geographic zones report 2 displays data as a table showing the Object name, time, the message about arrival (entry) in and departure (exit) from a particular zone, and the duration of stay in the specified zone, with the option of setting a time filter (set in the Object settings on the “Geofences” tab, in the idling control field). The report contains: Object - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated. Date - the time period for which the idling table is generated for the specified Object. Zone - the geographic zone in which idling was recorded. Start - the date and time the monitored object entered the geographic zone. End - the date and time the monitored object exited the geographic zone. Duration - the time the monitored object spent in the geographic zone, equal to the difference between the entry and exit times. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Geofences Report No. 3 Geofences report #3 is used to account for the Object s starting and ending geofences, with additional parameters on mileage and time. The report contains: Date - the date of the event. Vehicle type - the type of vehicle. License plate - the monitored object; Start time - the trip start time; Start zone - the starting geofence; Trip duration - the duration of the trip. Trip distance - the distance traveled during the selected period of time. Arrival time - the time of arrival in the zone; End zone - the ending geofence. Departure time - the time of departure from the zone; Duration in zone - the length of time spent in the zone**;** Drum sensor work - sensor operation**;** Drum sensor duration - the sensor operating duration**;** Drivers - the driver assigned to this monitored object. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Geofences Report No. 4 Geofences report #4 is used to account for time spent in a geofence. It is available when the additional Geofences module is enabled. The report contains: Object - the monitored object; Zone - the zone the Object arrived in; Entry - the time of entering the geofence; Exit - the time of exiting the geofence; Duration - the length of time spent in the geofence. Mileage (km) - the distance traveled. Total - the total values for duration and mileage. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

A brief report on a trip through geofences showing the zone name, start, end and mileage for the specified period. The report contains: License plate - the monitored object; Zone - the zone the Object arrived in; Start - the date and time movement started; Stop - the date and time movement ended; Mileage (km) - the distance traveled. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Geofences Summary Report This report is used to account for geofence visits by Objects. The report contains: Vehicle - the monitored object; Geofence - the geofence in which visits were recorded; First entry - the Object s first entry into the geofence; Last exit - the Object s last exit from the geofence; Number of visits - the number of visits during the specified period of time; Total duration - the total length of time spent in the geofence. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report is used to account for geofence visits by Objects, with trip details. The report contains: Object - the vehicle of the monitored object; Zone - the geofence in which visits were recorded; Start - the Object s first entry into the geofence; End - the Object s last exit from the geofence; Duration - the length of time spent in the geofence. Start location - the zone at the start; Stop location - the zone at the end; Coordinates - coordinates are used to determine a location by latitude and longitude. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report displays data on Objects that are outside geofences during the specified period. What the report shows Vehicle — the vehicle or monitored object Driver — the driver assigned to the vehicle at the time of idling Department — the group the Object belongs to Object type — the type of vehicle (passenger car, truck, trailer, etc.) Start — the date and time idling started Stop — the date and time idling ended Duration — how long the idling lasted (hh:mm:ss) Address — the address of the idling location (according to the geocoder). The value is shown as a hyperlink: clicking it opens a map with the idling point Coordinates — the exact latitude and longitude of the point

The report shows how many kilometers a vehicle drove inside each selected geofence during the specified period, and how long it spent there, both in motion and parked. When building the report, select one or more geofences. The system calculates the mileage, driving time and parking time inside the selected zones for the specified period. You can also use checkboxes to refine the calculation. Movement in geozones This checkbox turns on accounting for movement inside geofences. If the checkbox is selected: — the report counts and displays only the mileage recorded inside the selected geofences — data outside these zones is not counted Outside geofences This checkbox controls the display of mileage outside the selected geofences. If the checkbox is selected: — the system additionally calculates the mileage and time when the Object was outside the selected zones — separate rows with the distance and time outside the zones appear in the report What the report shows Each row is one vehicle in one geofence for the selected period. The report shows the following data: Date — the period for which the indicators are calculated Object — the vehicle for which the report is built Zone — the name of the geofence inside which movement was recorded Mileage (km) — how many kilometers the vehicle drove inside this zone Time — the total time spent in the zone Time in motion — how long the vehicle was moving inside the geofence Parking duration — how long the vehicle stood in the zone without moving At the bottom of the report there is a “Total” row that sums up: — the total mileage across all selected geofences — the total time spent — the total time in motion — the total parking duration

The report displays data on an Object s mileage outside geofences. If an Object did not leave the geofences and has no mileage outside geofences, such mileage values are cut off and are not displayed in the report. The report contains: Object - the monitored object; Duration - the duration of the mileage; Mileage - the mileage in km for the reporting period. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Intersections in Geofences This report displays information on Objects intersecting in geofences. The report contains: Geofence - the geofence name; Quantity - the number of Objects that intersected in the geofence; List of vehicles - the list of Objects that intersected in the geofence; Start - the start time of the intersection in the geofence; Stop - the end time of the intersection in the geofence. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The report contains data on parking in geofences. The report contains: Object - the vehicle of the monitored object; Zone - the zone where parking was recorded; Start - the time and date parking started; Stop - the time and date parking ended; Duration - the parking duration; Address - the idling address; If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report displays information on trips between geofences. The report contains: Direction - the direction of travel between geofences. Number of loads (number of trips) - the number of trips between zones. Trip duration - the duration of a trip from one zone to another.

The report shows vehicle movements between the selected geofences during the specified period. Use it to find out which zone a vehicle left and which zone it arrived in, how long the movement took, what distance was covered and how many stops occurred along the way. Before building the report, you need to select: — the period — one or more vehicles — the geofences whose movements you want to include in the report If the data is split by day, a separate block is generated for each day. The “Total” row shows the totals for the corresponding period. What the report shows Vehicle — the name or number of the monitored object Driver — the driver assigned to the vehicle Start time — the date and time the movement between zones started End time — the date and time the movement between zones ended Zone start — the geofence from which the vehicle started moving Zone end — the geofence in which the vehicle finished moving Number of stops — the number of stops recorded during the movement Travel time — the total duration of movement between zones Idling time — the total duration of idling Stop time — the total duration of stops Distance — the distance traveled by the vehicle between zones Time in zone — how long the vehicle stayed in the geofence Preparing geofences For the report to be generated correctly, create the necessary geofences in the “Geofences” module, then link them to the vehicle in the Object settings and set the type to “Working” . A working geofence is a territory where the vehicle is supposed to be or to perform tasks, for example a warehouse, a construction site, a production site or a section of a route.

A list of the account s geofences with addresses. The report contains: Zone name - the zone name in the system; Zone shape - the shape of the zone; Zone address - the geographic location of the zone; Zone group - the name of the zone group. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report works provided that toll roads are configured in the Geofences module. The report contains: Toll Road Name - the name of the toll road. Entrance Time - the entry time. Entrance Location - the entry location. Exit Time - the exit date and time. Exit Location - the exit location. Price - the price per kilometer. The cost may vary depending on several factors, including the vehicle type, time of day, day of the week and the specific toll road. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
This section contains reports for the Logistics module.

This report compares planned delivery parameters with actual results, letting you identify deviations and improve processes . The report contains: Number - the order number from the Logistics module; Customer - the customer name; Receipt number- the receipt number from the list in the Logistics module; Status - the request status; Group - the customer group; Start address - the starting address of dispatch; End address - the end address. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
Reports related to the Notifications module.

This report informs you of any changes to a monitored object, according to the settings in the Notifications module. The Notifications module provides conditions such as speed notification, ignition event, sensor malfunction and others. The report contains: Object - the monitored vehicle; Driver - the driver assigned to the vehicle; Time - the date and time the notification was received; Notification type - the notification name; Notification name - the name of the notification; Message- the notification message; Latitude - the geographic coordinate that defines the position of a point on the map. Longitude - the geographic coordinate that indicates the position of a point on the map. Location - the location of the notification; Speed - the recorded speed**.** If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The detailed report contains data on drivers, type, date, time and speed at the moment the notification was triggered. The report contains: Driver - the driver assigned to the vehicle; Object - the monitored vehicle; Notification name - the name of the notification; Notification type - the notification name; Message- the notification message; Date - the date of the event; Start time - the date and time of the notification status; End time - the date and time of the notification status; Number of occurrences - the number of notifications; Event value - the value; Speed control - the speed value for the notification; Max speed - the maximum speed recorded in the notification; Duration - the duration. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
Reports related to the PILOT Task Manager module.

The summary report displays data on total mileage by requests. Driver requests are located in the PTM module. The report contains: Date - the date and time the request was created; Vehicle - the monitored object; Folder - the location of the Object in the system; Distance - the distance value for requests and outside requests.
Route Control This section covers reports related to the Routes module.

Bus Routes This report displays information on visits to specified stops (geofences). The report contains: Between geofences - trips between zones; First departure - the time of departure onto the route; Last arrival - the time of arrival from the route; Quantity - the number of visits.

This report displays general information on visits to specified stops. The report contains: Between geofences - trips between zones; First departure - the time of departure onto the route; Last arrival - the time of arrival from the route; Quantity - the number of visits.
This section covers reports related to the Routes module.

This report belongs to the Routes module. After linking an Object to a route, build the Road Maintenance Work Completion report. A recalculation is available for this report. If a route is configured and linked to an Object and the report then turns out to be empty, you will need to recalculate it. If recalculation through the interface does not recalculate the data and resets the recalculation, contact support to have it recalculated. The report contains: License plate (garage number) - the Object in the system**;** Vehicle type - the vehicle type in the system; Start time - the date and time work started; End time- the date and time work ended; Route name - the route name; Route length - the route length; Mileage (Work cycle), km - the work cycle is a parameter showing how long, in km, the machine can work without a break. Area (Work cycle) ㎡ - the total area treated during one work cycle of the machine. Mileage (Idle cycle) km - the distance in km that the vehicle drives without a load. Mileage on other roads, km - the mileage on other roads.

This report belongs to the Routes module. It displays data on the operation of special equipment. The report contains: Vehicle - the Object in the system; Route- the route set for the equipment; Start - the date and time work started; Start address - the address where the equipment started work; End - the date and time work ended; End address - the address where the equipment ended work; Actual duration - the duration value; Reference duration - a standard or normative time value used as a benchmark for comparison and calibration**.** Route length - the length of the route traveled; Distance outside the route - the distance traveled outside the route; Number of violations - the number of violations on the route. For a report built for an Object with a map, when you click a row in the report, the track is highlighted in color.

The Route GPS report helps you monitor the execution of scheduled trips: visits to checkpoints, driving time, trip duration, distance traveled and unplanned stops. The report includes only those routes on which the Object made a trip during the selected period. If there were no trips on a route, the route is not displayed. The report is designed for circular routes consisting of three checkpoints: 1. the starting point — the company premises 2. the intermediate point — the customer s location 3. the end point — the same company premises What the report shows Vehicle No (vehicle number) — the Object number Customer Name (customer name) — the name of the second-to-last checkpoint of the route Actual Start Time (actual start time) — the date and time the trip along the route started Time arrived at customer location (time of arrival at the customer) — the date and time the Object arrived at the second checkpoint of the route End Time (end time) — the date and time the trip finished, when the Object returned to the final checkpoint. For a circular route, the end point is the same as the starting point Actual Route (actual route) — the route along which the trip was made Trip Status (trip status) — the result of the route execution. The status shows whether the driver visited all the planned checkpoints: Finished (completed) — all checkpoints were visited Unfinished (not completed) — one or more checkpoints were not visited or the trip is not yet finished Time In Transit (travel time) — the Object s driving time during the trip Trip Duration (trip duration) — the time from the start to the end of the trip Distance Travelled (distance traveled) — the distance the Object covered during the trip Number of Stops Outside Planned Geofence (number of stops outside planned geofences) — the number of stops made outside the route checkpoints Number of planned stoppage (number of planned stops) — the number of checkpoints provided for by the route Viewing the route on the map To study the Object s movement in more detail, expand the “Map” panel and click the required report row. The map shows data for the selected day: the Object s trips — as lines with arrows showing the direction of travel parking — as P markers the planned route — as a dashed line route checkpoints — as numbered markers If there were several trips during the day, their lines may overlap. A collapsible “Trips” panel appears on the left side of the map. For each trip it lists the start time, date and distance traveled. Click the required trip to keep only its route on the map. Click a checkpoint marker to see the point name the coordinates the address Accounting for parking The map shows all parking events related to the selected day. The last parking event is also counted if it started on the selected day and ended on the next one. For example, if the Object stopped at 17:00 and resumed moving at 09:00 the next day, the time of this parking event is included in Trip Duration (trip duration). Therefore, the duration value can sometimes exceed 24 hours.
This section contains reports for the Service module.

The “Availability Report” shows the availability of vehicles during the selected period, taking registered breakdowns into account. Use it to determine the fleet size, the number of unavailable vehicles, the total downtime and the availability percentage. To build the report, you need to configure the “Service” module. If breakdowns and downtime periods were registered for vehicles, the fleet availability percentage decreases. What the report shows Object or user group — the name of the Object or group for which the indicators are calculated Fleet size report — the total number of vehicles in the group Vehicles Down — the number of vehicles that were unavailable during the selected period Total number of downtime days — the total duration of vehicle unavailability % availability based on breakdowns — the share of time during which vehicles were available for operation, taking registered breakdowns into account

The Fleet Status report displays general information about an Object. The report contains: Make - the make of the Object in the system; Model- the model of the Object in the system**;** Year of manufacture- the year of manufacture of the Object in the system**;** Mileage- the total mileage of the Object; Driver name - the driver s name in the system; Driver change history - the history of drivers during operation; Next maintenance - data on maintenance completion; Comment - additional information.

The inspections report helps you monitor all completed service operations for each vehicle during the selected period. It is convenient for tracking both completed work and scheduled services. When building this report, you can choose which services are displayed: All — all service events: completed and scheduled Completed — the report displays only work that has already been done Scheduled — services that have been assigned but not yet performed The report shows: Which vehicle The service name, for example: oil change, brake check, cleaning When the service was performed Difference in days — how much time has passed since the service The mileage or distance at the time of the service Status — done, completed or pending Condition — one-time or recurring service Next service Costs — separately for parts and labor Comments — additional notes

A maintenance plan is a technical maintenance plan that defines the frequency and scope of inspection, adjustment, lubrication, replacement and repair work on equipment and vehicles. A maintenance plan is necessary to ensure reliable and safe operation of Objects, extend their service life and improve performance, and reduce repair and operating costs. A maintenance plan is drawn up on the basis of technical documentation, norms, standards and recommendations from manufacturers. The report contains: Make - the make of the Object in the system; Model- the model of the Object in the system**;** Year of manufacture- the year of manufacture of the Object in the system**;** Mileage- the total mileage of the Object; Driver name - the driver s name in the system; Average monthly mileage - mileage data for the reporting period; Interval between maintenance, km - the set interval after which scheduled maintenance of the vehicle must be performed**;** Date of last maintenance - the maintenance date; Last maintenance No. - the maintenance number; Date of next maintenance - the date of the next maintenance.

Operating costs are the total expenses associated with keeping equipment and vehicles operational and reliable. Technical characteristics, operating mode, operating conditions and other factors should be taken into account. The report contains: Make - the make of the Object in the system; Model- the model of the Object in the system**;** Year of manufacture- the year of manufacture of the Object in the system**;** Driver name - the driver s name in the system; Mileage- the total mileage of the Object in km; Current mileage- the vehicle s mileage for the reporting period; Maintenance and repair - data on maintenance and work performed; Fuel costs - fuel expenses; Total costs - the total of expenses.

The report contains summary data on service reminders. Reminders are created in the Service module on the Reminders tab. The report contains: Name - the Object name in the system; Object - the Object in the system; Type- the reminder type; Next due from now - the reminder due date; Repeat every - the set repeat value; Notify before - an advance reminder before the main reminder; Status - the status: done, overdue; Current location - the location. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

A service reminder report is a report that informs a customer of the need to carry out maintenance or repair of their equipment or vehicle . A service reminder report can be sent to the customer by mail, e-mail, SMS, messenger or any other convenient method. The report contains: Registration - the Object name in the system; Description - the reminder name; Service type - the types of service; Once every - the number of days of the reminder; Warning period - the number of days of the reminder; SMS notification - the number to which the notification was sent; E-mail notification - the e-mail to which the notification was sent. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The vehicle register is a register of vehicles. The report contains: Vehicle number - the Object in the monitoring system; Make - the make of the Object; Model - the model of the Object; Year of manufacture - the year of manufacture of the Object; Vehicle type - the type of vehicle in the system; Engine number - the engine number; Engine displacement - the engine displacement ; VIN - the VIN of the body; Vehicle license - license details; Vehicle registration certificate issue date - the issue date of the vehicle registration certificate.

The report on overdue services requires a configured Service module (services). The report contains: Account name Vehicle registration number. Mileage before service Service date Next service, km Days overdue Mileage over the allowed limit If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The vehicle usage report is a report that provides data on how and how much a vehicle is used over a certain period of time. The report includes mileage information. The report contains: Object or user group From 2500 km to 4500 km. More than 4500 km. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
This report is intended for the Tachograph module.

A tachograph report is a document that contains information about the driver s work, speed, route, time, and work and rest mode . To get a tachograph report, you will need to: Install a tachograph in the vehicle and connect it to a GPS tracker. Insert the driver card into the tachograph and select the operating mode. Monitor changes in the operating mode and comply with driving and rest time limits. The report contains: Vehicle number - the Object in the system Activity type - the type of the driver s activity Start - the date and time the activity started; End - the date and time the activity ended; Location - the location of the activity; End position - the address of the end of the journey; Duration - information on the duration of activities; Driver - information about drivers. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
Tags This section contains reports for the RFID module.

RFID Groups Report The RFID group report is used to view interactions with tags by group. The report contains: UID - the tag identifier; Name - the tag name; Group - the group the tag is linked to; Quantity - the number of interactions between the Object and the tag; Date - the time when the interaction with the tag took place; Address - the address where the interaction with the tag took place.

RFID Tags Report The report contains: Object - the Object that interacted with the tag; Driver - the Object s driver; Time - the time of interaction with the tag; UID - the tag identifier; Tag Name - the tag name; Group - the group the tag is linked to; Location - the place where the interaction with the tag took place.

This section contains reports for analyzing readings from temperature and humidity sensors installed on vehicles and other monitored objects. They help you track changes in readings, detect when the temperature goes outside the permitted limits and compare sensor data with the Object s location. With these reports you can: — view temperature and humidity readings for the selected period — analyze changes in readings as tables and charts — check that the temperature stays within the permitted range — configure the data display interval — compare readings from several sensors The set of indicators and available parameters depends on the selected report, the installed sensors and the Object settings.

The “Discrete Temperature Report” contains readings from the temperature and humidity sensors of monitored objects at a set time interval. Before building the report, select the reporting period and Objects, then enter a value in the Min. time (sec) field. The Min. time (sec) field defines the interval between the temperature readings shown in the report. The value is specified in seconds. For example: 900 — temperature readings are shown at 15-minute intervals 1800 — temperature readings are shown at 30-minute intervals What the report shows Date — the date and time the reading was recorded Temperature or humidity sensor — the value recorded by the sensor

The “Temperature Report” shows how temperature sensor readings changed over the selected period. A separate chart is built for each day and each monitored object. The horizontal axis shows time, and the vertical axes show temperature and humidity. Sensor readings are shown as lines of different colors, and the horizontal gray lines show the boundaries of the permitted temperature range. When you hover over the chart, a pop-up window appears with the date, time and sensor readings at the selected moment. If you open the map panel and select a point on the chart, the map shows the Object s location at that moment. This way you can trace the relationship between temperature changes and the route. How to configure a temperature sensor Configuring a temperature sensor helps you get accurate data on the condition of equipment or vehicles. Correct sensor configuration and specifying operating ranges helps automatically filter out invalid values so that you see only reliable information. A temperature sensor is added in the same way as any other sensor. For more information on adding sensors, see this article . Here we go through the parameters you need to specify for a temperature sensor so that reports are built correctly. To configure a temperature sensor: 1. Add a sensor 2. Specify the name and description 3. In the drop-down list, select the sensor type 4. Specify the data field. Select which parameter to take the data from (for example, engine_temp). It is important to select exactly the field in which the system receives temperature values. 5. Set the minimum and maximum threshold Configure the sensor s operating range — the permitted value limits within which the sensor operates normally. If the readings go outside this range, the system records a deviation. On the chart, this range is highlighted with gray lines, so you can immediately see when the temperature was within the norm. 6. Configure the minimum and maximum value filter Set the minimum and maximum values so that the system ignores erroneous data (for example, if the sensor returned an error or an invalid value). Such values are automatically excluded from reports.

The “Temperature Report No. 2” contains temperature sensor readings for the selected period. Use it to track temperature changes, check that the temperature stays within the permitted range, and determine the Object s location and speed at the moment the reading was recorded. What the report shows Object — the name of the monitored object for which the report was generated Date — the date and time the temperature reading was recorded Event — the event associated with the recorded reading Temperature — the temperature value according to the sensor data Temperature Name — the name of the temperature sensor Temperature Status — the status of the recorded temperature value Temperature High — the upper limit of the permitted temperature range Temperature Low — the lower limit of the permitted temperature range Location — the Object s coordinates at the moment the reading was recorded Speed — the Object s driving speed at the moment the reading was recorded Location — the Object s address at the moment the reading was recorded

The “Temperature Report No. 3” contains readings from the temperature and humidity sensors configured on Objects for the selected period. What the report shows Object — the name of the monitored object Date — the date and time the reading was recorded Temperature or humidity sensor — the value recorded by the sensor

The “Temperature Interval Report” contains temperature and humidity sensor readings for the selected period. Use it to track changes in readings and to determine the Object s speed and location at the moment they were recorded. The report can be built only for one Object, for a period of no more than one day and with an interval of less than 900 seconds. What the report shows Object — the name of the monitored object Date and time — the date and time the readings were recorded Speed — the Object s driving speed at the moment the readings were recorded Location — the Object s address at the moment the readings were recorded Temperature — the value received from the temperature sensor Humidity — the value received from the humidity sensor
Violations Control This section covers reports related to the Violations Control module.

Speeding Report The speeding report displays speeding data as a table showing the Object, date, time, distance, the limit value and the speed excess (max. speed), and the amount of fuel used. The report contains: Date - the time period for which the data is displayed. Object - the monitored object for which the data is displayed. Date and Time - the date and time when speeding was recorded. Address - the address of the monitored object where speeding was recorded. Coordinates - the latitude and longitude of the GPS coordinates on Google Maps. Duration - the time during which the monitored object exceeded the speed limit. Distance, km - the distance over which the monitored object exceeded the speed limit. Speed control, km/h - the maximum permitted speed (set in the Object settings). Excess - by how much the speed limit was exceeded. Max. speed - the maximum recorded speed. Fuel consumption - the average fuel consumption per kilometer. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Speeding Report No. 2 This report is used to account for speeding by Objects and the drivers linked to them. The report contains: Object - the monitored object; Driver - the driver linked to the Object; Date and time - the date and time of the violation; Address - the address of the violation; Duration (s) - the duration of the violation in seconds; Distance - the distance traveled while violating the speed limit; Speed control - the speed limit set for the Object; Excess - by how much the limit was exceeded; Max. Speed - the Object s maximum speed at the time of the violation. Precent - the speed limit excess expressed as a percentage. Fuel consumption (by norm) - the average fuel consumption per kilometer. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Speed Limit Violation Report The summary report displays data on violations. The report contains: Vehicle - the monitored object; Driver - the driver assigned to this Object during the trip. Time - the time and date of the event; Duration - the duration of the event in seconds; Distance - the distance traveled while speeding, in km; Speed control - the speed limit that was exceeded; Max. speed - the Object s speed at the time of speeding; Speed excess - by how much the speed limit was exceeded; Percentage - by how much the speed limit was exceeded, as a percentage; Location - the place where speeding occurred. Road type - the road type. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Speed Limit Violation Report No. 2 This report displays speed limit violations together with the drivers who were linked to the Object. The report contains: Object - the monitored object; Driver - the driver assigned to the Object; Time - the time and date of the violation; Duration - the duration of the violation; Distance (km) - the distance traveled while speeding; Speed control (km/h) - the speed limit that was exceeded; Speed excess - by how much the limit was exceeded; Max. speed - the Object s maximum speed; Location - the place of the violation. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report displays data on violations. The report contains: Object - the monitored object in the system; Time - the time and date of the violation; Duration - the duration of the violation**;** Distance (km) - the distance traveled by the Object in km; Speed control (km/h) - the speed limit that was exceeded; Speed excess - by how much the limit was exceeded; Max. speed - the Object s maximum speed; Location - the place of the violation. Road type - defines the characteristics and functions of the road surface that affect vehicle driving conditions. The types are highways, expressways and non-expressway roads. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The report on speed violations in geofences and on roads helps you monitor where and when vehicles exceeded the speed limit, both on ordinary roads and inside geofences (for example, on the territory of a warehouse, a construction site or in a particular district). This report combines data from two modules: “Violations Control” and “Geofences”. As a result, you see all cases of speeding both on ordinary roads and inside the specified geofences in one common report. When building the report, select the required Object and geofence to see all cases of speeding. How to set a speed threshold for a geofence You can set a separate speed threshold for each geofence: Open the card of the required Object Go to the “Geofences” tab 3. Set the geofence speed threshold for this Object: Click the required geofence Use the arrows to set the speed limit for this zone Click “Save” If a vehicle is in a geofence, the limit set for that zone is applied. The report shows: A list of all vehicles and drivers that violated the speed limit The date, time and place of each violation The set speed limit and the maximum recorded speed By how many km/h the speed limit was exceeded How long and how many kilometers the vehicle drove while speeding The type of road or geofence where the violation occurred Map links for quickly viewing the location of the violation

The Speed Limit Violation Summary Report shows which vehicles exceeded the speed you set, and when, during the selected period. This report helps you monitor compliance with speed limits. Before using the report, be sure to set the speed threshold for each vehicle: 1. Open the card of the required Object 2. Go to the “Settings” tab 3. In the “Additional” section, enter a value in the “Speed control, km/h” field. For example, if you set 90 km/h, all trips faster than this speed will be considered a violation. If the threshold is not set, speeding will not be recorded, and the report may be empty. Once you have set the speed threshold, the system tracks all trips on its own and flags cases of speeding. The report shows: How many vehicles there are in the group in total How many of them violated the speed limit Speeding penalties — points for each speed limit violation How long the vehicle was on the road while speeding How long the vehicle drove faster than the set threshold The maximum recorded speed The average of the maximum speeds across all trips
Passenger Flow This section contains reports for the Passenger Flow module.

Passenger Flow Statistics This report contains statistics on the number of passengers boarding and alighting, and on revenue. On the infrared map, you can use checkboxes to highlight only boarding or only alighting passengers. The report contains: Trips - the number of trips made; Boarded - the number of passengers who boarded; Alighted - the number of passengers who alighted; Revenue - the revenue received from passengers.

Bus Lines Report The report works together with the Trips module and was created for scheduled and unscheduled stops of a vehicle. The report contains: Trip No. - the number of the trip since the start of the day. Zone entry time - the time at which the vehicle entered the stop zone. Zone exit time - the time at which the vehicle left the stop zone. Zone - the zone between two stops. Passengers carried in this zone - the number of passengers who boarded the bus at the beginning of the zone. Passengers carried from other zones - the number of passengers who boarded the bus at the beginning of previous zones. Plan - the revenue plan for this stop. Amount - the revenue at this stop.

Passenger Flow Report The passenger flow report lets you keep a record of passengers boarding and alighting and of their number inside the bus while it travels along the route. The report contains: Time - the time the door opened. Door - the name of the door (front, rear). Boarded - the number of passengers who boarded. Alighted - the number of passengers who alighted. On board - the number of passengers on board. Stop - the name of the stop. Location - the place where passengers boarded or alighted. Mileage - the distance between the start and end points of the route. Duration - the time from the start to the end of the route. Distance - the distance between the start and end points of the route.

Passenger Flow Report (City Bus) The passenger flow report (city bus) lets you keep a record of passenger flow and fare payments on a bus line with a fixed fare (urban transport). The report contains: Time - the time the door opened. Door - the number of the door through which passengers boarded. Boarded - the number of passengers who boarded. Location - the place where passengers boarded. Price - the fare. Amount - the amount of money in the cash box for passengers boarding at this location (equal to the price multiplied by the number of passengers who boarded). Debug -ts: the event time as a timeStamp, id: the video index in the system. Total amount - the amount of money in the cash box for the day (the selected period of time).

Passenger Flow Report (City Bus No. 2) The passenger flow report (city bus) lets you keep a record of passenger flow and of scheduled and unscheduled stops. The report contains: Lap - the lap the Object makes along the route; Object - the monitored object; Scheduled - indicates whether the stop was scheduled or unscheduled; On route - whether the bus is on the route or not; Date and time - the date and time of the stop; Boarded - the number of passengers who boarded at the stop; Alighted - the number of passengers who alighted at the stop; Stop name - the name of the stop; Coordinates - the coordinates of the stop.

The report contains: Vehicle - the Object in the monitoring system. Boarding - the number of passenger boardings. Alighting - the number of passenger alightings. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

Round Trips Report No. 2 Round Trips Report No. 2 displays information on complete and incomplete trips and on the difference between passengers boarding and alighting along the monitored object s route. A trip is considered complete if all anchor stops were visited (set by selecting the checkbox on the Trips tab). The report contains: Lap - the number of the lap made by the bus; Lap start - the lap start time; Lap end - the lap end time; Duration - the lap duration; Boarded between finish and start - the number of passengers who boarded before the start of a new lap; Alighted at start - the number of passengers who alighted at the beginning of the lap; Boarded at start - the number of passengers who boarded at the beginning of the lap;; Alighted between start and finish - the number of passengers who alighted during the lap; Difference - the difference between the number of passengers who alighted and boarded; Full lap - indicates whether all anchor stops were visited.

Trips Report A report for recording a vehicle s trip. It works together with the Trips module. The report contains: Object - the selected Object; Route number - the route linked to the Object; Route name - the name of the route linked to the Object; Stop coordinates - the coordinates of the Object s stop; Stop name - the name of the stop where the Object stopped; Date - the date when the stop was made; Reference time - reference information on the route time. Stop arrival time - the time the Object arrived; Door opening sensor - indicates whether the door was opened; Boarded - the number of passengers who boarded; Alighted - the number of passengers who alighted. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report is active when the Convenient Route module is enabled. The report contains: Time- the time and date of the trip. Door - the door number. Boarded - the number of passengers. Stop - the stop. Location - the location. Price - the fare. Amount - the price. Convenient Route system data- reading of various types of tickets. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report is active when the Convenient Route module is enabled. The report contains: Vehicle - the monitored object in the system. Carried - the number of passengers Validator data- the number of readings of various ticket types. Difference - the difference. Trips - the number of trips. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report is active when the Convenient Route module is enabled. The report contains: Vehicle - the monitored object in the system. Carried - the number of passengers Validator data- the number of readings of various ticket types. Difference - the difference. Trips - the number of trips. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report is active when the Convenient Route module is enabled. The report is generated by drivers, with the driver s personnel number specified. If no driver is found by the personnel number, the driver field in the report will be empty. Configure an additional driver field in which the personnel number will be stored (at the partner). The report contains: Vehicle - the monitored object in the system. Driver - the driver s name in the system. Video - the video. Validator data - the reader of various ticket types. ASOP total - the total amount. Difference - the number of passengers and the difference in amounts. Trips- the number of trips per shift. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

This report is active when the Convenient Route module is enabled. The report contains: Vehicle- the monitored object in the system. Carried - the number of passengers and the amount. Validator data - the reader of various ticket types. Difference- the number of passengers and the difference in amounts. Trips - the number of trips per shift. If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.

The report is available if the “Accident Detection” module is enabled. It helps you analyze in detail what happened to a vehicle: when and where the incident occurred, how fast the vehicle was moving, from which direction the impact came, and which trips took place during this period. The top part of the report contains the main information about the event: Report period — the dates for which the report was generated License plate (garage number) — the vehicle identifier Crash (Event type) — the event description, in this case an accident Time — the exact time of the incident Device type — the name of the device that sent the data Coordinates — the point on the map where the event occurred (you can open the location on the map). Acceleration graph (Accelerometer Graph) The central part of the report contains a graph showing which forces acted on the vehicle at the moment of the accident: X axis (blue line) — forward/backward motion (acceleration, braking, head-on impact) Y axis (purple line) — right/left motion (turning, side impact) Z axis (green line) — up/down motion (a bump, hitting an obstacle) Red line — the vehicle s speed Sharp spikes or drops on the graph indicate the moment of the collision. Vehicle diagram Next to it is a vehicle model with a red arrow that indicates the direction of the impact during the accident. Trips and parking At the bottom of the report is a list of the vehicle s trips and parking for the selected period. The table shows: Status — moving or parked Start / End — the start and end time of the trip or parking Maximum speed — the highest speed during the trip Duration — how long the trip or parking lasted Distance (km) — the total mileage of this trip Start / Stop — the address where the trip started and ended Coordinates — the exact GPS coordinates After an accident, the device may send “Crash” tags many times. In the report, if more than a minute has passed between such signals, it is considered a new accident event. Therefore, there may be several records for one vehicle in the report. If you click a row with a specific accident, the system tries to load the vehicle s track for that time and show it on the map (the panel at the top). If there is no track data, the map simply does not change.

This section contains reports for the “Counterparties” module, also known as “Sales Representative”. They help you analyze the work of sales representatives and monitor customer visits. The reports show which retail outlets were visited, when the visits took place, and how much time the representative spent with the customer. With the reports you can: — monitor customer visits — see the actual time of visits — analyze the length of work at points — compare the work of different sales representatives

This report helps you see how sales representatives visit customers. It shows which points were visited, exactly when the visits took place, and how much time the representative spent with the customer. With the report you can: — check which customers were visited during the selected period — view the agent s arrival and departure times — assess the duration of visits — compare the work of different sales representatives What the report shows The top part of the report shows: — the period for which the report was generated — the date the report was generated Below is a table. Each row is a separate customer visit. Report fields No. — the row number in the report Customer ID — the customer s internal number in the system Customer name — the name of the retail outlet or customer Start time — when the sales representative arrived at the customer Departure time — when the representative left the customer Duration — how long the visit took Agent — the sales representative who made the visit

The counterparties report shows how a sales representative visited customers during the selected period. It helps you understand which counterparties the agent visited, what time they arrived and left, and how much time they spent at each point. What the report shows The top part of the report shows: — the period for which the report was generated — the date and day of the week — the Object — the sales representative for whom the report is built Below is a table. Each row in the table is a separate counterparty visit. Report fields Counterparty — the name of the customer or retail outlet in the system Start — the time the sales representative arrived at the customer End — the time the representative left the customer Duration — how long the visit took Address — the counterparty s actual address Below the table, summary information is usually shown: Total time — the total time of all visits during the selected period Unique visits — the number of different counterparties visited by the sales representative

The report builder is a tool that lets you create your own reports in the monitoring system to suit your tasks. It helps you configure which data to show, how to display it, and which blocks the report consists of. You configure the report form once, save it, and then reuse it whenever you need the information in a convenient format.
