Access to reports created in the builder is configured through user rights. In the Contract configuration, go to the “Staff and Groups” tab 2. Open the user card — double-click the user 3. On the “Rights” tab, select the checkbox for the report builder rights 4. Click “Save” You can also define which specific reports will be available to a user: 1. On the “Staff and Groups” tab, select the user in the list and click the icon 2. A window with a list of reports opens 3. Select the checkboxes next to the reports you are granting this user access to

The report builder lets you create your own report form with the columns, filters and calculation logic you need. In this article you will learn: How to create a report — step-by-step configuration of the report form How to run a report — running a report from the builder Report grouping — how to combine data by groups Interface overview — what the builder consists of Report configuration — how to configure a report further Import and export — how to transfer reports between accounts How to create a report 1. Go to the “Reports” section 2. Find the “Builder” button 3. Click it — the builder window opens In the builder: 4. Click “Add” 5. Select the report type 6. In the “Name” field, enter the report name 7. In the “Columns” block, click “+” and add the required fields 8. Specify the data, formulas, filters and other column parameters 9. If necessary, fill in the “Configuration” field 10. Click “Save” After saving, the report becomes available in the “Reports” section. Report example For example, you can create an Idle – Summary Table report. Report type: “Summary table” Added columns: Vehicle — the Object for which the report is built Idle time — the idling duration Total number of idles — the number of events Fuel at start — the fuel balance at the start Fuel at end — the fuel balance at the end In the “Configuration” field you can set a filter so that only the data you need appears in the report. For example, only Objects with idling: {"filter":[{"key":"total_idle_events_number","rule":" ","value":0}]} After the report is created and saved in the builder, it becomes available in the “Reports” section. How to run a report 1. Go to the “Reports” section 2. Select an Object (select its checkbox in the list) 3. Select the required report created in the builder 4. Specify the period and additional parameters 5. Click “Build report” The system generates the report according to the specified form. You can do the following with the finished report: — view and analyze it — export it to CSV, Excel, PDF — — print it Report grouping The data of a report created in the builder can be combined into separate blocks using grouping. Depending on the report type, the following options are available: by drivers by dates by Objects by Object groups To configure grouping: 1. Go to the “Reports” section 2. Select a report created in the builder 3. In the “Grouping” field, select the suitable option 4. Select Objects and, if necessary, other data for building the report 5. Click “Build report” For example, with grouping by Object groups, a separate block with the data related to it is generated for each selected group. Builder interface overview On the left is the “Reports” panel with a list of reports that have already been created. It contains the list of created reports and control buttons: The control buttons are also located here: — create a new report — import or export a report — refresh the list On the right is the configuration area for the selected report: Type — the report builder type Name — the report name Total — the main indicator for the summary Sorting — the order in which data is displayed Desc — descending sort Columns — configuration of the report contents Configuration — additional report configuration in JSON format. It lets you control how data is displayed in the report. Report configuration The “Configuration” field is intended for additional report settings. Parameters are specified in JSON format and define how data is processed and displayed. Splitting data by hours To split the data into hourly intervals, specify: {"split": "hour"} When the report is built, the data for each hour is displayed in a separate block. Splitting data by shifts Report data can be split by work shifts. For each shift, the system generates a separate interval and calculates indicators only from the data that belongs to it. To configure the split, specify the start and end time of each shift in the split parameter, for example, { "split": ["08-20", "20-08"] } In this example, two shifts are configured: from 08:00 to 20:00 from 20:00 to 08:00 the next day If the show parameter is not specified, the report displays all configured shifts. Example of a report for all shifts In the example, the “Loader Operation Timeline” report is split into day and night shifts. For each shift, a separate block is displayed with the Object, the start and end time of the interval and the equipment operation indicators. The night shift is displayed as one continuous interval from 20:00 of the current day to 08:00 of the next day. Since the selected report period starts at 00:00, the remaining part of the night shift — from 00:00 to 08:00 — is also displayed at the beginning of the report. Displaying one shift To include only one of the configured shifts in the report, add the show parameter: { "split": ["08-20", "20-08"], "show": 1 } The parameter value corresponds to the shift s sequence number in the list: show: 1 — show the first shift, from 08:00 to 20:00 show: 2 — show the second shift, from 20:00 to 08:00 Example of a report for one shift The example specifies the show: 1 parameter, so the report contains only day shifts from 08:00 to 20:00. A separate block is generated for each day. Night shifts are not displayed in the report. Splitting a shift at midnight By default, the shift from 20:00 to 08:00 is treated as one continuous interval. To split it at the calendar day boundary, add the split_days parameter: { "split": ["08-20", "20-08"], "split_days": 1 } The night shift will be split into two intervals: from 20:00 to 00:00 from 00:00 to 08:00 The day shift remains one block from 08:00 to 20:00. The show parameter is not specified because the report includes both the day and night shifts. All parameters can be used at the same time: { "split": ["08-20", "20-08"], "show": 1, "split_days": 1 } In this example, the report displays only the first shift, and shifts that cross midnight are split by calendar day. Filtering data The configuration lets you define which data should appear in the report. For example, for an Idle – Summary Table report you can add the following columns: Vehicle Idle time Total number of idles Fuel at start Fuel at end To include in the report only Objects for which at least one idle was registered, specify: {"filter":[{"key":"total_idle_events_number","rule":" ","value":0}]} As a result, rows in which the value of the “Total number of idles” field is zero are not displayed. Merging rows To merge several rows within one split period into a summary row, specify: {"merge": true} The merged row shows the values of the configured columns, and the intermediate rows are hidden. Configure the columns that should be included in the report and save the changes. Example of merging rows In the example, the report is grouped by drivers and split by day. A separate block is created for each driver, and their data for each day is merged into one row. The row shows the vehicle, the date, the start time of the first trip and the end time of the last trip, the total driving and idling time, and the total mileage for the day. Importing and exporting reports Reports from the builder can be transferred between accounts. To do this, use the “Export” and “Import” buttons How to export a report 1. Click “Export” 2. Select a location on your device 3. Save the file How to import a report 1. Click “Import” 2. In the window that opens, if necessary, turn on the Remove existing reports option if you need to delete existing reports in the builder 3. Select the report file 4. Click “Import” The report will be uploaded to the account.

When creating a report, you first select the report builder type. It determines: — which data will be used — which fields will be available in the “Columns” section — what the final report will look like Available report types The following types are available in the system: Summary table — summary data: totals, sums, the number of events and other aggregated indicators Work — the activity of an Object or sensors during the selected period Eco events — events related to economical and uneconomical driving and fuel consumption Chart — data visualization as charts Trips table — a list of trips with parameters: time, mileage, start and end Geofences table — geofence data: entries, exits, time spent Current state — the state of the Object at the moment the report is generated Sensor operation — sensor operation data for the period Sensor events — triggers, state changes and threshold events Connection loss — information on connection outages Notifications — a list of system notifications Cards — data on fuel cards and transactions Driver behavior — events related to driving style Fleet summary — general information on all Objects RFID tags — RFID data Refuel and fuel drain events — fuel operations PTM — specialized reports for the PTM module How report data is generated 1. You select the report type 2. The system loads the categories and fields available for it 3. In the “Columns” section, you select the data you need 4. The report displays only the selected columns The set of available columns depends on the selected report type The builder has: universal (basic) fields — available in most report types specialized categories — appear only for certain types Example 1. The “Current state” type Data on the current state of a vehicle is available for this type. In addition to the basic data (for example, make, model, speed), a “Services” category appears, where you can add maintenance fields: Last TO motohours — engine hours at the last maintenance Next TO motohours — engine hours at the next maintenance Mh until next TO — engine hours until the next maintenance Last TO date — the date of the last maintenance Last TO number — the number of the last maintenance Next TO date — the date of the next maintenance Last TO mileage — the mileage at the last maintenance These fields help you monitor the current state and maintenance of a vehicle. Example 2. The “Cards” type Data on fuel cards and transactions is available for the “Cards” type. A CardTransactions category appears in the columns, where you can select, for example: Transaction Type — the operation type Transaction Location — the location Transaction Time — the time Card number — the card number Distance Previous-Current — the distance between values Current — the current value Transaction Amount — the amount This type is used to analyze card operations. Examples of report types The builder offers several report types, each solving its own task. Below are a brief description and examples to make it easier to find your way. Summary table A summary table helps you get summary data on Objects for the selected period. You configure: which columns will be in the report which indicator to use for the total how to sort the data When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the order of rows Total — the main indicator for the summary Desc — descending sort Columns — which data to show Configuration — additional settings An example of a report built from the builder The “Total” field sets the main indicator on which the report is built. The “Sorting” field determines the order of rows. For example, if you select sorting by Vehicle, the rows in the finished report will be sorted by vehicle. With Desc enabled, the data is sorted in descending order. Work The “Work” report shows the activity of Objects or drivers during a period. With this report you can see: — when the event occurred — on which Object — where it was recorded — the parameter values The report can include the values of discrete, two-state and multi-state sensors. The required sensor is selected by the label assigned to it when configuring the column. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters The example in the screenshot creates an Overspeed CAN general report — a speeding report based on CAN data. A filter is set in the “Configuration” field — the report will include only events where the sensor value is greater than 85. {"filter": [ { "key": "sensor", "rule": " ", "value": 85 } ]} Chart A chart is a report type that builds a visual representation of data as graphs. It is designed to analyze how indicators change over time: speed, fuel consumption, temperature, mileage, equipment operation and other parameters. You can add several data groups: Speed — a graph of the Object s driving speed ODO — a mileage graph Fuel — fuel level and consumption Temperature — the temperature of various sensors (you can select specific ones). Special sensors — special sensors Hardware — data from hardware Eco Pies — eco events and violations (harsh braking, turns, collisions, unfastened seat belt, etc.). For each group you can: Turn its display on or off. Select specific sensors or event types Configure “Show axis” — whether to display a separate Y axis for this group Configure “Single axle” — use one common Y axis For Eco Pie you can select additional settings: Show per hour — show the number of events per hour Show duration — show the duration of events After the report is saved and built in the “Reports” section, the system displays an interactive chart: The X axis shows time The Y axis shows the values of the selected parameters (there may be several axes) Each parameter is assigned its own line color When you hover over the chart, a tooltip appears with the exact time and the values of all parameters at that point A legend at the bottom of the chart shows which lines correspond to which parameters You can zoom, pan and analyze individual time segments of the chart Eco events The “Eco events” type is used to build reports on events related to: — economical or uneconomical driving style — fuel consumption — the environmental behavior of the vehicle Such a report helps you analyze when and where eco events occurred and what type of event was recorded. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Summarize — the summary mode of the report Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Trips table A trips table is a report type used to view vehicle trips during the selected period. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters After the report is built, the system displays a table with trips for the selected period. Geofences table A geofences table is a report type for analyzing geofence visits and equipment operation inside them. The report can display entries and exits, the length of stay in a zone, sensor operation periods and other related data. When creating a report, configure the following parameters: Name — enter the report name Rows — select how rows are formed: Geofence visits — one row corresponds to one geofence visit Equipment work periods — one row corresponds to a separate operating period of the selected sensor inside a geofence Sorting — select the field by which the data will be ordered Descending (Desc) — turn on descending sort Columns — configure the data that should be displayed in the report Configuration — if necessary, specify additional parameters and filters The set of available data and columns may depend on the selected row formation mode. To build a report using a form from the builder: 1. Go to the “Reports” section 2. Select the report type 3. Specify the required Objects 4. Select the required geofences 5. Set the report period and click “Build report” After that, the system generates a table for the selected geofences. Current state table A current state table is a report type that shows the current state of an Object at the moment the report is built. The example shown displays service data, but depending on the selected report configuration, the set of data may be different. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Sensor operation Sensor operation is a report type that shows data on sensor operation during the selected period. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sensor groups — one or more sensor groups to be used in the report Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters The “Sensor groups” field lets you limit the report to the sensors you need. Sensor events Sensor events is a report type that shows events recorded by sensors: triggers, state changes, reaching threshold values and other events. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sensor groups — one or more sensor groups on which the report will be built Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Connection loss This report type lets you build an extended connection loss report yourself by selecting the columns you need and setting your own filter by outage duration. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Notifications Notifications is a report type used to view events created by the notification system. Such a report helps you analyze, for example: — which notifications were generated — when they occurred — on which Object — where exactly the event was recorded — through which communication channel the notification was sent When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Notifications Type — the notification types to include in the report Filter by — a filter by the channel or delivery method of the notification Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Colors — color display Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Notification type The Notifications Type field lets you select exactly which notification types will be included in the report: Speed Ignition events Ignition operation Sensor events Sensor operation Sensor value change Sensor malfunctions Device problems Temperature Humidity Connection loss Mileage Movement Parking Geofences Fuel level Scheduler RFID tags Composite notifications In this field you can select several notification types. In this case, the report shows all the selected types Delivery method The Filter by field is used to filter notifications by delivery method: SMS — a message to a phone Push (Mobile App) — a notification in the mobile app Email — an e-mail message Alert — a pop-up notification in the interface of the system Webhook — sending data to an external service Command to device — sending a command to the tracker Telegram — a notification via the Telegram bot In the “Columns” block you can configure what information will be displayed in the report, for example, Vehicle — the Object the notification relates to Notification Type — the notification type Notification time — when the event occurred Notification Name — the notification name Notification Location — the place where the notification was recorded After the report is built, the system displays a list of notifications for the selected period. Cards Cards is a report type used to view information on fuel cards and their transactions. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Driver behavior This report type is used to analyze driving manner. With it you can track: — harsh accelerations — harsh braking — speeding — other violations — indicators related to driving safety and economy When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Fleet summary This report type is used to get generalized information on the entire fleet. When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters RFID tags RFID tags is a report type used to view data related to RFID tags. Such a report helps you analyze, for example, — which RFID tags were detected — when the event occurred — where it occurred — which device or Object the record relates to When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters Refuel and fuel drain events Refuel and fuel drain events is a report type used to view fuel operations: Such a report helps you control fuel operations and analyze, for example, — when a refuel or fuel drain occurred — how much fuel was added or drained — where the event occurred — what the fuel values were at the start and at the end When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters PTM This is a specialized report type for data from the PTM module. It is used to view and analyze PTM-related records, for example: — the task number — the customer — planned dates — mileage When creating a report of this type, you can set: Name — the report name Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered Desc — descending sort Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report Configuration — additional parameters and filters

For a report to contain the data you need, you must add and configure columns in the builder. Each column determines what information will be displayed in the report and how it will be processed. To add a column: 1. In the report builder, click the button in the “Columns” block 2. Fill in the parameters of the new column Column parameters 1. Name Enter the column name that will be displayed in the report header. 2. Data Select from the drop-down list the data field that will be used in the column 3. Sensor groups Select the sensor group whose values should be shown in the column. When the report is built, the system automatically displays the values of the sensors from the selected group. Reports support output of the values of discrete, two-state and multi-state sensors. 4. Total Functions This parameter determines how the system calculates the totals at the bottom of the table (in the summary row). Value What it does None The total for the column is not calculated Sum Adds up all values in the column Average Calculates the arithmetic mean (sum ÷ number of Objects) Max. Shows the maximum value in the column Min. Shows the minimum value in the column Formula Lets you set your own calculation formula You can select several functions at once for one column. Example of using totals in a mileage report: CAN mileage — Sum, Max. GPS mileage — Min. CAN mileage at start — Sum CAN mileage at end — Average In the built report, total rows appear at the bottom of the table showing the values calculated according to the selected functions. 5. Units Specify the unit of measurement of the data (km, L, km/h, °C, hours, etc.). 6. Formula Lets you use mathematical expressions, for example, (%odometer_end% - %odometer_begin%) / 100 7. Filter For any column with numeric values you can configure filtering of report rows. In the “Filter” field, specify one of the conditions: X— the value is greater than X X— the value is less than X = X— the value is equal to X For example, if you enter 25 for the “Speed” column, the report will show only events recorded at a speed above 25 km/h. 8. Formatting function Lets you set special formatting of the value (rounding, date conversion, unit conversion, etc.). It is used to bring data to the required form. 9. Hide Select the checkbox if the column is needed only for calculations (for example, for a formula) but should not be shown in the final report. How to delete a column Click the column and click . How to configure the columns table Configure the columns table the way that suits you. Select which columns with parameters to display. 1. In the header of any column, click the arrow . A menu with column settings appears: Sorting data in ascending or descending order Selecting columns to display 2. To configure which columns to show: Click “Columns” — a list of parameters available for display in the table column opens Select the checkboxes next to the parameters you want to see How to use formulas in report columns The report builder has two ways of adding formulas: 1. A formula for an existing field — adding a formula to an already existing data field 2. A standalone formula — creating a new column based on a formula using several fields A formula for an existing field This method is used when you need to modify the data of an already existing field. How to configure: 1. Add a column with an existing data field (for example, “Idle time”). 2. In the “Formula” field, enter the expression to be applied to this field For example, a Fuel Consumption While Driving report with an “Idle time” column. The “Formula” field contains =%te%-%ts% — this expression calculates the difference between the end time (te) and the start time (ts) of the idle A standalone formula This method is used when you need to create a new column based on several data fields. How to configure: 1. Add a new column 2. In the “Data” field, select “Formula” 3. In the “Formula” field, enter an expression using data field identifiers For example, a Fuel Consumption While Driving report with a “Consumption while driving” column: In the “Data” field, Formula is selected The Formula field contains =%fuel%/((%te%-%ts%)/60/60) — this expression calculates fuel consumption per hour: — %fuel% — fuel consumption according to the sensor — (%te%-%ts%)/60/60 — time in hours (the difference between the end and start time of the event, divided by 3600 seconds) After the report is saved, the system automatically calculates the value for each row using the specified formula. For more information on formula syntax, see the separate article .

When you create a report, you first select the report type and then add columns with data. The set of available data depends on the selected report type: 1. You select the report type 2. The system automatically loads the available categories and data fields 3. In the “Columns” section, you add the data you need 4. When the report is built, only the selected columns are displayed Example: the “RFID tags” report type If you select the “RFID tags” type, RFID-related data becomes available. This kind of report helps you analyze: which RFID tags were recorded when the event occurred where it occurred which object or device the record belongs to When you create a report, you specify the main settings: Name: the report name Sorting: the field by which the data is ordered Desc: sort in descending order Columns: the data to be displayed Configuration: additional parameters and filters After that, you can proceed to adding columns: 1. Modules are separate components of the PILOT system, each responsible for specific functions. Thanks to the modular organization, you can: — configure the system for your company s specific tasks — pay only for the features you really need — add new modules depending on your needs How modules are connected Modules are connected by the Contract administrator in the Admin panel . Some modules have their own settings that must be activated correctly. If you have difficulties connecting a module, contact the support service. Module Reports When you enable a module, additional Reports appear to help you analyze operations. You can find them in the “Reports” section.

The “Video” and “CMS” modules let you connect different types of video devices to the system: dash cams, vehicle cameras, and body cameras. They give you access to online streams, archived recordings, and telematics data. The “Video” and “CMS” modules let you connect different types of video devices to the system: dash cams, vehicle cameras, and body cameras. With them you can view online streams and archived recordings, as well as receive telematics data. Mettax cameras can also send driver face recognition results to PILOT. These modules work together: to connect cameras and dash cams correctly, you need to activate both modules.

For dash cams and cameras to work in the system, you need to enable two modules: “Video” and “CMS”. They work together: “CMS” connects the devices and receives the data stream “Video” shows streams, stores the archive, and provides access to the player If you enable only one of them, the connection of cameras and dash cams will be incomplete. Enabling the modules If you have administrator access: 1. Log in to the admin panel 2. Go to the “Contracts” tab 3. Select the contract you need 4. Right-click the contract and select “Edit” 5. Go to the “Modules” tab 6. Select the check boxes next to the “Video” and “CMS” modules After that, the modules will be activated for the selected contract. Configuring CMS 1. Go to the “Module settings” tab 2. Select the “CMS” module 3. Find the “Configs” section; it is empty by default 4. Specify the keys: url: video.pilot-gps.com account: login password: password To get the login and password, contact technical support. For security reasons they are not published in this guide. After that, the CMS module will be configured. When everything is set up, the PILOT system will: receive video online save recordings from dash cams and cameras combine telemetry (speed, location, events).

The PILOT system supports different types of video devices. Each type has its own connection parameters: Howen Server 1 (telematics): Server URL, port 20009 Server 2 (video): video.pilot-gps.com, port 33000 Howen uses a separate key, url_howen, in “Module settings” No password is required to connect. CMS Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com Port: 6608 Cipia Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com Port: 1883 Teltonika DualCam Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com Port: 20233 Hikvision How Hikvision devices are connected depends on the specific model. Some models use the standard connection to the video.pilot-gps.com server. For example, for Hikvision G40: • Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com • Port: 6608 Other Hikvision models that can be connected to PILOT: DS-MCW407 (BWS): a body camera for video and audio with online transmission. AE-MN5043 (DVR): a mobile dash cam with GPS for vehicles. AE-VC583I-IS/P(H): a high-resolution vehicle IP camera (license plate recognition). Different Hikvision models may use different connection parameters. Contact support to find out which ones apply.

On the “Tariffs” tab, you specify the cost of operating the connected hardware. A tariff defines how much it costs to connect and operate each device. Select the tariff you need from the list for each manufacturer and save the settings. To configure tariffs for devices: In the admin panel, go to the “Contracts” tab 2. Select the contract you need 3. Right-click the contract and select “Edit” 4. Go to the “Tariffs” tab 5. Select a suitable tariff for the device 6. Click “Save”

After the administrator has configured the modules “Video” and “CMS” in the admin panel, the user needs to create an object and set up the cameras. Creating an object 1. Log in to the user account 2. Go to the “Main” section 3. Click “Create object” 4. Fill in the data in the object card : Vehicle number or object name Device ID 5. In the “Device type” field, select: CMS, if you have a CMS device Howen, if you have a Howen device or other types 1 — Device type 2 — Template. For CMS, the system already has ready-made global templates (settings for quick connection) Other devices have no templates, so simply select the device type. 6. Click “Save”. The settings are applied and the object appears in the list. Setting up cameras for an object After saving the object, you need to specify how many cameras are connected and how they will work. 1. Open the object card by double-clicking the object in the list 2. Go to the “Video” tab 3. Click “Add camera” 4. Specify: Camera name Device type Channel number If you select the Main stream check box, the camera transmits high-quality video (a sharper picture with more detail), but internet traffic consumption is higher. If you leave the check box cleared, the sub-stream is used: the picture quality is lower, but traffic is used more economically. 5. Click “Save” 6. Repeat for all the cameras you want to add Connecting an additional video device In PILOT you can add an additional video device to an object if you already have a primary device (for example, Teltonika). This is useful, for example, when: Teltonika collects telemetry (speed, tracks, sensors), while CMS or Howen handles video. This way, one object can work with both GPS data and a video stream at the same time. Adding an additional device 1. Open the object card 2. Go to the “Additional IMEI” field and click 3. In the window that opens, click the “Add” button 4. Select the device type from the list 5. When adding the device, you can select parameters: Ignore coordinates Coordinates from the additional video device will not be used, since the primary device already transmits coordinates. Ignore Retrans Data retransmission from the additional device will be disabled so that data is not duplicated and does not interfere with the primary telematics. 6. Click “Save”, and do not forget to also save the changes in the object card.

After you have saved the cameras in the object card, they become available in the system. In the object list, a camera icon is displayed next to the vehicle name: Green camera: the device is active, video is available Gray camera: the device is inactive How to view online video 1. In the object list, click the camera icon 2. A video player with a real-time stream opens The player shows all available camera channels (for example: road, cabin, side or rear views, depending on the hardware). The video displays: the duration of the current online stream • recording date and time • channel number • GPS coordinates: latitude and longitude • driving speed in km/h Streaming time limit For online video, you can set the stream to stop automatically after a specified time. This lets you limit viewing duration and control how long live video runs. To set the limit, click the settings icon in the upper-right corner of the video player. The “Streaming time limit” window opens. In it you can enable automatic stopping and specify the stream duration. To enable automatic stopping, select the “Automatically stop streaming” check box. Then specify: • Duration: how long the stream runs before it stops • Unit: the unit of measurement, for example minutes or hours After setting it up, click “Save”. The video player header will show the duration of the current online stream in the format: Live duration: current time / set limit For example, Live duration: 00:03:15 / 00:30:00 means that the stream has been running for 3 minutes and the set limit is 30 minutes. If automatic stopping is enabled, the system ends the online video after the specified time. Controlling the video player In the player you can use the following functions: Start / Stop: start or stop the stream Sound: adjust the volume or mute it Screenshot: capture the current frame 🔲 Full screen: expand the player to full screen Two-way communication In the upper-right corner of the player there is an intercom icon . With this function you can communicate with the driver in both directions: hear the driver and speak to them.

All recordings and photos from devices are available for viewing in your account, either in the “History” section or on the “Media” tab of the selected object. Media files in “History” In the “History” section you can not only view an object’s tracks but also work with video: watch recordings, download clips, or review recorded violations. 1. In the top panel, go to the “History” section 2. Select the object you need from the list by selecting its check box 3. Specify the time period 4. Click the “Search” button 5. In the search results, select the check boxes next to the track records you want to view 6. A “Media” tab appears in the bottom panel (next to “Events”) The “Media” tab is divided into two parts: Device: recordings stored on the device itself (a dash cam or camera) Storage Server: recordings stored on the server (for example, DMS/ADAS events: seat belt not fastened, fatigue, smoking, and so on) Device tab This tab shows everything that is still stored on the device. How to view a recording: 1. Click the icon next to the recording in the list 2. A player opens with the video for the selected time interval The video shows basic information: channel number date and time vehicle speed and/or coordinates In the player you can use the following functions: Play / Pause: start or pause playback Stop: end playback Seek: move through the recording Screenshot: capture a frame from the video Sound: adjust the volume (if the recording contains audio) Playback speed: slow down or speed up the recording Full screen: expand the player to full screen How to download a video: 1. Click the download button next to the recording 2. A window for downloading the video opens 3. You can download either the entire video or only the segment you need. To select a segment, specify the start and end time in the calendar 3. Click “Start” Wait while the system prepares the file (the device must be turned on and the recording must still be on the memory card). While the file is being prepared, a progress indicator is displayed in the window. It contains: — the amount of data already transferred and the total file size — the completion percentage — the current data transfer speed — the estimated time to completion For example, the value 7.5 MB / 136.3 MB (5.5%) • 266 KB/s • 8 min means that 7.5 MB of 136.3 MB has been transferred, the download is 5.5% complete, the current speed is 266 KB/s, and about 8 minutes remain. 3. Once the file is prepared, you can download it to your computer: click “Save” If the device has already overwritten the video recording, you will not be able to download it. Storage Server tab This tab contains recordings from the server. Safety-related events (DMS and ADAS) are uploaded to the server, for example: the driver was not wearing a seat belt smoking while driving lane departure signs of fatigue A description is stored for each event, for example: “Seat belt not fastened”, “Driver fatigue” How to work with media on the server To view the photo of an event, click the icon . Video is also available for some recordings: just click the play icon . To save a media file (photo or video) to your computer, use the download button . Where violations in Storage Server come from All violations you see on the Storage Server tab are detected by the device itself. When you create an object and apply a global settings template (for example, for CMS devices), a multi-position Alarm sensor appears in the object. The device sends violation codes, and PILOT automatically maps these codes to the sensor’s calibration table of values. The table translates technical codes into clear statuses, for example: talking on the phone unsafe following distance smoking while driving fatigue lane departure and other violations When the driver commits one of these violations, the device sends the code to the system along with a photo or video. A basic set of violation codes is already built into the calibration table, so the main events are recorded right away, with no additional setup. Media files in the object menu The object menu has a separate “Media” tab. To open it: 1. Find the object you need in the list 2. Right-click it 3. In the menu that appears, select “Media” The “Media” tab is divided into two parts: Device: recordings stored on the device itself (a dash cam or camera) Storage Server: recordings stored on the server (for example, recordings of violations) For details on what these sections contain and how to work with video, see above .

The Dashcam section in the main menu lets you watch the cameras of several objects at the same time. For example, you can display images from the cabins of different vehicles on one screen and quickly switch to the camera you need. You can open up to 64 video streams on the panel. The cameras of each object are grouped into a separate block. In this article: Panel interface : the main areas and controls of Dashcam Selecting cameras and building the panel : selecting objects and starting the video streams you need Adjusting the zoom : changing the size of all video blocks Viewing a camera in full screen : enlarging the image and returning to the general grid Controlling the video player : starting and stopping the stream, controlling sound, and taking snapshots Hiding and restoring cameras : temporarily turning off unneeded video streams and reopening them Closing an object’s video block : stopping all streams of the selected object Streaming time limit : automatically stopping viewing after a set time Panel interface On the left is the Camera management area with a list of objects and the cameras connected to them. On the right is the Dashcam workspace, where video blocks are opened. The top of the panel provides: : refreshes the list of objects and cameras : opens the selected cameras on the panel : changes the size of all open video blocks Camera counter : shows the number of open video streams : shows the duration of the current viewing session Streaming time limit: configures automatic stopping of streams Selecting cameras The Camera management list shows all objects with cameras. To see an object’s cameras, expand its row. The connected cameras appear under the object name with their names. Building the panel To open cameras: 1. Go to the Dashcam tab 2. In the Camera management area, expand the folder you need and find the object 3. Expand its row and select the check boxes next to the cameras you want to open You can select individual cameras or all available cameras of the object. 4. Check the number of selected cameras at the top of the panel 5. Click Build dashboard Separate blocks for the selected objects appear in the workspace. Each block shows the selected cameras. The total number of cameras open at the same time cannot exceed 64. If the panel is already built, you do not need to create it again to add another object. Double-click the row of the object you need in the Camera management area. Its cameras are added to the workspace, and previously opened streams continue to run without restarting. Adjusting the zoom With the Zoom slider you can change the size of all open video blocks at once: — zoom out to fit more objects on the screen — zoom in to see the image in more detail Viewing a camera in full screen To take a closer look at the image, double-click the camera you need. It expands to full screen. To return to the general camera grid: — double-click the image again — or press Esc Controlling the video player The main actions are available at the bottom of each video player: Start / Stop: start or stop the stream Sound: adjust the volume or mute it Screenshot: capture the current frame Full screen: expand the player to full screen Hiding a single camera If you do not need the image from a particular camera for a while, you can hide it. To do this, click the × icon in the upper-right corner of the corresponding video stream. After hiding: — the camera is no longer displayed in the block — its active stream stops — the other cameras of the object continue to work — the size and layout of the block do not change; a static area takes the camera’s place. Stopping unneeded video streams helps reduce internet traffic consumption and the load on your computer. Restoring hidden cameras To bring back a hidden camera: 1. Click the settings icon in the object block header 2. Find the camera you need in the list of hidden cameras 3. Select it to start displaying it again To restore all hidden cameras of the object at once, select Show All . If the block has no hidden cameras, the menu displays the message No hidden cameras . Closing an object’s video block To close a video block completely, click the × icon in its header. The block is removed from the workspace, and all its active video streams stop. The cameras of other objects continue to work. Streaming time limit To keep streams from staying on longer than necessary, you can configure them to stop automatically. 1. Click the settings icon on the right 2. The “Streaming time limit” window opens 3. To enable automatic stopping, select the “Automatically stop streaming” check box. Then specify: • Duration: how long the stream runs before it stops • Unit: the unit of measurement, for example minutes or hours 4. Click “Save” After saving, the current viewing time and the set limit are displayed next to Live duration : When the set time runs out, PILOT automatically stops the streams. If you do not need automatic stopping, clear the Automatically stop streaming option and save the settings.

The “Drivers” module is used to work with drivers in the system. With it you can: — create and edit driver cards — assign drivers to vehicles — configure drivers’ access to vehicles — view which vehicles a driver worked on and during which period

To add a new driver, go to the “Drivers” tab in the “Main” section. 1. Click “Add driver” 2. The driver card opens, where you need to fill in the data. The driver card has two tabs: “Main” and “Vehicle” “Main” tab This is where you enter the driver’s personal data: Driver name: full name or the name that will be displayed in the system Date of birth Gender Driving start date Driver’s license: number and expiration date iButton: authentication key (if driver identification is used). For example, the iButton field is used to automatically identify the driver by face ID received from a Mettax camera Email: email address Phone: contact number Group: the group the driver belongs to Description: any additional information For all users: if selected, the driver becomes available to all users of the system Labels: tags for searching and grouping drivers Photo: the driver’s photo. To upload a photo, click the icon under the image. The icon becomes available after the card is saved for the first time. After filling in the data, click “Save”. “Vehicle” tab On this tab you can: — assign the driver to a vehicle — configure access to objects — enable or disable alerts Assigning a driver to a vehicle 1. Select the “Assign driver to vehicle” check box After that, the “Object” and “Date” fields become active. 2. In the “Object” field, select the vehicle the driver will be assigned to 3. Specify the date and time from which the assignment takes effect If a driver is already assigned to a vehicle, they are not unassigned automatically. The system can have several drivers for one vehicle at the same time. This is designed for real-life scenarios, for example, when two drivers work in one vehicle or drivers change by shift or on the road. If you need a vehicle to have only one active driver at all times, enable the Single_Driver configuration in the contract in the admin panel. In this mode, when a new driver is assigned, the previous one is automatically unassigned. The system will not have two active sessions for one vehicle. If the driver uses an iButton, all previous drivers are automatically unassigned when the new driver authorizes. Show history The “Show history” button opens a window with the driver’s work history: — which objects the driver worked on — during which periods the vehicle changed Access to objects The “Access to objects” field lets you select which objects the driver will have access to in the system. If you select objects, access is limited to those specific objects; if you leave the field empty, access is open to all objects. Alerts If you enable the “Send alerts” option, the system sends notifications related to this driver. If you disable the option, such notifications are not sent. Finishing work with the card After configuring all parameters, click “Save” to apply the changes. The “Delete” button removes the driver card from the system completely. “Files” tab After the card is saved for the first time, the “Files” tab appears. You can store the driver’s documents there, for example: — driver’s license — medical certificates — contracts — other files How to add a file 1. Click the button 2. In the window that opens: — enter a description of the file — click “Choose file” and upload a file from your device 3. Click “Save”. The file then appears in the list on the “Files” tab. Working with files To download a file, click it in the “File” column. To delete a file, click the trash icon next to it. After adding or deleting files, do not forget to click “Save” in the driver card to apply the changes.

The “Drivers” tab in the “Main” section is used to manage drivers in the system. Here you can: — work with the driver list — manage the assignment of drivers to vehicles How to work with the driver list All drivers are displayed as a list on the “Drivers” tab. The table shows: Driver name Labels (tags) The vehicle the driver is currently assigned to iButton identification key (if used) Other data, depending on the table column settings How to configure table columns You can customize the driver list: select the columns you need and enable sorting and filters. 1. In the header of any column, click the arrow to open the settings menu 2. The menu offers: — sorting data in ascending or descending order — filtering by the selected column — selecting the columns to display 3. To choose which columns to show: — click “Columns” — select the check boxes next to the parameters you need; the table updates automatically How to open the driver card To open the driver card for viewing or editing: 1. Find the driver you need in the list 2. Double-click the row with the driver’s name The driver card opens in a separate window. Driver groups When you add a driver, you specify the group the driver belongs to. Groups are created on the “Online” tab (these are object groups), but you can also use them to organize drivers. The main actions are at the top of the list: Driver assignment: bulk configuration of driver assignment to vehicles Export drivers: export the list to a file Import drivers: load drivers from a file Add driver: create a new driver Refresh list: refresh the data How to configure driver assignment to vehicles To link drivers to vehicles, open the DriversLink window. To do this, on the “Drivers” tab, click the “Assign driver to object” button at the top of the list. In this window you can: — assign drivers to vehicles — configure access to vehicles by ID / iButton DriversLink lets you not only link a driver and a vehicle but also create an assignment group. Such a group stores: — the list of vehicles — the list of drivers — the selected access mode 1. Select the access mode At the top of the window, select the mode you need: [0] Off ID control is disabled. The vehicle is available without driver identification. [1] Only authorized ID can unlock the vehicle Only assigned drivers can use the vehicle. [2] Any ID can unlock the vehicle Any ID can start driving. The system only records who got behind the wheel. 2. In the “Objects” block, select the check boxes next to the vehicles to which the setting should apply 3. In the “Drivers” block, select the drivers who are allowed access to the selected vehicles. If mode [0] Off is selected, you do not need to select drivers. If mode [1] or [2] is selected, you must assign drivers. 4. Create an assignment group After selecting vehicles and drivers: Click “Save”. In the window that appears, enter a group name and click OK. The group appears in the list on the left. It stores: — the selected access mode — the list of vehicles — the list of drivers For the selected vehicles, the group name appears in the “Group” column. 5. Click the “Save” button at the bottom of the window. The selected settings are then applied to all vehicles in the group.

You can view drivers’ work history in two ways: — through the driver card — through the object menu History in the driver card In the driver card you can see which vehicles the driver worked on and when. How to open the history: 1. In the driver card, go to the “Vehicle” tab 2. Click the “Show history” button In the history window you will see: Period: you can select dates in the calendar and click “Refresh” to see the range you need Object: the vehicle the driver is assigned to Driver: the driver’s name Date and time the assignment started and ended (if the assignment is still active, the “To” field is empty) iButton: the code of the key the driver used (if identification is used) : export the history to a file : reload the data : delete a specific assignment record Driver history through the object menu This method lets you view the driver history for a specific vehicle and manage the list of drivers allowed to work on it. How to open the history: 1. Go to the “Online” tab 2. Select the object you need 3. Right-click the object 4. In the menu that opens, select “Drivers” The DriversLink window opens. The window is divided into two parts: the left shows the history, the right shows the allowed drivers. The left part shows the history of driver assignments to the selected object. In the history you can see: Period: select dates in the calendar and click “Refresh” to show the range you need. Object: the vehicle the driver was assigned to Driver: the driver’s name Date and time the assignment started and ended (if the assignment is still in effect, the “To” field is empty) iButton: the code of the key the driver used (if identification is used) : export the history to a file : reload the data : delete a specific assignment record The right part shows the list of drivers allowed to work on this object. Select the check boxes next to drivers; they will be considered authorized for this vehicle. After selecting, click “Save” to apply the changes.

Mettax cameras can recognize the driver’s face and send the driver’s identifier to PILOT. After successful recognition, PILOT automatically assigns the driver to the object on the same principle as for iButton and RFID tags. This function lets you determine who is operating the vehicle when several drivers use the same object. Preparing drivers on the device First, drivers must be registered on the Mettax device. After registration, the device creates a faceId identifier for each driver. How drivers are added depends on the camera model and settings. If you do not know how to register drivers on the device, contact the specialist who installed or configured the camera. After a driver is registered, the device must: 1. Recognize the driver’s face 2. Send the created faceId to PILOT 3. Send the recognition result in the faceRecogn parameter The faceId identifier is created by the Mettax device. The value received from the device is linked to the card of the corresponding driver in PILOT. Recognition data During a face check, the device sends the following parameters to PILOT: faceId: the driver identifier created on the device faceRecogn: the recognition result alarm: the type of check performed The faceRecogn parameter can take the following values: 1: the face was successfully recognized 0: the check was unsuccessful 2: the face could not be detected 3: the comparison ended with an error For automatic driver assignment, the device must send faceRecogn=1. The camera can send the following check events: alarm=647: periodic driver check alarm=648: driver check when the ignition is turned on Data display in raw points During a face check, the Mettax camera sends the alarm, faceId, and faceRecogn parameters in the object’s raw data. The highlighted row in the example shows the following values: alarm=647; faceId=1; faceRecogn=1; Here: alarm=647: the camera performed a periodic driver check faceId=1: the device sent driver identifier 1 faceRecogn=1: the face was successfully recognized In the rows above, the camera sent: faceId=20210301001; faceRecogn=0; The value faceRecogn=0 shows that the face could not be recognized. In the row with alarm=648, the check was triggered when the ignition was turned on. The value faceRecogn=0 also means the face was not recognized. For automatic driver assignment, the faceId identifier and a successful faceRecogn=1 result must arrive in the same point at the same time. The received faceId value must match the value in the iButton field of the driver card. Setting up the Face ID sensor For PILOT to use the received faceId to identify the driver, you need to create a special sensor with the iButton purpose on the object. 1. Add a new sensor to the object 2. Specify the following parameters: Purpose: iButton Type: Special Name and description Field: for example, faceId Conversion formula: *%faceRecogn%. It multiplies the faceId value by the recognition result. When recognition is successful (faceRecogn=1), the faceId value does not change, and PILOT can match it with the identifier in the driver card. With other values, the formula result does not match the original faceId. Maximum value: a value that allows the faceId identifiers in use to be stored 5. If necessary, enable “Close driver session when ignition is turned off”. After the ignition is turned off, the assigned driver is no longer considered active for the object 6. Save the sensor Checking the formula Before saving the sensor, check the formula on test data. 1. Click “Test” next to the conversion formula 2. In the window that opens, find the faceid and faceRecogn parameters 3. In the faceid parameter, enter a test driver identifier, for example: faceid=20210301001 The value 20210301001 is an example of a faceId created by a Mettax device. 4. Replace the automatically filled-in faceRecogn value with 1: faceRecogn=1. The parameter faceRecogn=1 corresponds to successful face recognition. 5. Click Test If the check is successful, the result should match the faceid value: Success: 20210301001 The formula *%faceRecogn% multiplies faceid by the recognition result. With faceRecogn=1 it returns the original driver identifier. With other values, the formula result does not match the original faceId. The automatically filled-in test values are not device data. Before checking, replace faceRecogn with one of the values supported by the Mettax camera: 0, 1, 2, or 3. Linking Face ID to a driver When a driver is registered, the Mettax device creates a unique faceId identifier for the driver. For PILOT to identify the driver automatically, this identifier must be entered in the driver card. 1. Find out the faceId assigned to the driver by the Mettax device 2. Copy the faceId value 3. Open the card of the corresponding driver in PILOT 4. Go to the “Main” tab 5. Paste the faceId value into the iButton field 6. Save the changes The value in the iButton field must exactly match the faceId identifier sent by the camera. A separate identifier is used for each driver. After successful recognition, the camera sends faceId and faceRecogn=1. PILOT matches the received faceId with the value in the iButton field and assigns the corresponding driver to the object.

LogBook is a portal that provides drivers with all data about their trips, events, and fuel expenses, as well as information about their driving style. Through this portal, drivers can track both business and private trips and receive reports on fuel and toll road expenses.

To connect LogBook, you need to complete two steps: Activate the LogBook module in the admin panel 2. Connect LogBook in the user interface Connecting the LogBook module in the admin panel Log in to the admin panel with your login and password Select the contract to which you are connecting the module Right-click the contract to open the context menu In the menu, select “Edit” In the contract settings window that opens, select the “Module settings” tab 6. Select the drivers module and set the key for it: logbook = 1 7. After adding the key, click “Update” and save the contract settings. Connecting LogBook in the user account interface Go to the user account In the “Main” section, go to the “Drivers” tab 3. Select the driver you need and open the driver card by double-clicking the driver in the list 4. Enable the LogBook module for the selected driver by selecting the LogBook Acces check box 5. Set the login for the driver’s access to the portal 6. Click the “Send to driver” button. An email with a link to access the LogBook portal is sent to the address specified in the driver card. The driver must have a real email address, otherwise they will not be able to receive the email. To set up the password and the driver’s access to the portal correctly, we recommend contacting technical support.

To log in to LogBook: Follow the link: logbook.pilot-gps.com 2. Enter your login credentials: login and password 3. Click Continue . You will then enter the system and can start using all its functions If you need to change your password If you forgot your password or want to change it, follow these steps: 1. Click Reset password 2. Enter your email address and click Reset password again 3. An email with a password reset link is sent to your address 4. Follow the link, enter a new password, repeat it, and click Continue .

After logging in to LogBook, you land on the main page. Let us identify the main interface elements: Left panel with the summary and filters Top panel with the section menu Left panel: filters and summary 1. Trip period At the top of the screen, select the period for which you want to view trips. To do this: Specify the date and time using the calendar icon Click the Refresh button 2. Main information The Main section displays: Timezone – the time zone in which trip times are displayed Driver – the name of the driver whose data is shown Current vehicle – the vehicle number or ID Vehicle – a drop-down list for selecting the vehicle you need if several vehicles are assigned to you 3. Mileage summary The Summary section shows the total mileage for the selected period: Total km – total mileage Business km – kilometers marked as business trips Private km – kilometers marked as private trips 4. Toll roads This section displays information about toll road expenses: Total Toll – total toll road expenses SANRAL / NON-SANRAL – toll roads split by operator type (if applicable) Business Toll – toll road amount for business trips Private Toll – toll road amount for private trips 5. Driver statistics The Driver statistic section displays driving style and safety indicators: Harsh Acceleration – number of hard accelerations Harsh Brakes – number of hard braking events Excess Idling – long stops with the engine running Over Speeding – cases of exceeding the set speed. Max speed – the highest recorded speed Driver score – the overall driving style score as a percentage: the higher it is, the more careful and economical the driving Top panel The main portal sections are at the top of the screen: Trips – a list of all trips for the selected period Events – individual driving events (hard braking, speeding, and so on) Fuel – data on refuels and fuel consumption Tolls – detailed information on each toll section Media – photos or videos associated with trips The upper-right part of the screen contains: Email – the current user Settings – access to account settings Logout – log out of the system

This article explains how to use settings in the LogBook portal. You will be able to: — configure a calendar with days off for working time tracking — go to and view the portal user guide — change your password — view the user’s action history on the portal Setting up days off and holidays So that LogBook correctly identifies trips on days off (for example, marking them as private), you can configure the calendar. Importing a production calendar 1. Go to the Settings section and select Holidays . 2. In the window that opens, select Import to automatically load the calendar for the year you need 3. Enter the following data: Year : specify the year for which you want to load the list of holidays Country code (2 letters) : for example, ZA for South Africa 4. Click Save to save the data Adding a day off manually 1. Open Settings and select Add 2. Enter information about the day off: Date : select the date of the holiday Name : specify the official name of the holiday Local Name : what the holiday is called in your language or in your company Type : the type of holiday (national, regional, corporate, and so on) Launch Year : specify the year from which this holiday is taken into account 3. Click Save User guide If you need information on working with the LogBook portal, you can read the user guide. Changing your password To change your password for logging in to the LogBook portal: 1. In Settings, select Change password 2. Enter a new password and repeat it for confirmation 3. Click Save to save the new password Viewing the action history With the Audit function, you can view the history of actions on the portal. How to view the action history: 1. In the Audit window, select: Start Date: specify the date from which to show events End Date: select the date up to which to show events Driver: select the driver or user whose activity you want to track. 2. Click Show You will then see a list of all actions in the specified period: Date: when the event occurred Driver: who performed the action Login: which account the action was performed under Operation: what exactly was done IP: which IP address the action was performed from Browser: which browser was used to perform the operation

The main portal sections are at the top of the screen: Trips – a list of all trips for the selected period Events – individual driving events Fuel – data on refuels and fuel consumption Tolls – detailed information on each toll section Media – photos or videos associated with trips Trips The “Trips” section displays all of the driver’s trips. Functions in the section: Auto Process – automatically sorts trips into business and private Show current position – displays the object’s location on the map Edit locations – helps you correct or refine the addresses of trip start and end points Reports – creates reports on trips and expenses for the selected period Check boxes Business and Private – use these check boxes to filter trips: show only business trips, only private trips, or all trips Automatic trip processing The Auto Process function helps automatically split trips into business and private. How to set up automatic processing: Click Auto Process in the “Trips” section 2. In the window that appears, select the period to which you want to apply automatic processing: Current Month: if you select this option, the system automatically processes trips for the current calendar month Select date range: if you want to process trips for a specific period, select the dates using the calendar. Specify: Start Date : the date from which to start automatic processing End Date : the date up to which to apply it 3. Specify the standard working hours in the fields: Start Work : specify the time from which trips are considered business trips. For example, 08:00. End Work : specify the time after which trips are considered private. For example, 19:00. All trips that take place between Start Work and End Work are automatically marked as Business Trips before Start Work , after End Work , and on days off (if configured) are automatically classified as Private 4. When all settings are specified, click Save to apply automatic processing Current object position The Show current position function displays the object’s current location on the map. When working with the map, you can use the following tools: Changing the zoom There are several ways to change the map zoom: 1. Buttons on the map toolbar and In the upper-left part of the map there are buttons for quickly zooming in and out. When you click the buttons, the map zooms in or out, but the point that was in the center stays in place. 2. Mouse scroll wheel Scroll the mouse wheel: away from you to zoom in, toward you to zoom out. The cursor indicates which area you want to look at in more detail. 3. Double-click Double-click the left mouse button at any point on the map, and it zooms in right away. Printing the map This function prints the current map view. When you click the print button , four print orientation options are offered: 1. Landscape: the map is printed in horizontal orientation. This orientation is convenient for displaying extended areas or objects arranged horizontally. 2. Portrait: the map is printed in vertical orientation. This format suits areas that are elongated vertically. 3. Auto: the system automatically selects the optimal print orientation depending on the current map view and its proportions. 4. Custom area: select this option if you want to print only a specific area of the map. To do this, select the part of the map you need with the mouse, and it is sent to print. Measuring the distance between points This tool helps you calculate distances between any points on the map. How to use it: Click on the map to mark the first point 2. Click again to mark the second point 3. A line with the distance appears between the points If you need to measure several segments, keep clicking on the map to add new points. The length of each segment is shown next to it. Street view The street view function lets you see panoramic photos of the area. Available viewing options: GSV: panoramic images from Google with high image quality and wide coverage OSC: panoramas created by the user community. They may contain more recent images in some areas To enable street view: 1. Select the check box for this option in the upper-right part of the map 2. Drag the yellow figure on the map to the place you want 3. Select the viewing option you want: GSV or OSC 4. After you select one of the options, the corresponding panorama service opens, where you can view interactive panoramas of the selected area. Traffic view The traffic view function shows current road congestion using color coding: Green: free-flowing traffic Yellow: moderate congestion Red: heavy congestion To enable traffic display, select the check box for this option in the upper-right part of the map. Selecting a map You can choose from several map types to display the area in the LogBook interface. The map type is the base layer of the map image used in the monitoring system to display spatial data. To change the map, click the map selection button . Object tooltip The tooltip appears when you have enabled the Show current position function and clicked an object on the map. It is intended to provide information about the vehicle’s state in real time. Editing locations The Edit locations function lets you refine the addresses of the trip start and end and set the type of these points. How to edit a location: 1. Select a trip from the list in the Trips section 2. Click the Edit locations button 3. Select the check box for what you want to edit: Start Location or End Location Start Location – the address where the trip starts End Location – the address where the trip ends Edit the address. 3. Select Type (the place type): in this field you can specify what kind of place is at the start or end of the trip, for example: Home, Office, Client, 4. If necessary, set Radius . It defines the area around the place (in meters) within which the vehicle is considered to be at the specified point. 5. Click Save to save all changes Reports With the Reports function you can save information about trips for the selected period to PDF or Excel. How to create a report: 1. In the “Trips” section, select the Reports function 2. Click the down arrow to open the format selection menu. 3. Select the file format to save: PDF or Excel Selecting the trip type In the “Trips” section you can manage which trips are shown in the list. To do this, select the check boxes next to the Business or Private types to filter the list display for your tasks. Business – the trip is related to work tasks Private – the trip was personal Filtering by trips How to change the trip type You can change the purpose of any trip: business or private. To change the type: 1. Find the trip you need in the list 2. Click the change type button 3. The trip type is updated; for example, a private trip becomes a business trip How to edit a business trip Extended editing is available for business trips: To open the details, click the edit icon next to the trip you need 2. At the top of the window you will see the trip date and time This form helps you describe the business trip in detail: Reason for trip: select a reason, for example: work, delivery, repair Reason Desc: you can briefly describe the purpose of the trip Contact Name: the person you were traveling to see Contact Details: phone, email, or other contact information. Company Name: the name of the client’s or partner’s organization Reference number: the task number Assign same reason to all end locations: if you select the check box, the selected reason and the entered data are automatically applied to all trips that end at the same point 3. Click Save to apply the changes Events In the Events section you can track events related to trips, such as: — when the object left on a route or returned — when a refuel took place — when speeding occurred, a sensor was triggered, and so on Events can be not only viewed as a list but also displayed directly on the map, which helps you better understand where and under what conditions they occurred. How to view events Go to the Events section. On the left you will see a list of event groups (Battery, Eco Driving, Fillings, Speed violations, and others); these are the available event types 2. Select the events you need using the check boxes, for example, Fillings (refuels), Speed violations, Ignition (ignition on/off). 3. Click the Show button How to view events on the map Select one or more events in the list Click Show on map The selected events appear on the map as icons at the places where they occurred. At the bottom of the map there is a player that you can use to view the route and events that occur during trips. Player To start the player, click In the lower-right corner of the map there is a check box you can select to follow the object on the map. You can also adjust the player speed to speed up or slow down the display of the route and events. If you need to remove the markers from the map, click (Clear map) Fuel The Fuel section displays all fuel-related transactions for the selected vehicle and period. Here you can: see the total fuel expenses for the selected period view fuel card transactions: — refuel date and time — fuel volume — the amount charged for each operation — refuel location (gas station) How to view fuel transactions 1. In the left LogBook panel, select the From / To period and Vehicle 2. Go to the Fuel section 3. Click Refresh to load all fuel operations for the specified period. All transactions are displayed in the list Toll roads The Tolls section displays all transactions for toll road sections for the selected period and vehicle. Here you can see when and where the vehicle drove on toll roads and what amount was charged. Media The Media section is for working with video and photos from the vehicle’s on-board cameras. To search for media files, you can use the filters at the top of the screen: Evidence Type — All – all media files are shown without restriction — Investigate – materials for reviews and investigations (accidents) — Trainable – recordings that can be used to train drivers — Vault – important materials placed in the “archive” that require long-term storage — Custom – custom materials with an arbitrary category Sub Category: select a subcategory to filter by (for example, NTF, FTI, and so on). Description: enter part of the text found in the Description column of the media files After selecting the values you need in the filters, click Refresh to load the list of media matching your parameters. For each media file, the list shows: Date: when the recording was made Group Vehicle: the number or ID of the vehicle the file was received from Driver: who was driving the vehicle at the time of recording Channel: which camera the file came from (front, cabin, and so on) Alarm: the event for which the file was saved (for example, hard braking, speeding, SOS press). Type: the material format Category Description: a brief explanation of what is shown in the recording or why it was made Location: where the recording was made: an address or coordinates on the map

The “Points of interest” module helps you mark places that are important to you on the map. These can be offices, warehouses, service points, parking lots, anything you need to monitor. How to work with the module: • Mark important places on the map with exact GPS coordinates • Use different icons to see the type of object at a glance • Add descriptions to each point • Group points by purpose • Save and load data in Excel Access rights To work with the module, you can configure access rights for each user. This lets you separate employee roles and protect points of interest from unwanted changes. To configure rights: 1. Go to “Contract settings” 2. Open the “Personnel and groups” tab 3. Select the user you need and double-click the user 4. In the user card, go to the “Rights” tab 5.
