Available configuration keys Configuration key Value Example continues_driving Max. continuous driving (min.) continues_driving = 250 max_driving_time Max. driving time between geofences (min.) max_driving_time = 10 (no more than 10 minutes between zones) max_parking_time Max. parking time in a zone (min.) max_parking_time = 60 (no more than one hour of parking in a zone) max_stay_on_route Max. time on a route (min.) max_stay_on_route = 600 (no more than 10 hours on a route) rest_time_day Minimum daytime rest (min.) rest_time_day = 15 (at least 15 minutes of rest during the day) rest_time_night Minimum nighttime rest (min.) rest_time_night = 15 (at least 15 minutes of rest at night) rest_time_full Minimum rest per 24 hours (min.) rest_time_full = 30 (at least 30 minutes of rest per day) works_day Specific days of the week (1–7 Monday–Sunday) works_day = 1,2,3,4,5 work_schedule Work schedule in JSON format, specifying working intervals for weekdays and days off schedule — general schedule template days_of_week — specific days of the week (1–5 — Monday–Friday) with intervals. wknd1, wknd2 — settings for days off (Saturday, Sunday). Intervals are specified in the HH:MM-HH:MM format { "wknd1": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00", "wknd2": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00", "schedule": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00", "days_of_week": { "1": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00", "2": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00", "3": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00", "4": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00", "5": "04:00-19:00, 19:00-04:00" } } In this way, through the contract configuration you centrally set the basic operating rules and save time when creating new objects.

The “Violation control” module automatically tracks speeding by a vehicle. While the vehicle is moving, the system compares its actual speed with the speed allowed on the current road section. If the speed exceeds the allowed value by more than the set threshold, the system registers a speed violation. How to configure violation control 1. Open the object card — double-click the object in the object list 2. Go to the “Violation control” tab Select the “Speed violation” check box to enable speeding control 4. Set a value in the “Allowed speed excess threshold” field If necessary, select the “Send alerts” check box to receive notifications about registered violations 6. Click “Save” After saving, the system starts tracking speeding according to the specified settings. Configuration parameters Speed violations Enables or disables speeding control for the selected object. If the check box is selected, the system tracks the driving speed and records violations according to the specified settings. Allowed speed excess threshold Determines by how much the vehicle s speed must exceed the allowed speed on the road for the system to register a violation. For example, if: the allowed speed on the road section is 80 km/h; the set threshold is 20 km/h, a violation is registered only when the vehicle s speed exceeds 100 km/h. Send alerts If you select this check box, the system sends a notification each time a violation is registered. Data on recorded speed violations is available in the “Events” module Speed limits When detecting speeding, the system uses the speed limits for each road section. By default, this data is taken from the OpenStreetMap (OSM) mapping service. The system stores an allowed speed value for each road type, which is used when calculating violations. If necessary, these values can be changed. To do so, click “Change speed limit values”. A table of speed limits for various road types and vehicle categories opens. The first column shows the road types used by OpenStreetMap. The names are displayed as internal OSM identifiers. For example: AT:rural — rural roads in Austria, DE:urban — urban roads in Germany, bus_guideway — a road intended for bus traffic. For each road type, you can set separate speed limits for different vehicle categories: General — the default value Trucks — for trucks Buses — for buses Passenger cars — for passenger cars If a vehicle category has its own value set, the system uses exactly that value when detecting a violation. How to change a speed limit 1. Click “Change speed limit values” 2. Find the road type you need 3. Double-click the cell with the vehicle category you need 4. Enter the new speed limit value. 5. Click “Save” 6. Close the window and click “Save” in the object card
The logistics module consists of several tabs: Trips Clients Warehouse Cargo type Cargo skills Settings Reports for this module are in the Reports section.
The Trips tab consists of several input elements: Add a new order +. Select a vehicle. Input window Trip list When you click a trip row, the trip is displayed on the map.
Add a client Click + Fill in the fields. Save. Display on the map You can also display geofences on the map by selecting them in the Geofences module.
Add a warehouse Click + Fill in the fields. Save.
Add cargo Click Add + Enter the parameters Save.
Add skills Click + Enter the data Save.

Default value - these parameters set the loading and unloading parameters. Geocoder settings - this setting lets you select the geocoder. Task type setting - in this parameter, select the default task type from the drop-down list. Speed coefficients - this field is used to specify the speed coefficient by day of the week and time.

The recalculation module reprocesses an object s data for a selected period and updates information about trips and geofence visits if settings have changed or information was displayed incompletely. Two types of recalculation are available: Trips — the system regenerates the object s trips Geofences — the system reprocesses data on the object s presence in geofences How to start a recalculation 1. Go to the “Main” section → “Online” tab 2. Find the object you need in the list 3. Right-click it 4. Select “Data recalculation” 5. In the “Recalculation type” field, select which data to update: Trips — the system recalculates the object s trips Geofences — the system reprocesses data related to the object s presence in geofences 6. In the “Number of days” field, specify the recalculation period 7. Click “Start” After the start, the request is queued for processing. Recalculation does not run immediately. Processing time depends on the selected period and the amount of data. The longer the period, the longer the recalculation may take. After processing is complete, the results are available in the recalculation history. How to view the recalculation result To check the status of a recalculation, click “History” in the “Data recalculation” window. A list of all recalculations that were run for the selected object opens. Here you can check the recalculation parameters, its status, and the processing result. The table shows: Object — the object the recalculation was run for Recalculation type — trips or geofences Days — the number of days selected at launch Requested — the date and time the request was sent Processed — the date and time of processing or of the last status update Result — the current status and information about the recalculation If the “Processed” and “Result” fields are not yet filled in, the recalculation may be queued or in progress. Open the history later to check its status. After a trip recalculation, the result may show: Run time — the processing duration in seconds Agents — the number of processed messages from the object Points — the number of processed points Tracks — the number of generated trips Parkings — the number of generated parkings After a geofence recalculation, the result may contain service records, execution time, and the number of processed geofences. This information is used mainly for diagnosing the system. For normal operation, it is enough to make sure the recalculation completed successfully. If the recalculation did not start, finished with an error, or no data appeared after it, contact support.

The “Trailers” module is designed for creating, configuring, and managing trailers used together with monitoring objects. A trailer can be used in two ways: — as an information object — it stores trailer data and can be linked to a vehicle — as a monitoring object — it has its own GPS tracker and sensors and transmits data to the system After a trailer is linked to a vehicle, the system displays them as a single combination and lets you track information about both the tractor unit and the trailer itself. In this article, we will explain how to: — create a trailer — configure trailer parameters — link a trailer to a vehicle — view trailer information on the map and in the object list — work with the link history — delete a trailer How to create a trailer 1. Go to the “Trailers” tab 2. Click the Add button The trailer creation card opens. Fill in the required parameters and click “Save”. Trailer parameters Trailer name — the name under which the trailer is displayed in the system Associated object — select the monitoring object from which the trailer receives location data, sensor states, and other parameters. The associated object is not the vehicle the trailer will be attached to, but the monitoring object whose data relates to this trailer. Type — select the trailer type If the type you need is not in the list, contact technical support to have it added. Width — specify the trailer width and select the unit of measurement: millimeters, centimeters, meters Group — select the group the trailer will belong to RFID — the RFID code transmitted by the vehicle s RFID sensor when a trailer is connected. Using this identifier, the system automatically determines which trailer is connected to the vehicle. Description — additional information about the trailer. Additional parameters Exclusive — determines the order in which trailers are linked. If the parameter is enabled, when this trailer is connected, all other trailers previously linked to the vehicle are automatically unlinked. Use this parameter if only one trailer can be connected to a vehicle at a time. Agro — used together with the agriculture module ( Agro ). Enable this parameter only for objects that work with the agro module functionality. Send alerts — enables sending notifications about events related to this trailer Access to objects Select in the list the objects for which this trailer will be available. If you leave the field empty, the trailer is available to all objects. How to link a trailer You can link a trailer to a vehicle in two ways. Through the trailer card At the bottom of the card, open the “Objects” section. Select with check boxes one or more vehicles to which you need to grant access or link the trailer. To find the object you need, you can use: the filter search with match highlighting — the characters found are highlighted in yellow After selecting the objects, click “Save”. Through the object card 1. Select the object in the list 2. Right-click it 3. In the context menu, select “Trailers” 4. Do one of the following: Link — to connect a trailer Unlink — to disconnect a previously linked trailer. Working with trailers After a trailer is linked: — the object icon on the map changes to a vehicle-with-trailer icon — the name of the connected trailer appears in the “Trailer” column of the object list Information on the map You can view the object s tooltip on the map with information about the trailer. To open the object s tooltip, left-click its icon. If trailer display is enabled in the settings, the object s tooltip shows information about the connected trailer. If there is an associated object, you can view the data coming from the trailer s GPS tracker. To enable trailer display in the tooltip: 1. Go to “Contract settings” 2. Open the “Personalization” tab 3. In the “Tooltip elements” section, select the “Trailer” check box 4. Save the changes Information in the object list To view trailer information in a tooltip, hover over the object in the list. For the tooltip to be displayed in the object list, in “Personalization” select the “Show object tree tooltips” option. Trailer history A link history is available for each trailer. To open the history: 1. Right-click the trailer on the “Trailers” tab 2. Select “Show history” The history shows: the object the trailer was linked to the trailer name the date and time of linking the date and time of unlinking the RFID code To delete a record from the history, click the icon . How to delete a trailer 1. Right-click the trailer on the “Trailers” tab 2. Select “Delete”

The module is designed for resending retransmission data for a specific period. The maximum possible period is no more than 14 days. The module is configured in the admin panel. max_days_resend_data - specifies how many days back data can be resent. This module has no Reports. Bulk retransmission setup is possible through the admin panel. Open the object s context menu. Select the field you need from the list of retransmissions. Editing and resending Retransmission window. Resend the data. Select a period and click add to queue. Additional menu Edit the record. Delete. Resend data - send the data again.

Data retransmission . This is the process of transferring data from one source to another in real time, often through intermediate servers or nodes. Here you can create any number of relays that forward messages from selected objects to other systems. A relay can be paused or resumed at any time. • Open the Online tab. • Open the object s context menu. • Select Relay list . + Start filling in the fields. Host - the host address for retransmitting data over the specified protocol (as an IP address or a domain name). Port - the port to which data is retransmitted over the specified protocol. Format - the retransmission format (select from the drop-down list). External ID - the retransmission identifier of a single monitoring object (the imei block is usually used). Path - when a domain name is used, this field contains additional parameters. USPW - if authentication is required, this field contains the user name and password. Time zone - specifies the time zone in GMT format. Speed control - speed control in km/h. Enabled - the current status. Json conf - a window for adding a configuration. Comment - additional information about the retransmission. Through the admin panel, you can create bulk retransmission for objects. SAW retransmission SAW retransmission is a system used to forward alarm signals and warnings from one device to another. This kind of retransmission ensures reliable delivery of critical notifications, especially in situations where a direct connection may be unreliable or impossible. Activate the module through the Admin panel. • Go to the user interface, to the object menu. Open and fill in the retransmission window.

The “Service” module is designed for managing vehicle maintenance. With the module: — monitor the condition of vehicles — plan maintenance — keep records of tires — record breakdowns and problems — set up reminders about service activities Module structure The module consists of the following tabs: Analytics Services Inspections Directories Downtime Tires The “Service”, “Inspections”, and “Directories” tabs have additional submenus that help you configure the module s functionality in more depth. Go to the articles about the module to understand each tab in detail. Access rights To work with the module, you can flexibly configure access rights for each user. This lets you separate employee roles and protect service data from unwanted changes. To configure the rights: 1. Go to “Contract settings” 2. Open the “Personnel and groups” tab 3. Select the user you need and double-click them 4. In the user card, go to the “Rights” tab 5. Find the “Service” module and select the check boxes for the necessary permissions The administrator can separately configure access to the following sections: • Services • Inspections • Directories (Suppliers, Service types, Works, Parts) • Downtime • Tires For each section, you can set the allowed actions: • Add — can create new records • Edit — can edit existing records • Delete — can delete records You can configure access according to the employee s role: for example, give a manager full access and leave other users with view-only access.

On this tab of the “Service” module, you can: View the list of fleet objects Use the dashboard to view data visually Track reminders and maintenance costs Analyze data for each vehicle Objects The object list shows data for each vehicle: Number of services performed Date of the last maintenance Whether the service is currently active Reminder about the next maintenance Current mileage Mileage until the next service Total maintenance cost Quick jump to the analytics of the object You can customize the display of the object list columns and use filters for convenient searching. How to customize the object list: 1. Click the arrow in the header of any column — a menu appears. 2. In the menu, you can: Sort the data in ascending or descending order Choose which columns to display To choose which columns to show: Click “Columns” — a list of parameters available for display in the list opens Select the check boxes next to the parameters you want to see Use filters to display objects in the list. How to use filters: Set up a filter by object type — select specific types of objects to view, for example, only passenger cars or special equipment 2. Or, for a more precise search, use the “Show filters” button — 3. Filter fields appear in the table header 4. You can use filters with the following conditions: Contains Equals Not equal Empty / Not empty Greater than / Greater than or equal to Less than / Less than or equal to Examples In the “Objects” column, select the “Contains” filter and enter part of the name — all objects with this value are displayed. In the “Last service” column, select the “Equals” filter, enter the date manually or choose it from the calendar — all objects serviced on that day are displayed. To refresh the object list, click the button . Dashboard The dashboard is a screen with visual data in the form of diagrams and charts. How to work with the dashboard: Expand the dashboard to full screen to work with the analytics Find the button Click it — the dashboard opens in full-screen mode, and you can focus only on the charts To exit full-screen mode, click the button 2. To refresh the data on the charts, click the button The dashboard includes a pie chart with the number of service reminder statuses. This chart shows how many vehicles are in each service reminder status: Active Overdue Completed Service needed soon The dashboard also has a chart with maintenance costs. It shows information about the cost of service maintenance by month. Object analytics To view the analytics of a specific object: 1. Find the “Analytics” column in the object list. 2. Click the chart icon You will go to the detailed analytics, where you can calculate: Life cycle estimate Maintenance cost estimate Fuel cost estimate In the analytics of a specific object, you manage the data yourself and customize the analytics to your needs. You can change the parameters at any time and immediately see the updated calculations. Analytics chart The chart shows how the cost of owning the object changes over the years. All data on the chart is calculated based on the values you enter in the sections: Life cycle estimate Maintenance cost estimate Fuel cost estimate When you change these parameters, the chart is updated automatically. What is shown on the chart: Bars show expenses by year: — maintenance costs — fuel costs — planned and actual values The TCO line shows the total cost of ownership of the object for each year The depreciation curve helps you see how the value of the object decreases over time Cost per km shows the average cost of one kilometer of mileage, planned and actual Life cycle estimate Fill in the following fields: Estimated service life (in months) Specify the service life of the object or equipment in months. For example: 60 months for a car. Expected purchase price. This is the price you expected to spend on the object. Disposal cost estimate How much you plan to spend on disposing of or writing off the object at the end of its service life. Estimated annual mileage (in miles) If it is, for example, a car, specify how many miles it travels per year. Actual purchase price The real amount that was spent on the purchase. Estimated residual value How much the object will be worth at the end of its service life. Fuel consumption (l/km) Specify how many liters of fuel are consumed per kilometer. Depreciation method Choose the depreciation calculation method that suits your object: Accelerated or double-declining balance method Writes off the value quickly in the first years. A doubled straight-line depreciation rate is applied to the residual value. For example: A car costs $10,000, service life is 5 years Straight-line rate = 1/5 = 20% Doubled rate = 40% Year 1: 10,000 × 40% = $4,000 Year 2: (10,000 – 4,000) × 40% = $2,400 This method is usually used for assets that lose value quickly or provide more benefit at the beginning of their service life. Sum of years digits A smoother way of writing off value than the accelerated method. First, all years of the service life are summed, then each year s share of this sum is calculated. For example: Service life: 5 years Sum of years: 1+2+3+4+5 = 15 Year 1: 5/15 of the value Year 2: 4/15 Year 3: 3/15 and so on The method is suitable for assets with uneven wear but without a sharp drop in value. Maintenance cost estimate Enter planned and actual values by year. This shows how closely expenses match expectations. Fuel cost estimate Similarly, set the plan and actual for each year.

On the “Services” tab, you can keep records of all service work, and create templates and reminders. Let s see how to work with it: All services All created service records are displayed here. You can: — work with the list of service records — create a new service record — add service objects — add completed works and parts — create a service reminder — add files — use additional functions in a service record Templates Templates help you quickly create standard service records. Here you will learn: — where saved service templates are stored — how to create and apply a template Reminders Keep track of upcoming services and do not miss important dates. You can: — edit reminders — change their status All services All records of completed service maintenance that you have added to the system are displayed here. How to work with the list of service records: Customize the list display: choose which columns and parameters to show in the table Delete unneeded records — click the icon next to the row you need Use the buttons in the upper-right corner: — Show filters — filter fields for the data open — Refresh — refreshes the list of services — Create service — click to add a new service maintenance record How to create a service record 1. Click the “Create service” button 2. In the window that opens, fill in the service information General information: Template — select a template to fill in the fields automatically. To learn how to create a service template, see here Event type — specify whether this maintenance is one-time or recurring Service name — enter the name Supplier — select from the drop-down list. To learn how to add a supplier, see below Maintenance status — mark whether it is completed or not Invoice number — enter a number, for example, an invoice or an internal document number Service type — select from the list Date and time — specify when the maintenance was or will be performed Comment — add an explanation if necessary Service objects Specify which objects are involved in this service. In the “Add objects” section, select one or more objects from the drop-down list. If you added an extra object, delete it with the button . Works How to add a work item: Go to the “Works” section 2. Click the “Add work” button 3. In the window that opens, fill in: Work name Maintenance type — select from the list To add a new type : 1) Click next to the field 2) Enter a name and select a category: service, work, or material 3) Click “Save” — the type appears in the drop-down list Cost and quantity Comment — if needed 4. Select “Finished” if the work is completed 5. Click “Save” The added works appear in the list. The total amount for all works in this service is calculated at the bottom. Parts How to add a part: 1. Go to the “Parts” section 2. Click “Add part” 3. In the window that opens, fill in: Part name Part type — select from the list Supplier or manufacturer — select from the list To add a supplier or manufacturer: 1) Click next to the field 2) Enter the name, phone, email, and address 3) Click “Save” Part code, cost, quantity Comment — if necessary 4. Select “Finished” if the part is installed 5. Click “Save” The added parts appear in the service s parts list. Their total cost is calculated automatically. Creating reminders In the “Reminders” section, set up automatic service reminders. How to create a reminder: 1. Go to the “Reminders” section 2. Click “Add reminder” 3. In the new window, specify: Reminder name Service date Optionally, you can specify: Repeat interval — how often the reminder should repeat How many days before the event to remind — for example, 2 days before Mileage or engine hours Mileage or engine hours interval Reminder delivery method — email and others To receive reminders by email, confirm it in “Privacy” . Reminder text: — specify the reminder subject — what exactly the notification should be about — write a title for your reminder — what will be written at the top of the message — create the reminder text with automatic data substitution. To do this, use variables: %current_time% — current time %reminder_name% — reminder name %current_moto% — current mileage %current_mil% — current mileage in miles %agent_id% — account number %vehicle_name% — vehicle name %driver_name% — driver name These variables are automatically replaced with real data when the message is sent. For example: Scheduled maintenance of %vehicle_name% is set for %current_time% 4. Click “Save” — the reminder is created and appears in the general list In a service record, customize the tables of objects, works, parts, and reminders. Select the parameters that will be displayed in the columns. Adding files You can attach documents and files to a service record to keep all maintenance data in one place. How to add files: 1. Open the service record and go to the “Files” section 2. Click and select a file on your device 3. The file is attached to the record To manage files in a service record: Download a file — click the icon next to the file you need Delete a file — click the icon to remove the file from the record How to finish creating a service After you have filled in the service information, click “Save” in the upper-right corner . The service appears in the general list on the “All services” tab. Additional functions Use the additional functions in the service creation form. Click the three dots in the upper-right corner to: Download — download a file with the service data Print — print the maintenance report Create template — save the current service as a template Delete — delete the service record Templates The “Templates” tab stores all saved service maintenance templates. Templates help you quickly create new service records without filling in all the information again. How to create a template 1. Create a new service maintenance record or open an existing one 2. In the service record, click the three-dot menu and select “Create template” 3. In the new window, enter the template name 4. If you wish, select from the list the make, model, and modification of the vehicle the template will apply to. If the make you need is not in the list, you can add it: click , enter the make name, and click “OK”. 5. Click “Save” — the template appears on the “Templates” tab How to edit a template To change a template: 1. Go to the “Templates” tab 2. Double-click the template you need 3. In the window that appears, edit the name, make, or model of the vehicle 4. Click “Save” How to delete a template To delete a template, click the icon next to the template record in the list. How to apply a template 1. On the “All services” tab, click the “Create service” button 2. In the new record creation window, select the template you need 3. After you select the template, all saved details are automatically added to the record: parts, works, reminders (if they were specified in the template) 4. All that remains is to select the objects and the date and time of the service 5. Click “Save” — the new service record created from the template appears in the service list Reminders The “Reminders” tab displays all created reminders. How to edit a reminder: Double-click the record in the list In the window that opens, change the data If necessary, change the reminder status: Active Overdue Closed 3. Click “Save” To delete a reminder from the list, click in the row you need.

Inspections are a tool for convenient and systematic checks of vehicle condition: — create inspection templates with the questions you need — plan and carry out inspections — record what was checked and in what condition — identify problems in advance to prevent downtime The tab consists of two parts: Forms — create inspection templates Completed — carry out inspections and view the results Forms Here you create inspection templates — blanks with questions that the check will follow. You can create forms for: Scheduled technical inspection Pre-trip check Acceptance inspection Unscheduled check You can have as many forms as you like, one for each case. How to create an inspection form Click the “Create form” button 2. You go to the form creation window. Here you need to fill in two blocks: General information Questions 3. When everything is ready, click the “Save” icon in the upper-right corner To edit an inspection form, double-click the form in the list. A window opens where you can change the general information and questions. To delete a form from the list, click . General information This is the form header. Fill it in as follows: 1. Inspection name — for example, “Pre-trip inspection” 2. Comment — write when and how to use the form. Example: “The inspection is carried out before departure. Pay special attention to the brakes and lighting” 3. Signature — select the check box if you want the inspector (the person carrying out the inspection) to sign the form to certify the inspection. Questions Now let s add the questions the inspection will follow. How to add a question 1. Click “Create question” 2. In the window that opens, fill in: Question title — brief and clear (for example, “Brake operation”) Comment — an explanation of what exactly needs to be checked 3. Configure the additional functions: Add comment — if you need to leave a text comment when answering Allow skip — if the question may be left unanswered Add photo — if you need to attach a photo to the question Photo required — if a photo is required for the answer Button names: For a positive answer (for example, “Yes”, “OK”) For a negative answer (for example, “No”, “Not working”) If skipping is allowed, also specify a name for the skip button (for example, “Skip”) 4. Click “Save” For example, a completed question may look like this As soon as you save the question, it appears in the new inspection form. To edit a question, double-click it. To delete it, click next to the question. When all questions are added, click in the upper-right corner to save the entire form. You can now use this form when carrying out inspections. Example of an inspection form Completed All inspections that have been carried out are displayed here. You can see: Which object was inspected Which form was used Who carried out the inspection When it was carried out How many questions were completed Which ones were skipped To work with completed inspections, use the icons in the list: — delete the inspection record — print the completed inspection form — download the inspection form How to view details Double-click the inspection you need — the completed form opens. Here you can: View all answers If necessary, correct erroneous answers How to carry out an inspection On the “Completed” tab, click “Create inspection” In the window that opens, select: The inspection form (created earlier) The object (vehicle) 3. Click “Continue” — the form with questions opens 4. Answer the questions: Select an answer If necessary, add a photo and a comment 5. Sign the inspection: Use the mouse or a stylus to sign If it did not work, click “Clear” and try again 6. Click “Done” — the inspection appears in the list of completed ones

Directories are a tool similar to a database that you can use when creating service records. Instead of entering the same data manually each time, you save it here once in advance and then simply select it from a list. You can create and store information about: Suppliers and manufacturers Service types Works Parts Suppliers This is where data about parts suppliers or manufacturers is stored. You decide how to use this information — for yourself, for accounting, for contact. How to add a supplier 1. Go to the “Suppliers” tab 2. Click 3. In the window that opens, enter: Company name Phone Email Address 4. Click “Save” — the supplier appears in the general list How to edit or delete a supplier To edit, double-click the record, change the data, and save. To delete, click the icon next to the record. Service types Here you create service maintenance types. How to add a service maintenance type 1. Go to the “Service types” tab 2. Click 3. In the new window: Enter the type name (for example, “Maintenance-2”) Select a category: Service (for example, scheduled maintenance) Work (an action — replacement, repair) Material (consumables, parts) 4. Click “Save” — the service type appears in the general list How to edit or delete Double-click the record to edit it. Click the icon to delete the service type record from the list Works On the “Works” tab, create and store a list of all works that you can quickly select when adding a service record. How to add a work item 1. Go to the “Works” tab 2. Click In the window that opens, fill in: Work name — for example, “Brake pad replacement” Maintenance type — select from those created earlier Cost — specify the price for performing the work Comment — add an explanation if necessary 4. Select the “Finished” check box if the work has already been done 5. Click “Save” How to edit or delete Double-click the work to change it. Click next to the record to delete it. Parts All the parts you have added that are used in maintenance are displayed here. How to add a part 1. Go to the “Parts” tab 2. Click 3. In the new window, enter: Part name — for example, “Oil filter” Maintenance type — select from the list Supplier or manufacturer — select from those added earlier Part code — if available Cost Comment — if necessary 4. Select the “Finished” check box if the part has already been installed 5. Click “Save” How to edit or delete To change, double-click the record in the list. To delete, click in the row of the part you need.

Downtime is the time when a vehicle is temporarily not in use. For example, when it is undergoing maintenance or repair. The “Downtime” tab displays all records of vehicle downtime periods. Working with the downtime list In the upper-right corner of the “Downtime” tab there are buttons for managing the list: Export — export downtime records to a file Import — load downtime records from a file Filter — select records by values in the columns Refresh — reload the data and update the list How to filter records Click “Filter”. Fields appear under the table headers where you can set selection conditions: Object — enter the name or number of the vehicle Start and End — select the date and time Duration — specify the downtime duration Duration for the current year — specify the total duration of downtime Downtime reason — enter text from the reason description You can fill in one or several fields. The table keeps only the records that match all the specified conditions. For example, to find the downtime of a specific vehicle, enter its name or number in the field under the “Object” column. To reset filtering, delete the entered values. How to create a downtime record On the “Downtime” tab, click In the new window: Select the object that is currently in downtime Specify the downtime reason Select the start and end date and time of the downtime using the calendar 3. Click “Save” — the downtime record appears in the general list How to edit or delete a downtime record To edit, double-click the record in the list, change the data, and save. To delete, click the icon next to the record. How downtime is displayed When you create a downtime record for a vehicle because of maintenance, a special icon appears next to the object on the “Online” tab, and its status changes to “Downtime” and is highlighted in yellow. Click the icon to open information about the maintenance period — you immediately see for which period the downtime is scheduled. Object behavior during downtime If the downtime has already started The object status automatically changes to “Downtime”, and it is excluded from the problems and alarms block. This helps avoid overloading operational monitoring with unnecessary events. If the downtime is scheduled for the future Only the icon is displayed, and the object status does not change until the downtime begins. How to add downtime through the object menu 1. Go to the “Online” tab 2. Select the object you need in the list 3. Right-click it to open the context menu 4. Select “Add downtime” After that, the object gets a downtime record and a wrench icon. How to remove downtime 1. Right-click the object 2. In the context menu, select “Delete downtime” 3. Confirm the action

On this tab, track the condition of vehicle tires. Here you monitor pressure and temperature readings and manage information about axles and tires. Tab overview When you open the “Tires” tab, you see three main blocks: Object list All the vehicles you are monitoring are displayed here. You can quickly find the object you need using: 1 — Search for objects in the list. Enter a name or number and the search highlights the result in the list 2 — Filter by object type . Select specific object types to view, for example, only passenger cars or special equipment 3 — Filter in the table header . Use filters with conditions: — Contains — Equals — Not equal — Empty / Not empty — Greater than / Greater than or equal to — Less than / Less than or equal to Axle and tire layout After you click an object in the list, you see its axle and tire layout. This is a visual diagram where you can: Add axles and tires See where and which tire is installed Monitor the condition of each tire Readings chart The chart shows the history of parameters for the selected object: Driving speed Tire temperature Tire pressure On the chart, you can select a date to see how the readings changed over time — this helps you notice overheating or a pressure drop in time.

In this article, we will look at how to configure the axle and tire layout for a selected object. First add axles, then install tires on them. After configuration, the system can display the number of axles and tires, their location, mileage, as well as pressure and temperature readings if sensors are connected to the tires. How to add an axle An axle can be added in two ways: through the axle and tire layout or through the object menu. To add an axle through the layout: 1. Select the object in the list 2. Go to the axle and tire layout 3. Click the “Add axle” button 4. In the window that opens, specify: • Axle name — for example, front axle or rear axle • Location number — the order of the axle in the diagram 5. Click “Save” The new axle appears on the object layout. An axle can also be added through the object menu. To do this, right-click the object in the list and select “Add axle”. The same axle settings window opens. How to add a tire After adding axles, you can install tires. Click the “Add tire” button on the layout 2. In the window that opens, fill in the tire parameters: Tire name Installation date and time — select using the calendar Mileage at installation Threshold mileage — for wear control Installation side — right or left Location number Serial number Pressure and temperature sensors — select from the list of available ones Click the “Save” button — the tire appears on the layout After you have added axles and tires, the following information appears for the object in the list: Number of axles — how many axles are configured for the object Number of tires — the total number of installed tires Tire location — exactly where they are installed (by sides and positions) Pressure — current values from the sensors Temperature — the temperature of each tire Mileage — the mileage of the object and the mileage of each installed tire This data helps you detect deviations, such as pressure drops or overheating, extend tire life, and avoid unscheduled repairs.

Tire templates let you save a ready-made axle and tire layout of one object and apply it to other objects. Use templates if several vehicles have the same axle and wheel configuration. You can open templates from the object menu on the “Tires” tab. To do this, right-click the object and select “Template”. Before creating a template, the object must have axles and tires added. If there is no tire data, the system shows an error message. To create a new template: 1. Open the object menu and select “Templates” 2. In the “Templates” window, click “Create new” 3. Enter the template name 4. If necessary, specify the make, model, and modification 5. Click “Save” The “Name” field is required. The “Make”, “Model”, and “Modification” fields can be left empty. To apply a template to an object: 1. Open the menu of the object you want to apply the template to 2. In the list, select the appropriate template 3. Click “Use” After the template is applied, the system replaces the object s current axle and tire layout with the data from the selected template. If the object already had axles and tires configured, they will be deleted and replaced with data from the template. If a template is no longer needed, select it in the list and click “Delete”.

The tire history shows when and where a tire was installed on or removed from an object. To open the history, right-click the object on the “Tires” tab and select “History”. The history shows: • Installation time — the date and time the tire was installed • Uninstall Time — the date and time the tire was removed • Axle Position — the axle position • Tire Position — the tire position • Mileage — the mileage at the time of installation or removal

The “Events” module helps you find events related to vehicles and other monitoring objects and view the places where they occurred on the map. With the module, you can: — find events for a selected period — view speeding, downtime, refuels, fuel drains, service reminders, and other events — select only the objects and event types you need — see the location of an event on the map — view notifications In this article you will learn how to: — find events for a selected period — open and view the events found — change how the event list is displayed — view where events occurred on the map — change the display color of event types How to find events 1. In the top menu, open the “Events” section 2. In the “From date” and “To date” fields, specify the period for which you need to find events 3. In the left part of the window, select monitoring objects 4. In the right part, select the event types you want to view You can select: — an entire event group, for example, “Notifications” or “Events” — individual events within a group, for example, “Speed”, “Downtime”, or “Inspections” To expand or collapse an event group, click the arrow next to its name . 5. Click “Search” After the search is completed, the events found appear in the list. How to open the event list The results are grouped first by object and then by event type. The number in parentheses shows the number of records found. To open the event list, expand in sequence: 1. The monitoring object 2. The event type you need For each event, the following are displayed: — the event name — the date and time of registration — a color label How to change the list view By default, the events found are grouped by object and event type. To change the list view, click the button in the upper-right corner of the panel. The events are displayed as a single list without grouping. Each record shows: — the object the event relates to — date and time — the event name or description Events are ordered by time: newer records are displayed higher. The colored square next to the description corresponds to the event type. To return to the list view grouped by object and event type, click the button again. Viewing events on the map To see where an event occurred: 1. Click the event row in the list 2. The map shows the place where the event was recorded — a colored marker appears. Its color corresponds to the color label next to the event in the list To open the event tooltip, click the marker. The tooltip shows: — the date and time of the event — the monitoring object — the event name and description — additional parameters (if available) To close the tooltip, click the cross in its upper-right corner or select another marker. If several events are close to each other, the map combines them into one common marker with a number. The number shows how many events are in this area. Zoom in on the map to see individual events. Some events do not contain coordinates. In this case, no marker is displayed on the map. For example, this may apply to certain service reminders. The event itself remains available in the list, and you can view it. To display all events found on the map, click in the upper-right corner of the events panel. To remove all displayed events from the map, click . How to change event colors Each event type has its own color. It is used both in the event list and on the map. If necessary, you can change the color. To do this: 1. In the “Event types” panel, find the event type you need 2. Click the color label next to its name 3. In the palette that opens, select a new color After you select it, the new color is immediately used for this event type both in the list and on the map.

The “Fuel cards” module helps you account for fuel expenses and monitor fuel card operations. With it, you can: — add fuel cards and link them to objects — view transactions and verify the correctness of operations — configure notifications about charges — load transaction data automatically or manually The module consists of three tabs: “Cards” — adding and configuring fuel cards and linking them to objects “Transactions” — viewing card operations: refuels, charges, and other received data “Services” — connecting and configuring fuel network services for automatic transaction loading

On this tab, you can add and view fuel cards. How to add a card 1. On the “Cards” tab, click “Add card” 2. In the new window: Enter the card number Select the gas station type (fuel network) In the “Objects” field, select one or more objects that use this card. For example, if one card pays for refuels of a tractor unit and a trailer, select both objects. To save the card, you must select at least one object. After saving, the card is available in the details of each linked object. Check the date added — it is filled in automatically, but you can change it if necessary 3. Click “Save” After saving, you can open the fuel card information. To do this, right-click the card in the list twice — a card with details then appears on the right side of the screen. You can also save the card information in PDF format — click the “Save” button

The “Transactions” tab displays operations made with fuel cards. Here you can find the operation you need, view refuel details, and check whether the object s location matches the gas station coordinates. How to find transactions 1. In the “From date” and “To date” fields, specify the period 2. In the “Card” field, select a fuel card 1 — Transaction period 2 — Fuel card selection After you select the parameters, operations for the specified period appear in the table. How to view operation details Select the transaction you need in the table. The “Operation details” area opens on the right side of the screen. It shows: the company — the data provider the fuel card number the date and time of the operation the gas station the object s location the odometer reading the fuel type the fuel quantity the price the total amount the refuel volume according to the sensor the coordinate matching result a map with the object s location Coordinate matching check PILOT compares the object s location at the time of the operation with the saved coordinates of the gas station. The coordinates are considered matching if the distance between the object and the gas station does not exceed 100 meters. The result is displayed in the “Coordinate match” field: green “Match” status — the object was near the specified gas station red “No match” status — the object was more than 100 meters from the saved gas station coordinates A lack of a match does not always mean an incorrect operation. The cause may be inaccurate gas station coordinates, an error in determining the object s location, or missing data. If the fuel card is not linked to an object, PILOT cannot determine its location for the check. In this case, a message appears saying that the card is not linked to an object. If no coordinates are specified for a gas station, contact technical support. Provide the name or identifier of the gas station, the address, latitude, and longitude. Table settings To change how the transactions table is displayed, click the arrow in the header of the column you need. In the menu that opens, you can: — sort records in ascending or descending order — select the columns to display — group records by the selected parameter — enable the grouped data view To select columns: 1. Open the menu in the header of any column 2. Select “Columns” 3. Select the check boxes next to the data you want to see in the table The “Gas station” column shows the fueling station specified in the transaction. The result of matching its coordinates with the object s location can be viewed in the operation details. This tab displays operations made with fuel cards.

On this tab, you can enable or disable transaction notifications and manually upload fuel card data. How to manage alerts 1. In the “Transaction notifications” section, select or clear the check box for the notification type you need. Email and SMS notifications are available. If you plan to receive SMS notifications, make sure an SMS package is connected and paid for. 2. Click “Save” Notifications are sent only for automatically loaded transactions. No alerts are sent for manually uploaded transactions. How to upload transactions manually 1. In the “Card transaction upload” section, select the file format you need 2. Click “Choose file” If the transactions were exported from the operator in Excel format, first save the file as CSV. When preparing the file, make sure that: the CSV format is used a comma is used as the delimiter the file structure matches the selected upload format 3. To see a sample file, click the icon next to the format you need 4. Click “Upload” to import the data

On the main PILOT map, you can view the gas stations of connected fuel networks. You can see the location of fueling stations and check which of them are near objects. The coordinates of added gas stations are also used when checking operations with fuel cards. PILOT compares the object s location at the time of the operation with the location of the specified gas station. How to display gas stations 1. Open the “Refuel types” list on the map 2. Select the check boxes next to the fuel networks you need The gas stations of the selected networks appear on the map . To hide the stations of a particular network, clear the corresponding check box. The list shows only the fuel networks connected for the account . If the network or gas station you need is missing, contact technical support. To add a gas station, prepare: — the fuel network name — the address — latitude and longitude Technical support will check the data and add the gas station to the system. Coordinate check during an operation After a gas station is added, its coordinates are taken into account when checking transactions. To see the result: 1. Go to the “Fuel cards” module 2. Open the “Transactions” tab 3. Select the operation you need in the list 4. Look at the “Coordinate match” field in the operation details: green “Match” status — the object was no more than 100 meters from the saved gas station coordinates red “No match” status — the object was more than 100 meters from the saved gas station coordinates If the gas station coordinates have not been added yet, PILOT cannot perform the check correctly. In this case, contact technical support and provide the station s address, latitude, and longitude.

This setting is available to technical support staff and administrators with access to the PILOT admin panel. If you do not have such access, contact technical support — specialists will help you connect the fuel networks you need. Connected directories determine which fuel networks a user sees in the “Refuel types” list on the main map. Before adding gas stations, prepare: — the fuel network name — the address and coordinates of the station, if it has not yet been added to the system To connect, you need the directory identifiers from the database. Add only the gas stations required for the account to work, so that the “Refuel types” list shows relevant networks. How to connect a directory 1. Open the contract card in the admin panel 2. Go to the “Module settings” tab 3. Select Fuel cards module 4. Click “Add” 5. In the key field, enter: types 6. In the value field, enter the identifiers of the gas station directories you need as a list, for example: [1,2,3] Use the actual directory identifiers from the database. 7. Save the changes After saving, the connected fuel networks appear in the user s “Refuel types” list. Networks not added to the types setting are not displayed in the list.

The “Composite objects” module is designed to combine several fuel objects and sensors into one logical object and track them as a single fuel accounting system. It helps you build a clear fuel flow scheme — from source and storage to dispensing — and correctly calculate receipts, consumption, and balances. The module is useful in the following scenarios: — if a tanker truck with several compartments is used — if there is a stationary gas station or fuel depot — if you need to account for receiving, storing, and dispensing fuel within a single scheme In the module, you can: — create and configure composite objects — add elements (objects) and sensors to them — use them in reports and monitoring for fuel calculations How to create a composite object Before creating a composite object, make sure the following are already configured in the system: — the required objects (vehicles, tanks, and other elements that will be part of the scheme) — the corresponding sensors All objects and sensors must be added and configured correctly in advance — only after that can they be combined into a composite object. 2. Go to “Main” → “Composite objects” 3. Click the button to add an object 4. Enter the name of the composite object 5. It appears in the list on the “Composite objects” tab How to add elements to a composite object 1. Open the composite object you created 2. Click the button to add an element 3. Specify: — object — an element of the composite object (select from the list) — sensor (select from the list of the object s sensors) — date — element type — its role in the fuel scheme: Tank — a container for storing fuel, for example, a tanker truck compartment, a stationary reservoir, a generator tank. Input flow meter — measures the volume of fuel entering the system, for example, receiving at a fuel depot, filling a stationary tank, recording receipts before storage. Flow meter — measures the volume of fuel leaving the tank, for example, refueling a vehicle, dispensing fuel to customers, supplying fuel to equipment. Input tank — an external fuel source, for example, a large external supplier reservoir. 4. Click “Save” The element becomes part of the composite object and appears in the list. Click it — it is displayed on the diagram. Add all the required elements. Diagram configuration The diagram block is at the bottom of the window. 1. Drag the elements with the mouse to the desired positions 2. Connect them with arrows — from input to output 3. Click “Save” below the diagram After that, the system uses this diagram in fuel calculations and reports. Working with the composite object list 1 — Filter in the object list 2 — Search If the list is long, you can: — use the filter — use the “Search” field To refresh the list, use the button . To create a new composite object, click . To delete an element or the entire composite object, click the delete button next to it in the list. To edit an object, double-click it in the list, and the edit window opens.

A notification is an automatic message that the system sends when a certain event defined in the settings occurs. Notifications let you receive information about events, for example: — engine start or stop — speeding — fuel level change — refuel or fuel drain — entering or leaving a geofence — loss of connection with the device — the need for maintenance With notifications you can respond to events quickly and keep track of the state of objects in the system. The “Notifications” module lets you set up: — the conditions under which a notification is triggered — the objects it applies to — the delivery method, for example by email, SMS, Telegram, as a message in the system, or as a Push in the mobile app

After the “Notifications” module is activated, a new “Notifications” tab appears in the contract settings. Through this tab, you can configure the events for which the system sends notifications to users. 1. Go to “Contract settings” and o pen the “Notifications” tab 2. Click the button 3. The notification settings window opens Basic notification parameters 1. Template Select a notification template if you want to use ready-made settings. A template is created after you configure a notification — to do this, fill in all the parameters and click “Save as template” . After that, you can reuse it. 2. Selection by objects or tags Specify which objects the notification applies to: By objects — select specific vehicles or equipment By tags — use this if you need to apply the notification to a whole group of objects at once 3. Type and name Set the notification name — it helps you quickly find it in the list and understand which event it is responsible for. Select how you want to receive notifications: SMS — a message to your phone Push — a notification in the mobile app Email — an email message Alert — a pop-up notification in the interface of the system Control Room — the event is displayed in the “Control Room” Webhook — sending data to an external service Command to device — sending a command to the tracker Command template — sending a preconfigured command from a template to the device Telegram — a notification through the Telegram bot To receive notifications by Email, confirm your email address in your personal settings in advance. If necessary, you can set an alternative message text — it is sent when the notification is triggered. If the “Control Room” module is connected, the “Algorithm binding” button becomes available. With it, you can configure automatic event handling scenarios — for example, define a sequence of actions that runs when a certain event occurs. 4. Notification time In the “Notification time” block, you can set the conditions under which the notification works: — select the time zone — specify the days of the week — set time intervals 5. Additional information Select the parameters you need — they are added to the notification text: — driving speed — the object s driver — the geofence the object is in (if the “Geofences” module is connected) — map link (Google) — direct link to the event — the event address The direct link to the event opens the object on the map from the notification. After following it, you will see the object s current position and its main parameters. The link is valid for a limited time, after which it becomes unavailable. 6. Notification types and conditions When creating a notification, select the event on which it should be triggered. For example: — speeding — sensor triggering — parking or movement — loss of connection — other system events Each notification type has its own trigger conditions. For example: — speed threshold — event duration For more about notification types and conditions, read the separate article . 7. Geofence parameters This setting is available if the “Geofences” module is connected. In the notification settings, you can specify in which geofences the notification should be triggered. To do this, select one or more geofences from the list or select all of them at once with the button . Then select where exactly the notification should be triggered: Everywhere — the notification is sent regardless of where the object is located In selected zones — the notification is sent only if the object is inside the selected geofences Outside selected zones — the notification is sent only if the object is outside the selected geofences After configuring all notification parameters, click “Save”. If you want to save the configured notification as a template so you can later use it as a template when configuring a new notification, click “Save as template”. If you enable the “For all users” parameter, the notification is sent to all users of the account. All created notifications are displayed on the “Notifications” tab in “Contract settings”. To learn how to work with this tab, read the article “How to work with the notification list” . Watch an example of notification setup in a short YouTube video: https://youtu.be/O4y0YhNp6b4

When you create a notification, you select the type of event the system will monitor and set up its trigger conditions. The conditions determine when the notification is sent — for example, when a speed limit is exceeded, during a long parking stop, or when a sensor reading changes. All available notification types are listed below. Movement and route Speed Movement Parking Mileage Routes Scheduler System and device status Connection loss Device problems Sensors and events Sensor events Ignition operation Ignition event Sensor operation Sensor value change Multi-sensor events Complex sensor event Sensor faults Indicators Temperature Humidity Pressure Fuel level Refuels and fuel drains Geolocation and object events Geofences Proximity to an object Advanced scenarios Formula Event media files iButton duplication Blocking for exceeding limits How to set up conditions 1. Select the notification type The notification type determines which event the system monitors — for example, speeding, parking, or a sensor trigger. 2. Set the parameters — for example, the speed threshold or duration 3. Add extra conditions if needed To add another condition, click the button To remove a condition, use the button You can also change the order of conditions with the arrows If a notification has several conditions, you can select a logical rule between them: AND — the notification is triggered if all conditions are met at the same time OR — the notification is triggered if at least one of the conditions is met Main notification types Speed The notification is triggered if the object s speed meets the specified condition. You can set the following conditions: If the speed is: — greater than the specified value — less than the specified value — equal to the specified value You can also specify how long the condition must be met: — seconds — minutes — hours — kilometers of travel For “Speed” notifications you can set a repeat interval. This helps you avoid a large number of identical notifications. For example: if the speed exceeds 60 km/h for more than 60 seconds, the system sends a notification. The next notification appears only after the specified interval (for example, 5 minutes) if the speeding continues. Ignition events The “Ignition events” notification type is used to receive messages when the ignition state of an object changes. Available conditions: On — a notification is sent when the ignition is turned on Off — a notification is sent when the ignition is turned off On and off — a notification is sent for both events Moving without the sensor on — a notification is sent if the object started moving but the ignition sensor is not on If needed, you can enable the “Failure trigger” option. It helps you track recurring errors or unstable sensor operation. When the option is enabled, additional fields become available: Number of errors — how many times the error must repeat for the notification to be triggered Reset time — after how many minutes the error counter is reset Ignition operation This notification type lets you monitor how long an object stays with the ignition on or off. After selecting this type, set the trigger condition: Longer than — a notification is sent if the ignition stays on or off for longer than the specified value. Enter a number for the duration and select the unit: seconds, minutes, hours, kilometers of travel Break duration — a setting that counts only events separated by a break of the specified length. For the break you also need to specify a value and a unit Sensor events The “Sensor events” notification type lets you receive notifications when the state of the selected sensor changes. Available conditions: On — a notification is sent when the sensor switches to the “on” state Off — a notification is sent when the sensor switches to the “off” state On and off — a notification is sent on any change of the sensor state Moving without the sensor on — a notification is sent if the object started moving but the selected sensor is not on. If needed, you can enable the “Failure trigger” option. It helps you track recurring errors or unstable sensor operation. When the option is enabled, additional fields become available: Number of errors — how many times the error must repeat for the notification to be triggered Reset time — after how many minutes the error counter is reset Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to. Sensor operation With this notification type you can monitor how a sensor value changes and how long the sensor stays in a given state. After selecting the type, set the conditions: • No change for longer than — the notification is triggered if the sensor value does not change for longer than the specified time. You need to specify a numeric value and a unit. • Longer than — the notification is triggered if the sensor stays in a certain state, or its value exceeds the condition, for longer than the specified time. You also need to set a value and a unit. • Break duration — a setting that defines how long a break in sensor operation must be to end the current event. • Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to. If a sensor with the specified tag is on, the system starts counting its operating time. When the duration reaches the “Longer than” value, an event is created and a notification is sent. After the notification is sent, no repeated notifications are sent for the same event while the sensor keeps working continuously. If the sensor turns off, the system starts counting the break duration. If the sensor turns on again before the “Break duration” time has elapsed, the event is considered ongoing and no new notification is created. If the sensor stayed off for at least the time specified in “Break duration”, the current event ends. The next period of the sensor being on is counted as a new event. For example: if “Longer than” = 10 minutes and “Break duration” = 2 hours, a notification is sent after the sensor has been working for 10 minutes. A repeat notification appears only after the sensor has been off for at least 2 hours, then turns on again and works for more than 10 minutes. Sensor value change The “Sensor value change” notification type lets you track how much the value of the selected sensor has changed over a certain period of time. After selecting this type, set the trigger condition: Difference greater than — enter a numeric value: how much the sensor value must change for the notification to be triggered. For example: 5 — if the value changes by more than 5 units. If you enable the “by modulus |x|” option, the system takes a change in either direction into account — both an increase and a decrease. Over a period — specify the time interval over which the change is analyzed: enter a number and select a unit (seconds, minutes) Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to. Multi-sensor events The “Multi-sensor events” notification type is used for sensors that work with a state table (for example, equipment status, device operating mode, switch positions). Such a sensor can have several possible values, and the notification is triggered when its state changes. Then set the conditions: Changes only — if you enable this option, a notification is sent only when the sensor value changes Ignore values outside the table — if you enable this setting, the system takes into account only the values listed in the sensor s table. All other values (not described in the table) are ignored, and no notification is sent for them Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to Complex sensor event The “Complex sensor event” notification type lets you set up a single notification for several sensor events at once. Select the groups of sensors the condition applies to. The “Reset time” field sets the period after which the system resets the event state. Sensor faults The “Sensor faults” notification type is designed to detect possible problems in sensor operation and to monitor that sensors work correctly. This notification also works as a fault indicator: — when a fault is detected, a yellow indicator appears next to the object status — when a sensor goes into the failure state, a red indicator appears You can enable one or several conditions at the same time: Outside the calibration table — a notification is sent if the sensor value goes outside the calibration table for the specified period of time No changes — a notification is sent if the sensor value does not change for the specified time Number of changes — a notification is sent if the number of changes of the sensor value is greater or less than the set threshold over the specified period of time. You can also take into account: Geofence enter — sensor changes are counted only when entering a geofence Geofence exit — sensor changes are counted only when leaving a geofence Additional rule — lets you set an extra condition for detecting a fault. You need to specify: — the sensor field name — the condition: , , = — the value Handlers and formulas can be used. Failure trigger settings — if a fault repeats several times, the sensor can go into the failure state. The trigger settings define: — Number of errors — how many faults must occur for the sensor to go into the failure state — Reset time (min) — the error-free period after which the failure status is cleared automatically Trigger reset rules — how long the object must stay parked or drive without errors for the fault status to be cleared automatically. You can set up the conditions under which the trigger is reset: — parking time (in minutes) — driving time (in minutes) — if needed, set a formula Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to Device problems The “Device problems” notification type is designed to detect incorrect tracker operation or data transmission errors. You can enable one or several conditions at the same time: Coordinates change without speed (Coords change without speed) — the notification is triggered if the object s coordinates change but its speed is zero. You need to specify a threshold and a unit Speed without coordinates change (Speed without changing coords) — the notification is triggered if the device transmits a speed but the coordinates stay the same Coordinates change — a notification is sent on a sudden or abnormal change of coordinates. You can set the parameters above which the event is considered a problem. Additional rule — lets you set an extra condition for detecting a fault. You need to specify: — the sensor field name — the condition: , , = — the value Failure trigger settings — if the problem occurs several times, the device can go into the failure state. The trigger settings define: — Number of errors — how many times the problem must repeat — Reset time (min) — after how many error-free minutes the failure status is cleared Trigger reset rules — you can set up the conditions under which the trigger is reset: — parking time (in minutes) — driving time (in minutes) — if needed, set a formula Pressure The “Pressure” notification type is used to monitor pressure sensor readings. The notification is triggered if the pressure value meets the specified condition. After selecting this type, set the trigger condition: • Condition — select how the system compares the pressure value: — Greater than — the notification is triggered if the pressure becomes greater than the specified value — Equal to — the notification is triggered if the pressure equals the specified value — Less than — the notification is triggered if the pressure becomes less than the specified value • Value — enter the numeric pressure value the sensor reading is compared with • Longer than — specify how long the condition must be met for the notification to be triggered. Enter a number and select a unit: — seconds — minutes — hours — kilometers of travel • Repeat interval — sets the pause between identical notifications if the condition continues to be met For example: if the pressure is below the set value for more than 10 seconds, the notification is sent once. The next notification appears only after the specified interval if the condition still persists. • Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to Temperature This notification type is used to monitor temperature from the selected sensor, for example in a refrigerator unit, an engine, or other equipment. Then set the conditions: If the temperature — sets the main rule by which the system compares the sensor readings with the specified value in degrees Celsius (°C). Available options: — Greater than — the notification is triggered if the temperature exceeds the specified value — Equal to — the notification is triggered if the temperature is exactly equal to the specified value — Less than — the notification is triggered if the temperature drops below the specified value — Out of range — the notification is triggered if the temperature goes outside the set range (for example, below +2°C or above +8°C) Longer than — lets you set the minimum time the condition must be met for the notification to be triggered. This helps filter out short and insignificant fluctuations (for example, when the refrigerator door is opened). In the “Units” field you can select the unit of this duration: seconds, minutes, hours. No change for longer than — a separate condition that helps detect possible sensor faults when its readings “freeze” at one value. The notification is triggered if the temperature does not change for longer than the specified period of time. Sensor groups — select which temperature sensors this rule applies to Humidity The “Humidity” notification type is used to monitor humidity from the selected sensor, for example in a cargo compartment or a refrigerator unit. After selecting the type, set the conditions: If the humidity: — Greater than — the notification is triggered if the humidity is above the specified value — Less than — the notification is triggered if the humidity is below the specified value — Equal to — the notification is triggered if the humidity equals the specified value — Out of range by — the notification is triggered if the humidity deviates from the set range by the specified value Enter the numeric humidity value the system compares the sensor readings with. The value is set in percent (%). Longer than — specify how long the condition must be met for the notification to be triggered: — Seconds — the condition is met for longer than the specified number of seconds — Minutes — the condition is met for longer than the specified number of minutes — Hours — the condition is met for longer than the specified number of hours No change for longer than — this setting lets you control situations when the humidity does not change for a set time. The notification is triggered if the humidity value stays unchanged for longer than the specified period Connection loss The “Connection loss” notification type is used to monitor loss of connection with an object. The notification is triggered if no data is received from the device within the specified time or distance. After selecting this type, set the trigger condition: Longer than — specify how long the connection loss must last for the notification to be triggered: — Seconds — the notification is triggered if the connection loss lasts longer than the specified number of seconds — Minutes — the notification is triggered if the connection loss lasts longer than the specified number of minutes — Hours — the notification is triggered if the connection loss lasts longer than the specified number of hours — Kilometers — the notification is triggered if the object has traveled the specified distance without a connection Mileage The “Mileage” notification type is used to monitor an object s mileage by the odometer. It lets you receive notifications if the mileage is greater or less than the set value over the selected period. After selecting the type, set the conditions: If the mileage: — Greater than — the notification is triggered if the object s mileage is greater than the specified value — Less than — the notification is triggered if the object s mileage is less than the specified value — Monthly limit exceeded — the notification is triggered if the mileage for the month has exceeded the set value Units — enter the numeric mileage value the system compares the odometer data with. The value is set in kilometers. Period — select the period over which the condition is checked: — Total — the condition is checked for the entire period since the notification was created — Per month — the condition is checked within the current month — Per day — the condition is checked within the current day Movement The “Movement” notification type is used to monitor object movement. The notification is triggered if the object is moving for longer than the set time or covers the specified distance. Set the conditions: Longer than — specify how long the object must be moving for the notification to be triggered.
