Enter a number and select a unit: — Seconds — the notification is triggered if the movement lasts longer than the specified number of seconds — Minutes — the notification is triggered if the movement lasts longer than the specified number of minutes — Hours — the notification is triggered if the movement lasts longer than the specified number of hours — Kilometers — the notification is triggered if the object has traveled more than the specified distance Break duration — this setting counts only movement events separated by a break of the specified length. If the break between two movement segments is shorter than the specified value, the system treats them as one continuous movement. For example, if you set a break of 10 seconds, a stop shorter than 10 seconds does not interrupt the movement event. Parking The “Parking” notification type is used to monitor object stops. The notification is triggered if the object stays still for longer than the set time. After selecting this type, set the trigger condition: Longer than — specify how long the object must stay still for the notification to be triggered: — Seconds — the notification is triggered if the parking lasts longer than the specified number of seconds — Minutes — the notification is triggered if the parking lasts longer than the specified number of minutes — Hours — the notification is triggered if the parking lasts longer than the specified number of hours Geofences The “Geofences” notification type is used to monitor geofence-related events. It lets you receive notifications when an object enters a geofence, leaves it, stops inside it, or passes through it without stopping. Available conditions: Entry — the notification is triggered when the object enters the selected geofence Exit — the notification is triggered when the object leaves the selected geofence Entry+Exit — a notification is sent both on entering and on leaving the geofence Stop in geofence — the notification is triggered if the object stops inside the geofence No stop in geofence — the notification is triggered if the object enters the geofence, does not stop in it, and then leaves it Min. speed — for conditions related to a stop or no stop, you can specify a minimum speed. This parameter helps determine whether the object is considered moving or stopped inside the geofence Fuel level The “Fuel level” notification type is used to monitor the fuel level from the selected sensor on the object. The notification is triggered if the fuel level meets the specified condition. After selecting this type, set the trigger condition: If the fuel level: — Greater than — the notification is triggered if the fuel level is above the specified value — Less than — the notification is triggered if the fuel level is below the specified value — Equal to — the notification is triggered if the fuel level equals the specified value Units — enter the numeric fuel level value the system compares the sensor readings with Refuels and fuel drains The “Refuels and fuel drains” (Fuel Refuelings Drainings) notification type is used to monitor events related to changes in fuel level. It lets you receive notifications about refuels and fuel drains on an object. After selecting this type, check which events should trigger the notification: • Refuels — the notification is triggered when the system detects a refuel • Drains — the notification is triggered when the system detects a fuel drain • Refuel start — the notification is triggered at the moment a refuel starts • Drain start — the notification is triggered at the moment a fuel drain starts Proximity to an object The “Proximity to an object” notification type is used to monitor the situation when one object approaches another within a set distance. In this notification type, one object is treated as a moving geofence, and the system tracks when another object enters or leaves this zone. After selecting this type, set the trigger condition: If the distance to the object is: Less than — specify the distance at which an object is considered to be near another object. The value is set in meters. Longer than — specify how long an object must stay within the range of another object for the notification to be triggered. The value is set in seconds. Enter — if you enable this option, the notification is triggered when the object enters the range of another object Exit — if you enable this option, the notification is triggered when the object leaves the range of another object Objects — select from the list the objects for which proximity will be tracked The system compares the objects from the list and determines when one object is at the set distance from another. The object being approached is treated as a moving geofence. For example, if a vehicle from the selected list gets closer than 100 meters to another object and stays nearby for more than 30 seconds, the system sends a notification. Formula The “Formula” notification type is used to check a custom condition set as a formula. The notification is triggered if the formula result is true or false. In the “Formula” field, enter the expression to check. You can use raw data fields, sensor values, handlers, and formulas in it. The notification is triggered if the check result is: • true — the condition is met • false — the condition is not met Blocking for exceeding limits The “Blocking for exceeding limits” notification type is used to send a notification if an object was blocked because of a violation of the set limits. If the system detects such a block, the notification is sent through the selected channel. After selecting this type, specify the delivery method, for example: • Email • SMS • Webhook • Telegram • Push If Email is selected, notifications are sent to the specified email address. This notification type is applied automatically to all existing objects and to all new objects created after it is set up. Scheduler The “Scheduler” notification type is used to monitor object movement during working and non-working hours according to its work schedule settings. After selecting this type, set the trigger conditions: • At the scheduled time — the notification is triggered if the object moves within the set working hours • Outside the scheduled time — the notification is triggered if the object moves outside the set working hours Longer than — specify how long the object must be moving for the notification to be triggered Break duration — this setting takes breaks between movement events into account. If the break is shorter than the specified value, the system treats the movement as continuous. For example: if you set a break of 10 seconds, a short stop of less than 10 seconds does not interrupt the movement event. Event media files The “Event media files” notification type is used to send a notification when the device successfully uploads to the storage server a media file associated with a recorded event. This notification is triggered not at the moment of the event itself, but only after the file has been successfully transferred and saved on the server. For example, a notification can be sent when the device uploads a photo of a violation, a video clip of the event, a snapshot from the driver s cabin or of the road situation, or another file created after the event was recorded. Such a notification can be used for events related to ADAS / DMS violations and warnings, for example driver distraction, phone use, smoking while driving, fatigue, collision risk, lane departure, or harsh braking. The “Repeat interval” parameter lets you set a pause between identical notifications if the device uploads several media files in a row for the same event. iButton duplication The “iButton duplication” notification type is used to detect situations when the same iButton is registered on more than one vehicle within a set period of time. Such a notification helps detect incorrect driver identification. For example, if a driver used the same iButton on one vehicle and then on another, the system may assume that the driver switched to the other object and update the assignment. As a result, trip, driver, and report data may become incorrect. After selecting this type, set the condition: Over a period — specify the time during which the system checks whether the same iButton was used on more than one object. The notification is triggered if the same iButton is detected on several objects within the specified time. For this notification type to work correctly: — an iButton sensor must be set up on the objects — the drivers module must be used — the notification must be linked to the objects you want to monitor Routes The “Routes” notification type is used to monitor events on routes already assigned to an object. In the settings of this notification you select which route events you want to be notified about. After assigning the vehicle to a route , the system starts comparing the object s trips with the assigned route: — records entering and leaving the route — takes passing checkpoints into account — includes trips in route reports In the settings of this notification type, you select which route events should trigger notifications: In stop zone — the notification is triggered when the object is in the zone of a checkpoint or stop. The radius of this zone is set on the map when configuring the route . Outside stop zone — the notification is triggered when the object leaves the zone of a checkpoint or stop. The zone boundary is also defined by the radius set when editing the route Route entry — the notification is triggered when the object enters the route boundaries. The route boundaries are defined by its width set on the map Route exit — the notification is triggered when the object leaves the route boundaries.

All created notifications are displayed on the “Notifications” tab in the “Contract settings”. Here you can: — view the list of all created notifications — create new ones — edit existing notifications and delete the ones you no longer need — work with notification templates — apply notifications to new objects automatically Notification list The table shows all notifications available in the current account. For each notification the table shows: ID — the internal notification identifier User — the user who created the notification Name — the notification name Type — the type of event the notification works on Date — the date and time the notification was created Vehicle — the objects the notification is linked to The following actions are available on the right of each row: Edit — open the notification for editing Delete — delete the notification Notification templates The tab provides notification export and import functions. You can use notifications that are already set up as templates and transfer them to another account. 1 — Export notifications 2 — Import notifications Exporting notifications When you export, the current list of notifications is saved to a JSON file. 1. Click “Export notifications” 2. The system creates a file in JSON format You can use this file as a template — for example, to quickly set up notifications in another account. During export, the following are automatically excluded from the file: vehicles, geofences, phone numbers, email addresses. This is because another account may have different objects and contacts. After import, you will need to specify this data manually. Importing notifications Import lets you load previously saved notifications from a JSON file. Before importing, choose the suitable option: Do not delete old notifications — the new ones are added to the existing ones Delete old notifications — the current settings are replaced with the imported ones How to import: 1. Select the file to upload 2. Click “Import” Automatic notification assignment The “Enable automatic notification assignment” option determines whether notifications are applied automatically to new objects. If the option is enabled, all created notifications are automatically assigned to new objects that you add to the account. If the option is disabled, you will need to add new objects to notifications manually.

A webhook is a way to automatically pass event data from the system to an external service or to your server. For example, if a vehicle exceeds the speed limit, the system sends a request to the address you specified and passes the event information. How webhook notifications work 1. You specify a URL — where to send the data 2. When the notification is triggered, the system sends a POST request with JSON 3. Your server receives the data and processes it as needed Before you start, make sure that: — the URL is correct and reachable — the server responds with code 200 (OK) — if the server does not respond or returns an error, the address is temporarily blacklisted How to set up a webhook 1. Go to creating or editing a notification 2. In the “Type and name” block, select the webhook sending method 3. To set up webhook notifications, click the edit field — the Webhook Details window opens, where you set the data sending parameters. In the Webhook Details window you will see three fields: 1. URL Specify the address the data will be sent to. 2. Header This is where the format of the transmitted data is specified. The required value is already set by default: ["ContentType: application/json"] 3. Body (request body) This is the data that will be sent. The following template is used by default: { "agent_id": "%AGENTID%", "vehiclenumber": "%VEHNUM%", "ts": "%TS%", "lat": "%LAT%", "lon": "%LON%", "speed": "%SPEED%", "data": "%DATA%", "zone": "%ZONE%", "driver": "%DRIVER%" } 4. Variables for the request body You can modify or extend the request body using the allowed variables from the list on the right. Keep to the format — "value": "%VALUE%". If the syntax is broken, the webhook will not work. Allowed variables Variable What it passes %ACCOUNTID% Account ID %AGENTID% Object ID %VEHNUM% Vehicle number %TS% Timestamp %DATETIME% Date and time %LAT% Latitude %LON% Longitude %SPEED% Speed %ODO% Mileage (from the sensor) %DATA% Notification data %ZONE% Geofence %ZONE_ID% ID of the first geofence %ZONE_NAME% Name of the first geofence %DRIVER% Driver %MAXSPEED% Maximum speed (for speeding notifications) %DUR% Duration of the violation %SPEEDLIMIT% Set speed limit (Speed control) How to insert a sensor value If you need to pass the data of a specific sensor: 1. Open the “Sensors” tab 2. Copy the exact sensor name 3. Return to the webhook settings window and in the Body field insert the variable in the format %Sensor name%. For example, if the sensor is called Fuel sensor status, write %Fuel sensor status%. How to get raw data You can pass data directly from the device: 1. Go to the “Points” tab 2. Find the parameter in the “Raw data” column 3. Insert it into the Body field in the Webhook window in the format %Parameter name%. For example, if the parameter is called Valid, write %Valid%. Request example When the notification is triggered, your server receives data that looks roughly like this: { "agent_id": 4328, "ts": 1545254055, "data": ["У286НМ 67", "Parkingdur", "2", "1", "мм"] } The data set depends on which variables you specified in the request body and which notification type is configured.

To start receiving notifications: 1. Go to “Contract settings” and open the “Privacy” tab 2. Find the “Notification settings” section 3. Check the notification types you want to receive: Speed Refuels Connection loss Idle time Violation control Drivers 4. For each selected notification type, choose how you want to receive it: Email — notifications by email To receive notifications by email, you need to confirm your email address. Alert — a pop-up notification in the system SMS — a message to your phone Telegram — a message in Telegram Push — a notification in the mobile app 5. Click “Save”

When an event configured in the system occurs, you receive a notification. It appears in the “Notifications” window. The first time you sign in, this window may open automatically. If you closed or minimized it, open it again by clicking the notifications icon on the top bar. The icon shows the number of unread notifications, so you can see right away whether there are new events. What the notifications window shows The window shows the list of all notifications. For each event it displays: — the date and time it was triggered — the object — the notification text describing the event Click a notification to expand it and see the details. The expanded view may show: — a more detailed description of the event — additional information — for example: address, geofence, a direct link to the event The following functions are available at the bottom of the window: “Clear” — remove the list of notifications from the window “Mute” — turn off the sound for new notifications “OK” — close the notifications window

In the “History” section you can see where and when notifications were triggered. How to enable notification display To make notifications appear in “History”: 1. Go to “Contract settings”, “ Map and geocoding ” tab 2. Find the “Display events on the map” section 3. Check the “Notifications” item 4. Save the settings How to view notifications 1. Open the “History” section 2. Build a track for the period you need 3. Go to the “Events” tab The event list shows the notifications that were triggered during the selected time. Click the notification you need in the list — a marker appears on the map showing the place of the event and information about it.

The “Trips” module helps you automate and simplify work with bus routes, schedules, and stops. With it you can: — create and edit trips — add stops and manage them — link buses to trips — set up schedules — monitor bus movement in real time — get schedule adherence reports

A stop is a geographic zone that a vehicle must visit while performing a trip along a route. 1. Go to the lower part of the workspace — this is where the list of all stops is located 2. Click the button to add a new stop 3. In the window that opens, specify: Name and description Coordinates: manually with the arrows or by moving the marker on the map Stop radius (m) — the zone within which arrival is recorded If needed, check the boxes: — technical stop — not counted in boarding and alighting, but used in route calculation A technical stop is a point on the route that: — is not shown in the schedule of passenger trips — does not take part in boarding and alighting records — no passengers are recorded at it — takes part in building the route — for example, it helps lay out the path correctly — can be used to monitor bus movement — for example, as a checkpoint — does not affect passenger flow reports — its data does not go into boarding/alighting statistics — terminal stop — the point where the route ends and the return journey begins If you check the “Terminal” box for a stop, the system treats it as the last stop on the route: — the system truncates the route — all stops after this one are not used in the trip — the bus starts moving in the opposite direction — that is, it switches to the return schedule (if the trip is bidirectional) — only the stops up to and including this terminal stop are counted in the schedule and reports 4. Click “Save” — the stop appears in the list The list shows all added stops with their ID, radius, type, and description. To edit a stop, double-click it in the list and make the changes in the window that opens. To delete a stop from the list, use the icon . Once you add trips, the list shows all created trips and the number of stops in each of them. Click the arrow next to a trip to expand its list of stops. Each stop entry has an arrow — click it to open the menu and configure the route: Forward / Back — change the order of the stop in the route U-turn — specify that the vehicle turns around at this stop and starts moving in the opposite direction To delete a stop from a trip, right-click it in the list and select “Delete”. How to link an RFID tag to a stop A stop visit can be detected by an RFID tag. When the vehicle reads the tag linked to a stop, the system processes the received data as a visit to that stop within the assigned bus line. Before linking, add and configure the necessary tags in the “RFID tags” module. The tag must be within the stop radius. To link RFID tags: 1. Create a stop or select an existing one 2. Click the tag icon next to the stop 3. In the “Stop RFID tags” window, find the tag you need by name or identifier 4. Check the box next to the tag 5. Select other tags if needed 6. Click “Save” Several RFID tags can be linked to one stop. In this case the system can process a visit when any of them is read. To show only the tags that are already linked, check the “Linked” box. If the tag you need is not in the list, check that it has been added and configured in the “RFID tags” module. Also make sure the tag is within the stop radius. After linking, add the stop to a bus line , and then assign this line to a vehicle . Only after all these steps are completed can the system match the read RFID tag to the stop and process its visit.

A trip is the movement of a vehicle from the departure point to the destination along a set route and schedule. 1. In the workspace, find the “Trips” block 2. On the toolbar, click the icon 3. In the window that opens, specify: Trip name and number Description Check the box if the trip is bidirectional (the vehicle runs back and forth along the route) Interval between trips (in minutes) Ticket price (if required) 4. Add the stops you need to the trip — select them from the list of available stops and click the arrow 5. Click “Save” — the trip appears in the general list To edit a trip: — right-click it and select “Edit” in the menu that appears — or double-click the trip in the list — a window opens where you can make changes and save them To delete a trip, select “Delete” in the same menu.

The trip menu contains several tools. To open the menu: — right-click the trip you need in the list — or click the arrow next to the trip Edit Click this button in the menu to open the trip editing window. In it you can: change the trip name and number update the description set parameters: direction, interval, price change the list of stops After making changes, click “Save”. Schedule A schedule is a timetable that shows what time a bus must be at each stop on a specific trip. With this function you can add a new schedule or view existing timetables. To learn how to add a schedule, see this article . Buses This shows all buses linked to the selected trip. To learn how to link a bus to a trip, read here . Show all stops Click this menu item and all stops of the route are displayed on the map. Click any stop on the map to see its name. Live view If you select “Live view” in the menu, you will see the whole route with stops and the schedule in real time. What the diagram shows: Buses on the route — numbered icons show the actual buses currently running on the selected route Arrival forecast — click a bus icon to find out when it will be at the next stop Stops — marked with triangles Arrows — show the direction of vehicle movement Green and yellow lines — show the current position of buses on the route Time scale — at the top and bottom of the diagram you can see when a bus is due to pass each stop Upload stops or a line for the route from KML KML is a special file format for storing geographic data, such as points, lines, and areas on a map. To upload stops or a route line from a KML file: 1. Click the corresponding menu item 2. Select the KML file you need on your device 3. Click “Save” The file is added to the route and displays the stops or the route line on the map, helping you set the geographic position of objects precisely. Calculate duration and route After adding all stops to the route, click “Calculate route duration”. The system calculates the travel time between stops and shows them on the diagram in the “Live view” section. Stops with arrival times appear in the live view only after the calculation — without it they are not displayed. The calculation usually takes up to 7 minutes. This function helps you see the order of stops, the vehicle s route, and the arrival time forecast for each stop. All this data is needed to create a schedule, monitor schedule adherence, and build reports. Delete To delete a trip, click this menu item.

You can use the following tools to work with trips: — route monitor Use this tool to view all routes of the selected trips in live mode. Check the route you need in the list and click this tool. — add a trip group Create a new group, enter its name, and click “Save”. The group appears in the trip list. To organize trips, simply drag them into the groups you need with the mouse. — add a trip Use this tool to create a new trip. To learn how to add a trip, read this article . — clear the map Clears the map of all routes, stops, and objects. — refresh the trip list Refreshes the data in the trip list so you see the latest changes and up-to-date information. Use this button if you added or edited trips and the updates did not appear right away.

A schedule is a timetable that shows what time a bus must be at each stop on a specific trip. How to add a schedule: Right-click the trip you need in the list and select “Schedule” in the menu that appears 2. In the “Schedule” window, click and enter the schedule name 3. Click on the right to add a schedule table 4. In the window that opens, select the schedule type: Daily By days of the week For a specific date 5. Click “Create” 6. The “Schedule” window shows the timetable for “Trip 1” with all stops. Set the bus arrival time at each stop Here you can also delete a trip or add a new one. When adding a new trip, specify its start time. If you check the “Continue” box, the system creates several consecutive trips with the specified interval (step) and departure time. If you leave the box unchecked, you can add and configure each trip manually, specifying its own departure time. 7. Fill in the schedule for each trip. Use the “Import” and “Export” buttons to load schedules from files or export them. Schedule tools Several functions are available in the “Schedule” window : — view the schedule history The schedule change history shows all periods when a given schedule was active for the trip: when and which schedule was assigned to the trip and until when it was used How to activate a schedule: 1. Find the one you need in the schedule list 2. Click the light gray check mark next to it — it turns bright gray 3. This schedule becomes active and is now applied to the trip 4. The system recalculates the route and timetable using the new schedule. This may take a few minutes 5. After recalculation you can generate the “Schedule adherence report” — export the current schedule to a file or load a schedule from a file — add a new schedule — delete the selected schedule — refresh the schedule

For a bus to operate on the right route and appear in the schedule, it must be linked to a specific trip: 1. Go to the “Online” tab 2. Find the object you need and right-click it. In the menu that opens, select “Trips”. 3. In the window that opens: Check the trip you need Specify the trip start date and time 4. Click “Save” Here you can also view the link history — click the “History” button to see active trips and link dates.

The “Schedule” module is used together with the “Trips” module. A schedule specifies the time at which a vehicle must pass the checkpoints of a trip or start the next pass along the route. Schedule data is used in the round trips report . The report lets you compare the planned time with the vehicle s actual travel time and determine the deviation from the schedule. The “Trips” module defines the vehicle s route, and the “Schedule” module defines the planned travel time along this route. How to create a schedule To create a schedule: 1. Open the “Schedule” tab 2. Click the “Add schedule” button 3. Fill in the schedule parameters: Name — enter the schedule name Bus line — select the trip the schedule is created for. The trip must be created beforehand in the “Trips” module. After you select the trip, the schedule is linked to the corresponding route. Time — specify the planned time of passing the stops of the selected trip. Enter the time and click the button . Each value is added separately and appears in the list at the bottom of the form. For example, for a trip with three consecutive stops you can add: — 07:15 — the time of passing the first stop — 07:30 — the second stop — 07:45 — the third stop Link to lap start — check the box if the added values should mark the start times of new laps For example, if you add 07:12, 08:12, and 09:12, the vehicle must: — start the first lap at 07:12 — start the second lap at 08:12 — start the third lap at 09:12 A new lap means the vehicle starting another pass along the selected route from its starting point. The added values are shown at the bottom of the form in the “Time” section. To delete a value, click the trash icon next to it. 4. Click “Save”

The integration passes data on trips and fare payments from the “Convenient Route” system to PILOT. Based on this data, you can analyze passenger flow and generate bus reports. The setup consists of three stages: 1. The contract administrator enables the required modules 2. The server administrator sets up API access 3. The user links payment terminals to buses Before you start the setup, prepare: the login and password for API access the API address the Terminal ID of each payment terminal Terminal ID is the identifier of the payment terminal installed in a bus. PILOT uses this identifier to determine which bus the trip and payment data belongs to. the list of buses with terminals installed Before the setup, prepare the API address, login and password, and the terminal identifiers for the buses. If you do not have this data, contact the contract administrator or PILOT support. The specialists will tell you where to get it. access to the PILOT admin panel access to the config.php file on the server 1. Enable the module This stage is performed by the PILOT administrator 1. Open the admin panel 2. Go to the Contracts tab. 3. Select the contract you need and right-click it 4. Select “Edit” 5 In the contract card, go to the “Modules” tab and enable the “Convenient Route” and “Passenger flow” modules 6. After enabling the modules, go to “Module settings” in the contract card 7. Find and select the “Convenient Route integration” module 8. In the “Configs” block, add the parameters Key Value Purpose version 2 Enables API version 2 field_name For example, Terminal ID, gosNum Defines the field the integration uses to match data to a bus 9. Click “Save” 2. Set up the API connection This stage is performed by the server administrator. Open the config.php file on the server and add the parameters: // Удобный маршрут 2.0 $convroute_url = 'http://195.19.176.128:3000/api'; $convroute_user = ' логин API '; $convroute_pass = ' пароль API '; Instead of the placeholders, enter the login and password received for your organization. Save the changes in the config.php file. 3. Specify the bus Terminal ID This stage is performed by a user with rights to edit vehicles. The way to fill it in depends on the value of the field_name parameter and the contract configuration. If the Terminal ID field is used: 1. Open the card of the bus you need 2. Go to the “General” section 3. Find the “Terminal ID” field 4. Enter the identifier of the terminal installed in this bus 5. Click “Save” In some configurations a separate Terminal ID field may not be displayed. If the field you need is missing or you are not sure where to enter the identifier, contact the contract administrator or PILOT support. 4. Check that data is arriving After the setup, wait for new transactions to appear in the “Convenient Route” system. Then generate a report: 1. Open the “Reports” section. 2. Go to the “Passenger flow” group 3. Select a bus 4. Specify the period in which payments were made through the terminal 5. Select the “Summary for Convenient Route” report 6. Generate the report 7. Check that data is present With the integration enabled, the following reports may also be available: Summary for ASOP No. 2 Summary for ASOP No. 3 Summary for ASOP No. 4 City bus + Convenient Route Passenger transportation report other reports of the “Passenger flow” group

The “Routes” module is designed for creating, editing, and monitoring route completion by vehicles. With the module you can: — create routes of any complexity — set up checkpoints — link a route to objects — analyze route completion in reports

To create a route in the system, you need to fill in the main parameters in the builder and add route points that will be displayed on the map. In this article we explain how to create a route and set its parameters so that the route is ready for use in the system. How to create a route 1. Go to the “Routes” tab 2. Click the button — the “Build route” form opens 3. Fill in the route parameters Main settings 1. Name Enter a clear route name, for example: “Route No. 5”, “Downtown delivery”, “Warehouse — Customer”. 2. Detection range (km) This parameter defines how far from the route line a vehicle is still considered to be on the route. Simply put, the system creates a “corridor” around the route. For example, if you enter 0.3 km, this means 300 meters on each side of the route line. As long as the vehicle moves inside this corridor, the system considers that it follows the route. If it leaves the corridor, a deviation from the route is recorded. The value can be a fraction (for example, 0.3). A value that is too small (for example, 0.05 km) can cause false triggers because of GPS error. A value that is too large (for example, 5 km) will count serious detours as part of the route. 3. Geocoder Select the service that automatically fills in the address from the coordinates of route points. Control time This is the planned time for completing the entire route. For example, if the route usually takes 2 hours 30 minutes, enter 2 hours and 30 minutes. This value is used in reports: — to compare plan and actual — to see whether the driver meets the standard Route completion percentage This parameter defines what percentage of points must be visited for the route to be considered completed. For example, if 10 points are set and the percentage is 90%, the driver can skip one point and the route is still considered completed. This allows for force majeure on the road — for example, an accident or a traffic jam when the driver has to bypass part of the route. “Active” check box If you want the percentage rule to actually apply: 1. Enter the required percentage (for example, 80) 2. Check the “Active” box 3. Save the route builder How to add route points A route point is a checkpoint where the passage of a vehicle is recorded. 1. Go to the “Points” section below the route settings 2. Click the button 3. Select the place on the map or enter the address manually. The point appears on the map 4. If needed, drag the marker to the exact place On the map, a point is shown as an icon with a number surrounded by a circle — the detection radius. This radius, which looks like a red dashed line on the map, determines when a vehicle has entered or left the checkpoint. If the vehicle enters the point radius, the system records the visit. To change the point radius, click it with the left mouse button and drag it to the size you need. The radius affects detection accuracy: the larger it is, the greater the allowed error in detecting a visit. A radius that is too large may count an arrival before the vehicle actually stops, and one that is too small may cause a point to be missed. If the vehicle did not cross the checkpoint radius, the system does not record its visit — this is counted as a deviation from the route. 5. Repeat the process for the other route points and click “Save” If you add two or more points, the system automatically builds a route between them. How to link an RFID / BLE tag to a route point A BLE tag is a small physical device (Bluetooth Low Energy) installed at a specific place, for example at a terminal stop or on a customer s premises. When a vehicle approaches this point, the tracker detects the tag and sends its unique identifier (the IButton parameter) to the system. Why this is needed: — if GPS is unstable or jammed — if accurate recording of arrival at a specific place is important — if you need route completion to be counted correctly Tags can be linked to route points only when the RFID tags module is enabled. First you need to set up the tags in this module. To learn how to create a tag, read this article . If you use BLE tags: 1. Open the route 2. Select a specific point 3. Click the tag icon next to the point you need 4. In the window that opens, select the tag you need and link it to the point The tag must be within the point radius. 5. Click “Save” You can link several tags to one point. After linking the tag to the point, save the route. When a vehicle drives the route, the system works as follows: 1. Checks whether a BLE tag is linked to the point 2. Looks for an IButton event within ±5 minutes of the passage time 3. If a tag is detected — the point visit is recorded via BLE 4. If no tag is detected — the standard GPS geofence check is used This way, even if GPS is unstable, the route is counted correctly — based on the actual arrival at the point. How to view or edit a route 1. Go to the “Routes” tab 2. Find the route you need 3. Right-click it 4. Select “Edit” 5. The route builder opens, where you can make changes or just view the settings

You can create a route not only through the routes module, as described in the previous article , but also from a track in the “History” section: How to create a route in “History” Go to the “History” section and select an object from the list by checking the box next to it Specify the time interval for the track search and click the “Search” button 3. The search results list shows the object s track records 4. Find the row with the track for the day you need. Right-click it and open the track menu 5. In the menu, select “Create route” 6. The route opens, displayed in gray on the map 7. If you want to create a route from part of the track, just mark the start and end of the segment you need by clicking points on the track line 8. After marking the segment, click the “Go to route builder” button to set the route parameters 9. In the route builder, set the required parameters and click “Save” Your route is now saved and appears in the route list.

For the system to track route events and build reports for a specific object, you need to link the route to the vehicle: Go to “Main” → “Online” Find the object you want to link a route to Right-click the object and select “Route” 4. In the window that opens, select the routes you want to link to the selected object 5. Click “Save” to link the route to the object After saving, the system offers to recalculate reports, because the routes for this object were changed or relinked. Recalculation is needed so that all data is up to date and reports correctly reflect the route changes. If you want to recalculate reports, click “Yes”. Specify the recalculation period (start and end dates) and click “Start recalculation”. Report recalculation runs in the background, and once it finishes, the data is updated.

In this article we explain how to work with a route in the system, what actions you can perform, and which tools are available for them. Route menu On the “Routes” tab you see all created routes. To open the menu and perform actions on a route, right-click the route you need. Route actions Let s look at the actions you can perform on a route in the menu. Move the map to the route center If you want to focus on the route, select this option. The map automatically opens on the route Edit route Click “Edit” in the menu to open the route builder. In this mode you can change the route parameters, add or delete points, and change other settings. Route recalculation To recalculate a route and analyze its data, open the “Recalculations” menu. It shows all objects linked to the route. For each object in this window you can start a recalculation or view the recalculation history. To do this, right-click the object — a menu with actions opens. When you click “Start recalculation”, a window opens for selecting the period. Specify the start and end dates, and the system recalculates the route passage for this period. When you click “List of recalculated”, you see the recalculation history — when and which recalculations were performed for the selected route. If you want to recalculate the route again, select the recalculation you need and click “Start recalculation”. The “Go to vehicle track” button displays the vehicle s track, where you can see how the object passed the route in that recalculated period. This button is active when at least one recalculation has been completed. Delete If the route is no longer needed, you can delete it. Confirm the deletion, and the route with all its linked points and objects is deleted. Viewing a route and points On the “Routes” tab you can see all created routes in a list. To expand a route and see its points, click When you select a route, it is displayed on the map. If you click a route point in the list, the map automatically focuses on that point so you can see its exact location. If you want to see individual route points on the map, check the “Show points” box. To view the route without points, uncheck this box. To rename a route point, right-click the point in the list and select “Rename”. Enter the new name and click “OK”.

PILOT Task Manager (PTM) is a PILOT system module for working with tasks. It serves as an electronic dispatch center and task manager: here you create tasks, assign executors, and monitor their execution. In PTM you can: — create and assign tasks — plan work by dates and routes — monitor status and deadlines — work with acts and the calendar PTM is used by: — dispatchers and logisticians — plan and distribute tasks — drivers and executors — receive tasks and mark their completion — managers — view reports and work results Access to the module functions depends on your role and access rights. If you have administrator rights, all functions are available to you. With limited rights, only the set of functions needed for your work is displayed. If you need access to additional functions, contact support.

To sign in to PILOT Task Manager: Follow the link: https://tasks.pilot-gps.com 2. Enter the login and password of your account 3. If you want the system to remember your sign-in details, check the “Remember me” box — next time you will be signed in automatically 4. If needed, change the interface language. To do this, click the language selection button in the upper right corner and select the language you need 5. Click “Sign in” — you go to the electronic dispatch center

After signing in to the PTM electronic dispatch center, you land on the main page. It gathers the tools for working with tasks, users, and settings. Below is a brief overview of the main interface elements. Left menu The left menu contains the main sections of PILOT Task Manager. Left menu Click the item you need to go to that section. Main menu sections: Dashboard Shows the tasks you are working with: you can view, open, and manage them. Acts The list of acts related to tasks — for example, completion certificates or transfer-acceptance certificates. Users Management of system users: roles, access rights, and settings. Queue Tasks that have not been assigned yet or require processing. Reference books Auxiliary data and settings used when creating tasks. Settings General settings of the PTM module. Calendar / Calendar v2 View tasks as a calendar User account Settings of the current user and access to personal information. The left menu can be collapsed or expanded to free up more screen space. To do this, click the arrow at the bottom of the menu . The left arrow collapses the menu to icons, the right arrow expands it and shows the section names. Top bar The account and notification controls are located in the upper right corner of the top bar: Top bar Reset table settings — deletes the column order and filters saved in the browser. Use it to return tables to the default view if they display incorrectly Sound — turns sound notifications on and off Bell — shows system notifications, for example about new tasks Envelope — important messages, for example reminders about the remaining SMS balance Account name — shows the current user Language — select the interface language Sign out — sign out of the system Profile icon — go to the user account User account To go to the user account, click the profile icon in the upper right corner. In the user account you can view and edit your profile data: Name Email Password Date of birth Phone numbers Additional information: address, position, department, description To change the data, click , make the changes, and click “Save”. Workspace The workspace is in the center of the screen. It shows the main content of the selected section: task lists, the calendar, users, and so on. The workspace content changes depending on which section you selected in the left menu.

The task dashboard is a section in PTM where you can see all created tasks and work with them. This panel is a window for viewing and managing tasks that have been assigned or are in progress. In this article we cover: — how the task table is organized and what information its columns show — buttons and functions for quick task management — how to create, upload, and export tasks using templates — which actions are available when you right-click a task row — how to switch between workspaces Task table The center of the panel shows a table of created tasks. Each row in the table is a separate task. The table columns show task data, for example: Task ID — the unique task number in the system Received at — when the task was created Task type — planned execution time or estimated task time Order type — the task category (for example, Delivery , Booking , etc.) Execution status — the current task status Date and time (planned) — planned date and time of arrival/departure Date and time (actual) — actual arrival and departure time (from tracker or driver data) Vehicle — the vehicle assigned to the task Driver — full name of the driver assigned to the task Accepted by driver — when the driver confirmed receipt of the task Started moving — actual time the movement started Started execution — time the work on the task started Completed execution — time the task was completed Task control panel At the top of the task table is the task control panel — a set of buttons for managing tasks quickly. Task control panel Add — create a new task Edit — open the selected task for editing Delete — delete the selected tasks Filter settings — configure task filtering to show only the tasks you need Start vehicle reassignment — start automatic selection and replacement of vehicles in tasks. Use this button when you need to update vehicle assignments, for example when the vehicle fleet changes. When the process is finished, a window with the results appears: Tasks found — how many tasks were processed Virtual vehicles — how many of them were assigned to virtual vehicles Real vehicles – how many tasks were assigned to real vehicles Substitutions made – how many tasks received a different vehicle Tasks recalculated – how many tasks were recalculated (routes, time, mileage, etc. after the vehicle replacement) Task templates On the right side of the task list panel you will find three buttons for working with task templates. Download a task template — this button lets you download an Excel template for bulk task creation. Click this button — a window opens: In the “Template” field, select the task type you need, for example “Organization”, “Private person”, “Waybill”, “Booking”, and others. The choice determines which columns the Excel file has 2. Click the “Download” button to download the template file 3. Open the downloaded file and fill it in with your data — addresses, dates, drivers, cargo, and so on Open the panel for uploading tasks from a template — this button is used to upload tasks to the system from a previously filled template file that you downloaded with the button Click this button — a window opens: 1. Click the Excel icon and select the template file on your device Click the “Upload” button. The system reads the file rows and creates or updates tasks in the log based on the template data Export to Excel — this button downloads the task list in Excel format Click this button — a window opens: 1. In the “Template” field, select a template. The choice determines which columns the Excel file has 2. In the “From” and “To” fields, specify the period for which to export tasks 3. If you want only the tasks displayed in the table with your filters applied (by status, vehicle, etc.) to be included in Excel, check the “Apply current filters” box. 4. Click “Download”, and the system generates an Excel file with tasks according to the selected template and filters. The download template works only if it has been set up in the system beforehand. If the template is not set up, the system shows an error. The setup is done in the “Templates” section by editing the template you need: there you set the parameters that are visible in the task table and exported to Excel. Task menu When you right-click a task row in the log, the task menu opens, offering various actions for the selected task: 1. Create from template Creates a new task by copying the main fields from the current task (client, route, cargo, parameters, etc.) so you don t have to fill them in again. The task is copied with the status “Not assigned”. 2. Pin task The logistician assigns themselves as responsible for completing the task 3. Export for requester Exports the task data to a file that can be sent to the requester (client). This export works through a configured template. 4. Assign logistician Opens a submenu for selecting the logistician who will be responsible for completing this task. 5. Edit Open the task card to change its parameters 6. Delete Delete the task from the system 7. Status audit Show the history of task status changes 8. Task audit The full history of changes to the task (creation, editing, logistician assignment, etc.). 9. Set status Opens a submenu for selecting a new task status, for example “Closed”, “Client refusal”, “Visit”, “En route”, and others. 10. Signatories Lets you view or assign responsible signatories for the task or documents related to it. 11. Print Print the task document. 12. Completion certificate Generates and prints the completion certificate for the task; available after the task is completed and if there is data for the certificate. Some menu items may be grayed out and unavailable until the task reaches the required status or the necessary data is filled in. Selecting a workspace on the dashboard Above the task control panel and the task table there are buttons that open additional workspaces: Resources Tasks Signature Tenders Resources Clicking it opens a panel showing resources — vehicles and drivers. In this section you can see: Resource status (online/offline) Current or nearest task Schedule and base address Use this area to track which resources are free, which are busy, and who can be assigned to the next task. Tasks The main workspace where all tasks are displayed. Here you can: — create, edit, and filter tasks — assign resources — track task execution statuses Signature A section for working with electronic signatures on tasks and documents. Tenders A section for working with transportation tenders. With this panel you can: — create tenders based on tasks — send tenders to contractors and carriers — track the proposals received

To create a new task in PTM, click the “Add” button above the task table on the dashboard — the task card opens. The task card is a form where you set all the important trip parameters. It is divided into several blocks: Upper part (left) Template — select the task type that determines the field structure for this task Vehicle — select the vehicle that will perform the trip Driver and Driver phone — enter the driver s full name and contact number Trailer Plate — the trailer number, if a trailer is used for transportation Route Name — internal route identification Cargo Name — enter the cargo name Minimum / Maximum Temperature — if the transportation requires a temperature regime, enter the minimum and maximum temperatures Upper part (right) Task information — shows the main route data here: Address list — the main address/route, with the ability to edit, delete, or add new route points. Details: Route point coordinates Redirect this point — use the point as a redirect address Visit time — planned arrival time Warehouse — the name of the warehouse or point Stay time — how long the vehicle must spend at the point Radius — allowed deviation from the route point (in meters) Add address — a button to add another route point Start time and End time — specify the time frame for completing the task Description — a field for a free-form comment on the task Completion certificate If a completion certificate template has been created in advance for the task template, it can be linked to the task. In this case, in the Pilot Driver mobile app the driver can not only complete the task but also fill in the completion certificate as a report. Two setup options are available: Certificate for a route point — lets you assign a separate certificate template to a specific route point. Select the template you need from the list of previously created completion certificate templates. Main task certificate — a certificate template assigned to the whole task. It is selected in the lower part of the task card. If no separate certificate template is selected for a route point, the main task certificate is used. After the task is created, the selected certificates are available to the driver in the Pilot Driver app. The driver can fill them in either for individual route points or for the task as a whole — depending on the settings specified when the task was created. Map The map shows the route with all the points included in the task marked. Lower part Counterparties — in this block you can select the company that will be linked to the task Certificate template — select the completion certificate forms, if such a template has been set up in the system Control buttons at the bottom of the card: Back — if you changed your mind about saving the task, you can return to the task table without saving the changes Save — when you have entered all the data, click this button to save the task and put it into work Forecast — use this button to calculate the route forecast How to create a task from a template To quickly create a new task based on an existing one, use the “Create from template” function: 1. Right-click the task row in the task table. 2. In the task menu that appears, select “Create from template” 3. The system automatically creates a new task with all the main data copied from the original task (for example, client, route, cargo, parameters). 4. After that you can edit the task by selecting “Edit” in the menu. You go to the task card, where you can make the necessary changes.

In this article we look at additional task actions that help you control task execution, and explain: — how to track how a task is being executed by the system and the driver — how to use the waybill — how to start task recalculation The task table has an “Actions” column with icons for performing operations on a task. Visualization of task progress Click the icon , and the task execution chart opens. The chart helps you track how the task was planned, how the system is executing it, and how the driver is actually executing it. Route progress Click the icon , and the waybill with route information opens. The waybill is a detailed report on how the vehicle drove its route. Use it to track the actual task execution by comparing planned and actual data. Main elements of the waybill The task parameters are shown at the top, such as: Task ID Date and time Execution status The center of the screen contains the table of route points . Each row corresponds to a separate route point (address). Main columns of the waybill table: Actions — this column contains icons for working with route points. For example: Mark geofence entry Mark geofence entry (ignoring location) Mark geofence exit Change the working radius of the geofence — click the point and specify the new radius Change the location and radius of the geofence using the marker on the map — move the marker on the map and save the changes Save changes — confirm the changes to the marker Address — the full address of each route point Type — the point type (for example, loading, unloading, intermediate point) Actual distance and time — the actual distance the vehicle traveled and the actual travel time Planned values — the planned time and distance for this route point You can configure the waybill table columns as you like. Choose which parameter columns to display: 1. In the header of any column, click the arrow . A menu with column settings appears, where you can: • Sort the data in ascending or descending order • Choose which columns to show in the table 2. To choose which columns to show: Click “Columns” — a list of parameters available for display opens Check the parameters you want to see On the right of the waybill is the map with the route : — route points are numbered — the red dashed line is the planned route on the map — the green line is the actual route — the current or last recorded location of the vehicle is marked When working with the map, you can use the following tools: Zooming There are several ways to change the map scale: 1. Buttons on the map toolbar and In the upper left part of the map there are buttons for quickly zooming in and out 2. Mouse scroll wheel Scroll the mouse wheel: away from you — the map gets larger, toward you — smaller. The cursor indicates which area you want to examine in more detail. 3. Mouse double-click Double-click the left mouse button at any point on the map — it zooms in immediately. Measuring distance between points This tool helps you calculate distances between any points on the map. How to use it: Click on the map to mark the first point 2. Click again to mark the second point 3. A line with the distance appears between the points If you need to measure several segments, keep clicking on the map to add new points. The length of each segment is shown next to it. Measuring area This tool helps you calculate the area of the section you select on the map. How to use it: 1. On the map, mark the corners of the shape you want to measure one after another 2. When you finish drawing the shape, the program calculates and shows its area Printing the map This function prints the current map view. When you click the print button , four print orientation options are offered: 1. Landscape — the map is printed in horizontal orientation. This orientation is convenient for displaying extended areas or objects arranged horizontally. 2. Portrait — the map is printed in vertical orientation. This format suits areas that are elongated vertically. 3. Auto — the system automatically selects the best print orientation depending on the current map view and its proportions. 4. Custom — select this option if you want to print only a certain area of the map. To do this, select the part of the map you need with the mouse, and it is sent to print. Viewing traffic The traffic view function shows current road congestion using color indication: Green — free-flowing traffic Yellow — moderate congestion Red — heavy congestion To turn on traffic display, check this option in the upper right part of the map. Selecting a map You can choose from several map types to display space in the PTM interface. The map type is the base layer of the cartographic image used in the monitoring system to display spatial data. To change the map, click the map selection button . The bottom of the map shows route parameters that help you track its execution: Route parameters Distance — total mileage on the route (for example, 36.59 km) Driving time — how long the vehicle was actually on the road, excluding stops Total time — the total route execution time, including driving and all stops At the bottom of the “Waybill” window there is a route player that shows the vehicle s movement along the route in real time. Route player Click Play ▶ to start route playback. The vehicle icon moves along the track from start to end. The scroll bar (timeline) shows the entire route interval. By dragging the slider, you can manually jump to any moment of the route and see the vehicle s exact position on the map Timeline Below the scroll bar the following are shown Date and time (for example, 14.08.2025, 15:55) — the moment corresponding to the current slider position Speed (for example, 6 km/h) — the vehicle s speed on the current section of the route Additional player functions: Follow — if you check the box next to the eye icon, you will follow the vehicle on the map during route playback. Playback speed control — with the slider on the right you can speed up or slow down route playback Task recalculation Click the icon , and the process of recalculating all task parameters based on current data starts. You can use task recalculation if new data has arrived from the tracker or if the task settings were changed and the calculations need to be updated without manual editing. During recalculation: — the system rebuilds the route points based on updated data — new settings are taken into account: auto statuses, auto forecasts, changes in templates and other parameters — the system recalculates task and point statuses, planned and actual times, mileage, and parking times

In the “Acts” section you can view all acts created for completed tasks. An act is an official document confirming that the work on a task has been done. Filtering acts To quickly find the act you need, use the “Search” bar — enter the task ID, act ID, name, address, or any other text related to the act. You can also filter acts by period. To do this, select the date in the “From” and “To” fields. Then click “Set date filter” . To reset the filter, click “Clear filter” . Actions with acts The main data is displayed for each act: Unique number and name of the act The address the act was issued for Task name and type The driver and vehicle that did the work Start, acceptance, and completion times On the right of each act row there are buttons for working with it: View act — opens the act for viewing Export act — save the act to your computer Print act — print the act for physical documentation Delete act record — delete the act if it is no longer needed

In the “Users” section you can manage all system users: dispatchers, logisticians, drivers, administrators, and other employees. Here you see the list of all users and can configure system access for each of them. Each row in the users table is a separate user. You will see: Login — the user name for signing in to the system Email — the work email address Full name — the full name Phone — the contact number Role — for example, logistician, dispatcher, administrator Driver — a mark if the account is linked to a driver Actions with users Above the table there are several buttons for managing users: Add — create a new user by specifying a login, password, contact details, and access rights Edit — change the information of the selected user Delete — delete the user account Download — export user information to Excel Upload — upload user information from a previously prepared file Update drivers — update the data of driver users Show drivers — if you check this box, driver accounts are also shown in the list How to add a user 1. Click the “Add” button at the top of the screen to open the new user card 2. Fill in the main information: Login — the name the user will use to sign in to the system Email — work email for notifications and access Password — create a password and confirm it Full name — the employee s full name Phone — contact number Address — work address, if needed Signatories — select a signatory template if this user will sign documents Permission templates — select a ready-made set of rights for the user (for example, Administrator, Logistician, Driver) Position — specify the position (logistician, driver, dispatcher, etc.) Passport — enter passport details if required User color — select the color that will be used to highlight this user in the system Description — add a comment or note 3. Configure access rights On the right of the user card there is a block with check boxes where you can configure exactly which actions are allowed for this user. Check the rights you need, and they are activated for this account. 4. Save the user card When all data is filled in and the rights are configured, click “Save”. The new user appears in the list and can sign in to the system with the specified login and password. If you changed your mind, click “Cancel” and the changes are not saved. How to edit a user To edit user data, select the user in the list and click the “Edit” button at the top of the table. The card opens, where you can make the necessary changes. You can also double-click the user s row, and the card opens automatically. After editing the user card, click the “Save” button to save your changes.

The “Queue” section shows tasks that are waiting to be sent to the driver for execution. The table shows information for each task: Task ID — the unique task number Task name — a short task description Driver — who will perform the task Time sent for execution — when the task was put in the queue While tasks are in the queue, you can select a task and click “Delete” to remove it from the queue. If the queue is empty, it means there are currently no tasks waiting to be sent for execution.

In the “Reference books” section you can create and configure data lists used when working with tasks, vehicles, and drivers. For example, these can be lists of drivers, task statuses, or cargo types. Reference books make creating tasks easier, because you only need to select the data you need from ready-made lists instead of entering it manually every time. How to enable the “Reference books” section 1. The “Reference books” section is not always available in the PTM menu and is enabled on request. To enable this section, contact technical support 2. After it is enabled, the section is empty, because there are no ready-made reference books in the system. You can add and configure reference books yourself, creating the lists you need How to create a reference book 1. Open the “Reference books” section 2. In the “Reference book list” panel, click the “Add” button 3. The “Add new reference book” window opens On the left, set the general information about the reference book: Name — the reference book name (for example: “Cargo type”, “Cancellation reasons”, “Service types”) Alias — the technical name of the reference book Primary key, Secondary key, Display key, Parent alias — these fields relate to the reference book structure and links with other tables. If you are not sure about the meaning of these parameters, it is better to consult technical support. On the right, set the structure of the reference book rows: 4. Click “Add” above the table on the right 5. Specify: Column alias — the internal field name Type — select the data type Check the flags as needed: “Empty value” — allow empty values for this field “Unique” — the field must contain unique data “Formula” — if the field will be calculated by a formula 6. Repeat steps 4–5 for all the fields you want in the reference book. When the structure is set up: 7. Click “Save” 8. The new reference book appears in the list on the left 9. Select it in the “Reference book list” — the “Reference book data” table opens on the right, where you can: — add rows — edit and delete records If creating the reference book structure is difficult, you can contact technical support. Then, once the structure is ready, you can fill it with values yourself. Reference book examples In the “Reference books” section you can create and configure various data lists that help simplify your work with tasks. The initial list is always empty, and you need to fill it with the information you need. Let s look at a few examples of reference books you can set up. Templates reference book The “Templates” tab stores the list of all task and document types. Each template determines which fields are shown in the task card, which columns the dispatcher sees in the log, and which completion certificate forms are used for the task. How to add a new template: 1. Open Reference books → Templates 2. Click “Add” . The “Add template” window opens In it, fill in: Enter a clear template name, for example: “City delivery”, “Service call”, etc. 2. Describe what this template is for 3. Set the additional flags: Default template — if enabled, this template is filled in automatically when a new task is created Send SMS to driver — when a task is created from this template, an SMS is sent to the driver Send SMS to initiator — the task initiator receives an SMS 4. Header template — this field stores the technical description of the table “header” and the Excel export. If you don t know what to enter here, contact technical support. 5. Click “Submit” — the new template appears in the list After you create a template and it appears in the list, you need to fill it with fields. Click “Parameters” to configure: — which fields are in the task card — in what order they are shown — which columns are in the task log — which fields are mandatory, service fields, etc. How to add a new field to a template: 1. In the “Templates” section, select the template you need 2. Click “Parameters” — the field table opens 3. Click “Add” 4. In the add form, fill in: Type — select the data type Alias — the internal field name in Latin letters Name — what the field will be called Group name Default value Weight — determines the order in which the field is displayed Settings — check the boxes: — Value is a formula result? — the field is filled in automatically by a formula — Field can be empty — if enabled, the field is optional — Field is active — the field is used and shown in the form — Field can be deleted — allows deleting this field from the template in the future — Visible only when editing — the field is visible only when the task is being edited and is hidden in view mode — Show warehouse name / Show order ID — special options for templates that need this data — Is a key index for search — the field will be used for search Field permissions: — Permission templates — select the roles (rights templates) that the field will be available to. — Deny editing for permission templates — roles for which the field will be read-only \ 3. After filling in, click “Save” in the parameter form. The new field appears in this template How to create a completion certificate for a template: 1. Go to Reference books → Templates 2. Select the template you need 3. At the top, click the “Completion certificate” button If this item is not displayed, it needs to be added in the rights of the permission template . If you have problems, contact technical support. 4. A window with the list of certificates for this template opens 5. In the window, click “Add” — the “Add completion certificate” form opens 6. Fill in the fields at the top: Name — what the certificate will be called Existing file — if you want to use an existing file template as a basis. File — if needed, you can upload your own template file from disk Compose the certificate text — write the text of the certificate on the “Editor” tab To have data from the task automatically inserted into the certificate: 1. On the right, in the “Certificate parameters” block, select the parameter you need: “Basic” tab — task number, dates, addresses, amounts, etc.; “Executor” tab — what the driver fills in the certificate in the mobile app. The fields for driver certificates must appear after the basic data in the certificate text “Template” tab — fields specific to this particular template 2. In the tab lists, select the fields you need (for example, text fields, check boxes, signature, etc.) and copy their names into the certificate text. 3. If needed, mark this certificate as the default for the template 4. Click “Save” Now, for tasks of this template, you can print the certificate in the configured form. Signatories reference book This is where you set up the people who will sign documents and certificates. With signature templates you can easily define who must sign documents and in what order. Task types This is where you set up various task types, for example “Delivery”, “Repair”, “Loading”. You can also specify priorities and a description. Task priorities This reference book sets various task urgency levels: “Not urgent”, “Urgent”, “Very urgent”. Task statuses This reference book defines all possible task statuses: “New”, “In progress”, “Completed”, “Sent to driver”, and so on. Address classifier This reference book stores addresses that have already been used in tasks. Instead of entering each address manually when creating a new task, you can select the address you need from this list. Drivers reference book Here you can store information about drivers working under the contract. This reference book is needed to assign such drivers to tasks. Notification settings In this reference book you set which notifications to send and how — via SMS, email, Push notifications, or Telegram. To add a notification, click and fill in the notification form: 1. “Notification information” block: Name — create a clear rule name, for example “Unloading time exceeded” Notification — select which event triggers the rule Resources — if the notification does not apply to all, select specific vehicles/resources. If it should be triggered for all — check “All”. 2. “Parameters” block Event color — select the color used to mark the notification in the interface Select delivery channels: — E-mail — specify e-mail addresses in the field below — SMS — specify phone numbers in the field below — Telegram — Pop-up window — Push to the mobile app For all users — if the notification should be visible to everyone Geofence address — specify a point/geofence if the notification is tied to a specific place 3. “Condition” block Here you specify exactly when the notification is triggered: Template type — if needed, limit the rule to specific task templates, or check “All”. Task types — select which types the notification applies to Device statuses — which tracker/vehicle statuses the rule works on Task statuses — for which task statuses Time in status, min — if it should be triggered not immediately, but only if the task is “stuck” in a status for longer than the specified time Check the filled-in fields and click “Save” at the bottom right. The new rule appears in the notification settings list and starts working according to the specified conditions. Permission templates Here you can configure sets of access rights for users so that each of them has only the necessary information.

In the “Settings” section, the administrator can set the PTM system operating parameters, configure integrations with external services, and define the default system behavior. All available settings sections are described below. Let s look at the available settings. GIS integration settings This section configures the map services used for working with addresses, geocoding, and travel time calculation. 1. Connecting map services You can use services such as OSM, DaData, Google, HERE, Yandex, City Guide, and others. To do this, specify: Host, API key, or Token Check boxes: — Use for geocoder — the service searches for addresses and coordinates — Use for forecasting — the service calculates routes and travel time 2. Geocoding priority: Set the order in which services are queried — the service with the highest priority is used first. 3. Map layers: Choose which maps (OSM, Yandex, Google, and others) are available in the system 4. Forecast parameters: Set the parameters for calculating the forecast time: — Average speed — Average loading/unloading time — Maximum driving time Calendar settings This is where you configure how tasks are displayed in the calendar. 1. Grouping by color: By task type — tasks are displayed in different colors depending on their type (for example, delivery, repair, etc.). By vehicle — tasks have different colors depending on which vehicle is assigned to perform them. 2. Show active tasks only: If you enable this setting, the calendar shows only tasks with the following statuses: New In queue Not assigned Sent to driver Accepted En route In progress Pending approval Task settings Use the task settings to define how the dispatch system works: 1. Requests: You can specify the request storage and the request template: Request storage — the reference book of requests received through the PARUS API integration. It is used to match requests with tasks in PTM Request template — a pre-configured template used to group and process related tasks 2. Color highlighting: Configure how tasks are highlighted in the table and calendar: — By task type — each task has its own color depending on the type (for example, delivery, repair, etc.) — By user — the color depends on which user is assigned as responsible for the task (for example, for different drivers or dispatchers). The user color is set in the user s card. 3. Closing reasons: You can enable selecting the task cancellation reason from a previously prepared reference book. 4. Auto statuses by geofence Auto statuses let you automatically change the task state based on visits to route geofences. Geofence radius, m — the radius of the virtual geofence automatically created around a route point Geofence accuracy, m — an additional value by which the geofence radius is increased when processing the task Start in, min — defines how many minutes before the planned start time the task can automatically move to processing Finish after, min — defines the time after the planned task end, after which the system can finish it automatically Mark time, sec — the minimum time the vehicle must stay inside the geofence for a visit to be recorded. The check is performed both when entering and when leaving the geofence Enable cyclic routes — allows correct processing of routes where a vehicle repeatedly moves between the same points and then returns to the base. Completion function — defines the condition for automatic task completion. The following options are available: — Return to base — the task is completed after the vehicle appears in the base geofence again. The following can be used as the base: the first route point the last route point that matches the first a point with the “Base” subtype an alternative geofence created in the PILOT system — Finish by shift — the task is completed after the estimated execution time ends: Planned end time + the value of the “Finish after” parameter — Last waybill address (entry) — the task is completed after entry into the geofence of the last route point is recorded — Last waybill address (exit) — the task is completed after exit from the geofence of the last route point is recorded.
