Additional task handling rules let you configure automation and refine task processing rules: Enable task auto-completion — forcibly completes tasks the specified number of minutes after the planned end time. Not recommended for use together with auto statuses Task execution time — used when calculating the planned end time if the execution time field cannot be edited manually Allow sending unassigned tasks to all drivers — lets drivers pick tasks themselves from the common queue in the mobile app Enable editing tasks in the table for the current day only — limits editing of tasks in the table to the current day. Works together with user permissions only for the dynamically generated task table (the table is generated dynamically based on all task templates). Enable task autofill by key fields — the system automatically fills in data from previously created tasks based on the values entered by the user Disable selection of system task types — hides service task types when creating new tasks Enable color highlighting of task statuses — highlights status cells in the table according to the current task status The current user is the initiator by default — when a task is created, the initiator is automatically set to the current user Enable tooltips for table rows — brief task information is displayed when you hover the cursor over a row Close task after signing — the task is closed automatically after the entire approval and document signing chain is completed Enable waypoint building bypassing auto statuses — creates waypoints based on the route regardless of how the auto status mechanism works Enable geofence priority on points — if a route point is linked to a PILOT system geofence, that geofence is used to record the visit Do not use the first point as the last point — disables automatic route closing and affects waybill generation Enable selection of a replacement vehicle — lets you assign a backup vehicle without changing the main vehicle assigned to the task Enable synchronization of address editing with the address classifier — when an address is changed in a task, the changes are automatically saved in the address reference book Integrations Integration with external services allows the system to exchange data with other platforms. You can: 1. Connect external services 2. Set up automatic data import and export via API, email, or webhooks 3. Specify which events and data must be passed to the system and back Integrations are used for: creating notifications automatically importing tasks from email using a specified template (for example, for the “Magnit” system) To connect an integration, you need to: 1. Select the integration group 2. Select the integration system 3. Fill in the connection parameters If only the notification mechanism is used, for integration with the “Magnit” system it is enough to specify the email address without a password. Webhook settings The following parameters are available for each integration: Webhook URL — the address for sending webhooks Webhook headers — additional HTTP headers, for example an authorization token Webhook parameters — the payload sent in the webhook Special functions are used for automatic data substitution: fn[getApiKey] — get the API key from the configuration (for the ERP Sarmix system only) fn[getAgentId] — get the vehicle ID from the PILOT system fn[getCurrentAgentLocation] — get the current vehicle location fn[getCurrentUTC] — get the current time of the vehicle packet in seconds fn[getCurrentZoneId] — get the ID of the geofence the vehicle is in fn[getTaskId] — get the ID of the task the vehicle is performing fn[getErpOrderId] — get the request ID (for the ERP Sarmix system only) fn[getCurrentSpeed] — get the current vehicle speed fn[getVehicleNumber] — get the vehicle number Webhook parameters configuration example The “Webhook parameters” field contains a JSON object with the data to be passed to the external system. Special functions are used for automatic value substitution. { "access_token": "fn[getApiKey]", "agent_id": "fn[getAgentId]", "geolocation": "fn[getCurrentAgentLocation]", "time_event": "fn[getCurrentUTC]", "zone_id": "fn[getCurrentZoneId]", "pilot_task_id": "fn[getTaskId]", "erp_order_id": "fn[getErpOrderId]", "speed": "fn[getCurrentSpeed]", "vehiclenumber": "fn[getVehicleNumber]" } As a result, the system automatically substitutes the actual values, for example: { "access_token": "123456789abcdef", "agent_id": "4521", "geolocation": "55.751244,37.618423", "time_event": "1750054800", "zone_id": "125", "pilot_task_id": "98765", "erp_order_id": "ORD-4567", "speed": "68", "vehiclenumber": "А123ВС777" } Additional integration parameters Algorithm ID — the identifier of an algorithm created in the PILOT system for processing notifications by an operator Algorithm data — the payload passed to the PILOT algorithm when a notification is triggered. It is configured by technical support when needed. The composition and structure of the data depend on the specific algorithm and processing scenario. Algorithm data configuration example { "-6": { "text": "Выполните действия", "options": [ "Действие 1", "Действие 2", "Действие 3" ] } } Algorithm timer — the algorithm execution wait time in seconds Sensor ID — the sensor identifier from the PILOT system Emails — the list of email addresses for sending notifications Account settings Here you can configure the main system parameters for your account: 1. Queue for the mobile app: Enable the task queue for drivers and define whether they pick tasks from the common queue themselves or tasks are assigned automatically. 2. Integration and profile settings: — Set the login and password — Specify the time zone and default language for the whole system — Enable the ExactFarming integration and configure the token for this integration 3. “Logistician – Dispatcher” workflow chain: Enable the workflow chain and select the permission template that will be used for logisticians and dispatchers. 4. Phone interface: Enable the new interface for mobile devices, and also configure automatic generation of completion certificates. 5. Sending messages: Configure the system to send notifications to requesters and drivers when needed 6. Event notifications: Configure notifications about various errors, such as geocoding problems, missing vehicle or track, incorrect time intervals, geofence overlaps, and track gaps.

The calendar shows all tasks as a schedule and helps you plan work by date. Main calendar elements: The center of the screen shows the calendar grid, where you can switch between different views: Day — for a detailed view of tasks for a specific day Week — to view all tasks for one week Month — for a general overview of all tasks for the month The calendar cells show tasks with the time and task number. In the filter on the left you can select which task types to show in the calendar. For example, you can filter only logistics, delivery, loading, repair, or other task types. Each task type is assigned its own color in the calendar. Main buttons and actions: Create — create a new task from the calendar Today — return to the current day in the calendar Arrows — switch to the previous or next period. “Day / Week / Month” switches — select the display scale you need in the calendar Search by task ID — enter the task number in the search field to find it in the calendar and click Icon — opens additional calendar display settings How to create a task in the calendar 1. Click the day you need in the calendar grid 2. A window for creating a new task appears on the screen 3. Enter the data needed for the task 4. Click “Submit” to save and launch the task Calendar V2 Calendar V2 is a schedule for managing tasks distributed across vehicles. In this version of the calendar you can see which task is assigned to each vehicle on a specific day. Calendar structure: The left column shows the list of all vehicles used to perform tasks. The top row shows the days of the week with dates. This way, in one row you see which tasks are assigned to each vehicle on each day. The cells show the tasks assigned to a specific vehicle on the selected day. Main actions and buttons: Refresh — click this button to reload the calendar and pull in the latest task changes Settings — open additional calendar display settings Arrows — use the arrows to page the calendar forward and back to view tasks for future or past days If you want to view a task or make changes to it, double-click the cell — the task card opens, where you can edit all the necessary parameters.

When you select the “User account” section in the menu, you go to the user account. In the user account you can view and edit your profile data: Name Email Password Date of birth Phone numbers Additional information: address, position, department, description To change the data, click “Edit”, make the changes, and click “Save”. You can also go to the user account by clicking the profile icon in the upper right corner of the top bar.

The “Atom” module creates a network connection with the auto-conductors on vehicles and opens remote access to their file system. Main module features: Real-time monitoring of auto-conductor status Remote download of video recordings from DVR cameras Download of files from passenger counting cameras Retrieval of diagnostic information about device operation Monitoring auto-conductor status When working with the “Atom” module, the object list shows information about the status of auto-conductors: Connection status — the icon shows whether the auto-conductor is on or off . You immediately see whether the device is available for work. Commands sent to an auto-conductor are processed only when the object comes online. If you see that the device is off, the commands are queued and executed as soon as the device connects to the network. Additional columns in the object list for device monitoring: 1 — Atom IP — shows the IP address of the auto-conductor 2 — Atom Update — shows information about the last device update 3 — Atom status — the auto-conductor connection status To learn how to configure the columns of the object table, see here . The tooltip with Atom information contains: — the Atom IP address — power state — current device status Uploading and downloading files from the auto-conductor How to upload files: In the main menu, go to the “Atom” section 2. Select an object from the list, which contains the following information: Agent ID — the object identifier Object — the object name License — the license assigned to the object MAC — the MAC address of the object Valid until — the auto-conductor license expiration date Comment — a user comment 3. After selecting the object, go to the file system. The file system shows the files available from the object with the following information: Folder — the file location in the folder hierarchy File name — the file name Size — the file size Date — the file creation date Available video file types: Files from /mnt/VREG — DVR recordings Files from /Video/ — recordings from passenger counting cameras 4. Find the files to upload to the server. To search, select the folder you need from the drop-down list and set the file creation date using the calendar. 5. Select the files you need by checking the boxes next to them. 6. Click the “Add selected to upload queue” button . In the file system, use two buttons to get up-to-date information: The “Refresh” button — click this button to refresh the entire list of folders and files. Use this button if you have connected to the device and want to see the current folder structure, or if changes were made to the file system. The “Refresh file information” button — click this button to refresh file details (size, creation date) in the current folder without reloading the whole structure. Use this button if you need to see up-to-date information about the files in the selected folder. How to download files: Go to the “Uploaded files” tab, which shows files that have already been uploaded from Atom to the server. 2. On this tab you see a list of files with the following information: Agent ID — the agent the file was uploaded from Object — the source object of the file Time — the file upload time Name — the file name Size — the size of the uploaded file 3. To download the file you need to your device, click the download icon next to it.

The “Driving quality” module helps you assess drivers driving style and identify dangerous or uneconomical maneuvers. The system automatically analyzes data received from the device installed on the vehicle and records various events, for example: — sharp acceleration — harsh braking — sharp turns — speeding — prolonged idling — other events configured in the rules For each recorded violation the system can assign penalty points. Based on this data, Eco-driving reports are generated, which let you assess the driving quality of each driver or vehicle. Driving quality events are generated from data transmitted by the device installed on the vehicle. The available events depend on the device model and the parameters it supports. The overall driving quality score is calculated taking into account the recorded events, the assigned penalty points, the selected penalty type, and the configured ECO weights.

Driving quality rules define which driver actions the system treats as violations and how they are taken into account when assessing driving quality. Each rule monitors a specific parameter received from the device installed on the vehicle, for example speed, acceleration, or idling duration. If the value meets the specified conditions, the system records a driving quality event. For each rule you can set: — the parameter to monitor — the event recording conditions — the event type — the message displayed in reports — the number of penalty points and how they are assigned You can create any number of rules and configure them to suit your vehicles, the installed equipment, and your company s requirements. How to open the driving quality settings 1. In the user account, double-click the vehicle you need in the object list 2. In the object card, open the “Driving quality” tab On this tab you can create and change the rules by which the system detects violations. Control rules The center of the window contains the rules table. Each row is a separate rule by which the system analyzes data received from the device. If the value meets the specified conditions, the system records a driving quality event. You can create any number of rules and configure them to suit your vehicles and equipment. Rule parameters Column Description Field The sensor or parameter to be monitored. For example, speed, acceleration, ignition, or another parameter received from the device Formula An additional mathematical or logical expression for processing the value before the check Type The type of driving quality event that is recorded when the condition is met. The system uses the type to classify the event and calculate “Eco-driving” indicators. You can use the built-in types or create your own Message The text displayed in reports when the event is recorded. For example: Harsh Braking or Speeding Min. The minimum value from which the rule starts to trigger Max. The maximum value at which the event is still considered a violation. For example, if you specify the range 132–250 km/h, a violation is recorded at a speed within this range Period The interval in seconds during which several identical triggers are counted as one event. For example, if you specify 600 seconds for idling, a new violation is recorded only 10 minutes after the previous one Penalty The number of penalty points assigned for the event. It can be 0 — in this case the event is recorded, but no penalty points are assigned Penalty type Calculation method for penalty points Main control types “Eco-driving” reports most often use four main event types: Acceleration — sharp vehicle acceleration Braking — harsh braking Cornering — a sharp maneuver when taking a turn Speed — exceeding the set speed threshold If needed, you can create your own event types . Penalty types For each rule you can choose one of three ways of assigning penalty points. Simple A fixed number of points specified in the “Penalty” field is assigned. For example, if the penalty is 5, 5 points are assigned for each violation. Weighted The penalty is calculated taking the severity of the violation into account. The more the violation exceeds the set threshold, the greater the total number of penalty points. This type is used when you need to consider not only the fact of the violation but also its seriousness. Multiplier The number of points is calculated by the formula: Violation value × Penalty For example: violation value — 5 penalty — 2 The total number of penalty points is 10. This mode is convenient when the size of the penalty should depend on the magnitude of the violation. How to create a rule You can create any number of control rules yourself. To do this: 1. On the “Driving quality” tab, click the “Add rule” button 2. A new row appears in the table 3. Fill in the rule parameters Specify: 1. Field — the sensor or parameter to be monitored 2. Formula, if needed 3. Event type — select from the list. If the type you need is not there, you can create it yourself 4. The message that will be displayed in reports 5. The minimum and maximum values that define the range in which the event is considered a violation 6. The period for merging repeated events 7. The penalty size and penalty type After filling in the parameters, click “Save”. After saving, the rule starts being used when processing data received from the device. To change a rule, change the parameters you need in the corresponding fields of the rule row. To delete a rule, click the icon in the row of the rule you need, then save the changes. Additional penalties At the bottom of the window there are penalty settings that apply independently of individual rules. The following parameters are available: Penalty for entering a restricted geofence — assigned when the vehicle enters a restricted geofence Penalty for an unauthorized driver — assigned if the vehicle is driven by a driver who is not permitted to operate this object Penalty for speeding per minute / unit — additional points for exceeding the set speed limit Enter the required values and save the settings.

A rule template is a saved set of driving quality settings. With a template you can apply ready-made rules to a vehicle without configuring each rule manually. You can pick a template by device type and vehicle type, apply it to an object, or create your own. In this article: Ready-made templates How to apply a template How to create a template How to set up template applicability Importing and exporting rules Ready-made templates To open the template list: 1. Open the vehicle card 2. Go to the “Driving quality” tab 3. Expand the “Template” list The list shows the suitable templates and a separate “Universal templates” group. Universal templates are not tied to a specific device or vehicle type, so they can be applied to different vehicles. The system also provides ready-made templates for certain telematics equipment models: CIPIA FLEX — for devices working over the Flex protocol, for example Smart 2333 GB100 ECO — for Queclink GB100 GV65 ECO — for Queclink GV65 Ruptela Teltonika Choose the template that matches the equipment and vehicle type. How to apply a template 1. Open the “Driving quality” tab 2. In the “Template” field, select the template you need 3. Click “Apply” 4. The rules from the template are loaded into the table. Check them and click “Save” at the bottom of the vehicle card. When a new vehicle is created, PILOT selects templates by device type and vehicle type. If the vehicle type is not specified, the “Passenger car” type is used for selection, but the field in the card is not filled in automatically. How to create your own template First set up the driving quality rules. To add a rule: 1. Click the plus icon 2. Fill in the rule parameters 3. Click “Save” in the rule row To save the configured rules as a template: 1. Click the save icon next to the “Template” list 2. In the “Save as template” window, specify: Template name Device type — optional Vehicle type — optional 3. Click “Save” If you leave the device type or vehicle type blank, the template can be used with any value of that parameter. The created template appears in the list of available templates. How to set up template applicability Applicability defines which devices and vehicles the template will be available for. Template scope A template can be linked: — to a device type and a vehicle type — to a device type only — to a vehicle type only — to neither type — such a template is considered universal If the device type is not specified, the template can be used with any device. If the vehicle type is not specified, the template suits all vehicle types. To set up applicability: In the upper right part of the window, find the tools for managing eco-driving settings Click the icon at the top of the “Driving quality” tab 3. In the “Template applicability” window, select: Device type Vehicle type Template Device type Vehicle type Template 3. Click “Link” In the “Device type” field you can select a specific equipment model. In the “Vehicle type” field you can select a specific vehicle type or leave the value “For all vehicle types”. In the “Template” field, select the template for which applicability is being set up. For example, a template can be linked to a FleetGuide device and the “Passenger car” vehicle type. To clear the selected value, click the cross icon in the corresponding field. After linking, PILOT takes the device type and vehicle type into account when selecting available templates. A template is not applied automatically: you choose it and confirm the application. After a template is applied, its rules are copied into the vehicle settings. If you change the rules manually, the settings will differ from the original template. Later changes to the template itself also will not change the settings of vehicles it was applied to earlier. Importing and exporting rules Import and export let you transfer rules between vehicles or save a copy of them. At the top of the “Driving quality” window, find the export and import tools. **Export ** — saves the current rules to a JSON file To do this: 1. Click the export button 2. Save the file to your computer All rule parameters are saved to the JSON file. **Import ** — loads a previously saved JSON file To do this: 1. Click the import button 2. Select the file 3. The settings are loaded into the table automatically Imported rules replace the current set of rules in the table. If needed, save the existing settings with export before importing a new file.

Driving quality types are event categories that the system uses to classify violations and generate “Eco-driving” reports. Each driving quality rule is linked to a specific event type. When the rule is triggered, the system records an event of the selected type. For example: Acceleration — sharp acceleration Braking — harsh braking Turn — sharp turn Speed — speeding Seat Belt — seat belt violation. Event types are stored in a separate reference book . When you create or change a rule, you select the type you need from this reference book in the “Type” field. If the standard types are not enough, you can create your own . After creation, the new type becomes available when setting up rules. How to open the driving quality types reference book 1. Open the “Driving quality” tab 2. In the upper right part of the window, find the tools for managing “Eco-driving” settings 3. Click the “Driving quality types” button The event types reference book opens. These are the types used when selecting a value in the “Type” column (Acceleration, Braking, Turn, Speed, Seat Belt) How to create a new type 1. In the event types reference book, click “Add” 2. Enter the event name 3. Click “Save”. After saving, the system automatically assigns the new type a unique identifier (ID). The system uses it to identify the event type unambiguously, and it does not need to be set manually. To change a type name, double-click the row, make the changes, and save them. To delete a type, use the “Delete” button . Delete types only if they are no longer used in rules. If a type is already in use, first replace it in the existing rules, and then delete it.

ECO weights (importance coefficients) define how strongly different types of violations affect the overall driving quality score. When the system records a driving quality event, it assigns penalty points. When the overall score is calculated, these points are taken into account using ECO weights. The higher the ECO weight, the more strongly violations of this type affect the overall driving quality score. Changing ECO weights does not affect event recording or the number of penalty points assigned. Only their influence on the overall score in Eco Driving reports changes. ECO weight settings apply to the whole account and are used when generating Eco Driving reports. Indicators The system uses the following indicators. Indicator Meaning Speeding Exceeding the speed limit Excess Idle Prolonged engine idling Harsh Brake Harsh braking Harsh Accel Sharp acceleration Harsh Corner Sharp turn The following are shown for each indicator: Numeric coefficient — the value the system uses when calculating penalty points Slider — lets you change the importance of the corresponding violation type Percentage — shows the contribution of this violation type to the overall score The total sum of all weights must be 100%. Example If you increase the ECO weight for Speeding, speeding affects the overall driving quality score more than the other violation types. The events themselves and the assigned penalty points do not change. How to set up ECO weights 1. Open the “ECO weights for driving” window 2. Change the values with the sliders 3. Make sure the sum of all ECO weights is 100% 4. Click “Save” to apply the current ECO weight values. They are saved as working settings that the system will use when calculating driving quality The weights most often changed are Harsh Brake and Harsh Accel, when you need to increase or reduce the influence of sharp maneuvers on the overall driving quality score. Additional commands are available at the bottom of the eco weights window: Update Defaults (Save as defaults) — saves the current values as defaults Load Defaults (Load defaults) — loads previously saved defaults Reset Defaults (Restore standard defaults) — returns the standard system settings: — Speeding — 58.3% — Excess Idle — 10.4% — Harsh Brake — 6.9% — Harsh Accel — 13.9% — Harsh Corner — 10.4%

The “Tachograph” module helps you track and analyze driver work based on data from the hardware. All data comes directly from the tachograph and cannot be changed manually. Use the module to track driver activity statuses: driving, rest, work, availability. Based on the activity data you can: understand how busy each driver is check whether work and rest regulations are observed analyze how the schedule was actually worked How to configure data for the module 1. Go to the admin panel, open the “Machines” tab and find the Object the tachograph works with 2. Right-click the selected Object — the context menu opens 3. Select “Edit” in the menu 4. In the Object settings window that opens, select the “Configuration” tab. 5. Add the module configuration with the button and click “Save” Which Sensors are required For the module to display reliable information, certain Sensors must be added to the Object card: Sensor purpose What it shows Sensor setup example Driver state Position of the driver mode switch: driving, rest, work, availability Card state Status of the driver card in the slot (inserted or not, in use or not) Tachograph mode Changes in the tachograph operating states For details on how to add Sensors, see the section “Sensors” How to view tachograph data 1. In the User account, go to the “Tachograph” section 2. Select the Object you want to analyze 3. Specify the period in the calendar — the days or hours you need data for 4. Click “Search” 5. You will see an activity summary: when the driver was driving, resting, available or working. The data is displayed as a clear interactive report on driver work and rest regimes for the selected period, broken down by days and weeks. How the system works internally The module receives data directly from the tachograph. This is “raw” technical data that the system converts into understandable states. This data is used to calculate driver activity statuses: driving, rest, work. How to decode tachograph data Let s look more closely at the tables with data received directly from the tachograph s digital interface — for example, via the CAN bus or another data transmission channel. This data is processed by the monitoring system and helps determine: Which driver card was installed (Table 1) What the status of each driver is — resting, working, driving the vehicle — as well as the current card state in each slot (Table 2) These parameters are generated as codes and bit values, so to be interpreted correctly they must be handled either by the system or by a specialist when configuring the hardware. Below is the decoding of this data according to the tachograph specification. Table 1 This table describes the structure of the packet that transmits the identification number of the driver card installed in the tachograph: 0x02 – driver card 1 or 2. The card number depends on the type of event for which this packet is generated. The codes of the events for which the packet is generated help determine exactly which card was installed and in what situation. Table 2 The table describes a data byte from the tachograph interface with ID: 98. This byte contains compressed information about the following parameters: The activity of each driver — rest, readiness for work, driving the vehicle, etc. The state of the card slots — whether a card is inserted or not, whether it is authorized or not. The byte is divided into bit fields — 8 bits in total, split into 4 groups of 2 bits, each responsible for a specific parameter. The information from this byte helps you: Connect external hardware to the tachograph Get accurate data on driver activity Configure the system so that it understands what exactly the driver is doing For example: if the value of bits 0–1 = 3, driver No. 1 is driving the vehicle. Calibration tables are also often built on the basis of this data. They are needed to convert the “raw” numbers from the tachograph data byte into understandable states. Instead of “raw” values such as 2 or 3, you will see “Rest” or “Card authorized”. One byte (8 bits) is split into four pairs of bits — each 2 bits are responsible for one state: Bits Parameter Values 0–1 Driver 1 activity 0, 1, 2, 3 2–3 Driver 1 card slot 0, 1, 2, 3 4–5 Driver 2 activity 0, 1, 2, 3 6–7 Driver 2 card slot 0, 1, 2, 3 Therefore you need to configure calibration tables to convert the values into an understandable driver activity and card state. Calibration table examples The “Driver state” calibration table. You use this table to decode bits 0–1 and 4–5 (driver activity). The “Card state” calibration table. You use this table for parameters 2–3 and 6–7 (driver card state). To learn how to configure a calibration table, read here . Where to view tachograph Reports The module generates a driver activity Report that helps you track: — periods when the driver is at the wheel — rest, availability and work time — work without a card or with an unauthorized card — time intervals for each driver

The accident detection module shows and processes “accident” events received from the vehicle. What the module consists of Notification settings — enabling the “Accident detection” Notification type in the “Contract settings” Event display in History — accident Events are saved in History and displayed on the Map and in charts How to enable Notifications 1. Go to the “Contract settings” 2. Open the “Notifications” tab 3. Click 4. In the list of Notification types, enable “Accident detection” 5. Click “Save” Once enabled, the system will monitor incoming Crash tags from the vehicle and send Notifications How Notifications are sent When an accident signal (a Crash tag) arrives from the vehicle, the system checks it: — if the data can be decoded (Crash_id), you will see the details in the Notification — if decoding is not possible, a standard message arrives: Crash detected! After an accident, the device may send the same Crash tag many times. So that you do not receive a stream of identical Notifications: 1. The system reacts only to the first signal and sends a Notification 2. Repeated signals are ignored until the first “clean” point without the accident tag arrives 3. If a new Crash tag arrives after that, you will receive a new Notification This way you get only one Notification per accident, not a stream of repeats. Accident history To find and view an accident Event: Go to the “History” section For accident Events to be displayed in “History” , enable them in “Contract settings” → “Map and geocoding” tab → “ Displaying events on the map ” section → “Accident detection” event 2. Select the dates of the suspected accident 3. Select the History Tracks 4. Open the “Events” tab in “History” 5. Find the Event address on the Map — it will be marked with a marker 6. Click the marker to see the Event chart What the chart shows The chart shows how the loads on the vehicle changed during the accident. The data comes from the accelerometer — a device that records acceleration and sudden changes in motion. The chart has three lines: Blue (X) — forward and backward movement of the vehicle (for example, acceleration, hard braking or a frontal impact). Purple (Y) — movement to the right and left (for example, a side impact or a sharp turn). Green (Z) — movement up and down (for example, hitting an obstacle, a bump or an impact from below). Sharp peaks and dips are the moment of impact. You can use them to see the nature of the collision: frontal, side or combined. Y axis (vertical) — shows the strength of acceleration / deceleration (in arbitrary accelerometer units) X axis (horizontal) — time (in milliseconds) What you can see on the chart In this example, before the accident the lines fluctuate around 0 — the vehicle is moving smoothly, without sharp acceleration. In the center there is a sharp dip downward (blue X and purple Y) — this is the moment of collision: strong braking with a lateral shift component. After the impact the lines return closer to zero, but a slight “ripple” remains — these are oscillations after the collision.

Purpose of the module Sensors are installed in containers and signal the PILOT platform when the container is filled up to the Sensor level. The Sensor is installed at a height of about 80% of the full tank, so that there is still time for the garbage truck to arrive. The waste removal company s operator sees in real time on the PILOT platform that several waste containers are approaching the upper mark, and creates a task to build an optimal route so these overflowing containers are collected sooner. The garbage truck Driver receives a task in the app to pick up specific containers, along with the optimal route to them. The operator sees the task being completed online in real time. In an emergency, for example a fire in a waste container, the operator also receives a Notification on the PILOT platform (as well as by SMS, push or e-mail, depending on the method they prefer) about the incident and the need to respond. Moreover, on the PILOT platform you can set up in advance a response scenario for emergencies (a fire in a waste bin, an accident involving a garbage truck, a vehicle leaving its route), and then any operator of the waste removal service company will know what to do when a particular situation occurs. This module has no separate icon, and it works through two connected modules. The Logistics module and the PTM module. The module also works with just one of these modules, but it is recommended to use both of the modules listed above at the same time. The module settings are shown in the context menu only for the waste container type. Create a task for PTM. To create a task, select Сreate a task in PTM . Waste collection tasks must be created only from the context menu of the waste bin Object. When the Logistics module is connected, the Client name will be available. The current time is set by default; you can change it, for example to a future period. The specified planned time will be taken into account when the task is completed. If you need to select more bins for one vehicle, select the first and the last container and hold shift. Next, you can track the progress of the waste collection task in the PTM module. In this case the PTM module is intended for viewing, not for creating tasks. Create a task for Logistics To create tasks, select the second menu item Create a task in Logistic . It is important to note that the Logistics module takes into account the settings from the Object s work schedule and the warehouse operation settings. Setting up the planned waste collection time. For Objects you should also fill in the parameters for Logistics. Creating a task in Logistics is not provided for; a waste collection task is created only from the context menu, as shown above. Created tasks can be found using the date filter. The window for creating a dump address in the Logistics module. The progress of request processing is shown in the Status column.

The “Fines” module helps you track unpaid and overdue fines associated with vehicles and Drivers. After the module is connected, fine data is received in PILOT automatically through the ELPAS service. ELPAS is an external service that obtains fine data from government sources and passes it to PILOT. Once configured, the module automatically requests new data and displays the fines found in the system. All fines are collected in one window, so you do not need to check each vehicle separately. Here we will explain: — how to connect and configure the “Fines” module — what data is needed to search for fines — how to view the fines found — how to work with the list of fines

The module is connected by the system administrator or the servicing Partner. If you have access to the admin panel, configure the module yourself using the instructions below. If you do not have access, contact your Partner or technical support. To find fines, PILOT uses an integration with the ELPAS service. The service checks charges by the organization s details, vehicle data and driver s licenses. 1. Enable the module Enable the “Fines” module: for the Partner for the sub-Partner for the Contract The module must be enabled at all levels. If it is disabled at even one of them, the system will not be able to receive fine data. 2. Add the ELPAS configuration 1. Go to Contract settings → Configs 2. Click “Add” 3. In the “Key” field, enter fine_api 4. In the “Value” field, enter elpas 5. Click “Save” The configuration must be enabled for the Partner, the sub-Partner and the account. Only then will the system be able to receive fine data. 3. Set up the tariff The module is paid, so a tariff must be set up for it to work. 1. Go to the Contract settings, “Services” tab 2. Click “Add” 3. In the list of services, select “Fines module” 4. Select the tariff for the module 5. Click “Save” If you do not know which tariff to use, contact technical support. 4. Fill in the organization s details In the Contract card, enter: TIN (ИНН) KPP (КПП). The ELPAS service searches by the combination of TIN and KPP, so both fields must be filled in. 5. Fill in the vehicle data For each vehicle you must enter the vehicle registration certificate (STS) number. To do this: 1. In the User account, open the Object card 2. Go to the “Info” tab 3. Enter the series and number of the vehicle registration certificate 4. Save the changes Repeat these steps for each vehicle. Copy the series and number exactly as they appear in the certificate. Even one wrong digit can prevent the fine from being found and linked to the right Object. 6. Fill in the Driver data Open each Driver s card and enter the driver s license number. Without the driver s license number, the ELPAS service will not be able to check fines issued to that Driver. Four identifiers are used to search for fines: TIN (ИНН) — identifies the organization that fines may be issued to KPP (КПП) — clarifies the organization s data and is used together with the TIN STS (СТС) — helps find fines for a specific vehicle DL (ВУ) — helps find fines by driver s license When fines appear After the setup is complete, wait for the next data update. Every night, once a day, the system automatically contacts the ELPAS service, receives information about new fines and updates the list. Each update loads fine data for the last 30 days. If the service finds new fines, they will automatically appear in the User account after the update completes.

After the module is connected, a purple fines indicator appears on the top panel of the User account. If the system finds new fines, the indicator shows their number. Click the purple indicator to open the “Fines” window. List of fines The window shows all fines found for the last 30 days. The following information is available for each fine: Vehicle — the Object the fine relates to Driver — the Driver associated with the vehicle Date — the date of the ruling Status — the current state of the fine, for example Unpaid, Overdue or Discounted. Ruling number — the number of the ruling Fine — the fine amount Pay by — the last day to pay Discount until — the end date of the discounted payment period Info — a description of the violation and additional information Last update — the date and time the data was last received. How to work with the list To view fines for a specific period, enter the dates in the “From date” and “To date” fields. To show only paid fines, check the “Show paid” box. By default, the “Fines” window opens in compact mode. If the violation description does not fit in the “Info” column, hover over the row content — the full information is displayed in a tooltip. To open the window full screen, click the “Expand” button in the top right corner.

To transfer data from the Wialon system, use the “Import from Wialon” module. Data is transferred through the migration wizard — select the Objects you need and transfer them to PILOT. Before transferring data, make sure your Wialon account has export rights — access to the Import/Export function. If you do not have these rights, “Import from Wialon” will not be able to export Objects. For a clear understanding of how to work with the migration wizard and transfer data from Wialon to PILOT, watch the video “How to transfer data from Wialon to PILOT” . https://youtu.be/TMAA7MX-EQU How to transfer data: 1. Connect the “Import from Wialon” module in the admin panel. After that, the “Import from Wialon” button appears on the “General” tab 2. Click the button 3. The migration wizard window opens, divided into two parts: On the left — the list of migration jobs On the right — the list of Wialon Objects that will be transferred 4. Create a new migration job: Click the “Add job” button In the window that appears, fill in the fields: Wialon login — your Wialon login Wialon password — your Wialon password Click the “Load Objects from Wialon” button A list of Objects that can be transferred appears below. Check the ones you want to import. Objects marked processed have already been selected in other jobs and are not available for selection. Click “Save” 5. The new job appears in the list on the left in the migration wizard window. All of its statuses will be empty — this means the job has not been run yet. 6. To start the data transfer, click the job in the list and click “Run job” Once started, the job cannot be changed. 7. After the job is started, the data transfer begins automatically The stage statuses will be updated in the migration wizard window — this usually takes no more than a minute. Wait for the process to finish: you will see the statuses change and new data appear. To follow the migration process and see current statuses, click the “Refresh” button . In this example, after the job with id: 322 was completed, the only Wialon Object was fully and successfully transferred to PILOT. Migration stages The migration stages are displayed for each Object: Stage Description start The job has started. Migration has begun, the system has started executing the job auth Authorization in the Wialon API. The system connects to Wialon to gain access to the data wlp Export of Object parameters. The main Object parameters are exported from Wialon (number of successfully processed files with Wialon Object parameters / total number of Wialon Objects in this job) wln Export of Object Events. Object Events are exported from Wialon (number of successfully processed files with Wialon Object Events / total number of Wialon Objects in this job) veh Creation of Objects in PILOT (number of successfully created PILOT Objects / total number of Wialon Objects in this job) sns Sensor import. Transfer of data about the Sensors installed on Objects evt Event import. All Events related to Objects are imported (for example, speeding, refuels, alarms) rc Data recalculation: rc1 — Tracks: recalculation of routes and movement Tracks rc2 — binary sensors: recalculation of data for Sensors with two states (for example, on/off) rc3 — sensors: recalculation of data for all Sensors rc4 — odometer: Mileage recalculation rc5 — eco: recalculation of driving style data (eco-driving) r6 — multi-sensors: recalculation of data for complex (multichannel) Sensors Migration stage statuses The status field values can be as follows: Value Description empty The migration stage was not run The stage completed successfully The stage completed with errors 1001 Wialon API error code no data Wialon API error message (no data)

Administrator — a user of the admin panel who is responsible for configuring and managing the monitoring system. Their main tasks include: — creating and managing user accounts — setting up access rights for different roles — monitoring user activity in the system — technical setup of hardware: servers, sensors, GPS devices — configuring platform parameters for a specific company’s needs, for example, connecting modules and setting up contracts Here you will find information on creating contracts, working with modules, using and working with the configuration, and making other settings for effective use of the system.

This section works for legal-entity Contracts that operate on prepayment. By default, two types of letter templates about the end of funds are added: after 7 or 14 days. In the template types you can edit and change the text as you wish, or keep the default Pilot templates. How does it work? All Contracts that are (Legal entity and Prepayment, Prepayment (lite)) are iterated, and if 7 or 14 days remain before the balance reaches 0, messages from the template are sent.

A Contract can be deleted from the system only if it has no Objects. If Objects remain on the Contract, first delete the Objects from the Contract through the user interface, and then delete the Contract through the Pilot system admin panel. Objects are not deleted in the admin panel.

You can create a new Contract based on an existing one by copying the settings and data you need. How to clone a Contract 1. Select the Contract you want to copy 2. Right-click to open the Contract menu 3. Click “Clone” 4. Enter the settings for the new Contract 5. Click “Save” — a window opens for choosing what to copy to the new Contract. What can be copied: Sensor templates — all Sensor settings and templates (fuel, temperature, doors, etc.) Individual prices per Object — personal tariffs set for individual Objects of the Contract Payment letter templates — texts and settings of e-mail Notifications (invoices, reminders, etc.) User assignment — who is assigned to which Objects or clients Additional fields — all custom fields Users — rights and display settings of the Contract s Users Reports from the Report builder — custom Reports created through the builder Geofences — all zones associated with the Contract (base, warehouses, routes, etc.) 6. Select what to copy to the new Contract and click “Save”

System modules are separate components that together form a complex system, providing its functionality and interconnected operation. Each module performs specific tasks or functions, and they can be developed and updated independently of each other. Only the system administrator can manage activation, through the admin panel. The list of modules in a Contract may vary depending on the Partner s settings. CMS and Video - a system component that lets you monitor the state and behavior of the driver and passengers inside the cabin. Drivers module - a system component used to manage and track the work of Drivers in the system. Counterparties module (Sales representative) - intended for managing information about counterparties, including clients, suppliers, Partners and sales representatives. This module helps organize interaction with counterparties and improve the quality of service. Control room - a system component for tracking the location of a vehicle and scanning its condition. Climate control - a system for automatically regulating climatic conditions in an enclosed space, for example in a vehicle, office or living space. The main goal is to maintain comfortable conditions for people, including optimal levels of temperature, humidity and air quality. RFID tags module - a module intended for monitoring the reading of RFID tags; a narrowly focused module created to control waste collection (there is a tag on the bin and a reader on the vehicle). Analytics module (Dashboard) - a system component that provides capabilities for collecting, processing and analyzing data from monitored Objects in order to obtain valuable information about them. Engine blocking module - a system component intended to prevent unauthorized access to and starting of the engine. Geofence module - intended for territorial control of monitored Objects. It lets you record the fact that an Object is in a given zone, exceeding the permitted idle time in the zone, and leaving the zone. Commands module - a system component that includes a set of commands that Users can send to devices. Time control module - a system component intended for tracking, recording and managing working time. Violation control module - a system component used to track and detect violations using a set of predefined rules. Logistics module - a system component intended for managing and optimizing logistics operations within the supply, storage and transportation of goods or services. Recalculation module - a system component used to perform recalculations and transformations of data in the system. Recalculation is possible for two types: Zones and Trips. Trailers module - intended for monitoring the state of trailers and semi-trailers attached to main vehicles. This module lets you track the location, state and movement of trailers, as well as view the history of connections and disconnections with the vehicle. Retranslation module - a system component used to forward data from one source to another or to several other sources at once. It acts as an intermediary between the sender and the recipient of the data. Service module - a system component intended for convenient planning or recording of vehicle technical inspections. Events module - a system component intended for tracking and recording the various Events configured in the system. It plays a key role in monitoring Objects and analyzing User actions. Fuel cards module - the choice of fuel depends on specific requirements, operating conditions and environmental factors. Notifications module - a system component intended for sending Notifications to Users about various Events, changes or states. It provides prompt information to the User and allows timely response to important Events. Trips module - a system component intended for automating and optimizing the operation of bus routes, improving passenger service quality and ensuring the efficiency of the vehicle fleet. Routes module - a system component intended for passenger flow control. PILOT task manager - a module intended for monitoring, managing and coordinating the execution of tasks or processes in the system. It gives Users the ability to observe and manage current processes Schedule - a module used to create, manage and optimize work schedules for vehicles and Drivers. Eco-driving - a component of the vehicle management system intended for monitoring, analyzing and improving driving style. Tachograph module - intended for monitoring and recording data on the work and rest regimes of Drivers, driving speed and other important parameters related to vehicle operation. Tachographs play a key role in ensuring road safety and compliance with regulatory requirements. Crash detected - a component of the vehicle management system intended for automatically detecting road accidents involving vehicles. The module uses various Sensors to monitor movement parameters. Rent Сar - a module intended for managing and automating vehicle rental processes. Waste collection module - intended for planning, optimizing and monitoring waste collection and removal operations. Agro module (Trailers module) - intended for automating and optimizing the management of agricultural machinery and resources in the agro-industrial complex. Hardware health monitoring module - a system component intended for monitoring the state of various components and systems of vehicles. This module helps identify faults, prevent breakdowns and optimize Maintenance. LogBook module - a portal for Drivers where they can track their Trip statistics, eco-driving data, fuel costs, toll costs and their ratings. Each Driver can access the portal and see only their own statistics, which are analyzed based on all Trips in all vehicles they have used.

The field editor is a tool that lets Users change or manage data fields. For example, in a text type or a table, the field editor can be used to change field properties such as its size, the type of data it contains, or how it is displayed. The view according to the settings in the User interface. When editing a field, you can change its type by selecting the one you need from the list provided. Be careful: when editing a field, the text for the name property must be entered only in lowercase Latin letters. For example, if the field name (fieldLabel) has the value "fieldLabel":"MVA Number", then in name you can write: "name":"mvanumber". Teltonika FOTA is a cloud service provided by Teltonika that lets you update the firmware and configuration of GPS trackers remotely. This tool simplifies the management of telematics devices, allowing you to perform the necessary updates from the office, without physical access to the devices. The Fota tab in the context menu of an Object is available only for the Teltonika device type. Details tab: Imei Device model Series Configuration Last connection and update Product code Requests tab: The Requests tab lets you upload files. The upload files for this service include firmware updates and configuration files, which can be uploaded and applied to devices remotely. To get access to the upload files and use the Teltonika FOTA service, you will need to register and set up an account on the official Teltonika website.

The system includes an integration with Teltonika FOTA. This integration lets you configure Teltonika devices from the PILOT system interface. This function can be activated both for a Partner and for an individual account (Contract). Activating Teltonika FOTA WEB in PILOT To remotely manage the configuration of Teltonika devices from the PILOT platform, you need to activate the integration. To do this, follow these steps. 1. Log in to your account in Teltonika FOTA WEB ( https://fm.teltonika.lt ) 2. Generate and copy the API Key. 3.Enter any name for the API Token and click the Create button. 4. Enter any name for the API Token and click the Create button. 5. Copy the generated token value. Open your account settings in the admin panel and add a new entry there Open the Configuration section and add the key fotaTokens . Format and value of the fotaTokens key: { : , : , : } - any name - the API Key obtained in the Teltonika FOTA interface You can specify more than one key, separated by commas.

How to configure SMTP: In the admin panel, go to the “Partners” section 2. Double-click the selected Partner — a window with settings opens. Select the SMPT tab. The tab is available to Partners only. The SMTP tab is intended for configuring e-mail sending through an external SMTP server. This is where you specify the parameters of the mail server through which the system will send Notifications, invoices and other e-mails. Setup parameters • SMTP Host — the SMTP server address • SMTP Port — the SMTP server port • SMTP Login — the login for authorization on the mail server • SMTP Passw — the password for authorization • SMTP Email — the e-mail address on whose behalf e-mails will be sent • SMTP security — selection of the connection type (no encryption, SSL, TLS — depending on the server settings) Please check the entered data carefully — the delivery of e-mails depends on the correctness of these settings. Checking the SMTP server After entering the parameters, you can run a connection check. The system uses the SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) protocol to test the connection and authorization. The check is performed as follows: 1. The system gets the SMTP server address from the request and checks whether it is specified 2. It gets the connection port. If no port is set, the standard port 25 is used 3. An SMTP client instance is created, and the connection timeout and debug level are configured 4. An attempt to connect to the server is made: — if SSL is selected, the prefix ssl:// is automatically added to the address — when connecting over SSL, certificate verification is temporarily disabled 5. After a successful connection, the EHLO command (the extended SMTP greeting command) is sent 6. The system gets the list of ESMTP extensions supported by the server 7. If TLS mode is selected and the server supports STARTTLS, the system: — initiates a secure connection — sends the EHLO command again 8. If the server supports authentication, a sign-in attempt is made using the specified login and password Error handling If an error occurs at any stage: — the information is written to the error log — HTTP code 400 is returned — an error message is output in JSON format Regardless of the result of the check, the connection is closed properly with the QUIT command. Finally, the function returns the connection parameters and the result of the check. This procedure helps make sure that the server is available, supports the selected encryption type and accepts the specified credentials. If the check fails, we recommend double-checking the server address, port, security type and sign-in data.

A configuration is a set of system parameters and settings that adapt the system s operation to specific tasks. Each configuration consists of a key — a unique identifier — and a value, which can be a number, text or a more complex data structure. How to add a configuration to a Partner: In the admin panel, go to the “Partners” section 2. Double-click the selected Partner — a window with settings opens 3. Go to the “Configuration” tab and click the “Add” button 4. Click “Refresh” and save the changes on the “Configuration” tab Use the icons to edit a configuration or delete it . Use the “Export” button to save the current Contract s settings to a JSON file. To apply previously saved settings to another Contract, use the “Import” button and select the saved JSON file. List of configurations To view the list of configurations, click the “List of configurations” button. The list shows all configurations that you can add in the system. SIM cards in monitoring systems are used to provide communication between monitoring devices and the server. They play a key role in systems that require remote tracking and data transmission. SIM cards are used in GPS trackers for vehicles to transmit location data in real time. This makes it possible to control routes, monitor schedule compliance and respond to deviations from the route. SIM cards allow monitoring devices (for example, GPS trackers and Sensors) to connect to mobile networks to transmit location, status and other parameter data to the monitoring server. This is especially important for devices that are in motion or in remote locations without access to Wi-Fi or wired networks.

Etisalat SIM — these are SIM cards and related services provided by Etisalat, one of the largest telecommunications operators in the Middle East, Africa and Asia. The Jasper platform is a platform for controlling and managing M2M SIM cards. It lets you use various settings and get the full history of connections between hardware in real time. Data is provided in both numerical and graphical form. It is a single control center, available remotely at any convenient time. As a reminder, M2M (machine-to-machine) is a solution designed to provide wireless data exchange between various devices (ATMs, terminals, security systems, sensors, etc.) and a single control center.
