To view all questions and results, tap . To exit the inspection, tap “Exit inspection”. How to carry out an inspection Tap the button in the upper right corner of the screen 2. Select the vehicle you are going to inspect To find a vehicle, use the “Search” field or the filters by vehicle model or year of manufacture. 3. Select the inspection type Inspection forms with questions are created in the web version and can be filled in in the mobile app. To learn how to create an inspection form, read here . 4. Answer the questions Answer all the questions in the inspection form. If necessary, attach photos to confirm the condition of the vehicle. 5. Add a signature If a signature is required, sign in the designated field. If you didn’t manage to sign the first time, use the eraser to clear it and try again. 5. Complete the inspection When you have answered all the questions and signed, tap “Next”. The inspection is completed and saved.

If the “Video” module is connected to your account and video devices are installed on your objects, you can view the video recorded by these devices. Viewing the video stream 1. In the “Objects” section, select an object with a connected camera 2. Open the object menu and go to the “Video” tab 3. On this tab you will see previews of all connected cameras 4. Tap the camera you need to go to the video player Playback controls In the player you can: Switch between cameras using the arrows Turn camera sound on and off Take screenshots Expand the video to full screen Viewing video history To view video history, tap the icon in the upper right corner of the player 2. In “History”, tap and select the date and time to filter recordings. Then tap “Apply” The history player shows the date and current time of the frame. By moving the slider, you can quickly jump to the moment of the recording you need. When viewing video history, you can: Take screenshots Change the playback speed Turn sound on or off Expand the video to full screen

With the mobile app, you can send commands to objects to control them remotely: 1. Go to the “Objects” section and select the object you want to send a command to 2. Tap the object menu and select the “Commands” tab **![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_komandami_custom_2.png)**![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_komandami_custom_3.png) 3. On the “Commands” tab, you will see a list of commands that can be run for the selected object, for example, sending an SMS command to the device, requesting settings, etc. Tap the command you need to send it to the device. In the “Command history” block, you can see all previously sent commands, their statuses and details: Command name Status Command type User who sent the command Date the command was sent Time of the last command status update Vehicle the command was applied to If you need to cancel a command, tap and “Cancel command”. To see the command history for a specific period, use the filters. Tap and select the date and time to filter commands by the period you need, then tap “Apply”.

Raw points are unprocessed data that the device sends directly to the system in real time. They show what values come from the sensors without filtering or processing. How to view raw points 1. Open the object menu 2. Go to the “Points” tab On this tab you will see the data that the device sends. To view the full set of unprocessed data: — tap “Raw data” — if needed, you can copy the data by tapping the “Copy” button Viewing points on a chart To view the data on a chart: 1. Switch to chart mode 2. Select one or more parameters to display on the chart. To do this, turn on the switch next to the parameter you need The chart shows the values of the selected parameters. If you hover over a specific point, a tooltip appears with the exact time and value at that moment. Configuring the display of point fields On the “Points” tab, you can configure how data is displayed: — select which parameters to show for each GPS point — filter the points you need by time range

To arm an object, a security sensor must be set up on it. If the sensor is set up, an “Arming” item appears in the object menu. For the function to work, command templates named arm and disarm must also be created in the system. Set them up in the web interface beforehand, and the arming commands will appear: Arm — arm the object Disarm — disarm the object When the security status changes, the corresponding icon appears next to the object in the list: — object is armed — object is disarmed How to set up command templates Command templates are set up in the PILOT web interface: 1. Open the user account 2. Go to the “Main” section 3. Click the “Commands” icon 3. A window opens where you can create command templates. How to create a command template 1. Click “Add command” 2. Select the object the command is created for 3. Click 3. Specify the parameters: Command type — GRPS Command kind — SMS_VIA_GPRS 4. In the “SMS” field, enter the command text, for example: setdigout 0 — disarm 5. If needed, select the hex checkbox if the command must be sent in HEX format 6. Click “Save as template” and enter a name Template names must be exactly as follows: arm — arm the object disarm — disarm the object The names are written in lowercase. The app uses these names to find and run the commands. Command examples Arming — arm Device Command template Teltonika setdigout 1 Adm 333 BLEOUTPUT 0 Disarming — disarm Device Command template Teltonika setdigout 0 Adm 333 BLEOUTPUT 1
The Telegram bot lets you work with the vehicles in your account, get information about objects, see their locations and use your phone as a GPS tracker.

In this article you will learn: — how to connect and log in to the chatbot — how to use the menu and the main functions — how to view the vehicle list How to connect to the chatbot 1. Open Telegram and find the bot @skyelectronics_bot 2. Tap the “Start” button 3. Select “Start authorization” 4. Enter your account login and password If you made a mistake, tap “Reset login” and start over. How to use the bot menu Tap the “Menu” button — the main functions appear: Help When you tap Help, you get a short welcome message from the bot. In it, the bot explains what it can do: — show the list of your vehicles — give information on each vehicle — provide your unique ID, which is needed for the tracker to work Advanced Menu When you tap this command, an extended menu with buttons appears: Vehicles — shows the list of all your vehicles Get ID — the bot sends you your unique ID The ID is the number of a virtual GPS tracker. It works like a real tracker in a vehicle, except that the data is transmitted through Telegram from your phone. Get user — shows which account you are currently logged in to Log out — you log out of the account in the bot Change language Use this button if you want to change the bot interface language. Version bot Shows the current version of the bot. How to get the vehicle list 1. Make sure you are logged in to the bot 2. Go to Advanced Menu to open the extended menu 3. Select “Vehicles” — the list of vehicles in the account is displayed If you select a specific vehicle, the bot shows: — a summary for the object — a map link to view the location When working with the vehicle list, you can search for the vehicle you need by typing text. Just write in the chat, for example: “Show vehicles” “Find vehicle 7009” The bot recognizes the digits and letters of the number and picks all matching options. If there are matches in the list, it shows only the vehicles that fit your query.

The Telegram bot can work as a virtual tracker. The bot creates a special ID that is used as the tracker number. When you turn on location sharing in Telegram, the monitoring system receives coordinates from this ID — just as it does from a regular GPS tracker. How to set up the Telegram tracker Get the ID Log in to the chatbot Open Advanced Menu to open the extended menu Tap “Get ID” 2. Create an object in PILOT In your user account, create a new object Open the object card → “Main” tab Enter the vehicle name or number In the “Device ID” field, paste the ID you received in the bot In the “Device type” field, select any option 3. Turn on location sharing in Telegram Open the chat with the bot Tap the paperclip ![](images/drex_ispolzovanie_telegram_kak_gps_trekera_custom_3.png) Select “Location” Allow access on your phone ![](images/drex_ispolzovanie_telegram_kak_gps_trekera_custom_4.png) Tap “Share live location” ![](images/drex_ispolzovanie_telegram_kak_gps_trekera_custom_5.png) Select how long to share the location Tap “Share” Your phone now works as a tracker. A message with your current location appears in the chat. It has a location icon — tap it, and Telegram opens a map where you can see the point showing your position. ![](images/drex_ispolzovanie_telegram_kak_gps_trekera_custom_7.png) ![](images/drex_ispolzovanie_telegram_kak_gps_trekera_custom_8.png) In PILOT, the object moves along with you — its coordinates are updated from your phone’s location.

To create a Telegram bot yourself, you need the official @BotFather service — the main Telegram bot through which all other bots are created and configured. 1. Follow the link: https://t.me/BotFather 2. Tap Start to open the menu ![](images/drex_kak_sozdat_svoj_telegram_bot_custom.png) 3. Enter the command: /newbot ![](images/drex_kak_sozdat_svoj_telegram_bot_custom_2.png) 4. Come up with a name for the bot BotFather asks you to specify the bot’s name — the display name that people see. 5. Come up with a username for the bot — its address in Telegram There is an important rule here — the username must end with _bot. For example, mycompany_bot, skyelectronics_helper_bot ![How to create your own Telegram bot](images/drex_kak_sozdat_svoj_telegram_bot_screen.png) 6. Get the token After BotFather creates the bot, a congratulations message appears. Right below it you will see: Token to access the HTTP API — the bot token Username — your bot’s user name 7. Send your bot’s token and username to technical support to connect the bot to PILOT The contract in the system must be active; otherwise the bot cannot send or receive data.

The Telegram bot lets employees send information to PILOT directly from a mobile device. An employee can select the current status and also send a photo or video from the work site. For example, an employee can send the statuses “On the way”, “Arrived at the site” and “Started work” in sequence, and after finishing, select the status “Work completed” and attach a photo of the result. Sent media files can be found and viewed in the PILOT web interface. Setting up Telegram statuses Statuses are created separately for each PILOT account. In the Telegram bot, an employee sees only the options that the master added in the settings of the corresponding account. Setup is done by a user with master rights: 1. Log in to the PILOT web interface 2. Open “Contract settings” 3. Go to the “Telegram statuses” tab 4. Click “+ Add” 5. Enter the status name 6. Click “OK” The created status appears in the general list. The value in the “Order” column determines its position among the other statuses. To delete a status, select it in the list and click “Delete”. After the account is connected to the Telegram bot, the created statuses become available to authorized users. How to send a status Logging in to the Telegram bot Before starting, an employee needs to link the Telegram bot to a PILOT account: 1. Open the PILOT Telegram bot 2. Start the bot with the /start command 3. Enter the PILOT account login 4. Enter the password 5. Wait for the message confirming successful authorization To log in, use the account in whose settings the master created the required statuses. How to send a status in the bot 1. In the bot menu, tap “Status” 3. Select the status you need from the list provided 4. Wait for the “Status sent” message The bot has accepted the selected status. After that, you can continue working with the bot: select another status when the work stage changes, or send a photo or video. How to send a photo or video Through the Telegram bot you can send materials that confirm completed work or show the condition of an object. For example, the work location, equipment before servicing, the result of the work, delivered cargo. To send a file: 1. Open the PILOT Telegram bot 2. Tap the paperclip icon 3. Select a photo or video on your mobile device 4. Send the file 5. Wait for the “Media saved” message The message confirms that the file has been received and saved in PILOT How to view sent media files The first time a media file is sent, a separate object named after the Telegram user is created in the PILOT object list. All subsequent photos and videos from this user are saved in the same object. 1. Open the “Online” tab in the PILOT web interface 2. Find the object named after the Telegram user in the tree 3. Right-click the object 4. Select “Media” 5. Specify the period for which to show materials 6. Find the record you need 7. Click the photo icon or the video icon to open the file To save the file to your computer, click the download icon next to the corresponding record. The “Media” tab shows the photos and videos sent by this user through the Telegram bot, as well as the date and time they were received.

PILOT Driver is a mobile app for drivers, couriers and delivery staff. It works together with PILOT Task Manager (PTM) and helps manage tasks and routes. Tasks for drivers are created in the PTM web version and then passed to the PILOT. Driver mobile version, where drivers can view and carry them out. With PILOT. Driver, drivers can carry out various types of tasks, for example: Cargo delivery — tasks for delivering goods, materials or construction materials, for example, delivering goods, collecting and removing waste or delivering concrete Taxi and tourism — for taxi drivers and drivers who work with tourists, PTM lets you manage transport orders Waste collection — drivers can work on waste collection routes, marking each route point as they complete the task How PTM works: 1. The driver receives a task with the route points to visit 2. While carrying out the task, the driver marks each route point as completed, confirming delivery or another job 3. After all route points have been visited, the driver marks the task as completed and, if necessary, sends a report on its completion

How to install the PILOT. Driver app 1. Open Google Play or the App Store on your smartphone 2. In the search bar, enter PILOT Driver or go to the app store using the link: Go to Google Play Go to App Store 3. Tap “Install” and wait for the download and installation to finish 4. After installation, tap “Open” or find the PILOT. Driver icon on your smartphone screen and launch the app How to log in to the app After you launch the app, on the login screen: 1. Enter your account login If needed, leave the “Remember me” option on so the app remembers your details 2. Enter your password 3. Tap “Next” After logging in, you land on the main screen with new tasks.

The “New” tab shows tasks that have been assigned to you and are waiting to be accepted. Until you tap the “Accept task” button, the task stays on this tab. Each task is shown as a card with the main information: — task name — task number — planned start date and time — planned end date and time — estimated duration To open a task, tap its card. Sorting tasks If the list contains many tasks, you can change the order in which they are displayed. To do this: 1. Open the “New” tab 2. Tap the list settings icon in the upper right corner 3. In the “List settings” window, select a sorting option: Newest first — later tasks are shown at the top of the list Oldest first — earlier tasks are shown at the top of the list 4. Tap “Apply” The list is updated automatically according to the selected sorting. Viewing a task To open a task, tap its card in the list. After it opens, the task card with information is displayed. The top of the card shows: — start date and time — end date and time Below is the “Accept task” button, which puts the task in progress. Task information The “Task information” section shows the main details of the trip. The set of fields depends on the task type, but usually includes: task name customer or counterparty details information about the vehicle, cargo, etc. Waybill Below is the “Waybill” section, which shows the route with all the visit points. For each point, the following are shown: address point number To see detailed information about a point, tap it in the waybill. The window that opens shows: — full address — current point status — “Actions” button The “Actions” button gives access to the following functions: Copy address — copy the address to the clipboard to use in a navigator or message Show on map — open the map showing the location of the selected point To open the route map, tap the map icon in the upper right corner of the task card. For more on working with the map, see the article “Route map”.

When a new task is assigned to you, it appears on the “New” tab. To accept a task: 1. In the bottom menu, open the “New” tab 2. Find the task you need in the list and tap its card 3. Review the task information: start and end times, route, point addresses and other details. 4. If you are ready to start the task, tap the “Accept task” button. After you accept it, the task automatically moves to the “Active” tab, where you can track its progress and work with route points.

The “Active” tab shows tasks that you have already accepted and are currently carrying out. Here you can track progress, work with route points and complete tasks. Each task is shown as a card with the main information: — task name and number — progress — the number of points completed out of the total — planned start and end time — a progress indicator showing how much of the route has been completed Sorting tasks If the list contains many tasks, you can change the order in which they are displayed. To do this: 1. Open the “Active” tab 2. Tap the list settings icon in the upper right corner 3. In the “List settings” window, select a sorting option: Newest first — newer tasks are shown first Oldest first — earlier tasks are shown first 4. Tap “Apply” The list is updated automatically according to the selected sorting. Viewing a task To open a task, tap its card. The task card shows: — planned start and end time — task type — additional information (contact details, cargo information and other data) — the route with the list of visit points If the task has been accepted, tap the “Start task” button to begin carrying it out. Working with route points After you start the task, the screen shows the “Next point” block — the address to visit next. The following actions are available for the selected point: Route — build a route in the navigation app installed on the device Arrived — mark your arrival at the point After you tap “Arrived”, the point becomes active. Additional actions become available for it: — add a comment — complete the point — open the “Other actions” menu You can use a comment to record additional information about the work performed, delivery or other events. Other actions Additional operations are available for the current point: Copy address — copy the address to the clipboard Show on map — open the point location on the map Postpone point — temporarily defer the point The postpone function can be useful in the following cases: — the recipient is temporarily absent — the point cannot be completed for external reasons — you need to visit another route point first After a point is postponed, it gets the “Postponed” status, and the app offers to move to the next route point. You can return to the postponed point later. Progress The current task progress is shown: — in the active task list — in the task card, in the “Progress” section Task menu In the upper right corner of the task card there is a menu button. It gives access to the following actions: Complete task — finish the task Show full route — open the map with all route points For more on working with the map, see the article “Route map” . Completing a task After you have performed all the required work and visited the route points, tap “Complete task”. After completion, the task automatically moves to the “Completed” tab, where you can view it.

If a report is set up for a task or route point, a “Fill in report” button appears in the app. A report can be linked to: — an individual route point — the whole task This depends on the settings specified by the operator in the web version of the system . The composition and number of fields in a report may vary. What data must be filled in is determined by the report form settings. How to open a report 1. Open an active task 2. If the report is linked to a route point, go to the point you need and tap “Arrived” 3. Tap the “Fill in report” button The report form then opens. Fields marked with the (*) symbol are required. Until the required fields are filled in, you cannot complete the report. Filling in a report Depending on the form settings, a report may contain various types of fields, for example: text fields numeric values selection lists switches comment and signature fields photos and files Fill in all the required data according to your organization’s requirements. Adding photos If the form provides for photo capture, tap “Add photo”. ![](images/drex_kak_zapolnit_otchyet__custom_3.png) ![](images/drex_kak_zapolnit_otchyet__custom_4.png) In the window that opens, select one of the options: Go to camera — take a photo with the device camera; Choose photo from gallery — attach an existing image. You can add several photos if needed. How to complete a report 1. Make sure all required fields are filled in 2. Check that the data you entered and the attachments you added are correct 3. Tap the “Complete” button at the bottom of the screen After successful completion, the report is saved and sent to the system.

The “Completed” tab shows all tasks that have been finished. Here you can view previously completed tasks and information about them. Each task is shown as a card with the following information: — task name — task number — start date and time — end date and time — actual completion time of the task Sorting tasks To change the order in which completed tasks are displayed: 1. Open the “Completed” tab 2. Tap the list settings icon in the upper right corner 3. In the “List settings” window, select a sorting method: Newest first — recently completed tasks are shown at the top of the list Oldest first — tasks completed earlier are shown at the top of the list 4. Tap “Apply” The list is then updated automatically. Viewing a completed task To open the information, tap the card of the task you need in the list. The task card opens with information about the route, visited points and results. Task information The top of the card shows: — start date and time — end date and time Below is the “Task information” section. Depending on the system settings, it may contain: — task name — company or customer name — contact phone number — office address — task description — cargo information — other additional data Waybill The “Waybill” section shows all route points that were part of the task. For each point, the following are shown: — name and address — point number — completion status — visit date and time To view information about a point, tap it in the list. The window that opens shows: — full address — point status — time work started at the point — time work ended at the point Actions for a point The following actions are available for a point: Copy address — copy the address to the clipboard; Show on map — open the point location on the map. Route map To view the route, tap the map icon in the upper right corner of the task card. The map shows the route and all the points of the task. For more on working with the map, its settings and controls, see the article “Route map” .

In the upper right corner of a new, active or completed task card there is a map icon. Tap it to open the route map. The map shows: purple line — the travel route numbered markers — route points The bottom of the screen also shows the waybill, so you can view the route on the map and the list of points at the same time. Map settings To open the settings, tap the gear icon in the upper right corner of the map screen. Map layer In this section, you can select the source of map data. For example: OpenStreetMap 2GIS Google Map Google Satellite Yandex Map satellite maps and other available options. Choose the map view that is most convenient for you. Show points The “Show points” switch controls the display of route points on the map. On — route points are displayed on the map Off — points are hidden, and only the route line is displayed. Map controls Additional control buttons are available on the map — zoom the map in or out — show your current location on the map

On the “Settings” tab, you can view information about your account, change the interface language and app theme, log out or delete your account. How to open settings 1. Open the app 2. In the bottom menu, tap the “Settings” icon The screen shows: — user name — e-mail address — “Language” section — “Theme” section — “Delete account” button — logout button in the upper right corner of the screen Logging out To log out of your account: 1. Open the “Settings” section 2. Tap the logout button in the upper right corner of the screen 3. Confirm the action After you log out, the login screen opens. To continue working, you need to log in to the account again. Changing the app language To change the interface language: 1. Open the “Settings” section 2. Tap “Language” 3. Select the language you need from the list 4. Tap “Change language” After you confirm, the interface language is changed. Changing the theme To change the app theme: 1. Open the “Settings” section 2. Tap “Theme” 3. Select one of the available options: Light Dark Same as system — the app uses the theme set on the device The selected theme is applied immediately after you select it. Deleting an account To delete your account: 1. Open the “Settings” section 2. Tap “Delete account” 3. In the confirmation window, select: Cancel — to cancel the deletion Delete — to confirm deletion of the account

PILOT Guarda is an app for vehicle security and monitoring. It helps you monitor the condition of a car, manage access to it and track its movements. The app is suitable for both personal use and fleet management. With the app you can: — Monitor the car’s condition View the current status, charge, events and other parameters — Manage access Open and close the car without using keys — Track movements See the current location and trip history Ways to control The car can be accessed: Via GSM (mobile network) — from any distance Via Bluetooth — when you are near the car

How to install the app 1. Open Google Play or the App Store on your smartphone 2. In the search bar, enter PILOT Guarda or go to the app store using the link: Go to Google Play Go to App Store 3. Install the app 4. After installation, tap “Open” or find the Pilot Guarda icon on your smartphone screen and launch the app How to log in to the app After you launch the app, on the login screen: 1. Enter your account login and password 2. If needed, leave the “Remember me” option on so the app remembers your details 3. Tap “Log in” After you log in, the “My cars” tab opens, where you can select the car you need and go to the screen with summary information about its condition. Login settings On the login screen, in the upper right corner, there is an icon . Tap it to open “Login settings”. Here you can change the server. Enter the address of the server you need and save the changes with the “Accept” button. Registration by QR code The app lets you register using the device QR code, which already contains the object data. 1. On the login screen, tap “Scan QR code”. 2. Point your smartphone camera at the QR code (on the device or in PILOT). Make sure the code fits in the frame on the screen — the app reads it automatically. 2. Select an action: Log in — if you already have an account in PILOT. In this case, the device is linked to your existing account automatically. Register — if you do not have an account. The app offers to create a new account, and the device is added to the new account. Registering a new user: 1. Fill in the details: — Email — phone number — password — password confirmation Tap “Continue”. 2. Confirm your e-mail A confirmation code is sent to the e-mail address you specified. Enter the code on the confirmation screen. If the message does not arrive, you can request it again after the timer ends. Tap “Confirm”. After successful confirmation, you are logged in to the app automatically, and the device scanned via the QR code is linked to your account.

To open the app menu, tap the menu icon in the upper left corner on any tab. After the menu opens, you will see: — user name — the selected car whose condition is currently shown in the app The menu gives access to the main tabs of the app: Car status My cars My tags History Video Geofences Reports Alerts FAQ User settings Below is a detailed description of each tab and its functions. Car status The “Car status” tab helps you quickly understand what is happening with your car right now. The screen shows: — car name or number — address of the current location — car status — whether it is stationary or moving — time in the current state — how long the car has been stationary or in another status — security state — on or off — lock control button — for opening or closing the car remotely — Bluetooth icon — shows whether the car can be controlled over Bluetooth To see the car’s location on the map, tap the icon on the “Car status” tab. The map screen then opens with the vehicle’s current location. To change the appearance of the map, tap the map layer selection icon . The “Select layer” window opens, where you can choose a suitable display option. If it is important for you to assess the traffic situation near the car, you can turn on traffic display. My cars The “My cars” tab shows the list of all vehicles available to you. To see the status of a specific car, tap it in the list — the screen with the car status opens. How to add a car: 1. Tap “Add” in the upper right corner 2. Scan the QR code: — point your smartphone camera at the QR code on the device — or at the code generated by PILOT 3. The car is added to your account automatically My tags On the “My tags” tab, you can view and manage the Bluetooth tags (beacons) connected to the device. This function is available for Teltonika devices. Tags are used for: driver identification controlling access to the car automatic scenarios (for example, disarming when approaching) Each tag is a separate device with a unique identifier. The tag list shows: tag name identifier (ID) status (active / inactive) Tap a tag in the list — the actions menu opens. Enable tag broadcast — when the device detects the tag, the system can automatically perform an action, for example, disarm the car Rename tag — a window opens where you can enter a new name and save the changes The “Refresh” button loads the current list from the device The tag list is generated on the device side (for example, Teltonika). For tags to be displayed in the app: — they must be configured and registered in the device — the device must send their list to PILOT You can find detailed setup instructions for Teltonika devices here: https://wiki.teltonika-gps.com/view/FMB920_Beacon_List History The “History” tab shows the car’s movement history . You can: — view routes — analyze trips — view events for the selected period Video The “Video” tab provides recordings from the video devices installed in the car. Geofences On the “Geofences” tab you can: — create geofences — edit them — set up notifications for entering and leaving Reports On the “Reports” tab, you can build a report for selected objects and parameters. Alerts This is where events and notifications are shown. The alert list shows: — the car or object — event type or notification text — date and time — event address ![](images/drex_menyu_prilozheniya_custom_20.png) **![](images/drex_menyu_prilozheniya_custom_21.png)** To open an event, tap it — a map opens with the event point and information. To filter notifications: 1. Tap the filter icon 2. Select a period 3. Tap “Apply” The screen then shows only the alerts that match the specified period. FAQ A link to the support site with frequently asked questions and a feedback form. User settings In the “Settings” section, you can configure the app and access. Language — tap the drop-down list and select the language you need Notifications: — Show address — adds the address to the notification text — Sound notifications — turns on an audible signal Users — add users and configure their rights. How to add a user: 1. Go to “Users” 2. Tap “Add” 3. Specify: Email phone name password 4. Select: available objects role (administrator or user) 5. Tap “Save” Beacon type (tag type) Here you select the type of Bluetooth tag used to communicate with the car: — iBeacon — an Apple technology that uses Bluetooth Low Energy. It transmits a unique identifier (UUID, Major, Minor) and works with nearby devices — Eddystone — an open BLE format that transmits an identifier, URL and telemetry PIN code You can set a PIN code for logging in: 1. Enter a new code 2. Confirm it 3. Tap “Save” Car settings Select a car to change its parameters: — change the car image — set up notifications — choose which events you want to be notified about and how: loss of connection with the car movement with the ignition off arming and disarming low battery For each event type, you can select one or both delivery methods: Push — push notification to your phone E-mail — notification by e-mail Change theme At the bottom of the screen there is a theme switch. Log out Tap “Log out” to exit the app.

The “History” tab shows information about the car’s movements and events for the selected period. Here you can see where the car was, how it moved and what events took place. Viewing a trip route To open a trip route: 1. Select the movement track you need in the list 2. Tap the route display icon The route with detailed information then appears on the map. To view the movement, use the route player — it shows how the car moved along the route. Events in history In addition to routes, history shows events. Tap an event in the list to see details — a point with information appears on the map. Examples of events: Parking — the car was stationary Alarm — a sensor or alert was triggered Arming / disarming History filters Filters help you quickly find the events you need. To set up a filter: 1. Open the filter settings 2. Select the parameters you need: Event type — for example, route, parking, alarm Time period 3. After setting up the filter, tap “Apply”. The list will show only the events that match the selected parameters. ![](images/drex_kak_prosmotret_istoriyu_custom.png) ![](images/drex_kak_prosmotret_istoriyu_custom_8.png) ![](images/drex_kak_prosmotret_istoriyu_custom_9.png)

If video devices are installed in the car, you can view the video recorded by these devices. Viewing the video stream Go to the “Video” tab in the app menu — the video players of the connected cameras are displayed. In the video player you can: Stop viewing Turn camera sound on and off Take screenshots Expand the video to full screen Viewing video history 1. In the player, tap the icon in the upper right corner 2. A list of recordings opens in chronological order 3. To open a recording, tap the row you need or the play button next to it While viewing a recording, the following functions are available: Play / Pause — start or pause playback Stop — end viewing Seek — move through the recording Screenshot — capture a frame from the video Sound — adjust the volume (if the recording contains audio) Playback speed — you can slow down or speed up the recording Full-screen mode — expand the player to full screen How to download video Tap the download button next to the recording you need in the history list. To filter recordings: 1. Tap the filter 2. Select the date and time 3. Tap “Apply”

The “Geofences” tab shows the list of all available geofences. On this tab you can: — view existing geofences — create new geofences — edit existing zones — set up notifications for geofence-related events How to create a geofence 1. Tap “Add” 2. Specify the parameters: Geofence name The group it will belong to (or create a new group) 3. Set the geofence shape: Circle — tap the map and drag to set the radius (you can change the radius by dragging the edge) Polygon — mark points on the map one by one to set the boundaries ![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_geozonami_2_custom_3.png) ![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_geozonami_2_custom_8.png) 4. Select the geofence color If needed, tap “Clear” to undo your changes. 5. Tap “Save” — the geofence appears in the list Geofence actions Tap a geofence in the list, then the menu ( ) — the available actions open: Delete — delete the geofence Set up notifications — set up alerts Edit — go to editing the geofence Collapse the geofence menu to return to the list Setting up notifications 1. Select the cars that will receive notifications. 2. Specify the notification parameters: Notification type Message text 3. Select how to receive it: Email SMS Alarm Push notifications in the app 4. To add an e-mail or phone number, tap “Add” and enter the details 5. Specify the conditions: entering the geofence leaving the geofence 6. Save the settings

On the “Reports” tab, you can generate a report for selected objects and parameters. 1. Select vehicles In the “Vehicles” field, select one or more objects to get the report for. 2. Select the report type Specify the report type you need, for example: — by mileage — by time in motion and parking — by fuel consumption — by sensors 3. Set the period Select the start and end dates. If needed, specify the exact time (hours and minutes) — the report is generated only for the selected period. 4. Select grouping Determine how the data is grouped: By dates — to track changes over time By objects — to compare different vehicles 5. Specify sensor groups Select one or more sensor groups if they are needed for the report. 6. Download the report Tap “Download report”. The file is generated automatically — you can open or save it.

The PILOT Guarda app can show detailed information about the car’s condition: battery charge, fuel level, temperature and other parameters. For this data to appear in the app, you need to do the following in advance: — set up sensors in PILOT — assign tags to them A tag is a unique name assigned to a sensor in the monitoring system. Thanks to tags, the app knows which sensor is responsible for what and displays the information on the screen correctly. Which sensors can be connected Tag What it shows garm_main_battery Car battery charge. As a rule, this is the supply voltage at the monitoring device garm_engine_lock_status Engine blocking status garm_fuel_level Fuel level garm_engine_temperature Engine temperature garm_flat_cable_fault_status Wiring harness fault status garm_on_board_temperature Car interior temperature garm_on_board_humidity Car interior humidity garm_output_1_status Output 1 status garm_output_2_status Output 2 status garm_output_3_status Output 3 status garm_engine_status Ignition status How to set up sensors Sensors are set up in PILOT: 1. Open the user account 2. Select the object you need. Right-click to open the object menu 3. Go to the “Sensors” tab 4. Create a new sensor or open an existing one 5. Specify the tag you need from the list above The app uses the tag to understand which data to show on the “Car status” screen. For example: — if a temperature sensor is assigned the garm_on_board_temperature tag, the app shows the car interior temperature — if an external power sensor is assigned the garm_main_battery tag, the app shows the car battery charge — if an ignition sensor is assigned the garm_engine_status tag, the app shows the engine state — on or off If the tag you need is not in the list, first create it , then assign it to the sensor. 6. Save the changes After that, the sensor data starts to appear in the mobile app on the “Car status” screen. 1 — Car battery voltage 2 — Ignition state 1 — Current fuel level in the tank 2 — Interior temperature Other parameters that can be shown in the app in the car summary: Balance — SIM card status of the monitoring device Temperature — engine temperature Door state — open or closed Headlight state — on or off Security state — on or off

For the “Open” and “Close” buttons to work in the app, you need to set up the arm and disarm command templates in PILOT. Command templates are set up in PILOT: 1. Open the user account 2. Go to the “Main” section 3. Click the “Commands” icon 3. A window opens where you can create command templates. How to create a command template 1. Click “Add command” 2. Select the object the command is created for 3. Click 3. Specify the parameters: Command type — GRPS Command kind — SMS_VIA_GPRS 4. In the “SMS” field, enter the command text, for example: setdigout 0 — disarm 5. If needed, select the hex checkbox if the command must be sent in HEX format 6. Click “Save as template” and enter a name Template names must be exactly as follows: arm — arm the object disarm — disarm the object get_beacon_ids — get the tag list The names are written in lowercase. The app uses these names to find and run the commands. Command examples Arming — arm Device Command template Teltonika setdigout 1 Adm 333 BLEOUTPUT 0 Disarming — disarm Device Command template Teltonika setdigout 0 Adm 333 BLEOUTPUT 1 Getting the tag list — get_beacon_ids A command for getting the list of Bluetooth tags registered on the device. Device Command template Teltonika getparam 1600;1601;1602;1603;1604;1605;1606;1607;1608;1609;1610 For the commands to work correctly: — the device must be online — a security sensor must be set up in the system — it is needed so the app can show the current security status After the templates are set up, the “Close” and “Open” buttons become active, and you can control the car from the “Car status” screen.

PILOT Tracker is an app that turns your smartphone into a GPS tracker. With it, you can track the device location in real time and send data to the server. How to install PILOT Tracker 1. Open Google Play on your smartphone 2. In the search bar, enter Pilot Tracker or follow this link 3. Tap the “Install” button and wait for the app to install How to turn on the tracker Open the app and turn on the “Service status” switch. When the service is on, location data starts to be sent 2. Make sure your phone is connected to the internet (via mobile data or Wi-Fi) 3. To link the device to your account in the system, send the Device ID to technical support How to configure tracker parameters The following settings are available on the app’s main screen: Service status • If the switch is on — the tracker is active and location data is being sent • If the switch is off — the service is stopped and no data is sent Device ID The unique device number (for example, 705943). You need to give this number to technical support so that your device appears in the system. Server URL The address of the server that data is sent to. You can change this address if necessary. Location accuracy The higher the accuracy, the more precise the track, but it requires more power and traffic. Choose the best setting for your use. Frequency Set how often the tracker sends data to the server (for example, every 5 or 10 seconds). A shorter interval means a more detailed track but uses more battery and data. Distance Specify the distance traveled after which new points are sent. For example, every 50 m. This lets you avoid sending data when the object is barely moving. Angle Select the angle at which a new point is sent (for example, if the turn angle is greater than the set value). Offline buffering If you turn this option on, the tracker saves location data when there is no internet connection. As soon as the connection is restored, all accumulated data is automatically sent to the server. Wake lock If turned on, the app keeps the tracker running in the background, even if the phone is not in use. “Status” tab The “Status” tab shows the tracker’s operation log — here you can see the current state of the service as well as information about its recent operation. At the top of the screen there is a “Clear” button, which deletes the current list of messages. “Information” tab On the “Information” tab you will find recommendations on how to configure your phone for the tracker to work. 1. Open the “Information” tab in the app 2. Scroll down the screen, and you will see step-by-step recommendations as well as screenshots that will help you configure your phone (depending on the model) 3. Follow the suggested steps in the device’s system settings so that the tracker keeps working without interruption.

PILOT Extensions is a tool that lets developers extend the functionality of the PILOT monitoring system. With it you can add new features, integrate external services and adapt the platform to specific tasks. PILOT Extensions is suitable for: — developers and integrators who want to adapt the system to specific business tasks and connect external services. — companies that need more functionality than the standard version offers, for example, creating custom reports, integrating with other systems or customizing interfaces and visualizations — teams that want to quickly develop and test new ideas by building prototypes and minimum viable extensions (MVPs) for further iteration — organizations that value flexibility and the ability to extend the platform so that it can adapt to change and grow with the business Where to find documentation and examples All the material you need to get started with PILOT Extensions can be found in the official GitHub repository: PILOT Extensions repository Quick start guide in Russian Quick start guide in English Usage examples and instructions for working with ChatGPT to generate code API documentation for working with maps and markers How to get started 1. Go to the PILOT Extensions repository on GitHub 2. Read the installation and setup guide in the README file 3. Choose a suitable template or example for your extension — you will find examples and instructions in the docs folder 4. Implement your logic 5. Integrate the extension into the PILOT interface as described in the repository documentation For a clear explanation of the process of creating extensions with PILOT Extensions, we have prepared the video “How to create your own app with PILOT Extensions” . It shows how to use artificial intelligence to generate code automatically, connect data from PILOT, work with the API and integrate the extension into the system interface. https://youtu.be/Gw1SdHo-kxM?si=mDjEIpw-oaqCc7EK What PILOT extensions look like in the interface If extensions are available for your account, you can open the list from the additional actions menu: 1. Click in the upper right corner 2. In the drop-down list, select “Extensions” A window with the list of available extensions then opens. Extension list The “Extensions” window shows all extensions available for your account. The list is displayed as cards. For each extension, the following are usually shown: extension icon name author short description enable switch button with information about the extension If there are many extensions, you can use the search bar at the top of the window to find the one you need quickly. How to enable or disable an extension To the left of each extension there is a switch. If the switch is on, the extension is active for the user If the switch is off, the extension is not available in the interface After you enable it, the extension may: appear as a new menu item open as a separate module add new interface elements or actions to the system Extension information To the right of each extension there is a button . If you click it, a page with information about the extension opens. Unpublished extensions In the upper right corner of the extensions window there is the Show drafts option. Turning it on shows in the list not only published extensions but also draft versions — that is, extensions that have not yet been released. A draft is a working version of an extension that is under development, testing or refinement. This option is used when you need, for example, to check an extension before publication or to test a new feature. The Show drafts option is available to administrators only. Example extension One example of an extension is Airports List. This is a module that shows a list of airports and their locations on the map. After you enable the extension: a new section appears in the interface a screen with the list of airports opens a map is displayed alongside when you select a row in the list, you can immediately see the airport on the map Such an extension adds a new working tool to the system, rather than just a separate setting.

BI Analytics lets you connect monitoring system data to external BI platforms to build your own reports, charts, dashboards and analytics panels. With the BI Analytics API you can retrieve data on vehicles, drivers, trips, fuel consumption, “Eco-driving” violations and other indicators, and then use it in any BI system that supports REST API. BI Analytics is suitable both for simple reports and for building corporate analytics with your own metrics, filters and visualizations. You can use the data in BI systems such as: Microsoft Power BI Tableau Qlik Sense Apache Superset Grafana other platforms that support REST API What you need to connect Before connecting, make sure that: — the analytics module is enabled on the partner account — the analytics module is also enabled on the user s contract — the parameter bi_analytics = 1 is set in the partner configuration — you know the login and password of the partner account — you have chosen the correct server address After these settings are done, you can connect to the BI Analytics API from any supported BI platform. API documentation (Swagger) To view the structure of BI Analytics API methods, you can use the API documentation in Swagger format: BI API v1 — Swagger In the Swagger documentation you can: — view all available API methods — view the structure of requests and responses — download the API specification in JSON format

Access to the BI Analytics API is configured at two levels: At the partner account level 2. At the user contract level For access to work, you need to: — enable the analytics module for the partner — enable the analytics module in the user’s contract — add the bi_analytics = 1 configuration in the partner card If you do not have access to the module or configuration settings on the partner contract, contact technical support. Enable the analytics module on the partner account 1. In the admin panel, go to the “Partners” section 2. Double-click the partner you need — the partner card opens 3. Go to the “Modules” tab and enable the “Analytics module” 4. Then go to the “Configuration” tab 5. Click the “Add” button 6. In the list, select the bi_analytics configuration and set its value to 1 7. Save the changes 2. Enable the analytics module on the user’s contract After the module is enabled on the partner account, you also need to enable it on the specific user contract. 1. In the admin panel, find the contract you need 2. Right-click it and select “Edit” 3. In the contract card, go to the “Modules” tab 4. Enable the “Analytics module” 5. Save the changes Once the analytics module is enabled on both the partner account and the user contract, and the bi_analytics configuration is set up, access to the BI Analytics API is enabled.

To connect to the BI Analytics API, you need to obtain the authorization data and configure the connection parameters correctly. To connect, you will need: — the login and password of the partner account — the address of the server your account runs on Once you have this data, you can use the BI Analytics API to connect to Power BI or any other BI system that supports working with REST API. Where to get the login and password To connect to the BI Analytics API, you need the login and password of the partner account. Use the same credentials that were issued to you when the partner account was registered. These are the same login and password that are used to log in to the admin panel. If you have access with main administrator rights, you can view this data in the partner account card, on the “Main settings” tab: Login — use as username Password — use as password How to choose the server address To connect to the BI Analytics API, you must specify the server address in the BaseUrl parameter of the request. Use the server your account runs on. Server Address Purpose Production https://pilot-gps.com Main server Saudi Arabia https://ksa.pilot-gps.com Regional server for Saudi Arabia Africa https://pilot-gps.africa Regional server for Africa Blade https://blade.pilot-gps.com Blade server Iglit https://gps.iglit.tech Iglit server In the request, specify the URL you need, for example, BaseUrl = "https://ksa.pilot-gps.com",

This article shows an example of connecting through Microsoft Power BI. You can connect in the same way to any BI system that supports working with REST API. How to add a query in Power BI 1. Open Power BI Desktop Launch Power BI Desktop on your computer. If it is not installed, download it free of charge from the official Microsoft website. 2. On the main ribbon at the top, click the “Get data” button. A list of available data sources opens 3. From the list of data sources, select “Blank query” 4. The Power Query Editor opens — a window where data queries are created and configured. In this window, find the “Advanced Editor” button on the toolbar at the top and click it. 5. The “Advanced Editor” window opens with an empty query template 6. Paste the query code (see the query example below) In the query you need to specify: Server address Login — your login from the partner account Password — your password from the partner account Dates — the start and end date of the period List of metrics — which data you want to get (see the full list of metrics below) 7. After pasting the code, click “Done”. Power BI starts connecting to the server and loading data 8. After that, Power BI may show the warning “Information is required about data privacy”. Click “Continue”. 9. The “Privacy Levels” window opens In it, Power BI checks whether it is safe to combine and process data from the sources used in the query. In our case, the query accesses one trusted data source, and authorization is already performed inside the query itself. So that Power BI does not block loading or interfere with the query, select the “Skip privacy level checks for this file” checkbox. Then click “Save”. 10. After you save, Power BI runs the query and opens a data preview in the Power Query Editor. A table with columns and rows appears on the screen — this is the data returned by your query. 11. Click “Close Apply”. The data is then loaded into Power BI, and you can work with it. You can now use the loaded data to create charts, tables and other visual elements. The following panes are usually displayed on the right of the main Power BI Desktop window: Visualizations — this is where the types of charts, diagrams, cards, tables and other visual elements are located. Select the type you need, then fill it with your fields Data — this shows the list of tables and fields loaded from your query, for example, date, object ID, mileage, fuel consumption, average speed. Use these fields in visualizations: select them with checkboxes, drag them with the mouse or swap them Filters — here you can limit the data by the conditions you need How to build a chart 1. In the “Visualizations” pane, click the chart type you need. An empty chart template appears on the report canvas 2. In the “Data” pane, select the fields you want to show 3. Power BI automatically places the fields in the chart In Power BI you can combine data: add the same field to different charts compare several indicators build several visualizations on one page replace fields without recreating the report If the query does not refresh or login errors occur Sometimes Power BI may keep the previous connection parameters for the data source. Because of this, even after you change the login, password or server address, the query may keep returning an authorization error. In this case, clear the saved permissions for the data source. How to clear permissions: 1. In the Power Query Editor, click “Data source settings” on the toolbar 2. In the window that opens, select the data source you need, for example, your server address 1 — “Data source settings” button 2 — Selecting the data source 3 — “Clear Permissions” button 3. Click “Clear Permissions” 4. In the confirmation window, click “Delete” 5. Run the query again. Power BI then applies the connection parameters anew

This article provides example requests for working with the BI Analytics API. You can use them as a basis for connecting Power BI or another BI system that supports REST API. Depending on your task, you can choose one of two options: Basic example — suitable for getting to know the API, testing the connection and building simple integrations. It shows the minimum set of steps needed to authorize, send a request and receive data. Advanced example — recommended for production integrations and regular data refresh. In addition to authorization and data retrieval, it includes API error handling, response structure validation, handling of empty results and automatic conversion of data into a format convenient for Power BI. We recommend using the advanced example in production projects, as it provides more reliable error handling and makes the integration easier to maintain. Basic request example let BaseUrl = "https:// server_address ", LoginJson = Json.Document( Web.Contents( BaseUrl, [ RelativePath = "api/bi/login.php", Headers = [#"Content-Type" = "application/json"], Content = Json.FromValue([ username = "YOUR_LOGIN", password = "YOUR_PASSWORD" ]), ManualStatusHandling = {400, 401, 403, 404, 500} ] ) ), Token = LoginJson[access_token], NodeId = LoginJson[user][node_id], AnalyticsJson = Json.Document( Web.Contents( BaseUrl, [ RelativePath = "api/bi/analytics.php", Query = [node = Text.From(NodeId)], Headers = [ #"Authorization" = "Bearer " Token, #"Content-Type" = "application/json" ], Content = Json.FromValue([ date_from = "2026-01-01", date_to = "2026-12-31", metrics = { "veh_driving_dist", "veh_fuel_cons", "average_speed", "veh_cars_counter" }, source = "vehicle", group_by = "source_day", format = "flat" ]), ManualStatusHandling = {400, 401, 403, 404, 500}, ExcludedFromCacheKey = {"Authorization"} ] ) ), DataList = AnalyticsJson[data], Tbl = Table.FromList(DataList, Splitter.SplitByNothing(), {"Column1"}), Expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn( Tbl, "Column1", {"source_id", "date", "veh_driving_dist", "veh_fuel_cons", "average_speed", "veh_cars_counter"} ) in Expanded Advanced request example This example includes API error handling, response structure validation and automatic conversion of data into a Power BI table. let BaseUrl = "https://pilot-gps.com", // --- API ERROR HANDLING --- ApiJson = (Response as binary, Context as text) as record = let Status = try Value.Metadata(Response)[Response.Status] otherwise 200, ParsedJson = try Json.Document(Response) otherwise error Error.Record( Context, "API response is not valid JSON", [ status = Status, body = Text.FromBinary(Response) ] ), ErrorMessage = if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "error_description") then ParsedJson[error_description] else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "msg") then ParsedJson[msg] else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "errors") then Text.Combine(List.Transform(ParsedJson[errors], each Text.From(_)), "; ") else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "error") then Text.From(ParsedJson[error]) else "API request failed", CheckedJson = if Status = 400 then error Error.Record( Context, ErrorMessage, ParsedJson ) else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "success") and ParsedJson[success] = false then error Error.Record( Context, ErrorMessage, ParsedJson ) else ParsedJson in CheckedJson, // --- LOGIN --- LoginResponse = Web.Contents( BaseUrl, [ RelativePath = "api/bi/login.php", Headers = [#"Content-Type" = "application/json"], Content = Json.FromValue([ username = "LOGIN", password = "PASSWORD" ]), ManualStatusHandling = {400, 422, 429, 500} ] ), LoginJson = ApiJson(LoginResponse, "BI Analytics login"), Token = LoginJson[access_token], NodeId = LoginJson[user][node_id], NodeQuery = if NodeId = null then [] else [node = Text.From(NodeId)], // --- ANALYTICS REQUEST --- AnalyticsResponse = Web.Contents( BaseUrl, [ RelativePath = "api/bi/analytics.php", Query = NodeQuery, Headers = [ #"Authorization" = "Bearer " Token, #"Content-Type" = "application/json" ], Content = Json.FromValue([ date_from = "2026-01-01", date_to = "2026-12-31", metrics = { "veh_driving_dist", "veh_fuel_cons", "average_speed", "veh_cars_counter" }, source = "vehicle", group_by = "source_day", format = "flat", page = 1, per_page = 100 ]), ManualStatusHandling = {400, 422, 429, 500}, ExcludedFromCacheKey = {"Authorization"} ] ), AnalyticsJson = ApiJson( AnalyticsResponse, "BI Analytics request" ), // --- DATA CHECK --- DataList = if Record.HasFields(AnalyticsJson, "data") then AnalyticsJson[data] else error Error.Record( "BI Analytics response", "Response does not contain data field", AnalyticsJson ), // --- CONVERSION TO TABLE --- Tbl = if List.IsEmpty(DataList) then #table( { "source_id", "date", "veh_driving_dist", "veh_fuel_cons", "average_speed", "veh_cars_counter" }, {} ) else Table.FromList( DataList, Splitter.SplitByNothing(), {"Column1"} ), Expanded = if List.IsEmpty(DataList) then Tbl else Table.ExpandRecordColumn( Tbl, "Column1", { "source_id", "date", "veh_driving_dist", "veh_fuel_cons", "average_speed", "veh_cars_counter" } ), #"Changed Types" = Table.TransformColumnTypes( Expanded, { {"source_id", Int64.Type}, {"date", type date}, {"veh_driving_dist", type number}, {"veh_fuel_cons", type number}, {"average_speed", type number}, {"veh_cars_counter", Int64.Type} } ), #"Sorted Rows" = Table.Sort( #"Changed Types", { {"source_id", Order.Ascending}, {"date", Order.Ascending} } ) in #"Sorted Rows"

When sending requests to the BI Analytics API, you must specify parameters that define which data to retrieve and in what form to return it. In addition to the request parameters, you must select metrics — the indicators that will be included in the result. They determine what data the API returns, for example mileage, fuel consumption, number of trips or eco-driving violations. Main request parameters Request parameters define the data source, the way the data is grouped and additional selection conditions. source The source field defines which data the selection is built from. Available values: vehicle — vehicle data driver — driver data group_by The group_by field defines how to group the result. Value What it shows Example response structure total Total for all vehicles or drivers for the period { "metric": 123 } day Total for all vehicles or drivers for each day { "20260301": { "metric": 123 } } rating Each source, total for the period { source_id: { "metric": 123 } } source_day Each source, each day { source_id: { "20260301": { "metric": 123 } } } ACCOUNT_ID The ACCOUNT_ID parameter lets you limit the export to the data of a single contract. If the request specifies the login and password of a partner account, then without ACCOUNT_ID the system exports all vehicles under all contracts available to this partner. If you specify ACCOUNT_ID in the request, only the objects of the selected contract will be loaded. Available metrics Metrics define which indicators the API returns. They are passed in the metrics parameter as a list. For example: metrics = [ "veh_driving_dist", "veh_fuel_cons", "average_speed" ] Below is the list of supported metrics. Vehicles — general Parameter Description veh_trips_cnt Number of trips veh_driving_dist Mileage (km) veh_driving_time Driving time veh_parking_time Parking time veh_ignition_time Ignition-on time veh_idle_time Idle time veh_motor_hours Engine hours Vehicles — fuel Parameter Description veh_fuel_cons Fuel consumption veh_fuel_filled Fuel refueled veh_fuel_drained Fuel drained Vehicles — violations Parameter Description veh_eco_fine Eco-driving penalty veh_eco_cnt Number of eco-driving violations veh_acc_fine Harsh acceleration penalty veh_acc_cnt Number of harsh accelerations veh_braking_fine Harsh braking penalty veh_braking_cnt Number of harsh brakings veh_turn_fine Harsh turning penalty veh_turn_cnt Number of harsh turns veh_speed_fine Speeding penalty veh_speed_cnt Number of speeding events veh_belt_fine Unfastened seat belt penalty veh_belt_cnt Number of seat belt violations veh_idle_fine Idling penalty veh_idle_cnt Number of idling violations Vehicles — costs Parameter Description veh_fuel_cost_per_kilometer Fuel cost per km veh_service_cost_per_kilometer Maintenance cost per km veh_amount_exp Total expenses cost_of_using Cost of use average_speed Average speed veh_cars_counter Number of vehicles Drivers Parameter Description drv_trips_cnt Number of trips drv_driving_dist Mileage (km) drv_driving_time Driving time drv_parking_time Parking time drv_fuel_cons Fuel consumption drv_fuel_filled Fuel refueled drv_fuel_drained Fuel drained drv_eco_fine Eco-driving penalty drv_eco_cnt Number of eco-driving violations drv_acc_fine Harsh acceleration penalty drv_acc_cnt Number of harsh accelerations drv_braking_fine Harsh braking penalty drv_braking_cnt Number of harsh brakings drv_turn_fine Harsh turning penalty drv_turn_cnt Number of harsh turns drv_speed_fine Speeding penalty drv_speed_cnt Number of speeding events drv_belt_fine Unfastened seat belt penalty drv_belt_cnt Number of seat belt violations Metrics for individual eco-event types To get data on individual types of Eco-driving events, use metrics in the following format: eco_{N}_fine — number of penalty points for the event type eco_{N}_cnt — number of registered events of this type Here N is the identifier (ID) of the driving quality event type. Each event type has its own unique ID, which the system assigns automatically when the type is created. This identifier is used in the API to form metric names. For example, in the types directory of driving quality, the standard events may have the following identifiers: ID Event type 1 Acceleration 2 Braking 3 Turn 4 Speed 5 Seat Belt If custom event types have been created in the system, they are also assigned unique IDs automatically. When composing a request, specify the ID of the required event type instead of N. Examples Parameter What it returns eco_1_fine / eco_1_cnt Penalty points and number of Acceleration events eco_2_fine / eco_2_cnt Penalty points and number of Braking events eco_4_fine / eco_4_cnt Penalty points and number of Speed events eco_5_fine / eco_5_cnt Penalty points and number of Seat Belt events You can view event type identifiers in the “Driving quality types” directory . The value is shown in the ID column. When a new type is created, the system automatically assigns it a unique identifier, which is then used in BI Analytics API metrics.

An API (Application Programming Interface) is a set of rules and tools that lets programs interact with each other. In PILOT, the API is used to exchange data between systems, services, applications and the platform. An API request consists of: URL — the API server address and the command Request parameters — the data sent to the server Request method — the way of interacting with the server How the API works in PILOT PILOT uses a distributed infrastructure that includes several servers, for example, BLADE, KSA, AFRICA, USA. Each server can have several nodes, each with its own number. When you send an API request to the system, specify the particular server (for example, BLADE) and the particular node within that server — node. This way, the request is processed directly on the selected server and node, without extra forwarding and with minimal response time. Example request https://blade.pilot-gps.com/api/api.php?cmd=list node=14 blade.pilot-gps.com is the server name node=14 indicates the node (server) where the request must be processed. To learn more about how to authorize and send requests to the PILOT server, read the next article . Request methods in the API GET A method for getting data. It is used, for example, to request the list of objects or account information. In a GET request, the command and parameters are passed directly in the URL. Parameters are added after the ? sign and separated by the character. Example https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=bindControl uid=123 imei=456 lineuid=789 cmd=bindControl — command uid=123, imei=456, lineuid=789 — parameters POST A method for sending data. It is used, for example, to create a new object or generate a report. In a POST request, the command and parameters can be passed in the request body, or the command is specified in the URL and the parameters are passed in the body. Example 1 URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=bindControl Request body { "uid": "123", "imei": "456", "lineuid": "789" } Example 2 URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php Request body { "cmd": "bindControl", "uid": "123", "imei": "456", "lineuid": "789" } PUT A method for updating data. This type of request is used, for example, to change the parameters of an object or account. PUT is most often used to update a specific resource, so the identifier is usually specified in the URL and the data to update in the body. Example URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php/123 Request body: { "cmd": "updateControl", "uid": "123", "imei": "456", "lineuid": "789", "status": "active" } DELETE A method for deleting data. For example, this method is used to delete an object or an account. In a DELETE request, the command and parameters are usually passed in the URL. Example https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=bindControl uid=123 imei=456 lineuid=789 Data format The API supports various formats for both requests and responses. JSON: { "cmd": "bindControl", "uid": "123", "imei": "456", "lineuid": "789" } Form-encoded: cmd=bindControl uid=123 imei=456 lineuid=789 XML: request cmd bindControl /cmd uid 123 /uid imei 456 /imei lineuid 789 /lineuid /request Data types The API uses various data types to transfer information between the client and the server. Let s look at the main data types you may encounter in API requests and responses. Data type Description Example in JSON format What they are used for String Text in quotes "name": "Маршрут №9" For text data: names, descriptions, identifiers Number Numeric value, integer or fractional "price": 15.35 For numeric data: prices, identifiers, coordinates, time Array Ordered list of elements of any type "points": [{"lat": "53.352142", "lon": "83.758749"}, {"lat": "52.534012", "lon": "85.178777"}] For lists of data: stops, goods, users Object Set of "key — value" pairs "uid": "1", "lat": "53.352142", "lon":"83.758749"} For structured data: information about a stop, user, order Boolean type (Boolean) Logical value true/false or 1/0 "bidirectional": 1 For flags or states: active/inactive, available/unavailable

This article explains how to authorize and send a request to the API. After that you will be able to send commands to the server and receive data from it. API address All requests are sent to the following address: https:// server_address /api/api.php server_address is the address of the server or host where PILOT runs. For example: For users: https://pilot-gps.com/api/api.php For administrators: https://admin.pilot-gps.com/ax/api.php The API can be located in different “folders” of the project, and this is reflected in the request address, for example: https:// server_address /backend/api.php https:// server_address /ax/api.php Folders (api, backend, ax and others) are simply the project structure. They show which set of commands you are accessing. Always use the full folder path given in the specific API command, otherwise the request will not work. Authorization type Basic Auth is used to connect to the API. For the regular (user) API, sign in with the login and password of your account. To work with the administrator API, use the administrator s login and password. What a request looks like The general form of a request is: https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd= command node= node_num cmd — the command you want to execute node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example response In reply to your request, the server returns a response in JSON format: { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", ...requested data... } code = 0 — everything completed successfully code = 1 — an error occurred msg — a message from the server (for example, OK or an error description) If you prefer to work with XML, add the parameter out=xml to the request, and the result will come in XML format. Example request: https:// address /api/api.php?cmd= command node= node_num out=xml The response in this case will be: response code 0 /code msg OK /msg ...requested data... /response If you are just getting started with the API, we recommend first reading the article “Working with API requests” to understand what commands, parameters and data formats are.

The Admin API is a special set of commands that provides extended capabilities not available to regular users. It is intended for managing the system and performing administrative tasks. With the Admin API you can: Create, modify or delete user accounts Configure access rights and roles Get information about the state of objects Configure system and module parameters To work with the Admin API, use the login and password of the administrator account.

This API is used to create a new account (contract), including account information and user data (including the administrator s login and password). After the request is executed, an account with a unique ID is created, and the first user (administrator) is added with the specified login and password. How to get the data To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /ax/api.php? Method POST Request parameters Required parameters: cmd=accountadd — command to add a new account bill_price — price list ID (must be obtained from the pricelist command). inn — organization s tax ID (INN) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Optional parameters: acc_deposit — deposit amount (0 by default) acc_type — billing type: — 1 by default — postpaid — 2— prepaid — 3— postpaid lite (with a shutdown threshold) org_type — organization type — 1 by default — legal entity — 2— individual — 3— sole proprietor bill_phone — organization s phone number comment — comment on the account code — 1C code kpp —KPP (tax registration reason code) block_limit — shutdown threshold for postpaid lite billing modules — comma-separated IDs of connected modules (obtained from the modlist command) bill_email — email for the account org_name — organization name Example request https:// server_address /ax/api.php?cmd=accountadd bill_price=143 bill_email=demo1@skyelectronics.ru org_name=PUP comment=lalala inn=123456789012 acc_type=1 org_type=1 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "id": "4018", "login": "demo1@skyelectronics.ru", "password": "blPs0S" }, "msg": "OK" } The API request returns: code — response status — 0— the operation was successful data — data about the new account id — unique account identifier login — login of the administrator created within this account password — administrator s password msg — message with the result of the operation

This API retrieves a list of accounts with basic information: contract ID, name, balance and number of vehicles. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=accountslist — command to get the list of accounts node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=accountslist node=1 Response { "id": 10, "org_name": "Test relaying", "org_type": 2, "balance": "0.00", "acc_deposit": "40000.00", "comment": null, "inn": null, "kpp": null, "bill_email": "relay@mail.com", "bill_phone": "43542554", "hidden": 1, "veh_count": 0 } The API request returns: id — unique account identifier org_name — name of the organization or contract org_type — organization type balance — current contract balance acc_deposit — deposit amount on the contract comment — additional comment on the contract inn — organization s INN (taxpayer identification number) kpp — organization s KPP (tax registration reason code) bill_email — email specified for invoicing or billing notifications bill_phone — phone number for billing inquiries hidden — deleted account flag: 0 — the account is not deleted, 1 — the account is deleted veh_count — number of vehicles assigned to this contract

This API creates a new PILOT user and assigns the main data to them: login, password, name, role, phone, email and available contracts. Method GET Request address To execute the request, use the address:: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters • cmd=create_user — command to create a user • login — login of the new user • password — password of the new user • name — user s name • role_id — ID of the user s role • phone — user s phone number • email — user s email • accounts — list of IDs of the contracts the user should get access to. If there are several contracts, separate them with commas • account_id — ID of the contract in which the user is created Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=create_user login=TestAPI13 password=Qwerty123 name=test Api 13 role_id=1 phone=789995 email=testapi13@mailinator.com accounts=1106,1131 account_id=1003 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success create user: 729", "user_id": 729 } The API request returns: • code — command result code. A value of 0 means successful execution • msg — text message with the result of the command • user_id — ID of the created user

This API is used to get the list of users of a specific account with basic information about each user. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=users — command to get the list of users accountid — ID of the account for which users are requested node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=users accountid=56832 Response { "data": [ { "id": 88977, "name": "valera_test", "login": "valera17totsenko@gmail.com", "passwd": "123456", "info": null, "email": "valera17totsenko@gmail.com", "lang": "en", "roleid": 0 } ], "code": 0, "msg": "OK" } The API request returns: id — user ID name — display name login — login passwd — password info — additional user information email — email address lang — user interface language roleid — role ID

This API changes the list of contracts that a PILOT user has access to. Method GET Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php?
