Request parameters • cmd=update_user_accounts_map — command to change user access to contracts • accounts — list of IDs of the contracts the user should have access to. If there are several contracts, separate them with commas • user_id — ID of the user whose access is being changed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=update_user_accounts_map accounts=1087 user_id=535 If you need to specify several contracts: https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=update_user_accounts_map accounts=1087,1131 user_id=535 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success" } The API request returns: • code — command result code. A value of 0 means successful execution • msg — text message with the result of the command

Use this API to get the list of rates available for an account, with information on currency, price and description. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=pricelist — command to get the list of rates node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Additionally: coden (optional) — currency code: — numeric (for example, 840 for USD, 810 for RUB) — alphabetic (for example, USD or RUR) Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=pricelist coden=840 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "id": 143, "code": "840", "currency": 2, "descr": "3 dollars per property per month", "name": "US dollar", "price": "3.00" } ], "message": "OK" } The API request returns: code — request execution code (0 — success) data — array of rates: id — unique rate identifier code — currency code (numeric) currency — internal currency identifier descr — rate description name — rate name (for example, US dollar ) price — rate price in the specified currency message — text message about the result of the request

This API is used to add payment information to a contract. You can specify the amount, date, payment ID in the external system and description. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /ax/api.php? Request parameters Required: cmd=payment — command to add a payment inn — contract INN (unique identifier) sum — payment amount (format dd.dd) id — payment ID in the external system date — payment date (format DDMMYYYY) descr — payment description (string), for example: “payment for connection” node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /ax/api.php?cmd=payment inn=123123123 sum=10.00 id=124 date=04042016 descr=test%20payment node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Payment inserted successfully", "data": { "payment_id": 124, "inn": "123123123", "sum": 10.00, "date": "04042016", "descr": "test payment" } }

Use this API to add an object to a contract. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters To get the data you need, add parameters to the request address. Parameters are specified after the question mark “?” and separated by the “ ” sign. Required: cmd = vehadd — command to add a vehicle account_id — contract number in the system vehmodel — monitoring device model. The model ID is taken from the response of the vehmodellist command imei — unique number of the monitoring device type — vehicle type. The vehicle type ID is taken from the response of the vehtypelist command. If the required type is not in the list, you can specify a new ID name — license plate or name of the vehicle msisdn — number of the device s primary SIM card msisdn2 — number of the device s second SIM card mac — MAC address, identifier of the bus conductor device. If the mac parameter is specified, the system automatically creates a record of the object in the “Buses” tab in the Admin panel. node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Optional: folder — name of the folder to add the vehicle to. If the specified folder does not exist, it will be created. If no folder is specified, the vehicle is added to the general list — the root folder info — additional information about the vehicle summer_fuel — fuel consumption in summer winter_fuel — fuel consumption in winter fuel_type — type of fuel used . 50-diesel, 80-92-95-98-gasoline, 100-gas. If the parameter is not specified, the system automatically sets diesel lost_connection_time — time after which connection loss is registered (in seconds) time_zone — vehicle time zone. Europe/Moscow is set by default initial_motor_hours — initial engine hours reading driver_id — driver identifier initial_mileage — initial mileage of the vehicle. If not specified, counting starts from zero speed_limit — maximum permitted speed. If not specified, speed control is disabled minsat — minimum number of satellites. 4 by default maxhdop — maximum HDOP. 21 by default mintime — minimum parking time for splitting tracks. 3600 seconds by default maxspeed — maximum possible speed. 250 by default minspeed — minimum speed for detecting the start of movement. 10 km/h by default minparking — minimum parking time on a route. 300 seconds by default model — make and model of the vehicle year — year of manufacture of the vehicle. If the year of manufacture is not specified, it defaults to 1900 vin — vehicle identification number engine_horse: — engine power organization — name of the owner organization column — column number subdivision — subdivision Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=vehadd account_id=4019 type=1 name=testveh imei=80987898789987 vehmodel=13 msisdn=7903 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "agent_id": "20518", "veh_id": "18994" } The API request returns: code — response code that shows how the request was processed msg — message with a text description of the result of the operation agent_id — identifier of the agent that processed the request veh_id — identifier of the vehicle this response refers to

This API is used to edit vehicle data. You can change vehicle information, including type, model, license plate, VIN, year of manufacture, engine power, initial mileage and engine hours, as well as the assignment to a folder, driver or subdivision. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters Required: cmd=vehedit — command to change vehicle information agentid— vehicle identifier, or imei — unique device ID node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Optional: type — vehicle type, the ID is taken from the vehtypelist command veh_number — displayed name/license plate of the vehicle veh_type — custom vehicle type (string) folder_id — folder in which the object is placed; if the folder does not exist, it is created automatically. The root folder by default model — vehicle model initial_motor_hours — initial engine hours driver_id — driver ID initial_mileage — initial mileage (0 by default) year — year of manufacture of the vehicle (1900 by default) vin — vehicle VIN engine_horse — engine power organization — organization column — column subdivision — subdivision Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=vehedit agentid=144 node=1 Response { "Success": "The vehicle data has been changed" }

This API is used to move a vehicle between accounts. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters To get the data you need, add parameters to the request address. Parameters are specified after the question mark “?” and separated by the “ ” sign. cmd = veh_move_account — command to move objects to another account vehicle_id — identifier of the vehicle to be moved to the account account_id — number of the new account node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd =veh_move_account vehicle_id=23 account_id=1005 node=1 Response {"code": 1, "msg": "Success move vehicle 23 to account 1005"} The API request returns: code — result code: — 1 — the operation was completed successfully — 0 — an error occurred during the operation msg —message with a text description of the result of the operation

This API is used to get complete information about a vehicle. You can request data either by agent_id or by the device IMEI number. The response returns detailed information: license plate, fuel consumption, speed limits, VIN, model, configuration settings, assigned driver and more. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters Required: cmd=vehinfo — command to get vehicle information node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed One of these parameters must be specified: agentid — vehicle identifier (agent_id) imei — unique IMEI number of the device Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=vehinfo agentid=81181 node=1 Response [ { "ownerid": 5374, "vehiclenumber": "Howen C", "typeid": 1, "summer_fuel": "10", "winter_fuel": "10", "idle_fuel": "2", "time_zone": "Europe/Moscow", "speed_limit": 0, "agentid": 81181, "account_id": 3925, "model": "", "year": "1900", "vin": "", "fuel_type": "50", "driver_name": "Test", "driver_phone": "12121212121" } ] The API request returns: ownerid — owner ID vehiclenumber — license plate or name of the vehicle typeid — vehicle type summer_fuel / winter_fuel / idle_fuel — fuel consumption norms (summer, winter, idling) time_zone — time zone in which the vehicle is used speed_limit — speed limit account_id — ID of the contract the vehicle is assigned to model / year / vin — model, year of manufacture and VIN of the vehicle fuel_type — fuel type driver_name / driver_phone — full name and phone number of the assigned driver config — JSON with additional configuration (settings for fuel, engine hours, restrictions, etc.)

This API provides a list of all vehicles assigned to a specific account, with their current state. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=vehicles — command to get the list of vehicles account_id — ID of the account for which you need to get the list of objects node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Optional parameters: is_show_deleted — show deleted vehicles (0 — show only active vehicles, 1 — show all vehicles, including deleted ones) The format of the requested data is an array of vehicle data. Example request Showing deleted objects: https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=vehicles account_id=2238 is_show_deleted=1 node=1 Response { "data": [ { "active": 1, "deleted": 0, "agentid": 2914, "configuration": "Teltonika FM1100", "current_mileage": 69332, "dir": 0, "driver_name": "SSS", "driver_phone": "", "folder": "ЮФО", "lat": "47.200989", "lon": "39.634436", "model": "HYUNDAI IX35", "msisdn": "79818775160", "on": 1, "partner_price": "0.00", "price": "0.00", "sats": 7, "speed": 0, "ts": "1457709039", "type": "Static", "uniqid": "356307045913463", "vehiclenumber": "IX35" }, { "active": 0, "deleted": 1, "agentid": 8026, "configuration": "Teltonika FM4200", "current_mileage": 17441, "dir": 0, "driver_name": "", "driver_phone": "", "folder": "ЮФО", "lat": "47.318118", "lon": "39.995648", "model": "", "msisdn": "79110181596", "on": 1, "partner_price": "100.00", "price": "350.00", "sats": 9, "speed": 0, "ts": "1457726726", "type": "Car", "uniqid": "354330031297057", "vehiclenumber": "nex" } ] } The API request returns: active — object activity status: 1 — active, 0 — inactive deleted — whether the object was deleted: 0 — not deleted, 1 — deleted agentid — unique device number configuration — name of the GPS hardware configuration (for example, Teltonika FM1100) current_mileage — vehicle mileage, km dir — direction of movement driver_name — driver s name (if assigned) driver_phone — driver s phone number folder — name of the folder/category in the system lat — geographic latitude of the last position lon — geographic longitude of the last position model — vehicle model msisdn — tracker SIM number on — ignition (1 — on, 0 — off) partner_price — price for the partner price — retail price sats — number of satellites with which contact is established speed — current speed, km/h ts — timestamp (UNIX time) of the last position update type — object type uniqid — unique device identifier (usually the IMEI) vehiclenumber — vehicle number

Use this API to get the list of all vehicle types in a contract. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=vehtypelist — command to get the list of vehicle types node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=vehtypelist node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "identifier": 1, "name": "Car" }, { "identifier": 2, "name": "Truck" }, { "identifier": 3, "name": "Passenger" }, { "identifier": 4, "name": "Agrimotor" } ], "message": "OK" } The API request returns: code — request execution code (0 — success) data — array of vehicle types: identifier — unique vehicle type identifier name — vehicle type name message — text message about the result of the request

This API blocks or unblocks objects by the agent_id, imei or account_id parameters. Depending on the status passed, the vehicle is either blocked or activated. Blocking or unblocking can be performed based on identifiers such as the agent, IMEI or contract number. How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Method POST Request parameters Required: cmd=setvehblock — command to block or unblock a vehicle. status — blocking status. Value: 0— blocked; 1— active (unblocked) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed One of these parameters must be specified: agentid — agent identifier imei — IMEI number of the device accountid — contract number Example requests Blocking a vehicle by IMEI: https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=setvehblock status=0 imei=1231231231 node=1 Unblocking a vehicle by agentid: https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=setvehblock status=1 agentid=2914 node=1 Response If the vehicle is blocked or unblocked successfully, you will receive the following response: { "code": 0, "data": [ { "agentid": 2914, "status": 1 } ], "msg": "OK" } The API request returns: code — response code. Value: — 0 — the operation was successful — other possible values: errors such as 400 or 500 if problems occurred. data — blocking/unblocking data agentid — Identifier of the agent whose status was changed status — Vehicle status: 0— blocked; 1— active (unblocked) msg — message about whether the operation succeeded

The API returns raw GPS track data of a vehicle for the specified period. This request can only be made for a period of no more than 10 days. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters Required: cmd=rawpoints — command to get raw points ts — start date of the selection in UNIX timestamp format te — end date of the selection in UNIX timestamp format agentid — vehicle identifier Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php? cmd=rawpoints ts=1760216400 te=1760302800 agentid=157773 Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "agentid": 2914, "height": 32, "direction": 1, "latitude": "47.215545", "longitude": "39.706906", "satsinview": 15, "servertime": 1458044666, "speed": 10, "triggerdata": "Priority=0;EventSource=0;DIS1=1;GSMVal=4;IN1=67;Vsourse=14547;", "unixtimestamp": 1458022428 }, { "agentid": 2914, "height": 32, "direction": 339, "latitude": "47.215938", "longitude": "39.706751", "satsinview": 12, "servertime": 1458044666, "speed": 12, "triggerdata": "Priority=0;EventSource=0;DIS1=1;GSMVal=4;IN1=67;Vsourse=14538;", "unixtimestamp": 1458022437 } ], "deb": [ 2914, 1458022428, 1458043980 ], "message": "OK" } The API request returns: code — request execution code (0 — success) data — array of points: agentid — vehicle identifier height/ altitude — altitude above sea level (m) direction — direction of movement (degrees) latitude/ longitude — coordinates of the point satsinview — number of visible satellites servertime — server time in UNIX timestamp speed — speed in km/h triggerdata — device trigger data unixtimestamp — event time in UNIX timestamp deb — array of debug information (agentid, start and end of the period) message — message about the result of the request

This API gets fuel consumption data for a specific vehicle over the selected period of time. It returns information about refuels, fuel consumed, drains and fuel sensor readings at the start and end of the period. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=fuel — command to get fuel data ts — start date of the selection in Unix timestamp format te — end date of the selection in Unix timestamp format agentid — vehicle ID (agent_id) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=fuel ts=1708981200 te=1709154000 agentid=6477 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "fill": 100, "fuel": 84, "stale": 0, "stop": 43 }, "msg": "OK" } The API request returns: code — request result code (0 = successful request) fill — amount of fuel refueled during the period fuel — amount of fuel consumed stale — amount of fuel drained or lost start — fuel sensor reading at the start of the period stop — fuel sensor reading at the end of the period msg — text message with the result of the request

This API is used to create a new folder in the system. You can specify the parent folder, the name of the new folder, and access rights for users. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters Required: cmd=addfolder — command to create a folder account_id — contract ID parent_id — parent folder ID folder_name — name of the folder to be created node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Optional: users— comma-separated list of IDs of users who should be given rights to this folder The value users=admins — gives rights to all users of the contract with the administrator role If the parameter is not set or is empty, the rights are copied from the parent folder Example requests Folder rights for all administrators: https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=addfolder account_id=5654 parent_id=654 folder_name=my_folder users=admins node=1 Folder rights for specific users: https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=addfolder account_id=5654 parent_id=654 folder_name=my_folder users=123,212,432 node=1 The folder is created with the rights of the parent folder (default): https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=addfolder account_id=5654 parent_id=654 folder_name=my_folder node=1 Response { "success": "Создана новая папка my_folder с идентификатором 27330" }

This API lets you change the name of an existing folder. To do this, send a request with parameters that identify the folder to be renamed and the new name for it. How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php Method POST Request parameters cmd=editfoldername — command to change the folder name folder_id — identifier of the folder whose name needs to be changed new_folder_name — new name for the folder node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=editfoldername folder_id=454545 new_folder_name=testname node=1 Response { "success": "Имя папки успешно обновлено" }

This API is used to get the list of folders. The response returns a list with unique folder IDs, their names and parent folders. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters Required: cmd=getfolders — command to get the list of folders node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Optional: account_id — ID of the account for which you need to get the list of folders Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=getfolders account_id=3925 node=1 Response { "9793": {"name": "АС-Капитал", "parent": "Колонна №1"}, "11462": {"name": "Ленэнерго", "parent": "Колонна №1"}, "12551": {"name": "Вектор", "parent": "test123"}, "16453": {"name": "test_alex", "parent": "1april"}, "18492": {"name": "31Novfolder", "parent": "Колонна №1"} } The API request returns: key (for example, 9793 ) — unique folder ID name — folder name parent — the parent folder that the current folder belongs to

This API deletes the specified folder and moves all vehicles from it to the root folder. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=deletefolder — command to delete a folder folder_id— identifier of the folder to be deleted node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=deletefolder folder_id=545 node=1 Response { "success": "Папка успешно удалена" }

Use this API to get the full list of modules available in a contract, with their identifiers and descriptions. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /ax/api.php? Request parameters cmd=modlist — command to get the list of modules node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /ax/api.php?cmd=modlist node=1 Response { "код": 0, "данные": [ { "descr": "Модуль топливных карт", "идентификатор": 7, "имя": "топливо" }, { "descr": "Модуль блокировки двигателя", "идентификатор": 8, "имя": "блок" }, { "descr": "Модуль уведомлений", "идентификатор": 27, "имя": "уведомление" } ], "сообщение": "ОК" } The API request returns: код — request execution code (0 — success) данные — array of module objects: descr — module description идентификатор — unique module ID имя — system name of the module сообщение — text message about the result of the request

This API is used to get the list of all hardware types (device models) used in a contract, with the manufacturer indicated. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php? Request parameters cmd=vehmodellist — command to get the list of hardware models node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=vehmodellist node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "identifier": 1, "name": "ASC-6 GPS/GLONASS", "supplier": "APK COM" }, { "identifier": 2, "name": "ASC-6 Lite GPS/GLONASS", "supplier": "APK COM" } ], "message": "OK" } The API request returns: code — request execution code (0 — success) data — array of hardware models: identifier — unique model identifier name — hardware model name supplier — hardware manufacturer message — text message about the result of the request

This article describes the main API commands that let you interact with Linux systems through the Admin panel. With these commands you can send, receive, delete and view the history of commands for Atoms . How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /backend/api.php List of commands cmd=atom_get_all — get the list of sent commands cmd=atom_get_commands — get the list of command templates cmd=atom_create_command — send a Linux command atom_delete_command — delete a Linux command Getting the list of sent Linux commands (command history) This command lets you get the list of all commands sent to an Atom. The history includes the Atom identifier, the command sent, and the execution status. Method: GET Request parameters cmd=atom_get_all — command to get the history ident — unique Atom identifier (for example, b0:44:6t:0d:a9:04) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=atom_get_all ident=b0:44:6t:0d:a9:04 node=1 Response [ { "id": 27899, "agent_id": null, "ident": "8v:f5:8c:01:13:70", "script": "ls /root/", "processed": null, "ts": 1712138610, "result": null } ] Getting the list of Linux command templates This command lets you get the list of Linux command templates that can be used to send to an Atom. Templates contain a description and the command that will be executed on the device. Method: GET Request parameters cmd=atom_get_commands — command to get command templates. ident — unique Atom identifier (for example, 80:c5:80:01:68:08). node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=atom_get_commands ident=80:c5:80:01:68:08 node=1 Response [ { "id": 36, "command_name": "Список Видео", "description": null, "command": "ls -lsh /video/*.avi" } ] Sending a Linux command With this command you can send a Linux command to an Atom. The command is added to the queue and executed on the device. Method: POST Request parameters cmd=atom_create_command — command to create a new command. ident — unique Atom identifier. script — command script (optional). node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=atom_create_command ident=b1:42:67:00:00:fd node=1 Response 27917 ( ID of the command added to the queue) Deleting a Linux command If a command has not been executed yet, you can remove it from the queue using this method. Deletion is only possible before the command is processed. Method: GET Request parameters cmd=atom_delete_command — command to delete ident — unique Atom identifier command_id — identifier of the command to delete node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /backend/api.php?cmd=atom_delete_command ident=b0:44:6f:0d:av:88 command_id=27921 Response "Success delete" API error codes 400 Bad request — invalid data format or a required parameter is missing. Possible messages: { error : Missing ident param } — the Atom identifier is missing. { error : Command already processed } — the command has already been executed. { error : Unknown macro: {Unknown macro} } — unknown macro command. 500 Internal server error — internal server error Working with commands in the interface In the PILOT interface, interaction with Atoms takes place through the “Auto Conductor → Buses” tab of the Admin panel, where the “Interact” command is available. Through this function: Commands (Linux commands) are sent to the Atom You can view the list of available commands (templates) The history of all sent commands is displayed The result of each command s execution is available

This API provides capabilities for managing vehicle rental contracts. With this API you can start, update and stop a rental, as well as authenticate and generate tokens for authorization. Authorization To use the API, you must authenticate with a Bearer token. Getting an authorization token Before sending requests, you must get a token by generating it with the login and password for the Admin panel. Authorization example Token generation request: curl --location --request GET 'https:// admin_address /backend/app/contracts.php' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "cmd": "generate_token", "login": "YOUR_LOGIN_FOR_ADMIN_PANEL", "password": "YOUR_PASSWORD_FOR_ADMIN_PANEL" }' Example response: { "code": 0, "odo": "0", "message": "007898667a1b5711682399ea38a84f61" } The response contains a token. Use it in the Authorization header for subsequent requests. Example header: Authorization: Bearer 007898667a1b5711682399ea38a84f61 Main commands To perform operations, you need to specify the cmd parameter, which defines which operation you want to perform. generate_token — get an authorization token start — start a vehicle rental update — update rental data stop — stop a vehicle rental Request parameters All parameters are passed in JSON format Parameter Type Required Description mva int Yes Numeric identifier of the rented vehicle ra int Yes Rental contract number plate_number string Yes Vehicle license plate driver_name string Yes Name of the driver renting the vehicle driver_phone string Yes Driver's phone number driver_passport string No Driver's passport driver_address string No Driver's address driver_license string No Driver's license number driver_license_exp string No License expiry date driver_email string No Driver's email driver_birth_date string No Driver's date of birth driver_sex string No Sex (m or f) driver_country string No Driver's country driver_rating int No Driver rating ts_expected int Yes Expected rental start time (Unix timestamp) te_expected int Yes Expected rental end time (Unix timestamp) ts_real int No Actual rental start time (Unix timestamp) te_real int No Actual rental end time (Unix timestamp) start_location object Yes Rental start location (with latitude, longitude or an address string — lat, lon, address) end_location object Yes Rental end location (lat, lon or address) rate_code string No Rental rate code under the contract car_group_charged string No Vehicle group checkout_branch string No Pick-up branch mileage_limit int No Mileage limit cid string No Identifier of the customer, the driver renting the vehicle Example requests Starting a rental curl --location --request POST 'https:// admin_address /backend/app/contracts.php' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer 007898667a1b5711682399ea38a84f61' \ --data-raw '{ "cmd": "start", "mva": 111, "ra": 67890, "plate_number": "ABC123", "driver_name": "John Doe", "driver_phone": "123-456-7890", "ts_expected": 1644927600, "te_expected": 1644981600, "start_location": { "lat": 40.712776, "lon": -74.005974 }, "car_group_charged": "Economy" }' Response { "code": 0, "odo": "1233", "message": "Success" } The response returns: code — response code odo — odometer value message — text message about the result of the request Updating a rental curl --location --request POST 'https:// admin_address /backend/app/contracts.php' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer 007898667a1b5711682399ea38a84f61' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "cmd": "update", "ra": 67890, "plate_number": "ABC123", "driver_name": "John Doe", "driver_phone": "123-456-7890", "mileage_limit": 2000 }' Response { "code": 0, "odo": "1208607", "message": "Success" } Stopping a rental curl --location --request POST 'https:// admin_address /backend/app/contracts.php' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "cmd": "stop", "ra": 67890, "driver_rating": 4, "end_location": {"address": "Ilino 2c"} }' Response { "code": 0, "odo": "1208607", "message": "Success" } Response and error codes 0 — the operation was successful 1 — vehicle not found 2 — no changes to update 3 — rental contract not found 4 — authentication error 5 — unknown error 6 — no rights to perform the operation 7 — the contracts module is not active 8 — this rental contract number is already used by another account 9 — the vehicle is rented by another account 10 — the vehicle is not rented 11 — invalid request 12 — invalid location parameter 13 — this rental contract number is used by another agent 14 — the passport was provided, but the driver name is not specified 15 — the driver name was provided, but the passport is not specified 16 — driver not found by the provided data 17 — the driver data does not match the previously saved data 18 — rental contract with this number not found 19 — this rental contract is already completed 20 — the vehicle is already rented 21 — the driver is specified incorrectly 22 — the existing contract was closed, a new one was created 500 — internal server error

The User API gives access to the PILOT functions and data that are available to a regular user. With it, you can: — view your reports and statistics on trips, objects and expenses — get information about your settings and personal data — request data related only to your account and your activity in the system These APIs do not give access to the data of other users or administrators. You see and work only with the information of your own account. To authorize in the API, use the login and password of the user account.

This API provides information about vehicles, including their current location, sensor data, technical information and additional parameters. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters To get the data you need, add a command to the request address. cmd=list — command to get the list of vehicles node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed The format of the requested data is an array of vehicle data. Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=list node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "list": [ { "agentid": 9003, "imei": "356307046873054", "typeid": 1, "type": "Car", "vehiclenumber": "Х444МР123", "vin": "TRDFG65876", "folder": "Geo-Center OOO", "created_time": 1414224633, "current_mileage": 881, "status": { "unixtimestamp": "1418744535", "lat": "43.5562", "lon": "39.9084", "speed": 0, "dir": 268, "alt": 246, "satsinview": 16, "sensors": [ { "name": "Parking", "description": "TEST SPEED" }, { "name": "Fuel sensor", "description": "Fuel sensor" }, { "name": "External power supply", "description": "External power supply" }, { "name": "Ignition sensor", "description": "Ignition sensor" } ], "sensors_status": [ { "name": "Ignition sensor", "id": "1187852", "hum_value": "off", "dig_value": "0", "raw_value": "0", "change_ts": "1627467122", "group": "" }, { "name": "External power supply", "id": "1187851", "hum_value": "26.27 V", "dig_value": "26.27", "raw_value": "26272", "change_ts": "1627467122", "group": "" }, { "name": "Fuel sensor", "id": "1187850", "hum_value": "1 l", "dig_value": "1", "raw_value": "1", "change_ts": "1626336197", "group": "" } ] } } ] } The API request returns: code — status code (0 — success) msg — status message list — array of vehicle objects, each of which contains: agentid — unique identifier of the tracking device imei — International Mobile Equipment Identity typeid — numeric identifier of the vehicle type type — vehicle type vehiclenumber — vehicle registration number vin — vehicle identification number folder — organizational group created_time — time of addition to the system in Unix timestamp format current_mileage —current mileage status — information about the current state: unixtimestamp — time of the last update lat — latitude lon — longitude speed — speed dir — direction of movement in degrees alt — altitude above sea level satsinview — number of visible GPS satellites sensors — array of available sensors sensors_status — detailed status of each sensor, including: name — sensor name id — sensor identifier hum_value — real value after calibration dig_value — digital value after calibration raw_value — raw value before calibration change_ts — time of the last value change group — sensor group

This API provides information about vehicles, including their current location. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/CRIT/api.php?node= node_id Request parameters To get the data, you need to send a request with authorization and a function specified: Username — user login Password — password functionName=api_objectlist — command to get the list of objects node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed The format of the requested data is an array of vehicle objects. Example request https:// server_address /api/CRIT/api.php?node=6 Content-Type: multipart/form-data Username=TestName Password= 123456 functionName=api_objectlist Response [ { "IMEI": "352016704092097", "PLATE": "5209", "NAME": "", "LATITUDE": 29.7682433, "LONGITUDE": 39.9979749 }, { "IMEI": "352016703961657", "PLATE": "6561", "NAME": "", "LATITUDE": 25.9131066, "LONGITUDE": 46.4645949 } ] The API request returns an array of vehicle objects. Each object contains: IMEI — identifier of the tracker installed on the vehicle PLATE — vehicle number NAME — vehicle name LATITUDE — current latitude of the object s location LONGITUDE — current longitude of the object s location

This API is designed to find vehicles within a given radius of a specified point, sorted by distance. It is suitable for rapid-response scenarios (for example, police and special services), when an operator needs to quickly determine which vehicles are closest to the scene of an incident. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters To get the data you need, add a command to the request address. cmd= get_nearest_vehicles group_id — ID of the vehicle group (orgdep.id) lat — latitude of the target point (from −90 to 90) lon — longitude of the target point (from −180 to 180) radius — search radius. Supports values such as 500M, 1KM, 10KM, 20KM, or a number in meters Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_nearest_vehicles group_id=228 lat=43.28191 lon=76.90723 radius=50KM Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "group_id": 123, "group_name": "Police Fleet", "location": { "latitude": 24.4539, "longitude": 54.3773 }, "radius_meters": 10000, "vehicles_found": 2, "vehicles": [ { "vehiclenumber": "POL-001", "agentid": 456, "veh_id": 789, "imei": "123456789", "model": "Toyota Land Cruiser", "vehicle_type": "Car", "location": { "address": "Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai, UAE", "latitude": 24.4550, "longitude": 54.3780, "altitude": 10 }, "status": { "active": 1, "speed": 0, "direction": 0, "altitude": 10, "satsinview": 12, "ignition": 1, "unixtimestamp": 1706964000, "zone": [] }, "distance": { "meters": 1234, "kilometers": 1.23, "straight_line_meters": 1200 }, "travel_time": { "seconds": 180, "minutes": 3.0, "formatted": "3 min" } } ] } The API request returns: group_id — ID of the vehicle group group_name — group name location — coordinates of the target point latitude— latitude longitude— longitude radius_meters — search radius in meters vehicles_found — number of vehicles found vehicles — array of objects with vehicle information: vehiclenumber— vehicle number agentid— agent/device ID veh_id— object ID imei— device IMEI model— vehicle model vehicle_type— vehicle type (Car, Truck, etc.) location— vehicle location address— address (from the geocoder data) latitude, longitude, altitude status— current vehicle state active— activity (1 = in operation) speed— speed, km/h direction— direction of movement altitude— altitude satsinview— number of satellites ignition— ignition (1 = on) unixtimestamp— event time in UNIX format zone— array of current geofences distance— distance to the target meters— in meters kilometers— in kilometers straight_line_meters— straight-line distance in meters travel_time— estimated travel time to the target seconds — in seconds minutes — in minutes formatted— formatted time (for example, 3 min )

This API provides detailed information about a specific vehicle. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/CRIT/api.php?node= node_id Request parameters To get the data, you need to send a request with authorization and a function and an object specified: Username — user login Password — password functionName=api_objectdetails — command to get object details parameters — IMEI of the object for which details are requested node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed The format of the requested data is a single vehicle object Example request POST https:// server_address /api/CRIT/api.php?node=6 Content-Type: multipart/form-data Username=TestName Password= 123456 functionName=api_objectdetails parameters=352217706092097 Response { "IMEI": "352016704092097", "PLATE": "5209 ", "INSTALLATIONDATE": "Dec 06, 2023", "NAME": "", "LATITUDE": 29.7682433, "LONGITUDE": 39.9979749 } The API request returns an object with information about the vehicle: IMEI — identifier of the tracker installed on the vehicle PLATE — vehicle number INSTALLATIONDATE — date the tracker was installed on the vehicle NAME — vehicle name LATITUDE — current latitude of the object s location LONGITUDE — current longitude of the object s location

This API returns the movement history of a vehicle for a given period: tracks with information on mileage, operating time, parking, start and end coordinates, etc. How to get the data Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/CRIT/api.php?node= node_id Request parameters To get the data, you need to send a request with authorization and a function and parameters specified: Username — user login Password — password functionName=api_objecthistory — command to get the object history parameters — string with request parameters in the format: IMEI,FROM_DATETIME,TO_DATETIME, where: IMEI — IMEI of the object FROM_DATETIME — start date/time of the period TO_DATETIME — end date/time of the period The format of the requested data is an array of the object s tracks for the specified period. Example request POST https:// server_address /api/CRIT/api.php?node=6 Content-Type: multipart/form-data Username=TestName Password= 123456 functionName=api_objecthistory parameters=352016704092097,2025-11-21 04:07:03,2025-11-23 04:07:03 Response [ { "FLCNSMD": 0, "ENDTM": "2025-11-21 19:05:30", "MILEGND": 106286.11, "ENDLCTN": "Sakaka, Al Jawf Region, 3628, Saudi Arabia", "IDLDRTN": "00:00:00", "CNT": 1, "WRKNGDRTN": "07:47:22", "MILEGN": 826.37, "DRVR": "", "startlatitude": 24.399892, "OBJTID": 1344487, "WRKNGSTRTTM": "2025-11-21 11:18:08", "endlongitude": 48.20568, "startlongitude": 39.644265, "STPDRTN": "00:12:28", "DY": "2025-11-21", "endlatitude": 29.960238, "OBJCTNME": "5209 ب د م", "WRKNGSTRTLCTN": "Sakaka, Al Jawf Region, 3628, Saudi Arabia", "MXSPDP": 136 } ] The API request returns an array of tracks for the specified period. Each array element describes one track and contains: FLCNSMD — fuel consumption in this track ENDTM — track end time MILEGND — total mileage at the end of the track ENDLCTN — address of the track end point IDLDRTN — total idle time in this track CNT — sequence number (index) of the track within the day WRKNGDRTN — total engine running time / ignition “on” MILEGN — mileage covered within this track DRVR — driver s name startlatitude — latitude of the track start point startlongitude — longitude of the track start point endlatitude — latitude of the track end point endlongitude — longitude of the track end point OBJTID — internal object identifier WRKNGSTRTTM — time of the first ignition on in this track STPDRTN — total parking time within the track DY — track date OBJCTNME — object name WRKNGSTRTLCTN — address of the track start point MXSPDP — maximum speed reached in this track

The API is designed to get the latest event of a vehicle over the previous 24 hours. The method supports account mapping: a user can get an event of a vehicle from a linked account if they have access to that vehicle. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/v3/events/live Replace server_address with the address of the PILOT server. Request parameters Add the following parameter to the request address: agent_id — vehicle identifier in PILOT. The vehicle must be available to the authorized user. Example request GET https:// server_address /api/v3/events/live?agent_id=2000 Authorization: Bearer token X-Node: 0 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "events": [ { "Cotract Number": 1102, "Company Name": "Boooch Test", "AgentId": 2000, "VehicleID": "10-14262 Sunny", "Road Type": "Blacktop", "EventID": 4531206, "Event Type": 103, "Event Message": "SpeedN|110| |112|10|ss|17", "Event Start Time": 1785746496, "Event Start Speed": null, "Event Start location": { "lat": "25.164997", "lon": "55.235535" }, "Event End Time": null, "Event duration": null } ], "process_time": 0.0222 } The API request returns: code — request execution code. A value of 0 means successful execution msg — result of the request events — array of events found process_time — request processing time in seconds The events array contains: Cotract Number — identifier of the account that owns the vehicle Company Name — account name AgentId — vehicle identifier in PILOT VehicleID — vehicle name Road Type — road surface type. In the current version, Blacktop is returned EventID — event identifier Event Type — event type Event Message — event text Event Start Time — event start time in Unix timestamp format Event Start Speed — speed at the moment the event started. If no data is available, null is returned Event Start location — coordinates of the vehicle at the moment the event started: lat — latitude lon — longitude Event End Time — event end time in Unix timestamp format. If no data is available, null is returned Event duration — event duration in seconds. Calculated as the difference between the end time and the start time of the event. If one of the values is missing, null is returned

This API is used to get up-to-date information about the current status of one or more vehicles, including location, speed, sensor readings and technical condition. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters To get the data you need, add parameters to the request address. Parameters are specified after the question mark “?” and separated by the “ ” sign. cmd = status— command to get status information imei — unique identifier of the GPS tracker agents — list of agentid identifiers, comma-separated, to request the statuses of several objects veh_numbers — vehicle registration number, exactly as it is specified in the system, with letter and digit case strictly observed node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed The request must contain one of three parameters: imei, agents or veh_numbers. Examples Request by IMEI https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=status imei=357073296325265 node=1 Request by several agent identifiers https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=status agents=51594,44841 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": [ { "agentid": 44841, "imei": "865473034076573", "configuration": "Teltonika FM2200", "typeid": 27, "type": "Car", "vehiclenumber": "NURKA", "folder": "REAL", "created_time": 1518167398, "uniqid": "865473034076573", "current_mileage": 65345, "initial_mileage": 0, "driver_name": null, "driver_phone": null, "model": "ВАЗ (Lada) Kalina", "info": " test", "vin": "XTA219470K0259832", "status": { "active": 1, "speed": 0, "direction": 27, "lat": "47.119755", "lon": "39.667492", "alt": 0, "satsinview": 16, "unixtimestamp": "1621432378", "moving": 0, "parking": 9267, "firing": 0 }, "sensors_status": [ { "name": "Ignition sensor", "id": "150549", "hum_value": "выкл.", "dig_value": "0", "raw_value": "12494", "change_ts": "1621423461", "group": "GROUP!" }, { "name": "Датчик топлива", "id": "368013", "hum_value": "1249.4 -", "dig_value": "1249.4", "raw_value": "12494", "change_ts": "1621432378", "group": "myGroup" } ] } ], "reqest_time": 0.0642 } The response is returned in JSON format and contains: imei — unique tracker number distance — distance covered during the specified period agent_id — identifier of the tracking device account_id — account number in the system code — status code (0 - success) msg — message about the request execution status data — array of objects with vehicle information: agentid — contract identifier imei — international identifier of the tracking device vin — vehicle identification number configuration — tracker model typeid — numeric identifier of the vehicle type type — vehicle type vehiclenumber — vehicle registration number folder — organizational group or branch created_time — creation time in Unix timestamp format uniqid — unique identifier current_mileage — current mileage initial_mileage — initial mileage driver_name — driver s name driver_phone — driver s phone number model — vehicle model info — additional information status — information about the current state: active — whether the object is active (1 or 0) speed — current speed direction — current direction in degrees lat — current latitude lon — current longitude alt — current altitude satsinview — number of visible satellites unixtimestamp — time of the last update moving — driving time in seconds parking — parking time in seconds firing — ignition state (1 — on, 0 — off) sensors_status — array with sensor information: name — sensor name id — sensor identifier hum_value — real value after calibration dig_value — digital value after calibration raw_value — raw value before calibration change_ts — time of the last value change in Unix timestamp format group — sensor group reqest_time — request execution time in seconds

This API gets information about a vehicle for the last 24 hours, including mileage, fuel level, refuels and fuel consumption. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = vehinfo_24_hours — command to get information for 24 hours agent_id — vehicle identifier (several can be specified, comma-separated) imei — device identifier (several can be specified, comma-separated) ts — timestamp (Unix timestamp) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=vehinfo_24_hours imei=10518,165182 ts=1617710825 node=1 Response { "10518": { "total_mileage": 745851.44, "fuel_start": 229.37, "fuel_stop": 229.37, "fuel_fill": 409.6, "fuel_drain": 153.15, "fuel_consumption_l": 256.45, "fuel_consumption_l_per_100km": 35, "fuel_consumption_norm_l": 161.5658, "fuel_consumption_norm_l_per_100km": 22, "engine_hours": 0 }, "165182": { "total_mileage": 100946.68, "fuel_start": 0, "fuel_stop": 0, "fuel_fill": 0, "fuel_drain": 0, "fuel_consumption_l": 0, "fuel_consumption_l_per_100km": 0, "fuel_consumption_norm_l": 22.313, "fuel_consumption_norm_l_per_100km": 10, "engine_hours": 0 } } The API request returns: total_mileage — total mileage fuel_start — amount of fuel at the start of the period fuel_stop — amount of fuel at the end of the period fuel_fill — refuel fuel_drain — fuel drain fuel consumption (l) — actual fuel consumption fuel consumption (l/100km) — consumption per 100 km fuel_consumption_norm(l) — standard fuel consumption fuel_consumption_norm(l/100km) — standard consumption per 100 km engine hours — engine hours

This API links a contract to a vehicle, specifying its license plate, start date, contract name and distance. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=link_contract — command to link a contract PlateNum — vehicle license plate Date — contract start time (Unix timestamp) Name — contract name Distance — distance (for example, mileage under the contract) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=link_contract PlateNum=test12345 Distance=1111 Date=1623927270 Name=1212 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "The linking is successful" } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message about the result of the action

This API removes the link between an existing contract and the specified vehicle. How to get the data Method DELETE Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters • cmd=unlink_contract — command to unlink a contract • PlateNum — vehicle license plate • node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed (optional) Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=unlink_contract PlateNum=test12345 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Deletion is successful" } The API request returns: • code — result code (0 — successful operation) • msg — server message about the result of the action

This API changes the values of additional vehicle fields in a single request by agent_id or imei. You can change all fields or only some of them; the number of fields is not limited. Method POST Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php Headers Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Basic your_credentials Request parameters cmd=agent_update_custom_fields — API command agent_id — vehicle identifier (if you are not using imei). imei — IMEI of the vehicle s device (if you are not using agent_id). custom_fields — object with key-value pairs for updating additional fields In custom_fields you can specify any number of fields, for example extra_field1, extra_field2, … extra_fieldN (provided that these fields have been created in the account). Field values can be numbers, strings or boolean values Example request Updating several fields by agent_id: curl --location ' https:// server_address /api/api.php ' --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --header 'Authorization: Basic dGVzdDExMUB0ZXN0LnJ1OkRlbW9fMjAyMg==' \ --data '{ "cmd": "agent_update_custom_fields", "agent_id": 30547, "custom_fields": { "extra_field1": "Путевой лист №123", "extra_field2": "2025-11-01", "extra_field7": "+79000000000" } }' Updating by imei: curl --location ' https:// server_address /api/api.php ' --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --header 'Authorization: Basic dGVzdDExMUB0ZXN0LnJ1OkRlbW9fMjAyMg==' \' --data '{ "cmd": "agent_update_custom_fields", "imei": "359339099999999", "custom_fields": { "extra_field3": "Пропуск №A12345", "extra_field4": "2025-12-31" } }' Example response { "code": 1, "msg": "OK" } The API request returns: code — execution code: 1 — success, 0 — error msg — text description of the result (for example, OK or an error message)

This API gets information about vehicle mileage and fuel level at a specific point in time. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=istatus — API command to get the status imei — object identifier in PILOT unixtimestamp — point in time in Unix timestamp format node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=istatus unixtimestamp=1408840780 imei=356495042533101 node=1 Response { "код": 0, "сообщение": "ОК", "общий_пробег": 0, "total_run_by_can": 0, "моточасы": 0, "топливные_датчики": [ { "info": "Датчик топлива 1", "идентификатор": 150325, "имя поля": "t_53lls1", "топливо": 0 }, { "info": "Датчик топлива 2", "идентификатор": 150326, "имя поля": "lls2", "топливо": 0 } ], "топливо": 0, "unixtimestamp": 1408840780 } The API request returns: общий_пробег — total vehicle mileage at that point in time (km) total_run_by_can — mileage according to CAN bus data (km) моточасы — engine hours in seconds топливо — amount of fuel in the tank at that point in time (l) топливные_датчики — array of data for each fuel sensor, if there are several: info — sensor description идентификатор — unique sensor ID имя поля — system name of the sensor топливо — fuel level according to this sensor (l) unixtimestamp — point in time for which the data is returned (Unix timestamp)

This API returns the mileage and engine hours of a vehicle for the selected time interval. How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET Request parameters cmd=istatus — command to get mileage imei — object identifier in the system start — start of the interval (Unix timestamp) stop — end of the interval (Unix timestamp) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=istatus imei=6794i start=1664917200 stop=1665003600 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "run": 126.79500000000007, "run_by_can": 0, "motorhours": 9897, "unixtimestamp_start": 1664917200, "unixtimestamp_stop": 1665003600 } The API request returns: run — mileage for the period, km run_by_can — mileage according to CAN data, km motorhours — engine hours for the period, seconds unixtimestamp_start — start of the interval unixtimestamp_stop — end of the interval

This API gets information about the mileage (odometer readings) and fuel consumption of a vehicle for the selected time interval. How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET Request parameters cmd=odo_and_fuel — command to get odometer and fuel data imei — device identifier (object ID) start — start time of the period in Unix timestamp format stop — end time of the period in Unix timestamp format node — the number of the node on which the command is executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=odo_and_fuel start=1767214800 stop=1767560400 imei=861076084529922 node=6 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "ok", "data": { "fuel": 7.6, "start_odo": 407121.6, "stop_odo": 407229.4 } } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message fuel — amount of fuel consumed during the period start_odo — odometer reading at the start of the period stop_odo — odometer reading at the end of the period

This API gets data on how much fuel was consumed during the selected period, as well as how long the vehicle was idling. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=fuelconsumtion — command to get the report imei — unique vehicle identifier start — start time of the selection (Unix timestamp) stop — end time of the selection (Unix timestamp) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=fuelconsumtion imei=7157153151020 start=1644741475 stop=1644914275 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "7157153151020": [ { "idle": 98872, "fuel consumed": 457.92 } ] }, "message": "success" } The API request returns: code — result code (0 = success, other values = error) data — data for the selected object: idle — engine idling time (in seconds) fuel consumed — volume of fuel consumed during the specified period (liters) message — text message about the result

This API provides the current status of a vehicle, as well as the time and distance to a specified point or geofence. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = get_status_and_distance — command to get the status and distance vehnum — fleet number or license plate of the vehicle, several can be specified, comma-separated zone — geofence name (if you need to calculate the distance to a geofence) point — coordinates of the point in the format latitude,longitude (if you need the distance to a specific point) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example requests https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_status_and_distance vehnum=М897ЕТ777 zone=Госпиталь%20Лапино node=1 https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_status_and_distance vehnum=М897ЕТ777 point=55.923032,37.659668 node=1 Response { "cstatus": 6, "cstatus_timestamp": 1554985159, "destination_name": "Zero coordinates", "distance": { "code": 0, "length": 27613, "msg": "OK", "point": "55.923032,37.659668", "time": 2002, "type": "point" }, "ignition": 1, "rbu": "08", "sensors": { "Unloading Sensor": "on|1554985138", "Loading Sensor": "on|1554985138", "Ignition Sensor": "on|1554985138", "FUEL SENSORS OPERATION SENSORS": "Operating|1554985138", "Fuel ... fuel": "202.96 Liter|1554995669" }, "source_name": "Loading_Chertanovo", "status": 4, "status_timestamp": 1554985072, "unixtimestamp": 1554995864, "vehiclenumber": "М897ЕТ777", "zone": [] } The API request returns: cstatus — current status of the object cstatus_timestamp — time the status was recorded (Unix timestamp) destination_name — name of the destination point distance — object with information about the distance and time to the point or geofence: length — distance in meters time — time in seconds type — object type (point or zone) point — coordinates of the point (if type=point) ignition — ignition state (1 = on) rbu — concrete batching plant (RBU) identifier sensors — state of various sensors (for example, loading/unloading, fuel) source_name — name of the data source status — object status status_timestamp — time of the last status change unixtimestamp — time the data was received vehiclenumber — vehicle number zone — array with the current geofences (if any)

This API returns a list of vehicle downtime (idle) periods for the selected time interval. How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET Request parameters Parameters are passed in the query string or in the body of a POST request: cmd=get_idle — command to get downtimes time_start — start of the period (timestamp, unixtime) time_end — end of the period (timestamp, unixtime) imei — IMEI of the monitoring device. If there are several devices, specify them comma-separated: imei=887556,io9987,76573 node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example API request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_idle time_start=16878956 time_end=16878755 imei=887556,io9987,76573 node=1 Example response { "code": 0, "data": { "2914": [ {"idle_start": "1641814740", "idle_end": 1641814984}, {"idle_start": 1641815547, "idle_end": 1641825619}, {"idle_start": 1641827105, "idle_end": 1641893307}, {"idle_start": 1641893623, "idle_end": 1641898037} // ... remaining records ... ] }, "message": "success" } The API request returns: code — result code: 0 — success 1 — error data — dictionary whose keys are vehicle identifiers and whose values are lists of downtime periods: idle_start — downtime start time (timestamp) idle_end — downtime end time (timestamp) message — text message about the result of the request

This API gets a temporary link for tracking an object on the map, with activation and deactivation by specified geofences. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=get_temp_link — API command to get a temporary link imei — identifier of the object (vehicle) in the system startgeo — geofence for activating the link stopgeo — geofence for deactivating the link max_duration — maximum link validity time in minutes (24 hours by default) Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_temp_link imei=356307045913463 startgeo=Rostov test API stopgeo=Rostov exit test API max_duration=800 Response https:// server_address /monitor_token.php?token=1f87a19c068ad47f3f769dc151527794 lang=en zoom=10 startgeo=Rostov test API stopgeo=Rostov exit test API The response returns a direct link to the map with a temporary token. The link takes into account the specified activation (startgeo) and deactivation (stopgeo) geofences

This API sends a command to a vehicle using a previously created command template in the “Commands” module. How to get the data Method GET Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=send_command — command to send a command to a vehicle agent_id — agent (vehicle) identifier template_name — command template name (created in the “Commands” module) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed (optional) Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=send_command agent_id=139849 template_name=test123 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": null, "command_id": 3989 } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message about the result of the action command_id — identifier of the command sent

This API gets the status of a complex command , including the overall status and the status/response for all objects and commands included in the complex command. How to get the data Method GET Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=get_command_status — command to request the status command_id — complex command identifier node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_command_status command_id=3989 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "message": "", "detailed_status": { "43207": [ { "type": "GPRS", "status": "accepted", "response": "Ver: 03.25.15_88 GPS: AXN_3.80_3333 Hw: FMB010 Mod: 3 IMEI: 352094083043221 Init: 2024-3-30 12:29 Uptime: 505289 MAC: 001E428490AF SPC: 0 (0) AXL: 0 OBD :0 BL:0,2 BT:3" }, { "type": "GPRS", "status": "accepted", "response": "Data channel: 1 GPRS: 1 Phone: 0 SIM: 0 OP: 25001 Signal: 4 New SMS: 0 Roaming: 0 SMSFull: 0 LAC: 10 Cell ID: 11522 NetType: 1 FwUpd: -65536" } ] }, "general_status": "completed", "version": "7.2.0" } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) message — server message about the result detailed_status — associative array with detailed information for each agent array key (for example, 43207) — agent identifier type — data transmission channel type status — command execution status (accepted, executed, etc.) response — text response of the device general_status — overall status of the complex command (pending, completed, failed) version — system version

Use this API to get data on vehicle refuels for the selected period. With it you can: — view fuel card transactions (fuel purchase operations, card balance, fuel type, gas station) — get data on refuels and fuel drains according to the vehicle sensor (coordinates, amount of fuel, event location) — monitor fuel remaining at the start and end of the day for each vehicle How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=fuel — command to get refuel data imei — vehicle identifier in the system start — start time of the selection (Unix timestamp) stop — end time of the selection (Unix timestamp) addr— refuel addresses node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=fuel imei=863591021267806 start=1404158400 stop=1406836800 addr=1 node=1 The response is returned in JSON format and contains three main blocks: 1. Fuel cards (cards) An array of cards with information about each card and its transactions: "cards": [ { "id": 601, // Card identifier in the PILOT system "card_num": "257464691", // Card number "balance": "0", // Card balance at the time of the selection "type_name": "Магистраль", // Card type "transactions": { // Card transactions "1404206488": { "operation": "Покупка", // Operation type (Purchase/Refund, etc.) "ts": 1404206488, // Transaction time (Unix timestamp) "azs": "АЗС название", // Gas station name "liters": "20.0000", // Number of liters "sum": "636.00", // Amount with discount "sumg": "658.26", // Amount without discount "fuel": "Дизельное топливо", // Fuel type "price": "31.80", // Price with discount "priceg": "32.91", // Price without discount "saldo": "0.00" // Card balance at the time of the transaction } } } ] 2. Refuels/drains by sensor (fillings) An object whose keys are the event time (Unix timestamp) and whose values are data on a refuel or fuel drain: "fillings": { "1404205495": { "ts": 1404205495, // Event time (Unix timestamp) "type_id": 1, // Event type: 1 — refuel, 2 — drain "liters": "23.2862", // Amount of fuel "lat": "51.9899", // Latitude "lon": "47.8203", // Longitude "address": "RU, Саратовская область, Балаково", // Address "fuel_start": "223.68" // Fuel in the tank at the start of the event } } 3. Fuel remaining at the start and end of the day (fuel) An object whose keys are the start-of-day date (Unix timestamp) and whose values are the fuel remaining: "fuel": { "1404072000": { "ts": 1404072000, // Start-of-day date (Unix timestamp) "te": 1404158400, // End-of-day date "start": "4.76", // Fuel at the start of the day (liters) "stop": "18.93" // Fuel at the end of the day (liters) This API adds a record of fuel consumption by card, including information on the amount of fuel, cost, location and driver. How to get the data Method POST Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters Required: cmd=add_fuel_transaction — command to add a transaction card_num — fuel card number operation — operation type (for example, refill) unixtimestamp — transaction time in Unix timestamp format place — location of the operation azs — gas station name liters — number of liters of fuel fuel — fuel type price — price without discount sum — amount without discount node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Optional: priceg — price with discount sumg — amount with discount driver — driver s full name lat — latitude of the transaction location lon — longitude of the transaction location info — additional information internal_id — internal transaction identifier Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=add_fuel_transaction node=1 Example request body (JSON): { "card_num": "1234567890123456", "operation": "refill", "unixtimestamp": 1695000000, "place": "Main street 12", "azs": "WOG", "liters": 50, "fuel": "Diesel", "price": 55.0, "sum": 2750.0, "driver": "Ivan Ivanov" } Response { code : 0, msg : OK } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message about the result of the action

Берковецкая, 6, между Варшавской и Житомирской тр., около Ашана и Эпицентра" }, { "lat": "50.6586", "lon": "29.8808", "type_id": 8, "type_name": "РосБерлио", "descr": " b АЗС Авиаком /b br Телефон: (+38045)7752175 br Адрес: 56 км. тр. М-07 (Е-373) Киев-Ковель-Ягодин-Люблин" }, { "lat": "55.551", "lon": "53.4085", "type_id": 8, "type_name": "РосБерлио", "descr": " b АЗС ООО Протон-А /b br Телефон: 8-919-680-07-77 br Адрес: 1130 км а/д М7, Татарстан, Актанышский район (слева)" } ] } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — success) msg — server message (for example, “OK”) list — array of gas station objects: lat — gas station latitude lon — gas station longitude type_id — gas station type identifier type_name — gas station type name descr — gas station description, including the address and contact phone number

Use this API to get information about vehicle trips for the selected period. When the “Geofences” module is enabled, each trip is split into segments by entering and leaving geofences. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=run — command to get the report imei — unique identifier of the object (vehicle) start — start time of the selection in Unix timestamp format stop — end time of the selection in Unix timestamp format zones — enable geofence information: — 0 — tracks are included whole, without splitting by geofences — 1 — tracks are split into segments at the moments of entering and leaving geofences eco— include eco-driving data in tracks node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=run imei=359772039289781 start=1406318400 stop=1406404800 zones=1 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "zones": { "1406341994": { "ts": 1406341994, "stopuid": "213854753412306", "stopname": "Гараж", "lat": "53.3861", "lon": "83.7127", "msgtype": 2 }, "1406353422": { "ts": 1406353422, "stopuid": "966971618589014", "stopname": "Барнаульский автовокзал", "lat": "53.3508", "lon": "83.7593", "msgtype": 1 } }, "tracks": { "1406341955": { "ts": 1406341955, "te": 1406341994, "length": 0.26, "maxspeed": "17", "avgspeed": 17 }, "1406341994": { "ts": 1406341994, "te": 1406353389, "length": 119.83, "maxspeed": "96", "avgspeed": 58 } } } The API request returns: Array of zones (zones) — points of entering and leaving geofences: ts — event time (Unix timestamp) stopuid — unique geofence identifier stopname — geofence name lat — latitude of the point lon — longitude of the point msgtype — event type (1 = entry, 2 = exit) Array of tracks (tracks) — trip information: ts — trip start time (Unix timestamp) te — trip end time (Unix timestamp) length — trip length in kilometers maxspeed — maximum speed (km/h) avgspeed — average speed (km/h) lats — latitude of the start point lons — longitude of the start point late — latitude of the end point lone — longitude of the end point eco — eco-driving data (when the eco parameter is enabled): Acceleration, Braking, Speed — indicators for each parameter

This API gets information about vehicle stops and parkings for the specified period. You can find out the coordinates, duration and the address of the stop or parking location. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=runstops — API command to get the report on stops and parkings imei — vehicle identifier in the system start — start time of the selection (Unix timestamp) stop — end time of the selection (Unix timestamp) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=runstops start=1676840400 stop=1676926800 imei=16518 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "stops": [ { "ts": 1676840400, "te": 1676873376, "dur": 32976, "lat": "56.733388", "lon": "61.051853", "address": { "road": "Р-351", "county": "Белоярский городской округ", "state": "Sverdlovsk Oblast", "region": "Ural Federal District", "postcode": "624053", "country": "Russia", "country_code": "ru" } }, { "ts": 1676875342, "te": 1676880065, "dur": 4723, "lat": "56.893278", "lon": "60.770452", "address": { "road": "Екатеринбургская кольцевая автомобильная дорога", "county": "Берёзовский городской округ", "state": "Sverdlovsk Oblast", "region": "Ural Federal District", "postcode": "623703", "country": "Russia", "country_code": "ru" } } ], "parkings": [ { "ts": 1676887881, "te": 1676889637, "dur": 1756, "lat": "56.781017", "lon": "58.40189", "address": { "road": "Подъезд к д. Зобнина от км 216+740 а/д «г. Пермь — г. Екатеринбург»", "county": "Achitsky District", "state": "Sverdlovsk Oblast", "region": "Ural Federal District", "postcode": "623235", "country": "Russia", "country_code": "ru" } } ] } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — success) msg — server message (for example, OK ) stops — array of stop data: ts— stop start time (Unix timestamp) te— stop end time (Unix timestamp) dur— stop duration in seconds lat— latitude of the point lon— longitude of the point address— information about the stop address (street, district, oblast, region, postal code, country, country code) parkings— array of parking data (same fields as stops)

This API lets you get a report on the movements of a vehicle for the selected period, with coordinates and geographic information (address, district, city, etc.). The data contains information about the start and end of each movement segment, average and maximum speed, route length and location by geo-coordinates. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = rungeo — command to get the report imei — unique identifier of the object in the system start — start time of the selection in Unix timestamp format stop — end time of the selection in Unix timestamp format node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=rungeo imei=356307045913463 start=1439413200 stop=1439586000 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "tracks": { "1439443509": { "avgspeed": 35.3889, "length": 12.7304, "maxspeed": 59, "ts": 1439443509, "te": 1439445837, "slat": "47.2037", "slon": "39.6325", "elat": "47.2037", "elon": "39.6325", "sgeo": { "city": "Rostov-on-Don", "road": "2-ya Krasnodarskaya ulitsa", "house_number": "80 к13", "state": "Rostov Oblast", "postcode": "344091" }, "egeo": { "city": "Rostov-on-Don", "road": "2-ya Krasnodarskaya Street", "house_number": "80 к13", "state": "Rostov Oblast", "postcode": "344091" } } } } The API request returns: code — execution code (0 = success) msg — status message tracks — object whose keys are trip start timestamps (Unix timestamp) and whose values are data on each trip These keys are also the unique track identifiers (track_id) that can be used in the gettrack method request to get the detailed route points. For each trip: avgspeed — average speed (km/h) maxspeed — maximum speed (km/h) length — route length (km) ts — trip start time (Unix timestamp) te — trip end time (Unix timestamp) slat, slon — start coordinates (latitude, longitude) elat, elon — end coordinates sgeo — address of the start location (city, street, house, postal code) egeo — address of the end location

This API loads the detailed points of the route (track) for a trip previously obtained via the rungeo method. Each track point contains coordinates, speed and the absolute registration time of the point in Unix timestamp format. How to get the data Method GET Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = gettrack — command to get the track. id — track identifier obtained in the response of the rungeo API node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=gettrack id=70685695 node=1 Response { "track_data": "47.2037;39.6325;10;1439443509:47.2037;39.6324;13;1439443510:47.2037;39.6323;15;1439443512:47.2036;39.6304;22;1439443568", "track_id": 70685695, "unixstarttimestamp": 1439443509 } The API request returns: track_id— unique track identifier; unixstarttimestamp— date and time of the track start in Unix timestamp format; track_data— sequence of track points separated by a colon (:). Each track point consists of four values separated by a semicolon (;): 1. latitude — latitude; 2. longitude — longitude; 3. speed_kmh — speed in km/h; 4. point_unix_timestamp — absolute registration time of the point in Unix timestamp format, UTC. Point format: latitude;longitude;speed_kmh;point_unix_timestamp Example: 47.2037;39.6325;10;1439443509 The value 1439443509 is the absolute registration time of the point, not the number of seconds from the start of the track. To calculate the time elapsed since the start of the track, use the formula: elapsed_seconds = point_unix_timestamp - unixstarttimestamp. For example: 1439443568 - 1439443509 = 59

This API helps you work with approved vehicle tracks: set periods, get tracks and use the track player.
