How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters Parameters are passed in the query string using the POST or GET method, depending on the command. To get the data you need, add parameters to the request address. Parameters are specified after the question mark “?” and separated by the “ ” sign. cmd=set_approved_tracks — command to set approved periods cmd=get_approved_tracks — command to get approved tracks veh — license plate or identifier of the vehicle ts — start of the period (timestamp) te — end of the period (timestamp) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Set approved periods Example API request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=set_approved_tracks veh=Р852ОВ77 ts=1537945200 te=1537952400 node=1 API response {"code":0,"msg":"ОК обновлено"} Get approved tracks Example API request http:// admin_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_approved_tracks veh=Р852ОВ77 ts=1537945200 te=153795 2400 node=1 API response { "code":0, "data":{ "approved":[ {"length":2.8051348330013,"ts":1537948809,"te":1537949431,"max_speed":"59","avg_speed":26} ], "not_approved":[ {"length":1.8650025635569,"ts":1537945206,"te":1537946030,"max_speed":"40","avg_speed":12}, {"length":4.1987356239849,"ts":1537948298,"te":1537948798,"max_speed":"65","avg_speed":37} ] } } The API request returns: approved— list of approved tracks not_approved— list of tracks that were not approved length— track length in kilometers ts— track start time (timestamp) te— track end time (timestamp) max_speed— maximum speed on the track avg_speed— average speed Track player The track player is a web service that lets you view vehicle tracks visually. Unlike the regular API, it immediately returns a ready page with a map and a track, rather than JSON or XML. Link for viewing a track: http:// server_address /api/track_player.php?login=demo pass=demo ts=1536933600 te=1536940800 veh=в848ае199 lang=ru node=1 You can use the URL as an iframe src to display the track on a page.

This API generates a report on vehicles, drivers, geofences, customers or tags for the selected period of time, with detailed configuration of the content. How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters Required: cmd=get_report — command to get the report report_type — report type (numeric identifier ) start — start of the period (Unix timestamp) stop — end of the period (Unix timestamp) veh_id — vehicle identifiers (comma-separated) explode — data splitting by: 1 — days, 2 — weeks, 3 — do not split group — data grouping: 1 — by days, 2 — by objects, 3 — by geofences, 4 — by drivers, 5 — by customers, 6 — by groups, 7 — by tags format — report format: json, pdf, xls tz — time zone used to generate dates and times in the report. Specify a valid IANA time zone identifier, for example Africa/Johannesburg. If an unknown or invalid time zone is passed, the API returns an error. Optional: drivers_id — list of driver IDs zones_id — list of geofence IDs fillings — include refuel data stales — include drains speed — include speed rashod — include fuel consumption stops — include stops run — include vehicle runs contr_time / type — control time tags — list of tag IDs template — report template ID outside_zones — include outside geofences work_hours — take only working hours into account fuel — include fuel vehicle_not_moving_time — downtime for the report vehicles_has_covered_km — vehicle mileage notifications — list of notification IDs Example GET request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_report report_type=1 start=1724623200 stop=1724709600 veh_id=1234,5678 explode=1 group=2 format=json tz=Africa/Johannesburg node=1 Example POST request { "cmd": "get_report", "report_type": 1, "start": 1724623200, "stop": 1724709600, "veh_id": "1234,5678", "explode": 1, "group": 2, "format": "json", "tz": "Africa/Johannesburg" } Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": [ { "veh_id": "1234", "date": "2025-09-22", "distance": 125.5, "fuel_consumption": 15.2, "stops": 5, "speed_avg": 60 }, { "veh_id": "5678", "date": "2025-09-22", "distance": 98.3, "fuel_consumption": 12.7, "stops": 4, "speed_avg": 55 } ] } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message data — array of report data veh_id — vehicle identifier date — report record date distance — distance covered (km) fuel_consumption — fuel consumption stops — number of stops speed_avg — average speed

This API gets the list of all reports available in the account, with their identifiers, names and the groups they belong to. How to get the data Request address To get the data, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters cmd=reports_list — command to get the list of reports node — the number of the node on which the command is executed Example GET request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=reports_list node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "id": 266, "name": "Административные действия", "group": "Администратор" }, { "id": 258, "name": "Заблокированные пользователи", "group": "Администратор" }, { "id": 263, "name": "Созданы пользователи", "group": "Администратор" }, { "id": 261, "name": "Отключенная учетная запись пользователя", "group": "Администратор" }, { "id": 265, "name": "Отключенные пользователи", "group": "Администратор" }, { "id": 267, "name": "Неудачные попытки входа", "group": "Администратор" } ] } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) data — array of reports, where each report contains: id — unique report identifier name — report name group — the group the report belongs to

This API creates a new geofence by specifying its name, type, color, group and geometry. How to get the data Method GET Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=geofenceadd — command to add a geofence zonename — geofence name zonetype — zone type (1 — polygon, 2 — circle) color — zone color in HEX format (for example, #FFFFFF) info — text information about the geofence group_name — name of the geofence group (created if it does not exist, optional) group_id — ID of an existing group (if specified, group_name is ignored, optional) geometry — GeoJSON describing the polygon or circle external_id — external identifier of the geofence (optional) node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request Polygon: http:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=geofenceadd zonetype=1 zonename=test_api_polygon external_id=12354 info=blabla color=%23FF3300 group_name=TEST_API geometry={"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[55.184334,25.112866],[55.183512,25.113472],[55.182154,25.112516],[55.183511,25.111016],[55.184923,25.112133]]]} node=1 Circle: http:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=geofenceadd zonetype=2 zonename=test_api_circle external_id=12345 info=circle_info color=%23FF3300 group_name=TEST_API geometry={"type":"Circle","coordinates":[55.184334,25.112866],"radius":150} node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": { "id": 158412, "zonename": "test_api_polygon", "zonetype": 1, "external_id": "12354", "created_at": 1610536445, "updated_at": 1610536445, "color": "#FF3300", "info": "blabla", "group_id": 6984 } } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message data — object with information about the created geofence: id — geofence identifier zonename — geofence name zonetype — zone type (1 — polygon, 2 — circle) external_id — external identifier created_at — creation time (Unix timestamp) updated_at — update time (Unix timestamp) color — geofence color info — text information group_id— geofence group identifier

This API returns a list of all geofences with their characteristics, including coordinates, type, color and group. How to get the data Method POST Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=geofencelist— command to get the list of geofences node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=geofencelist node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": [ { "id": 157828, "zonename": "Test Magnit", "zonetype": 2, "external_id": null, "created_at": 1609780839, "updated_at": 1609780839, "color": "#00CC00", "info": "geozone text info", "group_name": "TEST", "group_id": 6531, "geometry": { "type": "Circle", "coordinates": [40.036497, 46.981936], "radius": 305 } }, { "id": 153244, "zonename": "school", "zonetype": 1, "external_id": 1234, "created_at": 1609780839, "updated_at": 1609780839, "color": "#FF9900", "info": "kml upload", "group_name": "TEST", "group_id": 6531, "geometry": { "type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [ [ [55.184334, 25.112866], [55.183512, 25.113472], [55.182154, 25.112516], [55.183511, 25.111016], [55.184923, 25.112133] ] ] } } ] } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message data — array of geofence objects, each of which contains: id — geofence identifier zonename — geofence name zonetype — geofence type (1 — polygon, 2 — circle) external_id — external identifier (if any) created_at — creation time (Unix timestamp) updated_at — update time (Unix timestamp) color — geofence color in the interface info— additional information group_name — name of the geofence group group_id — group identifier geometry — zone geometry: type — type (Circle or Polygon) coordinates — coordinates (for a circle: [longitude, latitude]; for a polygon: array of coordinate arrays) radius — radius for a circular geofence (in meters)

This API lets you assign an existing geofence to a vehicle, setting control parameters such as speed limit, idle time and alerts. How to get the data Method GET Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=geofencelink — command to assign a geofence zone_id — geofence identifier (required if external_id is not set) external_id — external identifier of the geofence (optional, ignored if zone_id is specified) agent_id — agent (vehicle) identifier idle — idle control in the geofence in minutes (optional) speedlimit — speed limit in the geofence in km/h (optional) alerts — alerts: 0 — do not send 1 — idling 2 — border crossing 3 — borders and border checkpoints node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request http:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=geofencelink zone_id=158414 agent_id=66497 idle=10 speedlimit=80 alerts=0 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK" } The API request returns: code— result code (0 — successful operation) msg— server message about the result of the action

This API removes the link between an existing geofence and a vehicle. How to get the data Method GET Request address To execute the request, use the address: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=geofenceunlink — command to remove the geofence link zone_id — geofence identifier (required if external_id is not set) external_id — external identifier of the geofence (optional, ignored if zone_id is specified) agent_id — agent (vehicle) identifier node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed Example request http:// address /api/api.php?cmd=geofenceunlink zone_id=158414 agent_id=66497 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK" } The API request returns: code — result code (0 — successful operation) msg — server message about the result of the action

This API returns information about when objects visited specific geofences during a given period. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=ag_geozones — API command for getting geofence history start — start of the period (Unix timestamp) stop — end of the period (Unix timestamp) imei — vehicle identifier. You can specify several, separated by commas node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request for one vehicle https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=ag_geozones start=1606770000 stop=1608584399 imei=865291046424635 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": [ { "group": "Общие", "zonename": "База Голицыно", "ts": 1606805707, "te": 1606808500 }, { "group": "Общие", "zonename": "База Голицыно", "ts": 1606865643, "te": 1606868103 } ] } Example request for several vehicles https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=ag_geozones start=1606770000 stop=1608584399 imei=865291046424635,867481037184458 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": { "865291046424635": [ { "group": "Общие", "zonename": "База Голицыно", "ts": 1606805707, "te": 1606808500 }, { "group": "Общие", "zonename": "База Голицыно", "ts": 1606865643, "te": 1606868103 } ], "867481037184458": [ { "group": "Общие", "zonename": "База Голицыно", "ts": 1607949101, "te": 1607956478 }, { "group": "Общие", "zonename": "База Голицыно", "ts": 1608012176, "te": 1608041334 } ] } } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — success) msg — server message (for example, OK ) data — information about geofence visits For one object, data is an array of visits For several objects, data is an object whose keys are vehicle IMEIs and whose values are arrays of visits group— geofence group zonename— geofence name ts— time of entering the geofence (Unix timestamp) te— time of leaving the geofence (Unix timestamp)

This API returns information about vehicle mileage inside the specified geofences during the selected period. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = zones_mileage — command for getting mileage in geofences ts — start of the selection (Unix timestamp) te — end of the selection (Unix timestamp) imei — list of object IMEIs, separated by commas zones — list of geofence names, separated by commas (optional; if omitted, mileage for all zones is returned) node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=zones_mileage ts=1596229200 te=1597006800 imei=867857035056105,123123123 zones=Симферополь,Белогорск,Судак node=1 Response { "code":0, "ts":"1596229200", "te":"1597006800", "data":{ "867857035056105":[ { "zone":"Симферополь", "duration":88308, "mileage":259.84 }, { "zone":"За пределами города", "duration":21564, "mileage":283.47 }, { "zone":"Белогорск", "duration":704, "mileage":10.77 }, { "zone":"Судак", "duration":1332, "mileage":11.45 } ] } } The API response contains: zone — geofence name duration — time the object spent in the zone, in seconds mileage — distance traveled in this zone, in kilometers

This API deletes a geofence from the system. When a geofence is deleted, all its assignments to vehicles are removed automatically. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To make the request, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=geofencedel — command for deleting a geofence zone_id — internal geofence identifier external_id — external geofence identifier (optional) node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=geofencedel zone_id=473989 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": { "zones_deleted": [ 473989 ] } } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) message — server message about the result of the action data.zones_deleted — array of IDs of deleted geofences (zone_id) for which the operation succeeded

This API lets you add a new driver to the system or update an existing driver. You can specify the full name, iButton code, contact information, driver license number and the list of objects the driver will have access to. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = drivers_add — command for adding or updating a driver name — driver name (full name) code — driver iButton code (required) description — driver description (optional) phone — driver phone number (optional) license — driver license number (optional) email — e-mail address access — list of identifiers of the objects (agent_id) the driver is allowed to access, separated by commas node — number of the node on which to run the command If a driver with these parameters already exists in the system, the driver's data will be updated. Otherwise, a new driver will be created Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=drivers_add name=NewDriverName code=123456 description=DESCR phone=122212343 license=rrr3335552 email=new@email.com access=1122,3344 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "id": 16990, "name": "NewDriverName", "code": "123456", "description": "DESCR", "phone": "122212343", "license": "rrr3335552", "email": "new@email.com", "access": [1122, 3344] } } The API response contains: id— unique driver identifier name— driver s full name code— driver iButton code description— driver description phone— phone number license— driver license number email— e-mail address access— list of identifiers of the objects the driver is allowed to access

This API returns information about the drivers registered in the account. You can get data on each driver, including full name, contact information, description, access rights and identifiers. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = drivers_list— command for getting the list of drivers node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=drivers_list node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "id": 317, "name": "Ivan Ivanov", "code": "", "description": "Driver #3", "phone": "798345546", "license": "", "email": "", "access": [] }, { "id": 1122, "name": "Andrey Petrov", "code": "", "description": "Driver #1", "phone": "+525531696255", "license": "", "email": null, "access": [1122] } ] } The API response contains: id — driver identifier name — driver s full name code — driver code (if any) description — driver description phone — phone number license — driver license data email — e-mail address access — list of IDs of resources or objects the driver has access to

This API assigns a driver to a specific vehicle using its identifier (IMEI) and a tag (key). How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=linkdriver — API command that assigns the driver imei — unique vehicle identifier in the system driver — driver s full name driverkey— driver key (tag) number node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=linkdriver imei=548545218454 driver=ADAS+driver driverkey=89185717259 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": [], "message": "success" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — success, any other value — error) data — additional data (an empty array in this case) message — text message from the server (for example, “success”)

This API returns information about the activity of vehicle drivers during the selected period. The response lists the various work modes (for example, driving, work, rest). How to get the data Method GET Request URL To make the request, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = gettachodata — command for getting tachograph data agent_id — vehicle identifier / several vehicles, separated by commas imei — device identifier (alternative to agent_id) ts — start of the selection (Unix timestamp) te — end of the selection (Unix timestamp) node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=gettachodata ts=1624568400 te=1624586400 agent_id=120407,120646 node=1 Response { "С 220 СК 750": { "First driver": { "Work": 4997, "Drive": 248, "Rest": 9117 }, "Second driver": { "Driver available": 1722, "Rest": 9117 } }, "А 152 АК 790": { "First driver": { "Drive": 5436, "Work": 1706, "Rest": 9084 }, "Second driver": { "Driver available": 4995, "Rest": 9084 } } } The API response contains: vehicle number First driver / Second driver — data for each driver Drive — driving time Work — working time Rest — rest time Driver available — time when the driver was available for work

This API is for creating, getting, editing and deleting notification configurations in PILOT. It is not an API for sending notifications, but for defining the conditions under which notifications will be triggered in the system in the future. Methods POST, GET, PUT, DELETE Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// /api/ptm/notification.php address — website address POST Creates a new notification configuration. The request body is required. Request https:// address /api/ptm/notification.php Example request body { "id": 0, "agent_id": 123, "type": "speed", "geozones": [ { "name": "Склад", "zonetype": 1, "points": [ [55.7558, 37.6173], [55.7560, 37.6180], [55.7565, 37.6170] ] } ], "name": "Превышение скорости в зоне склада", "email": true, "emails_list": [ "dispatcher@example.com", "manager@example.com" ], "sms": true, "phones_list": [ "+79001234567", "+79007654321" ], "message_text": "Внимание! Превышение скорости в зоне склада.", "webhook": true, "webhook_url": "https://yourdomain.com/webhook-handler", "ts": 1680000000, "te": 1710000000, "timezone": 3, "zone_rule": "in", "speed_rule": " ", "speed_value": 80, "speed_time": 15, "speed_time_units": "ss", "ignition_rule": "on", "geozones_rule": "in", "break_duration": 0, "break_time_units": "ss", "tag_name": "грузовик", "temperature_rule": " ", "temperature_value": 30, "temperature_time": 0, "disconnect_time": 0, "disconnect_time_units": "ss", "odometer_rule": " ", "odometer_value": 100000, "odometer_period": "abs" } Example response { "success": true, "msg": "Уведомление успешно создано", "method": "POST", "notification": { "id": 123, "agent_id": 123, "type": "speed", "geozones": [ { "name": "Склад", "zonetype": 1, "points": [ [55.7558, 37.6173], [55.7560, 37.6180], [55.7565, 37.6170] ] } ], "name": "Превышение скорости в зоне склада", "email": true, "emails_list": [ "dispatcher@example.com", "manager@example.com" ], "sms": true, "phones_list": [ "+79001234567", "+79007654321" ], "message_text": "Внимание! Превышение скорости в зоне склада.", "webhook": true, "webhook_url": "https://yourdomain.com/webhook-handler", "ts": 1680000000, "te": 1710000000, "timezone": 3, "zone_rule": "in", "speed_rule": " ", "speed_value": 80, "speed_time": 15, "speed_time_units": "ss", "ignition_rule": "on", "geozones_rule": "in", "break_duration": 0, "break_time_units": "ss", "tag_name": "грузовик", "temperature_rule": " ", "temperature_value": 30, "temperature_time": 0, "disconnect_time": 0, "disconnect_time_units": "ss", "odometer_rule": " ", "odometer_value": 100000, "odometer_period": "abs" } } GET Gets a notification configuration by ID. Request parameters: id (required) — notification ID Example request https:// address /api/ptm/notification.php?id=123 Example response { "success": true, "msg": "Уведомление получено", "method": "GET", "notification": { "id": 123, "agent_id": 123, "type": "speed", "geozones": [ { "name": "Склад", "zonetype": 1, "points": [ [55.7558, 37.6173], [55.7560, 37.6180], [55.7565, 37.6170] ] } ], "name": "Превышение скорости в зоне склада", "email": true, "emails_list": [ "dispatcher@example.com", "manager@example.com" ], "sms": true, "phones_list": [ "+79001234567", "+79007654321" ], "message_text": "Внимание! Превышение скорости в зоне склада.", "webhook": true, "webhook_url": "https://yourdomain.com/webhook-handler", "ts": 1680000000, "te": 1710000000, "timezone": 3, "zone_rule": "in", "speed_rule": " ", "speed_value": 80, "speed_time": 15, "speed_time_units": "ss", "ignition_rule": "on", "geozones_rule": "in", "break_duration": 0, "break_time_units": "ss", "tag_name": "грузовик", "temperature_rule": " ", "temperature_value": 30, "temperature_time": 0, "disconnect_time": 0, "disconnect_time_units": "ss", "odometer_rule": " ", "odometer_value": 100000, "odometer_period": "abs" } } PUT Updates an existing notification configuration. Request https:// address /api/ptm/notification.php Example request body The same JSON format as for creation (POST), but with the current values and the required id. { "id": 123, "agent_id": 123, "type": "speed", "geozones": [ { "name": "Склад", "zonetype": 1, "points": [ [55.7558, 37.6173], [55.7560, 37.6180], [55.7565, 37.6170] ] } ], "name": "Обновлённое уведомление", "email": true, "emails_list": ["alerts@example.com"], "sms": false, "phones_list": [], "message_text": "Обновлённое сообщение о превышении скорости", "webhook": false, "webhook_url": "", "ts": 1680000000, "te": 1720000000, "timezone": 3, "zone_rule": "in", "speed_rule": " ", "speed_value": 90, "speed_time": 10, "speed_time_units": "ss", "ignition_rule": "off", "geozones_rule": "in", "break_duration": 0, "break_time_units": "ss", "tag_name": "фургон", "temperature_rule": " ", "temperature_value": 35, "temperature_time": 0, "disconnect_time": 0, "disconnect_time_units": "ss", "odometer_rule": " ", "odometer_value": 120000, "odometer_period": "abs" } Example response { "success": true, "msg": "Уведомление успешно обновлено", "method": "PUT", "notification": { "id": 123, "agent_id": 123, "type": "speed", "geozones": [ { "name": "Склад", "zonetype": 1, "points": [ [55.7558, 37.6173], [55.7560, 37.6180], [55.7565, 37.6170] ] } ], "name": "Обновлённое уведомление", "email": true, "emails_list": ["alerts@example.com"], "sms": false, "phones_list": [], "message_text": "Обновлённое сообщение о превышении скорости", "webhook": false, "webhook_url": "", "ts": 1680000000, "te": 1720000000, "timezone": 3, "zone_rule": "in", "speed_rule": " ", "speed_value": 90, "speed_time": 10, "speed_time_units": "ss", "ignition_rule": "off", "geozones_rule": "in", "break_duration": 0, "break_time_units": "ss", "tag_name": "фургон", "temperature_rule": " ", "temperature_value": 35, "temperature_time": 0, "disconnect_time": 0, "disconnect_time_units": "ss", "odometer_rule": " ", "odometer_value": 120000, "odometer_period": "abs" } } DELETE Deletes one or more notifications. Request parameters: id (optional) — ID of a specific notification agent_id (optional) — if passed, all notifications for the specified agent are deleted Example request https:// address /api/ptm/notification.php?id=123 You can also delete all notifications by agent_id: https:// address /api/ptm/notification.php?agent_id=456 Response { "count": 1 // number of deleted notifications } Notification configuration fields Field Description id Notification ID agent_id Agent identifier (device/vehicle) type Notification type (speed, temperature, ignition, etc.) geozones Array of geofences the notification applies to name Notification name email Enable sending by email emails_list List of email addresses sms Enable SMS notifications phones_list List of phone numbers webhook_url Webhook URL webhook Enable sending by webhook message_text Notification text ts, te Time range of the notification validity (Unix timestamp) timezone Time offset (for example, +3) zone_rule Zone rule (in, out) speed_rule Speed condition ( , , =) speed_value Speed value speed_time Exceedance time speed_time_units Time units (ss, mm, hh) ignition_rule Ignition state (on, off) geozones_rule Behavior in geofences (in, out) temperature_rule Temperature condition ( , ) temperature_value Temperature value temperature_time Temperature exceedance time disconnect_time Device disconnection time disconnect_time_units Disconnection time units odometer_rule Mileage condition odometer_value Mileage odometer_period Mileage counting type (abs, rel) tag_name Object tag (for example, “truck”)

This API is used to get events of notifications for the selected period, for example, speeding, movement outside a zone or other preconfigured alerts. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = notifications — command for getting notification events ts — start of the selection (Unix timestamp) te — end of the selection (Unix timestamp) notification — name of the notification to get events for node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=notifications ts=1606942800 te=1607115600 notification=test node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": [ { "vehiclenumber": "PS2", "agentid": 109792, "message": "Speed 10 km/h longer than 10 ss max speed=52km/h Duration: 42 sec", "ts": 1606988609 }, { "vehiclenumber": "PS2", "agentid": 109792, "message": "Speed 10 km/h longer than 10 ss max speed=29km/h Duration: 12 sec", "ts": 1606988438 }, { "vehiclenumber": "PS2", "agentid": 109792, "message": "Speed 10 km/h longer than 10 ss max speed=17km/h Duration: 13 sec", "ts": 1606988106 } ], "id": 3701 } The API response contains: vehiclenumber — license plate or internal vehicle number agentid — object identifier in the system message — text of the notification event ts — event time in Unix timestamp format id — request/session identifier

This API is used to get the media files of selected objects for a given period. You can get links to photos and videos related to events, including ADAS and DMS. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=get_media — command for getting media files agent_id — object identifier or identifiers of several objects, separated by commas start — start of the selection in Unix timestamp format stop — end of the selection in Unix timestamp format Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_media agent_id=1234,5678 start=1724623200 stop=1724709600 A successful API request returns information about the media files of the selected objects for the specified period, along with links to view them. When you follow a link, the image or video related to the event opens in the browser.

This API returns real-time events for vehicles, including information about the contract, company, driver, speed and location of the event start. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To make the request, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=live_events — command for getting real-time events node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=live_events node=1 Response { "1264": { "Contract Number": "CONTRACT ID", "Company Name": "Al Turki Enterprises", "Base Location": "LEK", "Vehicle Owner": "SUB-CONTRACTOR", "ID": 1680881937, "EventID, EventType": 0, "VehicleID": "5174 WA", "Asset Category": "Light", "Road Type": "Blacktop", "DriverID": 18262972, "Event Start Time": "1680881932", "Event Start Speed": 0, "Event Start Location": { "lat": "18.185841", "lon": "55.213230" } }, "1123": { "Contract Number": "", "Company Name": "Al Turki Enterprises", "Base Location": "", "Vehicle Owner": "", "ID": 1680881937, "EventID, EventType": 0, "VehicleID": "6076MB", "Asset Category": "Light", "Road Type": "Blacktop", "DriverID": 0, "Event Start Time": "1680881413", "Event Start Speed": 0, "Event Start Location": { "lat": "18.188658", "lon": "55.206314" } } } The API response contains: Object key (1264, 1123) — unique event identifier Contract Number — contract number Company Name — company name Base Location — vehicle base Vehicle Owner — vehicle owner ID — internal event ID EventID, EventType — event identifier and its type VehicleID — license plate or vehicle identifier Asset Category — vehicle category Road Type — road type DriverID — driver identifier Event Start Time — event start time (Unix timestamp) Event Start Speed — speed at the moment the event started Event Start Location — coordinates of the event start (lat, lon)

This API creates a new waybill for a given period. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=add_waybill — command for adding a waybill ts — start time (Unix timestamp) te — end time (Unix timestamp) agent_id — agent identifier name — waybill name node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=add_waybill ts=1596022528 te=1596488400 agent_id=44841 name=test+bill1 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "ts": 1596022528, "te": 1596488400, "agent_id": 44841, "account_id": 3934, "waybill": { "name": "test bill1" } } } The API response contains: code — result code (0 = success) data — object with the data of the created waybill ts — waybill start time te — waybill end time agent_id — agent identifier account_id — account identifier waybill.name — waybill name

This API returns waybill data for a specific period. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = get_waybill — command for getting waybills ts — start of the selection (Unix timestamp) agent_id — agent identifier node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_waybill ts=1596022528 agent_id=44841 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "ts": 1596022528, "te": 1596488400, "agent_id": 44841, "account_id": 3934, "waybill": { "name": "test bill1" } } ] } The API response contains: code — result code (0 = success) data — array with waybill information: ts — waybill start time te — waybill end time agent_id — agent identifier account_id — account identifier waybill — object with the waybill data: name — waybill name

This API deletes an existing waybill for the specified period. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=remove_waybill — command for deleting a waybill ts — start time (Unix timestamp) te — end time (Unix timestamp) agent_id — agent identifier node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=remove_waybill ts=1596022528 te=1596488400 agent_id=44841 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": 1 } The API response contains: code— result code (0 = success) data— deletion result (1 = deleted successfully)

This API lets you create a new user in PILOT with the specified parameters: login, password, role and contact details. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET Request parameters cmd=create_user — command for creating a user login — login of the new user password — user password name — user name phone — user phone number email — user e-mail role_id — user role: 0 — Admin, 1 — User vehicles — list of available vehicles (IDs or count) folders — list of available folders (IDs or count) node — number of the node on which to run the command The request must include the login and password of the administrator who creates the user. Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=create_user login=TestAPI3 password=123456 name=Test API role_id=1 phone=789995 email=testapi5@mailinator.com vehicles=15 folders=5 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success create user: 48" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) msg — server message with the ID of the created user

This API lets you change the login and password of an existing user in the PILOT system. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET Request parameters cmd=update_user_auth — command for editing authorization data login — new user login password — new user password user_id — identifier of the user whose data you want to change node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=update_user_auth login=TestAPI password=qwerty user_id=48 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) msg — server message about the result of the action

This API deletes an existing user in the PILOT system by the user s identifier. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method DELETE Request parameters cmd=remove_user — command for deleting a user user_id — identifier of the user to delete node — number of the node on which to run the command (optional) Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=remove_user user_id=48 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success remove" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) msg— server message about the result of the action

This API returns user data by the user s user_id. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters cmd=get_user — API command for getting user information user_id — identifier of the user whose information you want to get node — number of the node on which the command runs Example GET request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_user user_id=19 node=1 Example POST request Request body (JSON): { "cmd": "get_user", "user_id": 19 } Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success", "data": { "id": 19, "roleid": 1, "info": "", "msisdn": "123123", "email": "testTOTP@testTOTP.com", "name": "dasd", "account_id": 1000, "lang": "en", "parent_id": 2 } } The API response contains: code — result code (0 = operation succeeded) msg — server message data — object with user information: id — user identifier roleid — user role (0 — Admin, 1 — User) info — additional user information msisdn — phone number email — user e-mail name — user name account_id — identifier of the account the user belongs to lang — user interface language parent_id— identifier of the parent user (if any)

This API is used to get the list of all users registered in your account. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters cmd=get_account_user_list — API command for getting the list of account users node — number of the node on which the command runs Example GET request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_account_user_list node=1 Example POST request Request body (JSON): { "cmd": "get_account_user_list" } Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "id": 19, "roleid": 1, "info": "", "msisdn": "123123", "email": "testTOTP@testTOTP.com", "name": "dasd", "account_id": 1000, "lang": "en", "parent_id": 2 } ] } The API response contains: code — result code (0 = operation succeeded) data — array of account users: id — user identifier roleid — user role (0 — Admin, 1 — User, 2 — Logistic, etc.) info — additional information msisdn — phone number email— user e-mail name — user name account_id — identifier of the account the user belongs to lang — user interface language parent_id — identifier of the parent user (if any)

This API is used to get the list of accounts the current user has access to. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters cmd=get_account_map — API command for getting the list of available accounts node — number of the node on which the command runs Example GET request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_account_map node=1 Example POST request Request body (JSON): { "cmd": "get_account_map" } Response { "code": 0, "data": [ {"account_id": 1005}, {"account_id": 1000} ] } The API response contains: code — execution code (0 means the operation succeeded) data — list of accounts available to the user account_id — account (contract) identifier

This API returns the list of folders the user has access to within the contract. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters • cmd=get_folders_user — command for getting the list of folders For a POST request, the parameters can be passed in the body in JSON format node — number of the node on which to run the command Example GET request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_folders_user node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success", "data": [ {"id":1,"name":"DEMO"}, {"id":6,"name":"ИП Емельянов"}, {"id":11,"name":"FOLDER1"}, {"id":12,"name":"FOLDER2"} ] } The API response contains: • code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) • msg — server message • data — array of user folders: • id — folder identifier • name — folder name

This API returns the folders the specified user has access to. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters cmd=get_folders_user — command for getting the list of folders user_id — user identifier (required when requesting another user s folders) node — number of the node on which to run the command For a POST request, the parameters can be passed in the body in JSON format Example requests GET request: https:// server_address /api/api.php? cmd=get_folders_user user_id=19 node=1 POST request: { "cmd": "get_folders_user", "user_id": 19 } Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success", "data": [ {"id":1,"name":"DEMO"}, {"id":6,"name":"ИП Емельянов"}, {"id":11,"name":"FOLDER1"}, {"id":12,"name":"FOLDER2"} ] } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) msg — server message data — array of user folders: id — folder identifier name — folder name

This API lets you change the set of folders a specific user has access to. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method POST Request parameters cmd=update_user_folders — command for updating the list of folders folders — comma-separated list of folder IDs to assign to the user user_id — identifier of the user whose folders are being changed Example request { "cmd": "update_user_folders", "folders": "1,11", "user_id": 19 } Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) msg — server message about the result of the action

This API lets you grant a user access to specific contracts. For example, if a partner has several contracts in the system, the administrator can choose which of them a particular user will have access to. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method POST Request parameters cmd=update_user_accounts_map — command for changing the list of available contracts accounts — comma-separated list of contract identifiers The contracts (accounts) must belong to the same partner as the user. user_id — identifier of the user to whom access is granted node — number of the node on which the command runs If the user's partner in the system is 0, contracts cannot be assigned ( mapping does not work). Example request { "cmd": "update_user_accounts_map", "accounts": "1005", "user_id": 19 } Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) msg — server message

This API grants a user access only to the selected vehicles. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method POST Request parameters cmd=update_user_vehicles — command for changing the list of objects vehicles — comma-separated list of object identifiers (vehicle IDs). user_id — identifier of the user whose access is being updated node — number of the node on which the command runs Example request { "cmd": "update_user_vehicles", "vehicles": "2,18", "user_id": 19 } Response { "code": 0, "msg": "Success" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — operation succeeded) msg — server message

This API returns data on the operation of vehicle sensors for the selected period. With it, you can: — track the periods when sensors are on/operating (for example, ignition, equipment switched on). — get location information at the moment a sensor turns on. — analyze hardware behavior and vehicle operation. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=sensors — command for getting sensor operation data imei — vehicle identifier in the system start — start of the selection (Unix timestamp) stop — End of the selection (Unix timestamp) node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=sensors imei=356307046690011 start=1404637430 stop=1404645198 node=1 Response Each sensor is represented by an object whose key is the sensor identifier in the system: "sensors": { "9175": { "fieldname": "DIS1", "info": "Датчик зажигания", "id": 9175, "work": { "1404637430": { "ts": 1404637430, "te": 1404637834, "lat": "46.3825", "lon": "48.0031", "place": "Россия, Астраханская область, Наримановский район, Николаевское шоссе, 1б" // Address }, "1404638577": { "ts": 1404638577, "te": 1404639841, "lat": "46.3625", "lon": "48.0478", "place": "RU, Астрахань, улица Савушкина" } // ... next sensor operation periods } } } The API response contains: fieldname — sensor field name in the system (for example, DIS1) info — sensor name in the system (for example, “Ignition sensor”) id — sensor identifier in the system work — object with the sensor operation periods; the keys are the turn-on times (ts) ts — time the sensor turned on (Unix timestamp) te — time the sensor turned off (Unix timestamp) lat — latitude at the moment of turning on lon — longitude at the moment of turning on place — address or location at the moment the sensor turned on

This API returns the values of discrete sensors (fuel level, temperature, weight, etc.) for a given period. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET Request parameters cmd =get_discrete_sensor_data — command for getting sensor data imei — object identifier start — start of the period (Unix timestamp) stop — end of the period (Unix timestamp) tag_id — sensor identifier agent_id — agent identifier (optional) node — number of the node on which to run the command Sensor data can only be requested for a 24-hour period. Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_discrete_sensor_data imei=350424062310402 start=1677682645 stop=1677761845 tag_id=1158 node=1 Response { "sensor_data": { "966960": { "1677682772": { "sensor_id": 966960, "unixtimestamp": 1677682772, "calibrated_value": "95.09", "speed": "0" }, "1677682950": { "sensor_id": 966960, "unixtimestamp": 1677682950, "calibrated_value": "94.9", "speed": "12" } } } } The API response contains: sensor_id — sensor identifier unixtimestamp — time the value was recorded (Unix timestamp) calibrated_value — calibrated sensor value (for example, liters of fuel or degrees of temperature) speed — object speed at the moment of measurement

This API returns information about the battery charge of a vehicle by VIN. Works only for objects that have: the VIN field filled in on the object card a battery charge sensor connected You can specify several VINs in the request; the response will then contain information for all the specified objects. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/VTB/api_vtb.php Request method POST Working with this API takes two steps: 1. Authorization — getting a token to access the data 2. Data request — using the token to get battery information by VIN 1. Authorization Before requesting data, you must authorize. Request body: { "login": "your_login", "password": "your_password", "cmd": "auth" } Response { "token": "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" } In the response you will receive a token — a long unique string. This token identifies the user in subsequent requests. Without the token, the API will not return battery data. 2. Getting battery sensor data After you get the token, you can request battery information. Request parameters Number — list of VINs of the vehicles you want to get information about. DateFrom — date and time of the start of the period (in ISO 8601 format). DateTo — date and time of the end of the period. cmd=vehicle — API command for requesting vehicle data Request headers: Authorization: Bearer — pass the token obtained during authorization Content-Type: application/json — indicates that the request body is in JSON format Request body: { "Number": ["object_VIN"], "DateFrom": "2023-12-03T00:00:00", "DateTo": "2023-12-12T00:00:00", "cmd": "vehicle" } Response [ { "Number": "456789123", "ApplicationNumber": null, "CurrentStatus": "ACTIVE", "CloseDateTime": "", "LastSyncDate": "2024-08-28 15:42:45", "AlarmDateTime": "2024-08-28 15:42:45", "Latitude": "55.578352", "Longitude": "38.125267", "BatteryCharge": "полный заряд", "LocationLinesID": "", "FullAddress": "улица Гарнаева, Рынок, Жуковский, Московская область, Россия", "Country": "Россия", "Region": "Московская область", "Town": "Жуковский", "Street": "улица Гарнаева", "House": null, "numberRegion": 10 } ] The API response contains: Number — vehicle VIN CurrentStatus — current object status LastSyncDate — date of the last synchronization BatteryCharge — battery charge level FullAddress, Country, Region, Town, Street — object location Latitude, Longitude — object coordinates

This API is used to determine the IMEI of the device installed on a vehicle by the vehicle number. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=get_imei — API command vehnum — vehicle number node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_imei vehnum=IX35 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "imei": "356307045913463" } The API response contains: code — result code (0 = success) msg — server message imei — IMEI of the device installed in the vehicle

This API returns the raw data of a device for a given period. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = ag_events — command for getting raw points imei — unique device identifier ts — start of the selection (Unix timestamp) te — end of the selection (Unix timestamp) node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=ag_events ts=1498201000 te=1498201200 imei=356307045913463 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "1498201016": {"alt": 33, "lat": "47.2124", "lon": "39.6922", "sat": 15, "speed": 0, "ts": 1498201016}, "1498201037": {"alt": 29, "lat": "47.2124", "lon": "39.6924", "sat": 15, "speed": 6, "ts": 1498201037}, "1498201097": {"alt": 31, "lat": "47.2128", "lon": "39.6933", "sat": 15, "speed": 0, "ts": 1498201097} }, "msg": "OK", "vehicle": {"agentid": 2914, "created_time": 1359797592, "current_mileage": 90224, "folder": "Sky Electronics", "imei": "356307045913463", "type": "Cow", "typeid": 31, "vehiclenumber": "IX35"} } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — success) msg — server message data — object with raw points; the keys are point timestamps, the values are: lat — latitude lon — longitude alt — altitude sat — number of satellites speed — speed ts — event time (Unix timestamp) vehicle — object information: agentid — agent identifier created_time — object creation time current_mileage — current mileage folder — folder/group name imei — device identifier type — object type typeid — object type identifier vehiclenumber — vehicle number

This API returns the list of iButtons assigned to a vehicle during a given period. iButton is a small electronic device (tag) used to identify drivers or objects. It is typically used for access control, working time tracking, or recording the start and end of work with a vehicle. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=take_ibutton_list — API command, in this case ts — start of the period (Unix timestamp) te — end of the period (Unix timestamp) agentId — vehicle identifier node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=take_ibutton_list ts=1643662800 te=1645045200 AgentID=79673 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": [ { "ibutton": "ae00001000000000", "ts": 1643680128 }, { "ibutton": "ae00001000000001", "ts": 1643680128 } ] } The API response contains: code — result code (0 — success) msg — server message (for example, OK ) data — array with iButton information: ibutton — unique iButton identifier ts — iButton recording time (Unix timestamp)

This API is used to get passenger flow data for vehicles equipped with an automatic conductor system. With it, you can: — see how many passengers boarded and exited at each stop — get stop coordinates, event time and video identifier (if the system supports video recording) How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd= pass_counter — command for calling the API ts — start of the selection in Unix timestamp format te — end of the selection in Unix timestamp format node — number of the node on which to run the command Optional: imei — IMEI of the vehicle equipped with the automatic conductor. If omitted, data is returned for all vehicles with the equipment Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=pass_counter ts=1554670800 te=1554757200 imei=963852741159753 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "36571": { "agent_id": 36571, "stops": [ { "busline_id": 1371, "door_id": 0, "lat": "54.9346", "lon": "51.8981", "p_in": 1, "p_out": 0, "ts": 1554696995, "video_id": 13 }, { "busline_id": 1371, "door_id": 0, "lat": "54.9238", "lon": "51.9098", "p_in": 4, "p_out": 0, "ts": 1554697232, "video_id": 14 } ], "vehiclenumber": "autoconductor" } }, "msg": "OK" } The API response contains: code — execution code (0 = success) msg — status message (for example, OK) data — main object with passenger flow data. agent_id — vehicle ID in the system vehiclenumber — internal vehicle number or equipment name (for example, autoconductor) stops — array of stops with passenger flow data busline_id — route ID door_id — number of the door through which passenger movement was recorded lat — stop latitude lon — stop longitude p_in — number of passengers who boarded p_out — number of passengers who exited ts — event time (Unix timestamp) video_id — ID of the video recording related to the event (if any)

This API is used to manage bus trips and to assign vehicles to routes. It creates routes and assigns vehicles to trips. How to get the data Method POST Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php Request parameters To get the data you need, add a command. cmd — command to execute Available commands setLine — creating a new bus route bindControl — assigning a vehicle to a route bindLineToVeh — assigning a route to a vehicle by ID unbindControl — removing a vehicle assignment listLines — getting the list of routes setControl — assigning a bus to a trip unsetControl — removing a trip assignment data — data in JSON format passed in the request body Examples Creating a bus route The setLine command creates a new route with the specified parameters and adds the route stops. https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=setLine Request body { "account_id": "3008", "bidirectional": 1, "description": "Маршрут №9", "label": "123", "name": "Маршрут №9", "number": "12304", "type_id": 0, "uid": "dhqwdh" "points": [ { "lat": "45.0207", "lon": "33.9993", "name": "Аэропорт__", "price": 15.35, "radius": "91", "silent": 0, "stop_type": 0, "ts": 600, "te": 700, "uid": "819897e2-843b-11e4-bf52-002354656fea" }, { "lat": "44.9078", "lon": "34.0784", "name": "7я горбольница", "price": 15.35, "radius": "90", "silent": 0, "stop_type": 0, "te": 1000, "ts": 900, "uid": "819897e8-843b-11e4-bf52-002354656fea" } ] } Request parameters Parameter Data type Description account_id String Contract number bidirectional Number Bidirectional trip (1 — round trip, 0 — one-way) description String Route description label String Additional route label name String Route name number String Route number (text or digit) type_id Number Transport type: 0 — bus, 1 — trolleybus, 2 — tram, 3 — minibus. uid String Unique route identifier points Array List of route stops Stop parameters Parameter Data type Description lat String Latitude of the stop center (decimal number) lon String Longitude of the stop center (decimal number) name String Stop name price Number Fare from the previous stop (decimal number) radius String Stop zone radius in meters (number) silent Number Notifications ban: 1 — banned, 0 — allowed stop_type Number Stop type: 0 — regular, 1 — technical (passengers are not counted), 2 — terminal (the counter is reset — all passengers exit) ts Number Arrival time at the stop relative to the previous one (in seconds) te Number Dwell time at the stop (in seconds) uid String Unique stop identifier Response { "status": "success", "message": "Маршрут успешно создан", "data": { "uid": "dhqwdh", "lineuid": "2567" } } Response parameters Parameter Description status Execution status: success or error message Message about the result of the execution data Data about the created route data.uid Unique route identifier data.lineuid Unique identifier of the created route Assigning a vehicle to a route The bindControl command is used to assign a vehicle to a specific route. The command links a GPS tracker to a route, sets the validity period of the assignment and configures the URL for receiving event notifications, for example, arrival at a stop or door opening. https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd= bindControl Request body { "uid": "121e1e1e12", "imei": "12304", "lineuid": "2e23e23e2e", "ts": "1392294840", "te": "1392321600", "message_url": "http://example.com/message.php", "prognoze_url": "http://example.com/prognoze.php" } Request parameters Parameter Data type Description uid String Unique assignment identifier imei String Vehicle IMEI lineuid String Unique route identifier ts String Start time of the assignment (in timestamp format) te String End time of the assignment (in timestamp format; if omitted, the assignment has no expiration) message_url String URL for event notifications (for example, arrival at a stop) prognoze_url String URL for stop arrival forecasts Response { "status": "success", "message": "Привязка успешно создана", "data": { "uid": "121e1e1e12", "imei": "12304", "lineuid": "2e23e23e2e" } } Response parameters Parameter Description status Execution status: success or error message Message about the result of the execution data Data about the created assignment data.imei Unique assignment identifier data.lineuid Unique route identifier Or use the bindLineToVeh command to assign a route to a vehicle in a simplified way, by route ID. https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=bindLineToVeh Request body { "data": { "imei": "12304", "lineid": "12345", "ts": "1392294840" } } Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": { "imei": "12304", "lineid": "12345" } } Removing a vehicle assignment from a bus line unbindControl is the command for removing a previously created assignment of a vehicle to a route. The request passes the unique assignment identifier uid that was created earlier. https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd= unbindControl Request body json { "uid": "qiwduhqiwdqkdqkn" } uid — unique assignment identifier Response { "status": "success", "message": "Привязка удалена", "data": { "uid": "qiwduhqiwdqkdqkn" } } Getting the list of routes The listLines command returns the list of all routes available to the current account. https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=listLines { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "data": [ { "id": 2955, "name": "125К", "number": "125К", "bidirectional": 1, "description": "125К", "account_id": 18306, "active": 1, "label": null, "uid": null, "type_id": 0, "price": "0.00", "interval": 10, "folder": null } ] } Creating a bus route and assigning a vehicle to it The combined setLine and bindControl command creates a new bus route and assigns a vehicle to that route. Request body { "uid": "qiwduhqiwdqkdqkn", "ts": "1392294840", "te": "1392321600", "name": "test", "imei": "359772039289781", "number": "861A", "message_url": "http://example.com/message.php", "prognoze_url": "http://example.com/prognoze.php", "points": [ { "uid": "1", "lat": "53.352142", "lon": "83.758749", "name": "Барнаульский автовокзал", "radius": "50", "stop_type": 0, "price": 15.35 }, { "uid": "2", "lat": "52.534012", "lon": "85.178777", "name": "Бийский автовокзал", "radius": "100", "stop_type": 0, "price": 15.35 } ] } Response { "status": "success", "message": "Маршрут и привязка успешно созданы", "data": { "uid": "qiwduhqiwdqkdqkn", "imei": "359772039289781", "lineuid": "2e23e23e2e" } }

This API returns the current state of a bus: the route, the current and next stops, and information about the route itself (number, fare, headway, etc.). How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=currentBusState — command for getting the bus status vehnum — bus number node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=currentBusState vehnum=А%20086%20КХ%20116%20RUS node=1 Response { "code": 0, "lines": [ { "id": 1086, "name": "1А", "number": "1А", "bidirectional": 1, "description": "1А", "active": 1, "price": "25.00", "interval": 10, "folder": null, "currentstop_id": 0, "currentstop_order": 0, "nextstop_id": 5217, "nextstop_order": 48 } ] } The API response contains: id — route ID name — route name number — route number bidirectional — bidirectional flag (1 — yes, 0 — no) active — route active flag (1 — active) price — fare interval — headway in minutes currentstop_id — ID of the stop where the bus is currently located currentstop_order — sequence number of the current stop nextstop_id — ID of the next stop nextstop_order — sequence number of the next stop

This API returns the predicted arrival time of buses, trolleybuses and minibuses at the specified stop. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = stationForecast — command for getting the arrival forecast stopid — stop identifier (taken from the PILOT interface node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=stationForecast stopid=7400 node=1 Response [ { "curent_stop": 1, "line_id": 1371, "line_name": "№ 17 С. КАЛЬФА - ПЛ. СУВОРОВА - УЛ. ГЕНЕРАЛА ЖИДИЛОВА", "line_num": "17", "line_type": "A", "this_stop": 32, "time": 4065, "vehicle": "BUS FLIGHT", "vehid": 48854 } ] The API response contains an array of objects with forecasts for each route at this stop: curent_stop — sequence number in the route of the stop where the vehicle is currently located line_id — route ID line_name — full route name line_num — route number line_type — route type: A — bus, T — trolleybus, M — minibus this_stop — sequence number of this stop in the route time — predicted arrival time at this stop, in seconds vehicle — vehicle license plate vehid — vehicle ID

This API returns the list of all stops for the specified route, including coordinates, stop type, order and fare. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To make the request, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd=stopList — command for getting the list of stops line_num — route number node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=stopList line_num=1Б node=1 Response { "code": 0, "line": { "id": 1083, "name": "1Б", "number": "1Б", "bidirectional": 1, "description": "1Б", "active": 1, "price": "25.00", "interval": 25, "folder": null, "stops": [ { "id": 5085, "name": "Центр занятости", "lat": "54.9036", "lon": "52.3315", "radius": 60, "stop_type": 0, "descr": null, "stop_order": 1, "price": "0.00", "ts": 0, "te": 0, "dir": 0, "silent": 0 }, { "id": 5086, "name": "Автовокзал", "lat": "54.9039", "lon": "52.3236", "radius": 60, "stop_type": 2, "descr": null, "stop_order": 2, "price": "0.00", "ts": 0, "te": 0, "dir": 0, "silent": 0 } ] } } The API response contains: id— unique route/stop identifier name— route or stop name number— route number bidirectional— 1 if the route is bidirectional active— 1 if the route is active price— fare interval— headway in minutes stops— array of route stops: lat, lon — stop coordinates radius— stop zone radius in meters stop_type— stop type: 0 — regular, 1 — technical, 2 — terminal stop_order— order of the stop in the route silent— 1 — do not generate messages for this stop

This API builds a route between two points and returns an arrival time forecast depending on the selected transport type. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To make the request, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters cmd = route — command for building a route mode — transport type, one of: bicycle — bicycle bus — bus car — car pedestrian — pedestrian scooter — scooter taxi — taxi truck — truck origin — coordinates of the departure point (lat,long) destination — coordinates of the arrival point (lat,long) node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=route mode=bus origin=47.211908,39.613767 destination=47.201699,39.668183 node=1 Response { "code": 0, "data": { "routes": [ { "id": "79de74af-5040-441a-ab7a-62d3d9f7a4b4", "sections": [ { "id": "2cc5fff7-fd4f-43ac-bcda-00d662207c63", "type": "vehicle", "departure": { "time": "2023-02-22T09:40:07+03:00", "place": { "type": "place", "location": { "lat": 47.2119, "long": 39.61372 }, "originalLocation": { "lat": 47.211908, "long": 39.613767 } } }, "arrival": { "time": "2023-02-22T09:52:32+03:00", "place": { "type": "place", "location": { "lat": 47.2017113, "long": 39.668221 }, "originalLocation": { "lat": 47.201699, "long": 39.668183 } } }, "summary": { "duration": 745, "length": 5452, "baseDuration": 530 }, "transport": { "mode": "bus" } } ] } ] } } The API response contains: code — result code (0 = success) routes — list of built routes sections — route segments with data: departure / arrival — time and coordinates of the start and end of the route summary — information about the duration and length of the route transport.mode — selected transport type

This API provides information about rental contracts from the Rent Car (AVIS) module: open, booked and closed contracts. For each contract, it returns data about the renter, the rental start and end points, the planned pick-up and return dates, and the contract and vehicle numbers. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters To get the data you need, add the following parameters to the request URL: cmd=rentcar_contracts — command for getting the list of rental contracts. status — status of the contracts to get. You can pass one status or several, separated by commas: open — open contracts (the rental is currently active) booked — booked contracts (reservation, the rental has not started yet) closed — closed contracts (the rental is finished) The requested data is returned as an array of rental contracts. Example request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=rentcar_contracts status=open,booked,closed Response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "list": [ { "driver_name": "Тестовый арендатор", "driver_phone": "905074521698", "end_location": { "title": "Dubai" }, "start_location": { "title": "Dubai" }, "mva": "12312", "ra": "16", "te_expected": 1775901540, "ts_expected": 1775812680, "plate_number": "Private house" }, { "driver_name": "Тестовый арендатор", "driver_phone": "905074521698", "end_location": { "title": "rgergrr" }, "start_location": { "title": "erterter" }, "mva": "2222", "ra": "17", "te_expected": 1775901540, "ts_expected": 1775812680, "plate_number": "ABC-123" } ] } The API response contains: code — status code (0 — success) msg — status message (OK — the request was completed successfully) list — array of rental contracts, each of which contains: driver_name — name of the renter (driver) the contract is issued to driver_phone — renter s contact phone number start_location — rental start point (vehicle pick-up): title — name/address of the pick-up point end_location — rental end point (vehicle return): title — name/address of the return point mva — rental contract number (Master Vehicle Agreement) ra — reservation / rental agreement number (Rental Agreement) ts_expected — planned rental start time (Unix timestamp) te_expected — planned rental end time (Unix timestamp) plate_number — vehicle license plate number under the contract

This API lets you get information about the eco-friendliness of vehicle driving for a given period. How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request parameters To get the data you need, add parameters to the request URL. Parameters are specified after the question mark “?” and separated by the ampersand “ ”. cmd = mileco_drive — command for getting trip data start — date and time of the start of the period you want to get data for stop — date and time of the end of the period Time is specified in Unix timestamp format — the number of seconds that have passed since January 1, 1970. vehid — identifier of the vehicle to get data for. To get data for one vehicle, enter its ID; for several vehicles, list their IDs separated by commas. If you do not specify the vehid parameter, the system will automatically return information for all vehicles assigned to your account. imei — unique number of the vehicle s GPS tracker. Use this parameter to get data for a specific tracker. When you specify imei, the vehid parameter is not needed. Example API request with imei: https:// address /api/api.php?cmd=mileco_drive start=1738113401 stop=1738631801 time_diff_type=1 imei=86645655031889725 time_diff_type — grouping of data by time. By default, data is collected for each day. time_diff_type=1 — data will be collected for every 7 days time_diff_type=2 — data will be collected for every month node — number of the node on which to run the command Example request https:// url /api/api.php?cmd=mileco_drive start=1738113401 stop=1738631801 time_diff_type=1 vehid=32,53 node=1 Response { "32": { "29.01.2025_01:16|04.02.2025_01:16": { "date": "Wednesday, 29.01.2025 01:16 - Tuesday, 04.02.2025 01:16", "veh_id": 32, "distance": 842.75354055, "agent_id": 545, "account_id": 10025, "account_name": "ИП Иванов", "veh_name": "О 511 ГР 123", "veh_type": "Car", "eco_data": { "speed": { "msg": "Speed", "cnt": 0, "val": 1290, "fee": 12 } } } } "53": { "29.01.2025_01:16|04.02.2025_01:16": { "date": "Wednesday, 29.01.2025 01:16 - Tuesday, 04.02.2025 01:16", "veh_id": 53, "distance": 8.24949075, "agent_id": 545, "account_id": 10025, "account_name": "ИП Иванов", "veh_name": "О 619АК 67", "veh_type": "Bus", "eco_data": [] } } The API response contains data for each vehicle: veh_id — vehicle identifier imei — unique tracker number distance — distance traveled during the specified period agent_id — contract identifier account_id — account number in the system account_name — account name veh_name — vehicle name veh_type — vehicle type eco_data — driving data

This API returns the list of available time zones that can be used when configuring a user or an object. How to get the data Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https:// server_address /api/api.php? Request method GET or POST Request parameters cmd=get_time_zones — command for getting the list of time zones node — number of the node on which the command runs Example GET request https:// server_address /api/api.php?cmd=get_time_zones node=1 Example POST request Request body (JSON): { "cmd": "get_time_zones" } Response { "code": 0, "data": [ { "text": "Africa/Abidjan" }, { "text": "Africa/Accra" }, { "text": "Africa/Addis Ababa" }, { "text": "Africa/Algeria" }, { "text": "Africa/Asmara" }, { "text": "Africa/Bamako" }, { "text": "Africa/Bangui" } ] } The API response contains: code — result code (0 = operation succeeded) data — list of available time zones text — time zone name in Region/City format

To work with User API v3 , use the Swagger interface: https://pilot-swagger.pilot-gps.com/ This API version provides updated and structured methods for working with the system. In Swagger, you can: — view the list of all available methods — study request parameters and responses — test the API right in the browser

The method returns the last saved position of a vehicle. The vehicle is identified by its exact name in PILOT. The method is intended for integration with shipment tracking systems, including WIMT. Unlike methods that use IMEI, the request passes the vehicle name — truckNo. An interactive description of the method is available in Swagger — Track and Trace How to get the data Method POST Request URL https:// server_address /api/v3/vehicles/track-and-trace Replace server_address with the address of your PILOT server. Authorization The request uses standard API V3 authorization with a Bearer token. Pass the token in the Authorization header: Authorization: Bearer access_token Replace access_token with a valid API V3 token. Request headers Header Required Description Authorization Yes Bearer token for user authorization in API V3 X-Node Yes User node number. Used to route the request to the right server Content-Type Yes Request body format. Specify application/json Accept No Response format. Recommended value — application/json Example headers: Authorization: Bearer access_token X-Node: 3 Content-Type: application/json Accept: application/json Request parameters Parameters are passed in the request body in JSON format. Parameter Type Required Description shipmentNo String Yes Shipment or freight number. The method accepts the value but does not store or return it truckNo String Yes Vehicle name in PILOT. Must exactly match the vehiclenumber value countryID String Yes Country code, for example ZA. Returned in the response unchanged trackingFlag String Yes Tracking state, for example START or STOP. In the current version the value is accepted but not stored and does not affect request processing Vehicle lookup The method looks up a vehicle by the exact truckNo value among the vehicles available to the authorized user. The passed value must fully match the vehicle name — vehiclenumber — in PILOT. Take into account letter case, spaces and special characters. For example, if the vehicle is named KS51YPGP_F, the request must pass: "truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F" If the name does not match or the user has no access to the vehicle, the method will not return its position. Example request { "shipmentNo": "SHIPMENT-123", "truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F", "countryID": "ZA", "trackingFlag": "START" } Example cURL request: curl --request POST \ --url "https:// server_address /api/v3/vehicles/track-and-trace" \ --header "Authorization: Bearer access_token " \ --header "X-Node: 3" \ --header "Content-Type: application/json" \ --header "Accept: application/json" \ --data '{ "shipmentNo": "SHIPMENT-123", "truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F", "countryID": "ZA", "trackingFlag": "START" }' Response If the request succeeds, the method returns the last saved GPS position of the vehicle, the address, the time zone and the account name. Successful response fields Field Type Description code Integer Request execution code. A value of 0 means successful execution msg String Request result. OK is returned on success process_time Number Request processing time in seconds countryID String Country code received in the request. Returned unchanged timeZone String Time zone in IANA format, for example Africa/Johannesburg truckNo String Name of the found vehicle in PILOT latitude Number Latitude of the last saved GPS position longitude Number Longitude of the last saved GPS position source String Name of the account the vehicle belongs to streetName String Address of the last position, obtained by reverse geocoding lastRecordedOn Integer Time of the last GPS position in Unix timestamp format The shipmentNo, trackingFlag and trackLink fields are not returned in the response. Example successful response { "code": 0, "msg": "OK", "process_time": 0.001, "countryID": "ZA", "timeZone": "Africa/Johannesburg", "truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F", "latitude": -26.2041, "longitude": 28.0473, "source": "Example Fleet", "streetName": "Main Road, Johannesburg", "lastRecordedOn": 1785142800 } Time formats Time zone The timeZone field contains a time zone identifier from the IANA database: "timeZone": "Africa/Johannesburg" The IANA identifier defines a regional time zone and allows its rules to be applied correctly. The method does not return a fixed offset, such as UTC+02:00. Time of the last position The lastRecordedOn field contains the time of the last GPS position in Unix timestamp format: "lastRecordedOn": 1785142800 A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds that have passed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. The value does not depend on the time zone. To show the date and time to a user, convert lastRecordedOn taking the timeZone value into account. Address determination The streetName field is produced by reverse geocoding: PILOT converts the coordinates of the last position into a text address. "streetName": "Main Road, Johannesburg" The completeness and accuracy of the address depend on the available map data.

PILOT Task Manager ( Task Manager ) is a PILOT module for managing tasks. With the API of this module, you can: — create, edit and delete tasks — assign tasks to assignees — get the completion status and deadlines — get information about current and completed tasks

This API is used to create tasks in the system for contracts with the PTM module connected. API base path /backend/public/api/task Request URL To make the request, use the following URL format: https:// server_address /backend/public/api/task API access API access uses HTTP Basic authentication. The login and password must be in the format: PILOT_login:PILOT_password API request example https://demo:demo@tasks.pilot-gps.com/backend/public/api/task/create_universal API response format The API response is standardized and has the following format: { "success": true, // TRUE - successful request, FALSE - error "msg": "OK", // Error message, if any "httpCode": 200, // Error code "data": [], // Response data, if any "et": 0, // Request execution time "exceptionMsg": "Exception" // Exception message } Statuses and error codes: 200 — Request completed successfully 400 — Required parameters are missing 401 — Authorization error: incorrect login or password 404 — API route not found 500 — Server error How to create a task Request method: POST To create a task with the Universal template, you need to pass parameters.
