The Universal template is created automatically in the system; additional templates must be configured in advance in the PTM interface. Task parameters for the Universal template A task with the Universal template uses the following set of parameters: 1. external_id: External task identifier (string, NULL by default) 2. vehicle_plate: Vehicle number (NULL by default). If the number does not exist in the system, it will be created as a hired vehicle 3. driver_name: Driver s full name (NULL by default). If not specified, the value from vehicle_plate is used. If the driver does not exist in the system, the driver will be created as a hired driver 4. type_name: Task type (Delivery by default). If there is no such type, it will be created 5. template_name: Task template name (Universal by default). If the template does not exist, it will be created 6. time_zone: Time zone, offset from UTC (number, time in minutes from UTC, NULL by default) 7. time_zone_name: Time zone name (string, NULL by default) 8. c_begin_time: Planned task start time (number — timestamp in seconds, current time by default) 9. c_return_time: Planned task completion time (number, NULL by default) 10. route_name: Route name (string, NULL by default) 11. cargo: Cargo name (string, NULL by default) 12. temp_min: Minimum temperature (number, 2°C by default) 13. temp_max: Maximum temperature (number, 8°C by default) 14. description: Task description (string, NULL by default) 15. addresses_list (required): List of addresses or route points (strings with addresses or coordinates) Parameters related to the route address The address of each route point can be supplemented with various suffixed parameters that describe route characteristics and geographic data. 1. addresses_list: List of addresses or route points (strings with addresses or coordinates). 2. addresses_list_lat: Array of latitudes of the route points. If specified, it will be used for each address 3. addresses_list_lng: Array of longitudes of the route points. An array of numbers representing the longitude of the route points 4. addresses_list_date_point: Array of timestamps (seconds) indicating the planned arrival time 5. addresses_list_date_point_to: Array of timestamps (seconds) indicating the planned departure time. Calculated automatically if not specified 6. addresses_list_time_point: Array of loading/unloading times at the route point, in minutes 7. addresses_list_redirect: Flag for redirecting the current address to the next one. Indicates that the address is redirected to the next one along the route. 8. addresses_list_geofence_id: Geofence identifiers for each route point 9. addresses_list_warehouse: Names of warehouses or objects for each route point 10. addresses_list_ticket: Array of unique order identifiers for each route point 11. addresses_list_phones: Contact phone numbers for each route point 12. addresses_list_schedule: Working hours for each route point 13. addresses_list_vehicle_volume: Cargo volume in the vehicle 14. addresses_list_trailer_volume: Cargo volume in the trailer 15. addresses_list_action: Description of actions to perform at each route point 16. addresses_list_agent_id: Object identifier from the PILOT system, used for waste containers Example request fetch("https://tasks.pilot-gps.com/backend/public/api/task/create_universal", { "headers": { "Authorization": "Basic ZGVtbzpkZW1v", // base64 encoding of "demo:demo" "Content-Type": "application/json" }, "method": "POST", "body": JSON.stringify({ "external_id": "T-5677786754", "vehicle_plate": "PT 125 AA 66", "driver_name": null, "type_name": "Delivery", "template_name": "Universal", "time_zone": -180, "time_zone_name": "Europe/Moscow", "c_begin_time": 1723233360, "c_return_time": 1723238700, "route_name": "My route", "cargo": "Milk", "temp_min": 2, "temp_max": 6, "description": "Test", "addresses_list": [ "215, улица Народного Ополчения, Ростов-на-Дону", "47.227196,39.705228", "Client 2" ], "addresses_list_lat": [ 47.234256, 47.227196, 47.216077 ], "addresses_list_lng": [ 39.706467, 39.705228, 39.706928 ], "addresses_list_date_point": [ 1723233360, 1723234800, 1723237800 ], "addresses_list_time_point": [ 10, 20, 15 ], "addresses_list_rad_geo": [ 50, 40, 30 ] }) }); Example response { "success": true, "msg": "OK", "httpCode": 200, "data": { "id": 12563 }, "et": 0.5612 }

This API is used to get information about waybills for a given period. With it, you can: — get the list of tasks for each agent — view planned and actual execution times — find out execution statuses and details for route points How to get the data Method GET Request URL To get the data, use the URL: https://tasks . server_address /backend/public/get_waybill_for_pilot Request parameters from_ts — start of the selection (Unix timestamp, example: 1536181200) to_ts — end of the selection (Unix timestamp, example: 1538773200) agents — list of agent identifiers, separated by commas (for example: 13128,13130,...) Example request https:// server_address /backend/public/get_waybill_for_pilot?from_ts=1536181200 to_ts=1538773200 agents=13128,13130,21055 Response { "success": true, "msg": "", "items": [ { "agent_id": 13128, "c_begin_time": "1536200000", "c_end_time": "1536210000", "c_information": "{\"route\":\"Маршрут №54\",\"driver\":\"Иванов И.И.\"}", "c_initiator": "Диспетчер", "c_progress_time": "1536200500", "c_running_time": "1536200300", "c_status_id": 2, "c_status_name": "Выполнено", "id": 98765, "points_info": [ { "point_id": 1, "lat": "55.7558", "lon": "37.6173", "visited_at": "1536200600" } ] } ] } The API response contains: success — execution result (true — success, false — error) msg — error message (if any) items — array of task data For each task: agent_id — agent identifier c_begin_time — planned task start time c_end_time — actual task completion time c_information — string with additional task information (JSON, depends on the template) c_initiator — requester (who created the task) c_progress_time — actual time of visiting the first point c_running_time — actual time of departure to perform the task c_status_id — task status identifier c_status_name — task status description id — task identifier in the PTM system points_info — array of information about the visited route points

This section contains information on how to connect and configure various hardware. It describes the main connection steps, device operating features and examples of specific settings.

Jimi video recorders are configured with text commands. You simply send the device the command you need, and it starts working the way you want. With these commands, you can: — connect the recorder to the server — specify where to send video and trip data — enable online streaming — set up automatic video upload for certain events In this article, we will go through the commands that will help you start and properly configure the device. Main setup commands 1. Allowing the server connection COREKITSW,0 This command allows the video recorder to connect to the PILOT video server. In other words, it enables the device to work with the platform. 2. Setting up the telemetry server SERVER,1, domain name ,20056 or SERVER,0, IP address ,20056 Here you specify the server to which telemetry (movement, speed and event data) will be sent. 1 — if you use a domain name (for example: server.example.com) 0 — if you connect by IP address (for example: 192.168.1.100) 20056— communication port 3. Setting up the server for video upload UPLOAD, https://server_address/upload The address of the server to which video files will be sent, for example, during playback or event upload. 4. Setting up the server for online streaming RSERVICE, rtmp://server_address/live This command sets the RTMP server for live real-time video streaming. 5. Setting up the server for the file list FILELIST, https://server_address/filelist The address to which the recorder sends the list of available video recordings. 6. Automatic upload of event videos UPLOADSW, A , B This command lets you specify which events should trigger automatic video upload and which cameras to use. A — the event that triggers video upload. For example: CRASH (crash), SOS (panic button), OVERSPEED (speeding). B — upload mode: — OFF — disable automatic upload — ON — upload video from both cameras (front and interior) — 1 — upload video from the front camera only — 2 — upload video from the interior camera only For example: UPLOADSW,CRASH,ON — when the “Crash” event is triggered, the recorder automatically uploads video from both cameras. List of events The table below lists all the events the recorder can recognize. You can use them in the UPLOADSW command. № Event code Meaning 1 SOS SOS button pressed 2 CRASH Crash 3 VIBRATE Vibration / impact 4 OVERSPEED Speeding 5 RAPIDACC Harsh acceleration 6 RAPIDDEC Harsh braking 7 RAPIDTURN Harsh turn 8 DRIVE Driving mode 9 POWER Power change 10 VOLTAGELOW Low voltage 11 CLOSEEYES Fatigue / closed eyes 12 YAWN Yawning, a sign of fatigue 13 DISTRACTION Driver distracted 14 SMOKING Smoking while driving 15 PHONECALLING Phone use 16 RELAYOFF Relay off 17 RELAYRECOVERY Relay restored 18 MISSINGFACE Face not detected 19 NOSDCARD No SD card 20 SDCARDMOUNT SD card inserted 21 OIL Oil sensor event 22 OILTO Oil error 23 TEMPTO Engine overheating 24 UART UART error 25 LANEDEPARTURE Lane departure 26 VEHICLETOOCLOSE Another vehicle too close 27 FORWARDCOLLISION Collision risk 28 UART_DOOR Door sensor 29 AFIS Face detection (AI) 30 AFIF Face recognition error 31 AWSB Seat belt detection 32 ANWSB Seat belt not fastened

For Jimi video recorders (JC181, JC182, JC450, JC451, JC371) to connect to the PILOT server and transmit data and video, you need to send them several commands. You can send the commands to the device by SMS or through a remote management server (depending on how the device is configured). Below are examples of commands for setting up the connection to PILOT. 1. Server setup SERVER,video.pilot-gps.com,6608,NA,NA,NA,NA# This command tells the device where to send the data. video.pilot-gps.com — PILOT server 6608 — port NA — enter it if a parameter has no value (an empty field must always be filled with NA). 2. APN setup APN,internet,,,,,,,,,mtn,,mtn,,,,,,, This command configures the access point for the SIM card so that the device can connect to the internet. internet — access point name (APN) mtn — login mtn — password 3. Device identifier setup BCD,1# This command determines which identifier the device will use: 1 = last 12 digits of the IMEI 4. Time zone setup TIMEZONE,±hh:mm This command sets the time zone for the device so that event times on the server match the actual local time. For example, Moscow time is UTC+03:00: TIMEZONE,+03:00 5. Rebooting the device REBOOT After all the settings are made, reboot the device so that the new parameters take effect.

This article describes the requirements and recommendations for deploying PILOT on your organization s dedicated infrastructure. The information is intended for system administrators, engineers and integrators who prepare the infrastructure and keep the system running. Choosing the server configuration The configuration depends on the expected load: — the number of connected devices and the message transmission frequency — the number of concurrent users — the reports and integrations used — data retention periods — connected modules The baseline parameters are a starting point for production use. They do not guarantee performance under any load. Baseline configuration The recommended starting configuration is designed for a system with up to 30,000 connected devices without the video module: Component Recommendation Processor From 8 physical cores or dedicated server-class vCPUs RAM From 64 GB System partition From 100 GB SSD Database From 2 TB NVMe or enterprise-class SSD; for a physical server — RAID 10 Backups Separate storage; the capacity is calculated according to the retention policy Network Stable connection with guaranteed bandwidth and low packet loss If devices transmit data every 1–5 seconds, the load on the processor, database and disks increases significantly. For this mode, run load testing in advance and provide a reserve of resources. RAID increases disk fault tolerance but does not replace backups. Data storage Raw events from devices are stored in the database. The retention period is determined by the system settings and the available disk space. It should normally not exceed three months. When calculating the storage capacity, take into account: the number of devices and the average message frequency the retention period of raw events the volume of history, tracks and report data attachments, photos and media files the size and retention period of backups Calculate the backup storage capacity based on the size of a full database copy, the number of copies kept and the compression used. Provide a reserve of at least 20%. A fixed capacity of 1 TB is not suitable for every installation. Separating components Under high load, it is recommended to place the system components on separate servers. Server role When required Minimum recommended configuration Application server Baseline installation 8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM Database server Usually recommended from 5000 devices or with intensive telematics data transmission 8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, from 2 TB NVMe/SSD PTM and “Logistics” With a large number of tasks, routes or calculations The need for a separate server and its configuration are determined after the load is assessed Video server When the video module is used From 16 vCPU, 128 GB RAM, separate storage The database server must be in the same protected local network as the application server. PostgreSQL, Redis and Memcached must not be accessible from the Internet. Video storage The size of the video archive depends on the number of cameras, the average bitrate, the recording duration and the retention period. For a preliminary estimate, use the formula: Capacity, TB = number of cameras × average bitrate, Mbit/s × hours of recording per day × retention days × 0.00045 × 1.3 Choose the operating system of the video server taking into account the requirements of the hardware and its drivers. For new installations, use a supported edition of Windows Server, Windows Server 2019 or later. Extended support for Windows Server 2019 lasts until January 2029. Support dates are published on the Microsoft Lifecycle page. Operating system and software components The supported platform is Oracle Linux 8 x86_64 or an operating system image agreed with technical support. The installation includes: Nginx PHP-FPM and the required PHP extensions PostgreSQL Redis Memcached SocketProxy and device message handlers background jobs and monitoring tools The exact component versions are determined by the installation package of the specific PILOT release. Do not update them manually without checking compatibility and agreeing on the time of the work. Virtual environment Deployment in a virtual environment is supported provided that the resource requirements are met: CPU resources and memory must be reserved the disk subsystem must provide the required number of input/output operations per second — IOPS significant overcommitment of virtual machine resources is not allowed: the allocated resources must be backed by physical infrastructure Test environment For a test environment with up to 100 devices, the following configuration is sufficient: Component Parameters Processor 4 vCPU RAM 8 GB RAM Storage 200 GB SSD Such an environment is not intended for production use or load testing. Network requirements Open incoming connections only when necessary. Purpose Protocol and port Connection source Web interface and API HTTPS, TCP 443 User workstations and permitted integrations Redirect to HTTPS HTTP, TCP 80 If necessary Receiving device messages TCP/UDP ports of the protocols in use Devices and trusted networks Administration SSH, TCP 22 VPN, bastion host or agreed IP addresses only Monitoring According to the monitoring system settings Permitted addresses only The PostgreSQL, Redis and Memcached ports must be accessible only within the server segment. For outgoing connections, the server may need: DNS and NTP time synchronization HTTPS access to operating system repositories and external services SSH access to gitlab.pilot-gps.com via TCP port 22122 for installation and updates access to the geocoding, routing, map and integration services connected in the system Configure access rules for external services by domain names and agreed ports rather than by static IP addresses: service addresses may change. If a local map tile server is not deployed, user workstations also need access to the map resources. For the duration of the installation, give the server controlled access to the required repositories and services. Unrestricted Internet access is not required. Backup and recovery Before putting the system into operation, define a backup policy. It should include: database backup backup of the configuration, certificates and integration settings separate backup of media files and the video archive, if they are used storing copies outside the main server encrypting copies and restricting access to them regular recovery testing The backup frequency and retention period are determined according to the requirements of the system owner: RPO — the acceptable period of data loss in case of failure RTO — the acceptable time to restore the system A successfully created backup does not prove that it is suitable for recovery. Periodically perform test recovery and check the result. Preparing for operation Before starting the system, you need to: 1. Set up a TLS certificate for the production domain name 2. Restrict access with a firewall: allow only the necessary connections 3. Close direct access to service components from the Internet 4. Set up personal SSH accounts with key-based authentication 5. Ensure time synchronization 6. Set up monitoring of service availability, free space, load, processing queues and backup results 7. Agree on the time for updates and appoint responsible employees Access for technical support Remote technical support requires secure SSH access via VPN or an intermediate access server — a bastion host. Grant access only to authorized specialists, for a limited time and with action logging. What to prepare before installation To agree on the installation, prepare: Domain name, static IP address and TLS certificate Expected load parameters and the list of modules used The list of device protocols and ports Network rules and addresses for administration Information about the space allocated for the database, backups and media files Requirements for RPO, RTO and data retention periods Contacts of the employees responsible for the infrastructure and access Monitoring parameters and the channel for receiving alerts Post-installation check After installation, the system is accepted. It includes checking: — receiving data from devices — generating reports — operation of integrations — operation of monitoring — test recovery from a backup
